I found Ming Lee while looking for a 'restaurant near me'. I was skeptical based on location, but do not let that deter you!
I have not been disappointed with any of the dishes I've tried. We chose Ming Lee over and over, taking almost biweekly trips to Waterville.
The Crab Rangoon are to die for. Today I shared an order of Shrimp Pad Thai; enough for three people.
Fast, friendly service and delicious food.
Don't hesitate!

name: Kyle Robblee
text: My favorite Chinese restaurant by far!!! The staff is always friendly and the owner always comes by to see how everything is and to greet you. Mae is very down to earth and humble. I love that it is a locally owned business and it still thrives on its orignal concept of great customer service, food and atmosphere. Large portions and great prices that can't be beat! Highly recommend this place to anyone craving great Chinese food.

name: Fantasy Forge
text: I used to eat at Ming Lee almost daily for 3 years until i found a more authentic Chinese restaurant half a mile away. Ming Lee's food is always of great quality and the portions are huge, but the reason i only gave 3 stars is because it does not resemble the taste or style of Chinese cooking. The food has been way too westernized everything is covered in the same tasting sauce/gravy. Don't get me wrong this is an extremely popular restaurant the wait staff are excellent and the owners are always around to welcome you back, it just isn't Chinese. I lived in China for many months and while there sampled the food from many regions some of the most amazing comes from Xian. If you like highly westernized Chinese food then Ming Lees is the place for you.

text: My favorite Chinese restaurant, I always get the D17 dinner, General Tao, it's the only spicy food I ever eat, very delicious. It comes with pork fried rice and an egg roll for $9.80. They have all the awesome drinks that you would expect from them,  with equally outrageous names. Another great menu item is the Pu Pu Platter for 2 for $21.95, that is a sampler of beef teriyaki, chicken wings, chicken fingers, egg rolls, chicken teriyaki, boneless  spare ribs, and crab rangoons. You can add more people for $12.00 each, or go solo for $11.50. This is a great place for a romantic dinner to share a bowl drink and a Pu Pu platter with or a big group of friends to just have a great time. It does get packed at dinner time, so if you are bringing a large group call in advance and plan on a wait, but it's well worth it. If your short on time, you can always do a classic Chinese takeout. Either way, I would recommend this restaurant to die hard fans of Chinese food and new comers alike.

text:
I really really wanted to give this place 5 stats because it's a MB dealer. Being an MB owner comes with perks for being treated above and beyond when you visit for service. My experience wasn't the case really as I visited for a routine 40,000 mile service.

A part we needed wasn't ordered correctly so it wasn't installed and I wasn't going to stick around 4 days to get the right part in. The lady who was my contact wasn't on top of calling me back with updates or answers to questions I had...and She couldn't even remember who I was after I left and returned 5hrs later.

When they were done with my service and had washed the van (standard practice), the inside passenger side was all wet. The person washing the van had left the window down. Once it was noticed he put the window up but DIDN'T wipe or clean down the inside mess he made.

The needed service on the van was done right and to my liking thought. So for reliable service I'd say bring it in. But if you're looking for that little extra customer care be careful.

text:
The food is very good. Cakes r the best I've ever tasted, as are the scones. My issue is with being overcharged. This has happened to me at least 3 times. As much as I like the food I think I may stop giving them my business. My sister & I stop in a lot & get the half priced pastries. What happens is they often still charge u full price for the half priced stuff. U don't get a receipt unless u ask for one and then it's not itemized so u have no idea what u pay for individual items. This last time, yesterday, I once again paid then realized it was more than it should've been. I called & asked the prices of cream horns & scones. The woman confirmed the price & that I was charged full price for the cream horn. No apology or offer to refund. It's only 1.25, but if I wanted to pay full price I'd have gotten a fresh one, not the bargain ones. The most annoying thing is the woman who rang me up said "These are all the half priced items correct?" And still charged me full price, then didn't give me a receipt. I've been here a lot & try to save when I can because their prices r quite high.
I know this has happened numerous times, but it's a bit embarassing to go back & complain about being overcharged & hold up the line.

If I do get a big craving for a scone perhaps I will get ONE and only one, so I'll know what I am charged for that one item.
Their pastries are quite good though and cakes are the best around. Just be aware if buying half priced items.

Food and service were on point . It was our first time so we went in with an open mind .
Walking in ,there were 2 people on the front porch smoking cigarettes and we don’t smoke so the smoke wasn’t a pleasant introduction .
While eating it was apparent the “smokers” were employees , which I find additionally unappealing .

While leaving we were greeted with the same cloud of smoke as we exited the front door , a group of 3 or 4 including the same 2 from earlier were smoking on the front porch .

I get it , people smoke . Don’t do it on the front porch . Don’t do it in front of a restaurant . The thought of your stinky ash tray hands touching my food is not appealing to me .
The place was plenty busy ,so they don’t need my money .

name: G to the B
text:
I only visited to discuss the building but I got to observe the store for 5-10 minutes.  I was impressed by the excited activity of the small crowd of ladies discussing prints for projects they were planning.  The owner was right into it as well and there were even cheers as different members of the group made their selections.  Everyone seemed to have a great time, and the store was jam-packed with fabrics and threads and the like.
I was also surprised to find that the modular building down below the original building is an open space with tables and chairs for seamstresses to sit and work and chat with one another.  There's room there for sewing and quilting bees, and perhaps classes.  I formed the impression that there is a thriving community grown around Mainely Sewing, and I slightly envy its members although I've no interest in sewing, quilting, or embroidery.  If you do, or are looking for that sort of community, I think Mainely Sewing deserves a strong recommendation.

name: Alex Seise
text: I'd be lying if I said this wasn't my favorite place to go shopping for gifts and souvenirs in the entire world!  Land's End Gift Shop is so perfectly nostalgic and quaint, and its location perched above the rocks of Bailey Island overlooking the Atlantic Ocean is second to none.  The panoramic views are just part of the joy of shopping here.  From a great selection of tourist-centric supplies (like t-shirts and branded novelties) to Maine-made artisanal products, you can find a present for anyone on your list here.  During the on-season, the upstairs is filled with Christmas ornaments and decor, a perfect way to remember the coast of Maine when you're sitting by the fireside around the holidays.  When you visit, plan to spend a few minutes on the porch overlooking the ocean, or checking out the rocks below.  It's the closest you can get to perfection in New England, for sure.

name: Rejean Beauchamp
text:
(Translated by Google) To do some shopping and take pictures.

We took a break of about 30 minutes there on October 8, 2018 at noon to take a few pictures and also to stroll a little in this business. This last activity is more of a specialty of my wife than mine. I am more inclined to admire the landscapes and to take pictures and I was fulfilled at that level. I don't think my wife succumbed to buying anything, but I'm not really sure. We recommend this business if you have a weakness for this kind of shop but especially for the picturesque and serene seaside environment. We offer pictures.

Notice written on October 16, 2018 in Salaberry de Valleyfield, Quebec, Canada.

(Original)
Pour y faire quelques achats et prendre des photos.

Nous y avons fait une pause arrêt d’environ 30 minutes le 8 octobre 2018 sur l’heure du midi pour y prendre quelques photos et aussi pour flâner un peu dans ce commerce.  Cette dernière activité est davantage une spécialité de mon épouse que la mienne.  Je suis plus porté vers l’admiration des paysages et pour prendre des photos et je fus comblé à ce niveau.  Je crois bien que mon épouse n’a pas succombé à acheter de quoi mais je n’en suis pas vraiment sûr.  Nous recommandons ce commerce si vous ave un faible pour ce genre de boutique mais surtout aussi pour l’environnement pittoresque et serein de bord de mer.  Nous vous proposons des photos.

Avis rédigé le 16 octobre 2018 à Salaberry de Valleyfield, Québec, Canada.

Me and my bro also got a slice of pizza, and it was only a bit better then the calzone. The sauce was very watery, the bread of the pizza was about as thin as the cardboard of their pizza boxes (about the size of two finger nails stacked), and the crust tasted like paper mixed with flour. Also the crust had a lot of flour on it. Over all the quality of sbarro's food was worse than my old elementary school's cafeteria food; their food was pretty bad. On a more positive note, the Starbucks here had good food and the staff were pretty quick, despite the long line and didn't mess up any of my Mom's orders.

text:
I don't believe I've EVER given a 2star before.  I just wanted to use the restroom. That I did, the cleaning person was mopping the floor, or if you could call it that! Just pushing dirt,&mud around on the floor which SHOULD have been swept beforehand. Yet,as you can see, the broom and dustpan were tucked away in a corner. A pic above shows where they were& where they'd been the entire time.  Then go out to wash your hands and the foaming hand soap dispensers weren't even in the Restroom, the refill containers were stored on the sink& what a Challenge it was to get the soap on your hands w/out the bottle falling onto the floor or in the sink. No Papertowels, just EMPTY dispensers, &the hot air blowers,WELL they worked just fine, if you wanted a pressure DRY!
THE ONE POSITIVE NOTE, about this visit, it was the first time I'd noticed the Electric Car Plug Stations Telsa's 8 booths(looked similar to the old payphones(back when you could find one!) It was after Dark around 7pm,& the Rest Area was almost EMPTY.
OH YEAH LET'S NOT FORGET TO MENTION if YOU want a Bottled water or soda, be prepared to pay $2.75, for it. OMGOODNESS, I couldn't believe it. No I didn't get one.
This was my Worst Experience here,yet I was headed Southbound & whenever I've stopped before it's been Northbound and that gets 4stars. 2 stars here for this experience was GENEROUS!

name: John C. Madden
text:
It’s a service plaza, so having clean restrooms is the most important thing.  And they’re pristine.  It’s like there’s two or three Rumbas roaming around in there constantly.

For amenities, it’s a plus (for me, maybe not for you) that there’s a Starbucks there.  Coffee is a must for most folks in the road, so when your standards don’t have to drop, you’re thankful.  After that, you have all the usual fast food suspects — Burger King, Sbarro, Popeye’s.  No healthy options unless you want to scrounge around “Z Market”, the tacky, airport-like convenience store, to try to find a bag of cashews or something.  Be careful, though, because you’re going to need a loan to pay for it.  Ridiculously overpriced, as is the gas.  And that’s where this place has to get knocked down to two stairs.  I just can’t tolerate the blatant only-place-in-town price gouging.

text: It was conveniently located off the south bound travel lanes of the Maine turnpike.  It was clean but is usually busy with tourist.  The food service venders there charge way too much for what you actually get(especially for fast food) and they don't participate in any of the national or local meal promotions  (especially the Burger King), which is where I felt I was being rushed to order by the counter person. I understand they get alot of people through there a day, but they need to realize that they are in the people busness. So after looking over the menu quickly and saw what they were charging compared to other locations, I decided to leave without ordering anything.  Again, the establishment was clean and you could get fuel for your vehicle there, but the staff and meal prices were undesirable. Sorry folks, only two stars. You'd be better to get off the turnpike and go to a local establishment for your meals and stretch your legs. I think it'll be worth the extra effort of getting off then back on (cheaper too).

text:
Launch entrance is from Mere Point Road NOT Birch Island Road. There is a two lane back down launch area with a float system in the middle to separate the launch sides.

Boats may be tied up for short periods at the end of the ramps.

Kayakers should unload their boats onto the grass area between the parking lots and the actual launch and hand carry boats down when ready to launch. There is a separate wooden kayak slide next to granite steps off to the left as you face the motorized launch area for kayakers.

No swimming off the docks.

Be prepared for the SW winds that build mid morning and stay up through late afternoon.

The new owners have worked hard to upgrade Cook's from the run down past, but they still have work to do.  I was served a plate of broiled haddock with baked potato and a small plastic tub of coleslaw.  It all looked bleak, and tasted worse.  The fish was overcooked and looked like it had sat under a hot lamp for far too long.  I sent it back and received a fried haddock sandwich that was at least ready quickly and reasonably tasty. name: Alex Seise
text: Cook's Lobster House is an institution from my youth.  I can't begin to tell you how many long-lasting family stories have either started, happened at or finished in this restaurant.  But believe me: this place is worth the hype.  First and foremost, the location is incredible, nestled in the harbor between lobster boats, the cribstone bridge and deep navy blue waves.  Amazing!  The wall of windows in the dining room is fabulous.  The food is equally good.  I'm a scallops fiend, and every time I've had them here, they are cooked to absolute, tender perfection.  Some might bemoan the smaller menus, or the higher prices, but I think they're all worth it in the end: for a perfectly quintessential coastal Maine dinner, come on out to Cook's and behold the delights of the experience.  You won't be disappointed!  And if you love nostalgia, this is the place to be.  The nautical themes in the restaurant haven't changed a bit in years, and it's so comforting to return to this beacon of great memories year after year.

text:
Is this a Maine thing? We always enjoy playing tourist before the crowds set in.

Cook's Lobster House has been a local tourist destination all my 50 years. Eating there (rarely) as a youngster was confusing: you feel joy at the pretty destination and you feel guilt for someone paying more than boat price for your food! There's no guilt now - I'm just looking for ways to make pleasant memories with my mother with the time available.

At this visit my mother, 81, was disappointed to not have bread served while we waited for our lunch. We ate here a month prior, just before Mother's Day, and when bread wasn't served mother asked about it, and bread and butter were promptly dropped in front of her. He did a kindness by not telling her it wasn't on the menu. In comparison, at this visit when bread was asked about but not received it left a disappointing feeling.

Our meals were great. I had the seafood medoly again and it was as tasty as the last time. The freshness of the scallops shown through in every bite.  Mother's baked stuffed lobster was as close to her own recipe as she's found. The server was a kind, effervescent young lady who appeared genuinely happy (so rare these days!) but the  [refusal to serve] bread set a tone. Unfortunately it doesn't take much when your entire day revolves around the lunch experience. Clearly, there was a difference in the levels of experience between the two servers. One didn't appreciate the importance of bread to the older woman, so it wasn't important. The other one saw that bread was important to the older women so therefore bread was important.

It seems like it would be helpful if restaurant kitchens kept a notebook of helpful hints like that from their servers. Even the newest ones will have important things to offer.  You're not competing against each other, so why not help each other?
Final words, "Mind the bread." (Mind the details.) Don't be like most tourist destinations that leave one feeling like they didn't try very hard and didn't care very much because they got your money and they're never going to see you - the tourist - again.

text:
Lowe's is a massive hardware store, great for homeowners and handymen alike. The prices are really good on many items. Lowe's has a department for everything in your house, from building it from scratch to remodeling it with some high quality tile and carpet, trim and lighting, appliances and vacuums, and they even have a cleaning and "Staples" isle for paper goods and cleaning stuff.

Restrooms are provided, handicap accessible parking is available, self checkout is available, pro membership is available, credit cards are available.

Lowe's has a specific return policy, make sure to keep your receipt, and understand the policy before purchasing items, if you loose your receipt, you can only get a "Merc. Card", which is basically a in store only gift card, which you can only use in a store, with a valid ID, and you cannot buy some items like gift cards with them. Keep the receipt or your money is stuck in the company!

Will update to five star when they put in the effort to look up receipts on the computer, and do legitimate returns for legitimate reasons.

Otherwise, GREAT company.

name: E Robinson
text: 3/18/20 - Lovely day with temps near 50F.  A good southern breeze was kicking up some wave action here.  Lots of common eiders gathered offshore.  If there is a prettier place in town, I don't know where it is.  In any kind of weather year round this place is worth the short walk.  Plenty of fresh air, common eiders and red breasted mergansers , song birds in the rosa rugosa, and enough geology on display to help you remember that long forgotten optional college course.  The views here are great, and when the wind and waves come piling in, the show can be spectacular (just don't get too close!).  Thanks to the generous people who made possible the public access to this gorgeous preserve.

We had our elderly dog with us on the outside deck.  She got a big bowl of water and lots of positive attention. Our wait staff have been gracious and attentive each visit.

I've seen some other reviews which contained negative comments.  That has NOT been our experience.  We know locals who come to Mae's frequently.

text:
Bruno's . . . found a "gem" in Bath, just off Rt. 1 if you like brick oven pizza!  On a chilly winter Sunday night, my wife and I were seated by Darcie ( Owner with her husband Rob) at a window table . . . Over looking the Bath Brewing Company across the street.

Small restaurant seating,  for about 20 people . . . However  there's a connecting room for a sports  bar with two TVs on the wall, more people there watching NFL playoff games. We preferred less noise, and stayed in the restaurant  venue.

We enjoyed the Greek salad, and double cooked cajun-rub wings ( baked and fried) with a sweet chili dipping sauce. Then we split a 12 inch Margherita pizza, with a "call out" on their homemade crust, fresh basil, and added extra cheese & pepperoni! Very Good !

Kudos for hanging local artists' work on their walls . . . New England scenes priced about $300 each. Nice touch! This will become a new favorite on our list of GOOD pizza restaurants for a couple's night out.

(The owners mentioned new noise reduction boxes on the ceiling to help benefit customer conversations.)

text:
Recently opened in down town Bath but I was waiting for my husband to get here from school in Rhode island and give them time to work out the opening kinks before giving them a shot.

Wow! Such a great addition to this small town and so excited to have it so close. We finally went on a Saturday for a late lunch/early dinner. Greeted the minute we walked in the door and our waiter was at our table within minutes to get drinks started. We chose one of the seats right up front in the window overlooking the main Street. So cute!

The menu us small and pretty short and sweet but it does not lack great options. The 8" pizza provides 4 large slices, so easy to share. The small bread sticks is enough for a table of 4 as well. The decor is great and the restaurant seemed very clean.

We ended up going with some wings (Buffalo style), an 8" Bruno and my husband made a custom 8" pie with pepperoni, ham and bacon.

I chose to try the Backyard patio pounder from the drink menu as it was described as a refreshing drink with watermelon, vodka and a hint of lemonade and wow was he right. It was subtle but delicious!

The food was on point as well. Between the cheese, the crust, the sauce. All of it was great! The prices are comparable to competitors but the flavor tops them by far.
You have ample free parking behind main Street so you never have to worry about finding a spot.

Pretty sure we will be regulars in here and you will see our faces often.

name: Peyton Twombley
text:
This is a great place to get some excellent Authentic Mexican food, with a well balanced menu. Often when going to a Authentic Mexican restaurant you get stuck with mostly spicy foods, but not a El Rodeos. They have plenty on the the spicy side, while still having lots of options for those who can’t eat spicy foods.

Prices vary but there’s options for every patrons budget, staff a really friendly and eager to assist. Portion sizes in comparison to price is generously large, definitely a good bang for the buck.

Now with us being in the mist of a Pandemic, hygiene is on a lot of our minds. As the the saying goes if you want to know wether hygiene is a priority at an establishment check the restrooms. El Rodeo restrooms are spotless, the restaurant feels roomie and is kept clean.

Definitely one of my first pick more often than not when eating out. I do wish the had delivery available.

text: I tried their "To Go" service where you order online and then pick up. I am convalescing from a foot surgery, so it's not feasible for me to shop right now. It was not a bad experience; it was actually quite good. Shopping at your leisure from home was fairly simple. If you needed something specific, say, ripe bananas, there was a place to write a note to whom ever was picking out your groceries. Pick up was easy, however, if the item is out of stock, then you have to decide on the spot if you want a substitution or not. This will possibly change the total you thought you were going to pay. If you're flexible, this is not a huge problem, but if you're buying ingredients for a recipe, it is a little more challenging. All in all, a good experience for my first time using it.

name: Christian Akers
text:
Firstly, if you go almost anytime on the weekend.. expect to wait. This location has a very high volume of customers during their peak times, often to the point that everyone is awkwardly crammed into the small lobby.

Secondly, the training for Olive Garden wait staff is service oriented. Very formulaic, they'll always ask certain questions without fail, e.g., would you like a wine sample? Or the host asking you how you're doing while walking you to your table. It creates a "friendly" sort of atmospheres, despite likely being feigned.

For food quality, the bread sticks are terrible. They're plain, poorly processed in a factory, and have an awful texture should they be ordered ToGo or kept covered because they absorb the condensation and become instantly ruined. Salads only have two dressing options, Italian or ranch. Otherwise, the food quality is decent but very overpriced for what you ultimately receive. You will spend minimum $40 for two people if you tip and order anything other than water.

I've never really been a fan of Olive Garden but my mom had just gone through with a scary medical test and she wanted lunch there so who was I to complain?
The soup was a strange witch's brew that had potato, sausage, cheese, and I think kale. It was startlingly good.
My main meal was the Meatball Pizza Bowl which was fantastic. While the meatballs themselves were a little bland and tough, the sauce and cheese and awesome bread bowl more than made up for them.
TL;DR My first good Olive Garden experience ever. Also, the test came back negative and my mom doesn't have cancer!

text:
A higher-end Italian food chain restaurant.

Over the years, Olive Garden has gone up and down in regard to their quality. Lately, after not returning for close to a decade, I have stopped in a few times and I've been pleasantly surprised each time.

The restaurant is clean, service is fast, and the wait staff are all on the younger side and are energetic and pleasant.

I decided to get my own custom pasta dish consisting of Alfredo sauce, mushrooms, chicken, and angel hair pasta. It was delicious, and so was dessert - the cannoli trio, with one each of regular, strawberry, and chocolate cannoli. They had a nice selection of wine, and with most meals you still get unlimited bread sticks and soup or salad.

Overall, I really have no problems with this location. Would recommend for a relatively cheap family dinner spot, or a casual dinner date.

text:
(Translated by Google) A second visit very pleasant.

We came here for the first time as a family on December 28, 2016 and loved our experience. We came back as a couple this time for the dinner on November 3, 2018 and were just as satisfied. We were well served by Deanna M. We ordered two cocina mia at $ 10.99 with soup or salad and garlic bread sticks at will. My wife took a spaghetti and I, the whole grain linguines. We spoiled ourselves by ordering salad a second time without wasting anything. Total of $ 23.74 with tax and we left $ 3.80 tip in Deanna. We recommend this restaurant by inviting you to look at our few photos.

Written on November 24, 2018 in Salaberry de Valleyfield, Quebec, Canada.
__________________________________________________

A very satisfying supper.

Dinner with family last night December 28, 2016 with our son. Our waitress, a lovely lady who seemed to have a lot of experience in the business, served us very well. Her name was Valerie A. We waited a maximum of 10 minutes before a table was assigned to us. We ordered salad three times without wasting it with two orders of bread sticks. We all ordered cucina mia at $ 9.99 but our son added a shrimp sauce for an additional $ 3.99. Everything was delicious. My wife ordered wheat linguine with the meat sauce, our son too but with asiago sauce alfredo garlic and me, cavatappi noodles with marinara sauce. Everything was delicious. Total of the addition of $ 36.68 with tax. We offer you some photos including the one of the addition with the description of our orders.
We recommend this restaurant.

Reviewed December 29, 2016 in South Portland, Maine, United States.

Un souper très satisfaisant.

Souper en famille hier soir le 28 décembre 2016 en compagnie de notre fils. Notre serveuse, une charmante Dame qui semblait avoir beaucoup d’expérience dans le métier, nous a servi très correctement. Son nom était Valerie A.  Nous avons attendu au maximum 10 minutes avant qu’une table nous soit assignée. Nous avons commandé de la salade trois fois sans n’en gaspiller aucunement avec aussi deux commandes de bâtonnets de pains.  Nous avons tous commandé des cucina mia à $9.99 mais notre fils a ajouté une sauce aux crevettes pour un $3.99 additionnel. Tout était délicieux. Mon épouse a commandé des wheat linguine avec la sauce à la viande, notre fils aussi mais avec une sauce asiago alfredo garlic et moi, les nouilles cavatappi avec sauce marinara. Tout était délicieux. Total de l’addition de $36.68 avec taxe. Nous vous proposons quelques photos dont celle de l’addition avec la description de nos commandes.
Nous recommandons ce restaurant.

name: Andrew Hong
text:
Claws was the first lobster roll joint we've stopped at in Maine. We arrived around lunch time and it was pretty busy, but luckily, placed our order ahead before we got there. It took about 10 minutes for our order to come out, which is quick considering there was a long line of people waiting to place an order.

The staff here were very friendly and professional. They catered to your needs and were attentive.

There's a parking lot for about a dozen cars but plenty of parking on the street if needed. The outdoor dining area offers a great view out into the water.

The lobster roll came with a very generous portion of lobster as you can see in the photo. It was fresh and soft; practically melted in your mouth. The roll that it came on offered a nice crunch to contrast the lobster.

My immediate impression with that first bite was that Claws set the bar high for the best lobster rolls Maine has to offer. I will definitely stop here again whenever I'm back in town.

name: Ignacio Cetrangolo
text: Huge selection of food and drinks that makes it hard to choose. Still, you cant go wrong with anything you choose. The lobster mac n cheese won a special #1 in Maine award and it sure is tasty. Portions are pretty hefty too. The view over the water is very nice and a nice summer day makes it perfect to sit outside and enjoy the delicious food. Note that there is parking available.

name: Shawn Surma
text: We have been coming to Rockland for many years and this is the first time to stop here. Boy are we glad. My clawesall roll was amazing. My wife had the lobster Mac and cheese and loved it. Large menu and great variety even for those that don’t want seafood. We will be back.

name: Blake Roussel
text:
So stop number 3 on our lobster journey day 2!
So claws is a great little place on the side of the road! We ordered the lobster roll lightly dressed in mayo with side of butter, and a heaping plate of fresh fried clams with onion rings! (Don’t forget the onion rings!!)

Lobster roll, well let’s begin with the fact that you guessed it (well you might not have) ours was all claw and knuckle meat from the lobster! Which means this was one tender lobster roll. Bun was buttered and toasted as expected and piled high with lobster meat. (2nd biggest portion on a roll we have come across) lightly tossed in mayo, we always like to add the butter... why is that? BUTTET MAKES EVERYTHING BUTTER I MEAN BETTER!
Lobster roll was awesome, no complaints!

Fried clams! Oh man I love clams and boy these didn’t disappoint us at all. Battered and fried perfectly with the right amount of seasoning. Dipped in the fresh made tarter sauce which was fantastic... sitting atop a huge mound of lightly battered (my favorite way) onion rings! Man this basket was worth every penny!

Stop by and tell them BLAKE sent you! Maybe one of these days they will know who I am!

name: Pam Benson
text: This lunch cost 74.00.... The oyster basket was 24.00 and consisted of 8 oysters that were rubber and fries that seemed to have been sitting too long. We ordered Clam cakes, over cooked dark, and too chewy...The salad was my choice of meal. Tribal Trio Salad. Consisted of tiny old tasting shrimp with absolutely no flavor. The lobster was fresh and good. The crab salad was best of all. 24.00 for the salad. As seen i was so not liking the salad. Greens were crisp, peppers were limp and there were strawberries and my best liked part besides the crab salad was the kiwi. The rest found the trash. The staff was very pleasant. I never saw anyone clean the tables off including mine which I did. I read other menus of various places before I began my journey with my friend from Fryeburg, Maine. Spent the morning at the Breakwaters and was very eager to enjoy a meal. Only to be disappointed. We will not return.

name: John Pozadzides
text:
In theory, this spot looks great! And it was certainly packed! But a few big shortcomings left us disappointed...

We didn't like the fact corn on the cob is served steamed, but not shucked. The veggie pasta literally didn't have any pasta in it - and it wasn't very tasty or appetizing. And it took 50 minutes to receive our food, despite the fact they only had about 5-6 orders to fulfill while we were there.

To cap things off, all seating is outdoors, and they have a MAJOR mosquito problem. I mean several insects attacking each person at the table simultaneously. Enough to seriously ruin any meal. It made us all question how they couldn't at least have a mosquito mister system.

If you can catch them when the bugs aren't out, and they aren't busy, maybe give them a try. But make sure and stick to the lobster. It's what they do best.

name: David Cruz
text: Outdoor seating under a covered deck. You order at a window when your food is done they call your name. The staff are very friendly, and the food mostly seafood is reasonably priced, and very good.

name: Rev. Ria Ferris
text: Claws is a must-visit if you're in the Rockland area. The parking lot is small and cramped, but if you're lucky enough to get a spot when business is a little bit slower like we did, you'll be in for a treat! The lobster quesadilla was delicious and priced very fairly. Large chunks of lobster all throughout, adding the flavor you're expecting. Also, the lobster roll topped with shrimp is yummy too. The seating is picnic table-style under an enclosed canopy adding to the ambiance of a good day outside if the weather is nice. Two thumbs up!

It was soft shell lobster so they were not needed, I wish they would have asked before doing so because when I went to return them, I was told you only get $4 back. Overall this is a four star establishment, but I gave three stars because I felt money being the motivating factor need the place to seem a little dishonest. resp.text:
Hello Matt.  I am responding to your review because I am absolutely shocked hearing about your experience.  Please expand on your comments so I can better understand.... When did you visit (we have been closed since October and reopen in late May)?  What did you order (it sounds like you visited at least twice in order to say "the dishes change depending on the chef)?  What part of the "service" was rude (we don't have servers - just friendly faces at the order and pick-up windows)?

I am very concerned that you would post a review like this in the middle of winter that truly does not reflect our reputation.  We pride ourselves on the best customer service and also on keeping our dishes consistent.  We only have one "chef", myself, and I am there every day to ensure the quality of each and every item that leaves the out window.  If our service and dishes were so horrible, I would hope that you would have mentioned it to us at the time of service when we could have fixed it.

Sincerely,
Luanne Stinson
owner/chef

text: Thurston's Lobster Pound is a fabulous restaurant in Bernard, Maine with incredible harbor views.  Best haddock chowder in the area.  Dinning inside or outside or take out. text: The lobster pound I would choose to bring a foreigner, or someone not so familiar with this kind of eatery. It's somehow more like an usual outdoor restaurant, although with a lot of the local charm. Depending on how hungry you are, it can be either FAR or else a nice leisurely drive from the more popular/touristic locations in the island. Avoid at crowded hours. Great drinks.

text: We went here for lunch one day. There are no reservations and it is hit or miss for how busy it can be. The lobster is caught and served fresh. All of the food was excellent and a service was very good. They also had a variety of amazing desserts including Berry and whoopie pies.

text: Thurstons had the best lobster roll on Mt Desert Island. Their lobster dip was also incredible. We ate blueberry pie and blue berry ice cream for dessert. They even let us eat it on the dock, which was serene. It's a little off the beaten path but well worth it.

text: Amazing food and views! We had crab cakes and chowder - the best we had in two trips to Maine!

text:
Awesome.
Amazing staff.
Food was absolutely delicious; lobster, lobster bisque, coleslaw, potato salad, clam steamers, haddock chowder, blueberry margaritas, blueberry icecream .. everything was perfect.
Harbor side dining is fantastic.
Absolutely the best.

name: Adam Palmer
text:
Beautiful view, fresh lobster! This places puts Maine's greatest offerings together in one.

When you walk into the Lobster Pound, you are greeted by crates of fresh, live lobsters and a chalkboard menu with everything from the Maine coast you could want. Lobster in every form (whole, stew, dip, on a roll...am I starting to sound like Bubba from Forrest Gump?) plus clams, sides, desserts, and cheap beer.

I admittedly had never eaten a whole lobster before so I figured there was no better place than Maine to do it. I told them the kind of lobster I wanted (Select) and the weight (2.5 lbs.) and they chose one of the lobsters from the crates after weighing a few. I bid my future dinner good bye and sat down with an Atlantic Brewery Bar Harbor Blueberry Ale (honoring Maine again).

The lobster was sweet and plentiful and the butter wasn't even necessary, which is exactly what you should expect from a place like this. We also shared the hot lobster dip which had generous chunks of claw meat which I would recommend (though the chip game could have been stepped up more).

Perhaps even better than the food is the view (see attached picture). If you sit on the water side (and I should note, you choose your own seats), you overlook the beautiful harbor and the houses on the other side of the bay. We went as sundown was approaching and the colors were beautiful. However, be aware of bugs. We were their dinner that night!

name: J Gadde
text: Really good food, but also helpful staff for out of towners like us that wanted to know the right size lobster to order, how to open a lobster properly, the best sides, etc

name: Danielle Dorrie
text: I brought my friends from Florida here for a birthday celebration. It was a fantastic experience. We waited a bit (pro tip - you can grab a drink from the bar while you're waiting to select your lobster!) and my friend picked a 3 pounder, which was delicious. The blueberry cake was phenomenal - if you're looking for a great Maine experience, this is worth the trip!

name: Jesse Fowler
text:
As a past stern man on a lobster boat, I had refused to pay an outrageous amount for lobster. That being said, I did pay for the meal here. Oh wow.... that was amazing. The muscles were the best I've ever had, the corn, the slaw, everything. I get it, I spent $35 per meal, but I'm not even upset. Great experience, great food, amazing location.

Btw, the people next to us were talking about how hard shell and soft shell are the same thing and that places charge more to rip people off. Not true! Soft shell is less meat, but soooo much tastier. Hard shell is good if you're going to freeze it or need to ship it. They do pay the boats more for these. I'll always pick soft as they taste so much better.

Also, tourists, there is meat in the body. Rip the top off, throw it away. Then look at where the legs connect to the body. I hate seeing those go to waste.

text: Crazy.  Had a cheeseburger.  Delicious. Rest of table had lobster. No one was ffg disappointed.

name: Daniel Babicz
text:
Just Wow. This place has it all... from an amazing view, to amazing food. This was by far the best place to get a lobster roll in all of Bar Harbor region. The lobster was succulent and sweet, not rubbery, the roll was warm and toasted. We had the lobster dip which blew our minds away... we could eat that stuff all day long. Try out the Blueberry Beer with your roll if it is in season!!!
Update: 2017: returned to Thurstons for my second trip to Maine, and again the food never ceases to amaze me. You HAVE to try the Haddock Stew. I am now obsessed with trying to recreate the recipe. Grab a Jumbo Lobster roll and a corn on the cob too!

text: ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC.  Simple but creative (and DELICIOUS) food, good wine, fun cocktails,  beautiful setting, lovely staff.  We sat in the newer bar area to eat. A smaller menu, but WOW!!  Flavor, flavor, flavor.  Best meal in a very long time.  Excellent crab as well as top lobster stew!!!

name: Neil Ashton
text: Great choices in lobster. Yup! You can pick out any size from a pound and a quarter to "how big do you want" at least up to the legal limit (5 pounds). The big ones cost more but how often are you going to have a shot at a 3 or 4 pound lobster? Nothing fancy. This place is part of a working lobster pier. The young people serving you do their job VERY well. Tip them. They deserve it. And enjoy sitting at a table with the ocean breeze going through. We go here often during the months they are open. I hope heaven is like this! If you can't tell by now, this is a place I really enjoy. Come visit me. I'll do my best to get you there for dinner. But don't tell anyone. Fortunately,  the tourists don't know about it yet.

name: Jenay Robert
text: We loved the lobster roles at Thurston's! Lobster was fresh. Prices were comparable to other lobster pounds in the area. Service was fast and friendly. We heard there could be long lines at dinnertime, so we went around 3PM and had no wait. Will definitely visit again.

name: Joe Lee
text: Lobster was good was a long wait. Feel like it was alot of hype for about average lobster. Also try'd the lobster roll got good reviews, but I would not get it again.

name: Heath Larson
text: Per the recommendation of a local, this is THE place to go for a fresh lobster on the quietside of the island.  The prices were a bit high but so was the quality.  Huge selection of entrees, sides, and don’t miss the homemade pies for dessert!  Great view of the lobster boats in Southwest Harbor.  The line was a bit long but they are VERY efficient here, so it didn’t take long, and they even had a handy can of bug spray our for those of us waiting outside.

name: Mark Rowe
text: Very good food, great service and a cool place to get some good lobster. Only downside was that it was quite expensive given they’ve just pulled it out of the water - must be a gold mine! Still, super tasty and worth the drive.

name: Mason Lugo
text: Great service and delicious brews

name: nathan bailey
text: Typical lobster pound...no dancing lobster or anything that would set them apart food wise but the location is awesome.  They are on the southwest side of MDI so it’s a great escape from Bar Harbor. They offer two levels of indoor and outdoor seating and it’s truly my favorite spot on the island for lobster.  I have had steamers, chowder, lobsters etc and it’s all been good over the years.  Definitely worth a trip

name: James Walker
text:
I had the plain lobster dinner and my fellow diners had mussels and clams steamers. While the steamers were a little gritty, everything tasted great.

It is a casual place. You get in line and give your order at the counter. Then you find a table and they bring your food to you.

name: Sethany Crafts
text: Great Staff, great food

name: Roxanna Mcgrail
text: The best tasting Lobster from the local islands to anywhere north or south the atmosphere and lounging are unequaled to many others. There is not one dining seat that does not have a view of the beautiful and historic Bass harbor bay and beyond. And did I say the service and food were fabulous?! 🤣 Love the Radcliffe's 😘

name: Shana
text: Best lobster on the island, tasty and very fairly priced. We also had the mussels which were really good. Sides are just okay. Worth the drive from Bar Harbor if you are staying there.

name: Erin McCabe
text:
A must do.
Laid back, lobster, and libations, what more can you ask for?!
Great view and wonderful service. The lobster roll was great and the lobster dip I could probably eat every day.
The regulars were kind and welcoming.
We will be back as much as we can.

name: Ashley Schultz
text: The food was excellent! It was our first time eating whole lobster that way, and it took us awhile, but we got it done! The corn and slaw were good as well, and the atmosphere is nice with a lovely view of the harbor. Quite a few of the girls working acted like they hated their job, their lives, and all of us customers. Rude and just very angry seeming.

name: Gordon Grant
text: Not open Sunday. I appreciate your family values. If you're website was clear about not being open I wouldn't have driven 45 minutes to find you closed.

resp.text:
I wish I could attach a photo here, but this is copy/pasted from the header on our website:

“Serving Lunch and Dinner Monday through Saturday from 12:00 am to 8:00 pm
Open the Sundays of Labor Day and Columbus Day Weekends”

Hi Gordon,
We’re a very busy, family owned restaurant. We have a couple of little kids, and our staff is made up of local folks who have families as well. We’re closed one day per week to provide ourselves, our family, and our staff a bit of time to enjoy this beautiful area and all that it has to offer in the summer season. I apologize that this so severely impacts you, but I do think it is somewhat unfair to rate us 1 star because we’re not open when you’d like to come.

name: Jennifer Smith
text: Always excellent. The lobster can't be fresher, and the sides are great. We come every year now.

name: The Haymakers Wife
text: Best lobster roll I had on our 1 week roadtrip  through the coast of Maine❣️

name: Elia Clemente
text: This place is a must stop if your visiting Acadia National Park or Bar Harbor. The food is very fresh and made to order. The prices are reasonable and the veiws are great. They have high chairs for the little ones if you need one. The parking is free. They serve local beers and some domestic/imports as well. The line can get long for lunch and dinner so be prepared to wait, but not too long. They're plenty of tables so you always get a good view. The drive to get here can be tricky so use GPS. The lobster roll was amazing and so moist. Go for the jumbo size.

name: iAm PapaMercy
text: A bit out of the way but worth it. Food was excellent. The view is breathtaking.

name: Maria Wooten
text: Worth the drive to this local gem! The food is always great and the drinks are yummy too! And of course, you can't beat sitting right by the water while you enjoy your meal.

name: David Johnston
text: Great views, good food. Lobster roll was excellent.

name: Bill Hixon
text: Great food with a great view !!

name: Tiff Yarbrough
text: Great, fresh food with a fabulous view!

name: Francisco Companioni
text: Best pound I've been to yet and I've been coming here for over 6 years now. Def worth the trip to the quiet side of the island to eat here. Have the lobster melt with cheddah if you're a grilled cheese fan it's amazing! Great views of an active harbor with actual fishermen bringing in their fresh catch to land. Really enjoyed flying my drone over this place! Will def return, soon.

name: Gabe Quaglia
text: Great lobster roll. The boiled lobsters were phenomenal. Steamed mussels were very good (although they didn't come with water for washing which would be my only complaint) Lobster dip was delicious. Staff was knowledgeable about food allergies and very helpful. The view was about as good as it gets, huge sweeping views of a bay with what I assumed were working lobster boats. Probably the best meal I had in my week on MDI.

name: JoAnn Catuosco
text: The rest of my family's food was good, but the food I had ordered did not come. Parking is also somewhat difficult.

name: Gretchen Dennis
text: Thurstons is a fantastic place on the water. Lobster, mussels, clams you name it we ate it! The lobster stew was to die for! Truly amazing!

name: Cheri Greenwell
text: The corn was fabulous, blueberry cake tasty, portions large. Nice full bar and screened outdoor seating with beautiful views.

name: Tyler Brown
text: Amazing place, great view of the harbor, delicious food, and quick service. I really liked the ordering system there, where you give your order at the counter, pay, and they give you a sign for your table with a number (think wedding seating). Wouldn't hesitate to go again next time I'm in the area.

name: Lindsey
text: Amazing Lobster Bloody Mary cocktails!! I highly recommend them... My boyfriend and I had to have two each. I wasn't able to try the food, but I have heard that the lobster roll is beyond delicious! Highly recommend. Great view of the water!

name: Julie Sweeney
text: Order at the counter and take ur number stand to ur table. It's only buggy at night. The lobster stew is phenomenal. The prices are very reasonable for a lobster pound.

name: Julie Day
text: 1 1/2 pound lobster dinner what's not to love, sitting on the water eating lobster that was probably caught that morning absolutely delicious can't be beat! Highly recommended!!

name: Brenda Merritt
text: Get there early or you'll stand in line forhowever long it takes for a person to eat a lobster. The lobster chowder is out of this world! The food is great and you get to pick out your own lobster.

name: russ reynolds
text: Huge lobsters. Great service. And the cinch was the blueberry cake!

name: Adam Riemer
text:
The best lobster pound on MDI, and I loved how far out of the way it was because it was way less touristy than anything close to Bar Harbor.

We had fantastic Lobster Dip, and one of the best crab cake rolls I've ever had. Loved this place, wish I could eat here every day.

name: Mark Addis
text: Not sure I get the appeal of this place.  There is nothing special on their menu you can't get anywhere else in the Bar Harbor / Mt. Desert area.  We have been travelling throughout Maine over the past month and experienced Lobster, Scallops, and other seafood in many different ways.  Nothing here was bad, but it was overpriced in my book.  You're paying a premium for the scenery and views of a mooring yard with lobster boats.  There are plenty of other places that go a lot further for their ingredients at better prices.  $18.95 for a lobster roll and a tiny bag of chips just wasn't for us.

name: Marianne MacLusky
text: Perfect Maine location and food.  The staff is great, friend and very patient.  It is busy, but that adds to the experience.

name: Jeff Thurston
text: No "Family" discount here, but dependably great foods and service with a view. Real coastal Maine locale that's not easy to find, but worth the effort. We'll be back.

name: Sandy McGarry
text: Great food and great scenery as always❣

name: Ricky Long
text: The line was pretty short when we arrived. They offer different sized lobsters, and charge by the pound. We ordered their lobster roll, crab melt, and their mussel dinner. After ordering, they give you a number and the food gets delivered to your table. Food was good, but not mindblowing. Portions were a bit on the small side. Their blueberry cake was really good. After din Can't comment on the view since the fog rolled in upon our arrival.

name: David W.
text: Best lobster pound experience on the island. Can't beat the views. Make sure you get there early. Try to visit at an off time. Makes the wait easier and the food faster.

name: David Blanchard
text: If you like your lobster rolls simple with a little mayo and not too expensive, they're the best and the view is great

name: Dan Potash
text: Great location and atmosphere. Had the lobster chowder and the roll. Both very good, though the chowder was just too rich, if that's possible.

name: Kenard Puchalski
text: The best lobster meal that I have eaten in my entire life. After a day of hiking (about 11 miles) we hit this place. We were satisfied with every thing. Lobster, crab cakes, mussels, corn, blue berry cake, beer. Yummy.

name: b s
text: This place was awesome and worth the drive over

name: Blake Latham
text: Lobster and lobster roll to die for. The best!!

name: Laurie Cameron
text: Food and service were great

name: goskime
text: Great Lobster & Crab rolls.  Blueberry cake and steamer's.

name: David Lyster
text: Very good Lobster. Good price.  Rest of meal was so so.  Very long wait

name: Jeffrey Greb
text: Loved it !!! Sit in the bar area and get the hot buttered LOBSTAH !!

name: M Reaves
text: Thurston's is your basic, no frills lobster pound. Order at the counter, pay, pick up your beers, sit and then indulge. There's plenty of room for a crowd and it was crowded tonite.The price for our very large soft shells was as good as we've read about and well less than we expected. They were cooked perfectly and were scrumptious. Right out of the water.  Everyone was helpful and courteous, particularly to us newbies from south of the Mason-Dixon Line. No need to look elsewhere. We'll be back at least once more during our 4-day stay on the island.

name: Rob Koenig
text: Great location friendly service..

name: John S
text: Great place to stop for lobster if you are on MDI. You can choose the size of lobster and they pull it out of the water container right in front of you. The sides my group got, clams and muscles were OK, mostly just steamed and put on the plate, the clams were a bit sandy. Main attraction here though is the lobster so focus on that... :)

name: Josh Manney
text: What a view to go with the tasty lobster!

name: kathe coopersmith
text: The lobster stew was the best soup we had during our nine days on the island.

name: chris rl
text: Very casual. Fun to watch the traffic on the water plus the view is very nice.im probably the o nly person who goes to main that does not like lobster  but I found their crab cakes and crab dip to be very yummy. I would definitely recommend.

name: Lynd Blatchford
text: Thurston's is very popular with tourists looking for a lobster dinner. My reaction after eating there is that it is overrated and overpriced. I had boiled lobster which I found second rate, too salty and overcooked. I will not return.

name: Philip Pietrangelo
text: This place is your classic lobstahhh shack. I really love the fisherman's atmosphere and you know you are getting fresh food when the restaurant is built on a fishing dock.  The bar offers drinks to hold you over while you wait to place your order. I definitely would come back for more.

name: Michael Stephens
text: What a deluxe spot for Maine seafood! I went on a Monday evening, and there was a line out the door.The staff is friendly, and the atmosphere is variegated and light and very literally seaside. But beware of the mosquitos! Big suckers that attack at the door, such that the restaurant keeps repellant outdoors for customers where the line stretches back. They're everywhere, including in the bathrooms. They're attracted to the lobster.

name: Kim Hazlett
text: Always the perfect way to end a visit to Acadia National Park!

name: Ashley Williams
text: This was the best lobster I have had in a long time. Service was quick and the price was decent.

name: Chris Albanese
text: My favorite lobster pound on all of MDI. The lobsters are amazingly fresh, the laid back atmosphere is perfect, and the view is awesome. Service is great too.

name: Taber Fellows

name: Lawrence Eaton

Delicious and fast service.
The crab sandwich was phenomenal!!

resp.text:
We did have to make a very difficult decision to end our season early this year. Regretfully, this is inconvenient for lots of people, arguably more so for us as the business owners than anyone.
I have certainly done my due diligence as far as attempting to update all online hours on sites like TripAdvisor and google and yelp (our own website’s hosting company has been ghosting me since April) and do apologize that they have not all been willing to verify that we are closed.

name: Matt Hughes
text: Absolutely the best Lobster Rolls! You have to order the large one!

name: Roger Buzby
text: Excellent and knowledgeable staff plus the freshest lobster around!

name: Jeremy Butler
text: Great place awesome food

name: John Palfrey
text: The ideal Maine lobster spot.

name: Jarrod Daughtry
text: Thurston's has a beautiful setting, but the service and food was subpar at best. There are other places I'd visit before going back here, again. Overall, just an average experience all around.

name: Casey T
text:
Doing one thing and doin' it right!

Lobsters people that's what it's ALL about. Be it whole lobsters served with a side of melted butter OR if you're going for the clean and tidy option of a lobster roll served on a perfectly grilled buttered split bun. These crustaceans were handled with love and cooked to perfection. Yea, it's true. This isn't any white tablecloth experience. You order at the window then find yourself a table. What it IS about is great lobster and eating it at a beautiful location.  Given what local Bar Harbor establishments are charging for lobsters that are "meh", Thurston's is a steal deal.

If you're willing to go 'off menu' and try their other offerings, the haddock chowder was flavorful and fresh. Chunks of haddock paired with perfectly cooked taters. Yummy!  The coleslaw was OK, nothin' to write home about, but sometimes you need some crunchy slaw to play off the richness of that lobster.

So if your in MDI, get yourselves to Thurston's pronto!  You'll be SO happy you did!

Special Note: To all you folks working the counter, cooking the food, and running it out to us hungry customers, a big THANK YOU!  You guys know the true meaning of great customer service!

resp.text:
I apologize sincerely that you made a trip over to find us closed. As a seasonal business we struggle every year to get the multitude of online search engines, yelp, TripAdvisor and the like, to update our information correctly when we request them to. Google is especially hard, because even though several requests have been made, there is no option to “temporarily close” a listing. Often, it is much more difficult than it should be to be in control of one’s own business information on the internet.
We always open the Friday of Memorial Day Weekend. This year that will be on the 25th of May. I’m sorry again for the inconvenience.

name: Michael Lobsenz
text: Great food with great views.

name: Arnd Stöckl
text:
(Translated by Google) Cooked mussels were very good. Hot lobster dip was also very good. Food highly recommended.
Very nice view of the bay.
A star deduction because the barmaid was rude to us.

(Original)
Gekochte Muscheln waren sehr gut. Hot Lobster Dip hat uns auch sehr gut geschmeckt. Essen sehr empfehlenswert.
Sehr schöne Aussicht auf die Bucht.
Ein Stern Abzug weil die Bardame uns gegenüber unfreundlich war.

name: Nancy Hulme
text: Their specialty drink, chocolatte is indescribably delicious! In fact, all if their coffees and teas are some of the best I've had. Breakfast sandwiches, scones, bagels are fantastic....and they also make chocolates and truffles. Five+ stars!

name: Nancy
text: Absolutely delicious breakfast sandwich and breakfast burrito found here! We grabbed both as a mid-hike snack and it gave us the boost of energy we needed to finish the trail. The choco-latte was also the perfect start to my morning with a nice kick of spice at the end. Highly recommend ordering ahead for pickup to avoid waiting in line.

name: J'aime Dahn
text: Great service, great food, great coffee and always reliable! Walk up service only right now due to covid, which is great. I'm just glad they are still open during these times.

name: Summer Cornetta-Webb
text: Had a delicious choco-latte & avo toast. My baby really loved the toast and I had to fight with them to get some. Absolutely worth the drive and eating in the car.

name: Nicole King
text: The iced choco-latte is to die for! I have even been trying to replicate it at home. I can't get enough. Service was a bit slow and they were out of pastries. Be prepared to wait. However, we would definitely try it again! Nice addition to downtown.

name: Mark Morgan
text: Went 3 or 4 times. Great service and coffee. Loved the mocha one, cardamom, and regular. There were some rude customers that did not know how to pick up tea. The staff handled it well as they could. Keep up the great work!

name: Jason Georgacakis
text: The coffee and breakfast sandwiches here are good. A few of the other drinks on the menu like the horchata the chai we're not so good. Gladly the staff exchange drinks for free.

name: Steven Jones
text: My drink was good, but after waiting over 20 minutes for my partner's drink they came out to tell me they were out. I asked for a water and a refund for the drink they wanted. They gave the water and said they would process refund later as it was an online order, but they never did. Disappointed, but would give them a second chance.

text: Very nice coffee shop preparing gourmet lattes and cappuccinos! My wife's hot chocolate wasn't warm enough, i asked the staff to just heat up in the microwave but they prepared a new cup. That was very nice of them.

text: This is a very cute place to come into to grab a snack or a drink. The service is great and the presentation is also very good. The inside is kind of tight if there is lots of people but it is still worth checking out.

name: MB Luce
text: Great coffee shop!! Their house made Chai is incredible, and it's very rare to find Horchata on any menu. Bagels are delicious, too. Highly recommend stopping in during a visit to Bar Harbor!

name: Mark Cunningham
text: Easily the best coffee on the island. Great food. Amazing service. And as a bonus local art adorns the walls 😀

name: Steve M
text: A must visit! Great atmosphere, excellent coffee and food! Breakfast bagel sandwiches are phenomenal!  Definitely grab a bag of The Boss to take home for the Dark Roast/Espresso roast lovers. Iced Cafe De La Olla was also excellent! A++ Staff!

text: Excellent place for a light breakfast or coffee. Offers both indoor and outside seating. Dogs not allowed inside but neither were the unicorns. Baked goods were lovely and I wanted more.

I'd tell y'all what my favorite bagel and cream cheese combination is, but when y'all find out, they'll be sold out and I won't be able to get mine.

No, seriously though, I will say the cheddar bagel with roasted red pepper cream cheese is probably one of my favorite breakfast on the Island. ❤️❤️

text: My wife works at the hospital on MDI and she loves to go to choco-latte. That day I met her at the hospital we went to choco-latte for a coffee. I had the mocha latte which was creamy nice temperature and nicely served. The staff was pleasant and friendly it was no line and no wait which is great. They also had a wonderful assortment of pastries to choose from. My wife had a fresh bagel with cream cheese which was toasted to perfection and covered with cream cheese. If you are in bar harbor and looking for a latte and a snack be sure to stop by Choco latte.

text: What an awesome get away place. very clean, very reasonable prices. Just minutes away from the waterfront and mountain trails. We liked it so much this is our second stay in 3 weeks. We will be back.

text: Nice little inn to stay at. Decently priced during my visit. Had a small hiccup with the shower head valve not being able to turn completely off and dripping all night making it a little annoying. I let staff know and they moved me to a new room or the rest of my staff while they fixed the other rooms issue. Neighbors in next room were complete jerks blasting TV all night and yelling randomly. Overall though a decent stay.

name: Becky Clark
text: We had the lobster bake for two, two slices of blueberry pie, and clam chowder. Prices are very reasonable and it’s a decent quantity of food. Lobster bake cake with two lobsters, two ears of corn, two potato salads and a pound of mussels. Seafood tasted fresh. The blueberry pie was delicious as well. Tables are socially distanced and sanitized often. There is a sink outside to wash your hands. Food was ready quickly and service was great. Probably my favorite place to eat in bar harbor.

name: Andrew Hong
text:
We have been trying out new lobster roll spots for the past four days and C-Ray has jumped to the top of the list.

Some of the places we have tried had great lobster, but bland bread, or vice versa, but C-Ray has the perfect combination of a generous portion of lobster meat and a perfectly pressed roll. The service was top notch. There was plenty of parking and outdoor seating when we had arrived around 4pm.

If you need a break from lobster rolls, their lobster melt was absolutely delicious.
I will definitely come back here when I am in town

name: Melinda C.
text:
Excellent! The light and tangy mayo mix  makes this lobster roll stand out in the crowd! The lobster rolls have generous meat and the brioche bun is toasted to perfection. C-Ray has a comfortable, relaxed atmosphere with plenty of shaded spots that beg you to stay a little long for blueberry pie.

(Note: Photos are only half of pie and half of the lobster roll since they are big enough to share with someone special!)

name: Conrad Lumm
text: Excellent lobster rolls and steamers. Incredibly responsible about social distancing, cleaning, and hygiene. More expensive than some shacks in the area, but well worth it for an occasional treat. It's nice that you can choose whether you want mayo in your lobster, too.

name: Master iOqY
text:
For around $40 you get two lobsters, two ears of corn, and a pound of muscles. That equals a happy tummy. We were in Bar Harbor for about 3 days and we visited C-Rays twice. The friendly owner used to be a lobsterman but now mans the boiling pots just outside where you order. There's a few seating areas around or you can take them home.

A must visit when in Bar Harbor!

name: Khal NEPA
text: Simply THE best lobster roll on our visit to Maine. Great local beers as well, try the Thai Pepper for a great beer. Will be back next time I'm in Maine.

name: Tena Wood
text: The steamed lobster and mussels were phenomenal! Super great service! Can’t go wrong stopping here. You’ll leave happy. 🙂

name: Sam Kroesen
text: We all had the lobster roll. It tasted great. They seemed to use good quality bread. It was buttery and delicious. The potato salad was also great. It was pretty pricey and out of the way for us. We had to try it based on the reviews and we were glad we did.

name: Donna Sgrignuoli
text: Steamed Corn,  lobsters, butter mussels, all perfectly prepared and ready to eat,  delicious.  About 40 total for two. We took them to our RV to eat.

name: Manu M
text: I loved it, best price and they cook delicious 😋. I’ll visit again.

name: Donella Held
text: Clam chowder was so good! Fast, friendly service. Plenty of seating and parking. We also had crab and lobster rolls, clams and mussells and grilled cheese. The only item that wasn't a hit was the lobster melt.

name: Craig Corbeels
text:
I don't usually eat lobster, but when I'm in Maine, I need to eat lobster.

Lobster isn't something I order on a regular basis - in fact, I think I've only had it a few times in my life. In general, I don't go out of my way to eat any seafood. But that doesn't mean I don't like it.

On my latest trip to Bar Harbor, I knew I needed to try some lobster, and C-Ray's praises were sung by my other family members, so my girlfriend and I came right here. We sat out at one of the picnic tables and split just one lobster roll because we weren't too hungry, but we were both impressed. I can't really say what makes lobster good, and as you can tell by my review I'm no lobster expert. All I know is that I enjoyed it. The bread was toasted just right and the generous portion of lobster was flavorful without being overwhelming. One thing that I did like about C-Ray's lobster roll was that it wasn't loaded with mayonnaise like many others are. It felt like the lobster was the focus, as it should be. Do recommend!

name: Rick Tindol
text: This was another stop on our Maine Lobster Roll Tour.  I had the standard lobster roll with the mayo sauce.  Was very good and had a large amount of lobster. Came with Cape Cod chips and a pickle.  My son had the naked roll (no mayo) with drawn butter. Also good.  My youngest son had a grilled cheese... He gave it a thumbs up.  Plenty of outdoor seating... Some picnic tables under umbrellas, and some under a barn.

text: Fresh flavors! Delicious! Beware that this is very Original ice cream parlor and when your mint ice cream isn’t served mint green colored it’s not because it’s not mint it’s because they use ACTUAL Mint and it’s delicious! Honey Baked Apple is amazing!

name: Sanjay Hiranandani
text:
What a cool little place! We were in Bar Harbor shopping, and asked a few of the merchants whose stores we shopped at where we should get ice-cream, and the unanimous favorite of our small sample was Mount Desert Island Ice cream - and we were not disappointed. They have adapted their venue well to a COVID (un?)friendly street facing stand with separate order/cashier and service windows, all the staff are masked and gloved, and plexiglass separated from customers, and the service is friendly and efficient.
The ice cream though, is smooth, creamy, and just plain amazing. The Bay of Figs, while it didn't conjure up images of battleships hurtling toward Havana, was smooth, creamy, and full of rich fig flavor and tasty fig bites in a way that would have made Fidel Castro drool on his hefty beard. The Vegan Kulfi, was just as amazing with the authentic coarse Indian kulfi texture and flavor, and we had a hard time believing that it wasn't chock full of heavy cream, until an interrogation of the staff resulted in the understanding that the base was made of cashew, which not only was an awesome substitute for a perfect kulfi texture, but also, combined with a top secret combination of ingredients, a key component of the genuine Indian flavor.
As a plus, right out front of the store across the alleyway, is a large grassy park, where you can eat, have your kids (or adult friends) make a total mess with not a care in the world, and let them run around and roll in the grass to clean up after and get their energy out. You won't be disappointed.

text: A nice departure from the regular ice cream shops on the main strip. They have interesting flavors like spicy chocolate and lime pineapple

name: Jason Georgacakis

name: Alicia Gomez
text: The ice cream is super flavorful. You could see them cooking up new batches of ice cream in the back room! I really enjoyed the salted caramel.

name: Donella Held

name: Shawn Sullivan
text: The Family really enjoyed the ice cream.  I was particularly fond of the sweet basil ice cream they had on the menu. This ice cream is a must have if you are in Bar Harbor. The do take credit cards, which seems to be a worry most customers had when entering the establishment.

name: Sam Gibson
text: Been to every location in Maine. Can't get enough of this place! Fresh and delicious...best ice cream in Maine..no contest!

name: M Reaves
text: Bar Harbor prices but the flavors are creative, the portions are big and the quality of the ice cream is fantastic. We tried the Maine sea salt caramel, local maple and pecan, and vanilla blackberry jam and crumble.  Delicious!!

name: Nora Bobb
text: Was ok wouldn't get ice cream here again.

name: Morgan
text: A must stop if you are in Bar Harbor. They have two locations with so many different flavors!!! Try the sea salted caramel or Nutella, they are great!

name: Chris Campbell
text: Maybe not for kids? Surprising and rich ice cream flavors. Everything from salted caramel to wasabi. If the one across the green is too busy, the second location is away from the crowds and easily walkable.

name: Bill Lakenan
text: You'll fall in love with flavors you can't imagine. My son got chocolate wasabi and it was fantastic. Definitely recommend trying 'The Dude' (Big Lebowski reference) which is a White Russian in ice cream form. Also try Cereal Milk where they soak Capn Crunch in milk overnight then use the milk to make I've cream. Yummmmm.....

name: Alicia Welton
