text: Extremely friendly and welcoming place with delicious coffee, tea, and inexpensive fuss-free snacks. Try the sambousas and the potage. An understated and comfortable place to get some work done or catch up with a friend. A perfect neighborhood hangout spot, warm vibes all around.

name: Christina Remillard
text: Coffee's were so good, glad we got 2! Going back, food looks really good

name: Matthew Davis
text: Really good coffee and avocado toast. Will be back to try everything else!

name: Winston Brathwaite
text: Girlfriend lives the coffee here and it always smells great inside. Their sambusas are excellent.

name: Stanley Hill
text: Great service and good coffee and paninis.

name: Mac Coldwell
text: This a terrific spot in the West End. The coffee is excellent. I had no idea Burundi coffee beans were so good. And they are roasted beautifully for this shop. I usually get a cold brew. The smells of the food being cooked there are always tempting. I've had the meat sabousa which was delicious. There is also a good assortment of pastries there. The owners and staff are warm and friendly. They are observing safe social distancing practices. The cafe is on the ground floor and is accessible by wheel chair. The whole place has a great community feel to it. What a great addition to the West End neighborhood.

name: Kenny Adorisio
text: This place is a new favorite. The drip coffee and cold brew are great. The meat sambousas are a tasty snack. The owners are incredibly friendly and are driven by their mission to direct more money back to the coffee farmers in Burundi.

name: Michael Hopkins
text: Delicious coffee. Great pastry, if limited selection. Glad I stopped by.

name: Cody Hussey
text: Wonderful people running an excellent shop with amazing breakfast foods and coffee. A staple of the community.

name: Hannah Watson
text: Excellent coffee, friendly staff and their avocado toast is out of this world and HUGE.

name: George Bragdon
text: Stopped in this weekend for some coffee and sombousas and was not disappointed! Had a cold brew with their Burundi Star Coffee which has nice refreshing sweet notes which is perfect for the heat. Sambousa was delicious and had just a hint of heat that left me wanting another (or several!).

name: Chris Lee
text: Great coffee and wonderful service directly from the owner

name: Emily Kelly
text: Delicious iced coffee and avocado toast!

name: Tom
text: Has a lot of potential.

name: Julia P.
text: Drinks were AMAZING but the food was just pretty good. Definetly would come back for cocktails!! Staff is super kind and accommodating. They have some outdoor space under a tent for extra covid spacing. We had a lovely time, thanks so much!

name: Sandy Bryant
text: Quite, cozy date night place! Server was awesome, with a great personality. Food was delicious...try the fried chicken platter = AMAZING! Good service + good food is an A++++ rating in my book.

name: Susan Kinney
text: Out of this world food and top notch service! It was my first time there but I am already planning my next visit. We had the stew, mussels, gnocchi, beets, cheese plate and thrice fried fries. Oh and the sea salt caramel dessert!!?? To die for!!! Wish I could give more then 5 stars!!

resp.text: This is so amazingly sweet, we want to give YOU ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️🌟

name: Sarah Rideout
text: Visited the East Ender late in the afternoon on a Sunday. They weren’t offering their regular menu until 5pm so we ordered from what seemed like their bar snacks menu. Made the best of it and the food was really good. We got fries, the fried chicken platter, and their selection of artisanal cheeses. Definitely suggest the thrice cooked fries!

name: Holly Stires
text: Fast, friendly service and delicious food! They also have a Temperance drink menu so you can have something non-alcoholic.

name: Inna Z
text: We walked in because the wait in nearby restaurant was too long. It was a mistake. My lobster risotto barely had any lobster and it wasn't risotto, just over cooked rice. The burger lacked salt, was falling apart, and was tasteless.

name: Gary Fernandes
text: Excellent chilli and lime chicken wings. Spaghetti squash went remarkably well with hake fish and chips. Thrice cooked fries were fantastic, but have them hot for maximum effect.

name: Heleen Raes
text: We stumbled upon this cute restaurant by accident and are very happy about it! We arrived around 8:30PM and were still gracefully seated near the window by the lovely host/server. They have an extensive drink menu and a smaller food menu, but it has something for everyone. Most of the food came from local farms and businnesses so it’s a great way to support those and have a lovely meal!

name: Mac Coldwell
text: This is one of the many gems in Portland. They do a wonderful dinner, but it is one of my favorite lunch spots when I have time to dine in. Their menu is updated often, but there is always something delicious. It's been a while since I have seen/had their trout fritters, but I love those things. Their burger is tasty. The dinners I have had there are also delicious. I remember a pork and grits that was wonderful. The cocktails are also really tasty and crafted well. There servous is always friendly and attentive.

name: Chillidoe
text:
Why...Did...I...Come...Here,
I have been sitting here, waiting and wondering if anyone is going to show up with the drink I ordered over 15 minutes ago. While on the subject of losing my patience, I came here because I was hungry, not to sit here debating on if I'm actually going to get my order taken before closing time. I wouldn't wish this service even on the man who killed my mother. PLEASE stay away from this establishment, there are plenty of good eateries near by with employees that will at least acknowledge your presence in their restaurant.
Absolutely Disgusted,
Chillidoe

name: Andrew Elegante
text: I've only been here for brunch but it was fantastic. I'd seen an amazing dish on the website that wasn't labeled and didn't seem to match anything on the menu so I ordered the duck hash (their signature). Turns out it was the dish on the website (!) and it was amazing. The hash part is done as more of a croquet/tater tot which adds an interesting texture and the squash it came with had a delightful orange zest in it. Very yum. Did not try any cocktails but the coffee was good

name: Raphy & Sara Feolino
text:
Quick, friendly service.

Great location! Street parking.

Order:
Happy Hour CHICKEN LEG RILLETTES WITH HOUSE MUSTARD & PICKLES $7: this was so good! Especially loved the way the bread was prepared.

FRIED FISH SANDWICH $13: delicious, lite, refreshing & filling. Salad was not drenched in dressing but could be a little less salty.

The pickles were a highlight with each dish. They were very sweet!

name: Tony Manzella
text: Very good food and friendly staff. Our entrees were awesome. The dessert was not quite as good but still very good.

name: terry delargy
text: Lovely, cozy place with comfortable old-school booths. Menu is very good and not slave to trends.  The scallops were the best I've ever tasted!

name: Amethyst Cannon
text: Weather was perfect to dine outside and have a drink. Great staff.

name: Laura Pandolfo
text: I hate to review this place because I think it's such a gem... I want it all to myself! Good beer and wine selection, fantastic service, and a small but special menu of dishes they do REALLY well. You can't go wrong with anything on the menu, but my favorites are their grilled chicken tikka and fish & chips. My favorite thing about East Ender is that it feels special and intimate without being overly priced... hard to come by in Portland these days!

name: Jeff Howe
text: Stopped in on Sunday after walking into town from the Eastern Prom, thinking that the outdoor seating was for the Duckfat restaurant. Ordered a beey salad and the fish & chips to split. The beet salad was excellent, with pepita's and a white cheese (can't remember exactly) with balsamic dressing, but it was the fish & chips that really stood out. The chips were fine, but the fish was superb, very flavorful and the crust was perfect, crispy and flakey, and not soggy in the least. When the bill came, we realized that we weren't at Duckfat at all, but at The East Ender. Turns out that their outside seating areas are close together, and we weren't the first to make the mistake. The waitress was super gracious about it and explained that while the two restaurants were wholly separate, they had a good and cooperative relationship. In short it was a very pleasant visit for an excellent mid-day snack, and we'll put it on the list for a full meal some day when normal dining resumes.

name: Cade Blackburn
text: Really good spot with convenient on street parking. Had the Braised Pork Shoulder,  it was nice and tender. They have good drinks, good beer selection and reasonable price. Check them out.

name: Tim
text: Delicious food, excellent service in spacious outdoor space.

name: J P S
text: The waitress was wonderful but food was average.  The risotto was not as creamy as it could have been and not a lot of lobster.

name: A Hattaway
text: A small eatery good for a quick, satisfying meal. Menu is concise, making selection easy. Decent beer and wine options. Service was rushed, which was strange on a winter Monday night with low traffic.

name: bridget o'brian
text: Very good meals.Service a little slow. Very comfortable place and easy for talking.

name: Kristen Murphy Caldecutt
text: Went for brunch. Pleasant waitstaff and tasty food. Good drinks options too!

name: Tod B
text: Very nice.  Cold rainy mid-May day.  I'll admit we only came over for a beer while we waited for our table next door but I will be back.  Looked like really good food.

name: Michael Mozill
text: Nice place for warm food on a winter afternoon.

name: everett buron
text: Decent enough to get a drink whilst waiting for a table at Eventide. The wings were too cooked and dry

name: Mrs Tiffany Alexandra Shain
text: A favorite place for... I think about a decade now for my husband and I. While the restaurant adjacent to this one is amazing, we always like to giggle at each other and do a little high five while people starve outside in line next door LOL

name: Breezy
text: Our third time eating here and still as great as the first.  Awesome beer selection and a nice assortment of food options.  I went with the smoked burger last time and it was delicious.  This time, I got the grilled chicken tikka sandwich and it was even better.  So good - will be back again next time!

name: Kerry Angell
text: Interesting menu options and some good fallbacks like burgers. Service staff was friendly  knew the menu.  Nice rustic atmosphere.

name: Roman Popov
text: Located right next to DuckFat, East Ender has surprisingly less folks. So if in doubt whether you will be able to grab a table during rush hour or lunch, don't fret - they will likely be able to accommodate you. I'd highly recommend trying chicken wings in lime rub and brussel sprouts - these both were really impressive appetizers!!!

name: John McDonough
text:
5 of us had dinner this evening and enjoyed it very much. 2 burgers, 1 fish and chips, chickpea and chicken.
Good selections of beer and drinks.
Only negative is portion sizes are smaller than normal entrees and appetizers, all food was more like bar bite size.
It was enough food but a bit pricey for portion size.

(To note, the correct door to use says "lounge upstairs" so it's a touch misleading, thinking that's the lounge door).

Slow service. There are six tables. We were the latest of four taken tables total (mostly parties of two). Got ignored for the couple that came in after us, no big deal. Finally got order in. Waited on drinks. The party with jerkface was sat a short while afterwards, ordered wine, and server literally went to pour it right away. Still no drink. Asked again, it was obviously forgotten. Bloody Mary made with fish oil or something, so it was gross, unfortunately.

Seemed overwhelmed with the four tables, now adding a fifth, so the overall feel was just that we were an annoyance. Food was okay, nothing special. This is where everyone else gets a FAIL!!! You can ask for well-done and it'll be extra crispy!! Now... THAT'S ITALIAN!! The meatball subs/grinders are yummy too!

Ok... I love the above... But my recent discovery there has got to be my very favorite... Their CHICKEN PARM AND SPAGHETTI SMOTHERED IN CHEESE SERVED WITH A PlECE OF GARLIC BREAD (or as hubby likes it... Just plain bread).! Now don't let the container fool you; It SEEMS SMALL but let me tell you, l can eat, but l get halfway done (and l am stuffed!) and save the rest for lunch the next day. Who am l kidding... I eat it for BREAKFAST the next day!! Hubby can finish his, but complains about his big gut for 2 days later!! Okay you get the picture.. But wait theres more!! text: First time seeing the "gardens aglow", it was worth the price per car load. While the ride takes about 15 minutes it's money well spent. The attention to details was fantastic! We would absolutely recommend checking out the lights as well as a summer stop to the Botanical Garden.

text: What a magical place. We went to the Gardens Aglow event and we're blown away by the sight. 650,000 lights and 2 1/2 months to create. A work of art not to be missed.

text: Wonderful place to visit with friends and family. Be sure to bring good shoes and hike along the miles of trails, otherwise you're missing out on the full experience. Bring lunch to eat in the grass or on one of the many benches, or purchase one of the fresh smoothies, honey, etc from the shop.

name: Katherine W
text: What else can we say but— wow! What a pleasant surprise during our visit to Boothbay. We've been to botanicals gardens throughout the US, and the Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens ranks up there as one of our favorites. The  variety of plants and flowers were beautiful, and the garden's situation along the water is lovely. We especially enjoyed the Sensory Garden, Dahlia Test Garden, Meditation Garden, and the Fairy House Village. 10/10 recommend!

name: eDee Bruns
text: Would highly recommend .... you go with my sister Julie and keep an open speaker phone between cars. We had a blast! Also let one kid hang outside the window and record!

text: Absolutely GORGEOUS! Miles of walking trails surrounded by the most incredible flowers, trees, plants, ponds, and wildlife. Would be a perfect place to propose (or even have a wedding!), or just to get out and explore for the day. I will be back every season!

name: Ian Toal
text: We went for the drive through light show and it was well worth seeing. We drove through a lot of the park and the light show was really nice. It felt good to be doing something "normal" to ring in the new year.

The staff is super friendly and helped up out with a few of our questions and concerns.

text: Don’t skip this place. It’s so beautiful! There are so many interesting things to do for everyone! The stuff is very friendly!

name: Joe Mammone
text: The AGlow event is simply stunning. We'll worth the trip. The cafe was a refreshing stop where we got hot pretzels, scones and hot chocolate.  Loved it but ran out of time even though we had spent two hours there!

text: Lights were beautiful...  Unfortunately only one shuttle bus runs so we waited 25 or so minutes to be picked up after we saw the bus drive by us on the way to the suggested parking site. We went on a Sunday night so it wasn't very crowded. Definitely would go next season.

name: Ascended Spirit
text: What a beautiful garden, it is huge, you won't get through it in one day.

name: Stephen Arlaud
text: We usually visit the gardens once a year. We had noticed they had built a new entrance building aside from the original entrance building at a new location. You now enter at this new location and walk a new trail across a bridge into the gardens. There is new and expanded free parking, now with lighting. The new areas are nicely landscaped. The gardens are very nice with trails all over the property. There is a shuttle that runs around some areas of the park. Everything in the garden is well marked including the plants and trees. Artists have done very nice sculptures throughout. You can easily spend hours and part of a day here. This site is nicely located right on the water with boat rentals and tours. Food and drinks are available at two locations, one being a sit down cafe with inside and outside seating. You should visit this garden at least once, it is well kept up and clean. The thing to know is the gardens are open for “Gardens Aglow” in the holiday season near Christmas. I have been once to this and is absolutely beautiful with the gardens completely lit up with just Christmas lights. It really is a sight, but dress warm and drink the hot chocolate they have available.

name: Alice Bean Andrenyak
text:
Gardens Aglow make the Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens have a winter season.

Spring, summer and fall the gardens keep changing as the different flowers and flora go through their seasons. Gardens Aglow bring lights to awaken the gardens and let so many people experience winter's darkness with glee and wonder.

The gardens are for families young and old, couples, friends, photographers,  solo wandering, and the workshops are top notch.

A Maine gem not to be missed.

text: Beautiful lights, arranged a bit differently than years past.  But very well set up.

name: Remi Paluszak
text: A truly wonderful place, well maintained, brand new facilities, available staff, reasonable prices that are clearly being utilized to improve the facility. We came here with the whole family, grandparents, my wife and I and two kids and had plenty to do and explore for many hours. Our 8-year-old, who is very content playing on his iPad all day, thanked us for bringing him here and said that he had a lot of fun. Besides "flowers or plants" the paths weave through the well designed gardens like a labyrinth, bringing up unexpected discoveries. There are ponds populated by fish and frogs, many insects and birds. There is a little playground where you can explore bird calls, gardens with herbs and vegetables, a newly established butterfly conservatory, a place to learn about gardening and maintenance and there even was a puppet theater. All this, which I perceived as the most important aspect, was well integrated into the existing fauna and landscape instead of replacing it. Parking was easy and accessible, entrance swift, the facilities clean and well maintained. The location is apart from any environmental distractions like busy roads and allows to be fully present. What came as a pleasant surprise was that the cafe, at first glance expansive and simple, was actually quite good in terms of quality and quantity and did not mislead. The salads and sandwiches simply tasted as if someone had just picked the greens and vegetables from the gardens. The staff was accommodating and one person was able to help me with a band-aid for a blister on my foot. Maybe that is normal but I was pleasantly surprised that they had them readily available. My suggestion to these gardens would be to create a strong photography program or events and info packets with information what can be found there, when, where and, for novices, suggestions for composition/settings. I have never been to a botanical garden that is not full of "photographers" as it presents with so many subjects. Keep up the good work!

text: The gardens are beautiful and expansive with many nooks for relaxation or play. I particularly enjoyed wandering the five senses garden and relaxing in a porch swing beside a massive succulent display and clever whale fountain. The children's garden was adorable and I heard many cheerful cries and pattering feet. While there is clearly plenty to do in the main areas, there are also creative locations you can hike to: a fairy garden for the children, a seaside meditation space, a tiered rhododendron garden, and more. I also appreciated the informational plaques dispersed throughout the visit. Overall, I am confident in my five star rating and hope many others have the opportunity to appreciate this beautiful space and the friendly staff who make all feel welcome.

name: Ruth Shaw
text: It is not possible to have too much of the beautiful experience of visiting the Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens. Parking is easy with a short walk to the visitors center, and a drop off as necessary near the door before parking. Kind and informative check-in folks, with maps, and suggestions as needed, and extensive walkways to journey to every corner to the gardens. Regular tour buses picking up and dropping off for those who prefer a ride. Lunchrooms, bathrooms, and an interesting shop are all available. But these excellent qualities are only the framework for extensive and beautiful gardens, something for all ages. Wind sculptures, water gardens, a butterfly garden (still in it's infancy -much more is planned), places with special magical to appeal to children, even a meditation garden well off the beaten path. Go there! Your spirit will be refreshed by the experience of a journey to these gardens.

text:
Visited Garden's Aglow and I was impressed!! Thousands of well placed lights decorating everything! Lots of colors. Some lights blinked in waves along branches or 🌲 s. The tunnel of light had operatic music playing as the lights swirled above. Benches, a rope bridge, bridges and awnings were also decorated. Two cafes were available, though, I didn't eat there. Food and drinks were a little pricey. A popcorn vendor was there as well. People littering with popcorn was common.
A shuttle service from the Boothbay Harbor 🔥 department building, by the Center, was available so you didn't have to deal with traffic. Last ride was from the garden was 8:45 PM.
I recommend a visit!
Update: July 4th, 2019;  Impressive!! A lot of work went into the gardens, displays and trails. Very scenic. Forest trails and benches right by the river. The man made waterfall was very nice. An area was set up for kids to play and learn.
The butterfly exhibit was interesting. The Butterfly Place in Massachusetts is still the best. The gardens have butterflies, dragonflies and bees. The 🐝 s didn't bother anyone.
The trails are well maintained. Bathroom was in good condition. Water fountain available. You can fill your water bottle there.
I recommend bringing sunscreen, bug repellent, water, comfortable shoes for light hiking, hat and small umbrella if you sunburn even with sunscreen.
Plenty of parking. AAA discount available.
Boat ride sells out quickly so I recommend seeing if you can book online. I heard people who went out saying they had a good time.

name: Clayton & Cindy Putnam
text:
Such a holiday delight, GO ! See IT !
I can't  say enough . . .  walk around the acres of holiday lights strung all over the trees, bushes, and water bridges at the Botanical Gardens in Booth Bay, Maine.

The cost was $16 for adults, and kids about $9 each for entrance into the Botanical Gardens. You need to buy your tickets ahead of time . . .  online works.  I believe the holiday lights are up 2 weeks before Thanksgiving to New Years. Over that 6 week period, you can buy tickets for the 4 pm time slot, or the 6 pm time slot. But check out the website for details.

Watch the weather, and temperatures! It was cold the night we went, temps. in the teens with wind gusts up to 25 mph. Dress with all the trimmings, for your head, hands, and feet! There were 600,000 lights this year! FANTASTIC!

The best news, try the hot chocolate stations! They take cash or credit. They offer a few delightful flavors, I highly recommend  the butter rum or peppermint!
Enjoy the Best hot chocolate  ever . . . as you walk around and see the best MAINE  light display ever!

text: It was beautiful and had it not been for the extreme cold and crazy crowds, it would have been an awesome time for my 3 year old and us. All kinds of parking. Gift shop items are a bit expensive. Amazing job with the lights. A couple more random observations. For really cold evenings, they should have more than just the two heater "stations" located at the hot chocolate station and spread them out a bit. Keep people informed of when the shuttle to the parking lot is coming. People had been waiting quite a while, so we just walked it, which wasn't really too awfully far anyway, but it was freezing. On that note, protected, heated shuttles would have been awesome too, but it's also not usually 10° in December. Crowds were terrible at times. It really hurt the experience in my opinion. I'd like to try again when it's less busy and a bit warmer. They should consider doing things with the lights year-round if possible!

text:
There must be hundreds of thousands of colorful lights on display.  Brick or stone walking paths will guide you through the different arrangements.  We pushed a family member who was in a wheelchair quite easily.
Durring the times of the light displays you may purchase tickets that will guarentee a parking spot at one of the onsite parking areas.  Or you may chance it to find a spot at one of the many parking areas.
If all of the parking is full at the botanical garden, you may park in designated areas in town and take the free shuttle to the gardens.
They have restrooms available and a couple of places to sit and purchase refreshments or take a break.
The staff was very courteous and helpful.
This display of lights is enjoyable for the  young and old. We plan to return in the summer to view the gardens and plants.

name: Tiffany Derosier
text:
Just an incredibly beautiful place to visit.
New things to see as the various plants grow and bloom through the spring and summer. We like to go for a Sunday picnic lunch and enjoy the quiet afternoon.  We have visited many times. A favorite is the welcoming early spring season when a very impressive show of multitudes of tulips are in full bloom.

It is spacious and accommodating from parking and services, to facilities and the many areas of trails, woods and themed hardscapes on the grounds. Some things to be sure to checkout include; the butterfly enclosure, the children's garden, the senses garden, and if you like to walk alot check out the rhododendrons in the spring. If you don't want to walk you can also hitch a ride to and from, with their free in park shuttle service.

Some unique and interesting man-made sculptures also adorn the area's around the gardens. They are tastefully applied so that it doesn't overwhelm or take away from the natural beauty of the gardens and grounds.

More than just flowers, it is a relaxing place where you can enjoy all elements of the natural setting where a tremendous number of plants, shrubs, and trees are cultured among a landscape of various elements with walking paths, lawns, waterscapes, stones and rock formations, and even places to sit and rest while enjoying the view or meditating.

Even at the onset of winter when there are no plants to see, they offer a light show they call "Gardens Aglow".  It is just a wonderful sight to behold. One of those things you just need to do at least once.

Whenever you go, there is plenty to see. Plan on several hours to make it well worth taking it all in. You will most likely see something you haven't seen before and learn something new.

We then tried to give our tickets to the people at the front desk and they didn't want to take them because they didn't want to make it look like they were giving free tickets away. name: Ron Lusk
text:
"Beyond all expectations." Keep that phrase in mind as you walk through this collection of gardens. From the wetlands—no! Before that! From the layout of the welcoming Visitor Center on, this place is beyond all expectations. The Visitor Center? Yes: the first part of the visitor center you see is shaded covered hallways, with restrooms and drinking fountains. If you had been caught in summer coastal traffic on the way up (we weren't) this would be the sight most welcome to your eyes—unless you were the driver, where the ample free parking might be a contender for that prize.
Then through the Visitor Center—don't balk at the price: for the two to three hours (minimum) of fascination here, the price is low—through the Visitor Center to the long wooden bridge over the frog-filled wetlands. A docent will give you an introduction to the park, let you know there's a shuttle to run you to distant parts, and send you warmly on your way. Below, the bullfrogs will cheer you on.
I won't cover it all. To me, the most touching part is in the Lerner Garden of the Five Senses, which is designed for accessibility. There are upright garden beds, so someone who uses a wheelchair can experience the plants close up; insets *under* the horizontal planter beds, so a wheelchair can "pull up to the table"; special programs, to allow everyone to get a taste of gardening, or nearly everyone.
I could go on about the children's garden, the rhododendron garden with its beautiful waterfall (we were late for the most brilliant of blossoms ☹️), the cacti and other succulents everywhere, the… well, you get the idea.
Go and see. If you don't like plants, bear with your friends who do and bless them with your patience and wonder. And, maybe, something will catch your attention, or your heart, and you'll say, "I liked it more than I expected."

text:
My third trip.  I got to the Giles Rhododendron Garden this time.  Many wonderful blooms and I can't wait to go back later this summer for a different set.

Increased parking over last year! Bigger Gift shop, quick grab and go snacks and sandwiches, though a bit pricey. If you can, bring your own.  Lots of places to lunch on the lawn or at picnic tables in the children's garden. Lots of fun things for the kids to do in the Children's garden including a treehouse, working a pump well- and during the warmer months feeding chickens.

Most of the garden is easy walks on paths.  There are some longer walks but fairly gentle. They do have scooters available on a first come first served basis for a fee that will get you to all the major areas of the gardens.  I took the Maine Woods Trail between the Rhododendron Garden and cross road between the Carriage House and Birch Allee, it was an easy woods walk, but not for those with compromised mobility.  The Haney Hillside Garden is lovely walk down but very steep coming back up. You can take a shuttle back up if you follow the Shoreland Trail to the shuttle stop. I went partway down the Brook Trail but only had sneakers on.  I recommend having hikers on, I didn't feel comfortable going down the steeper area.

name: Maine CarGuy
text:
I cannot stress this enough: TAKE THE FREE SHUTTLE BUS!

You do NOT want to try driving to the site in your car. Yes, it's a short drive from Boothbay Harbor, but...

The entrance is a LONG dirt road through the woods, barely wide enough for two cars to pass. There are no turn around spots. Once in line you are stuck there. I guarantee it will be at least 30 minutes to get into a parking spot which will likely be 2 or 3 football fields away from the admissions/entrance building. There are like 5 handicap spots, and even those are a considerable distance from the entrance area.

TAKE THE FREE SHUTTLE!  It drops you right in front of the door. Our driver was great. The whole bus sang Christmas Carols during the trip. About a 15 minute ride from downtown Boothbay Harbor.

Stunning Christmas lights on display. You won't be disappointed. Overpriced food from local vendors available on site. Save $$ by eating in Boothbay instead.

text: I love Starbucks coffee. I think it's the best around. And, you know the quality of drinks and food you will be getting here everytime. They have also messed up my drinks several times and offered me weak excuses as to why my drink was wrong and never offered to replace my drink or give me credit towards another drink. It's the closest one to me so I will always go here, but it's not the best Starbucks I have gone too for customer service (and I have gone to MANY!).

text: The museum is free on Fridays, so we took advantage and planned our visit on a Friday.  It's a very nice and well kept museum with some great pieces from well renowned and local artists (Picasso, Renoir, Monet, etc).  Due to COVID, our visit was limited to an hour, but I could have easily spent 2 hours here.  It's a nice way to pass the time on a rainy day in Portland.

name: Perks Advisor
text: The Portland Museum of Art provides culture to the city and is a worthwhile visit.  Even on the outside the Museum offers a sculpture garden.  I particular found the person created from stone and wire an interesting one.  Inside they have a number of quality pieces and have a fair number of sculptures as well.  The museum is centrally located and easily accessible.

name: Michael Joyce
text:
Overall we love Museum of Art!
I am not a fan of their modern exhibits, especially it's the first thing you see when you come in it kind of sets the tone in my opinion in the wrong direction.
Maybe one day you'll move that rotating display someplace else.

name: Bonnie
text: It feels good to be in such a beautiful building, surrounded by such inspiring pieces of art. There is a small food court downstairs if you’re into that.  The art literally takes your breath away, some of it is so stunning. Ten for sure!!! Also you can’t beat the convenient location to all the great coffee shops, restaurants, and bars in Portland and the Old Port.

name: Kate Robinson
text: Spacious museum with historical and modern collections. There is a locker space to leave jackets and bags. We enjoyed every gallery as each had something exciting to see. Layout makes sense so you can work your way through each gallery and see everything. We will go back again as it is worth seeing new exhibits and also looking at favorites in the collection.

name: Tanner Paladino
text:
Amazing pieces throughout the 3 floors available to us today. Was Friday and free entry after booking online.

Thank you for allowing me to see the amazing works of Rockwell Kent, Pablo Picasso, Andrew Wyeth, and so many amazing artists. Cheers

text: The ugliest building downtown is the art museum. Yep. Sums up the place.

text: Nice collection in a beautiful space for a small City. Friday afternoons seem to be free. Otherwise it's $18 per adult for admission.

text: A very extensive collection that provides a little bit of everything. The McLellan House section offers a unique atmosphere for viewing the portions of the collection on display there, as well as a scene of architectural history.

text: Small collection of international artists but a very well designed space. If you are into museum you will not be impressed, but you will. Ot be disappointed either.

text: Great exhibits. The impressionist room was wonderful and you need to see the Monet and the Bierstadt.

text: Always inspiring. Really a great way to spend a morning.

text: Too good to take it all in in two hours.  A little bit crowded but, hey, that in itself, speaks volumes. The shows now on display were unique.  You could literally, spend hours in the N.C. Wyeth exhibit alone.  Don't miss this opportunity.

name: Marie Szakos
text: The Portland Museum of Art in Portland, Maine is a place full of art treasures. From paintings by Winslow Homer to Claude Monet, to find beauty in every piece one beholds is obvious. They have sculptures by Edgar Degas. Also, you will find 6 rooms of life sized sculptures which we did not have the pleasure of seeing. The giant sculpture of Ulysses S Grant is mind blowing. Even the bathrooms have fine art on the walls.

name: Standish Penton
text: Lovely exhibits. Than you

name: Johan Halvorsen
text: Amazing!    I visited for my first time and was very impressed. There are a lot of famous artists represented.

name: Lynn Hansen
text: A good use of an hour or two on a rainy day.  Small museum.  Scored a Groupon for $9.

name: J A
text:
I love Romanticism and was surprised to find it here. I loved the Grant marble sculpture and the Dead Pearl Diver. Beautiful!

I also enjoyed the photograph portrait exhibit.

One star docked because I didn't like most of the art in the museum. But the stuff that I liked made it all worth it.

name: G Aquino
text:
I was quite surprised by the huge and diverse collection, with works by Monet, Picasso, and Warhol figuring prominently. We planned to be here for an hour but ended up staying for two. While impressive, it would have been nice to see a section of the museum dedicated to local artists, especially the up-and-coming ones who need a venue to showcase their art.

The museum is housed in three interconnected buildings, two of which form the McLellan-Sweat Mansion, a national historic landmark. The other building, named after native son Charles Shipman Payson, was added in the 1980s and houses the main entrance.

Finding street parking was a challenge. After several futile attempts, we finally settled for the Spring Street Parking Garage a block away.

name: C D
text:
Cons

As a Bank of America card holder, I wish I was able to get a free admission. For $18.00 I wish there was more variety in the museum.

Pros:

The museum is very nice and has beautiful pieces throughout.
I particularly loved the live music in the cafe to wind down and relax which is nice intimate touch
The customer service is friendly and knowledgeable.

Overall for a rainy day it was good experience.

name: A Layton
text: Amazing art at this museum.  It was such a treat to get to expose my son to some of the greatest artists in the world.

name: James Doyle
text: This is probably the best art museum in the United States, north of Boston. It is medium-sized, so it is possible to fully explore it in about two and a half hours. It has some excellent pieces and a gallery dedicated to art depicting Maine. It is housed between two buildings; a modern, purpose-built structure which holds the majority of the collection and patron services, and a historic house, which appears to have lost its original charm through renovation. It is largely devoid of art, but I expect that this will change. Located in the tourist center of downtown Portland. Free on Friday evenings.

name: Chris Slesarchik
text:
Relaxing and chic atmosphere with friendly service. An excellent place for an uncommon dessert experience. Prices are definitely on the expensive side but the attention to detail and balance of sweetness and unique flavor combinations make a visit worth it if you can afford it (expect to pay anywhere from $8-18 for a single portion). Menu has plenty of options to choose from and has everything from fruity/tart to chocolate and everything in between. Drinks were great and even included mocktails and quality coffee drinks.

Keep in mind you will be paying for the experience here, so if you’re just looking for a sugar rush this might not be the place. I could easily have eaten the entire super moist chocolate cake to myself even though it is listed as “for two”, but maybe that’s just a testament to the quality! Be sure to bring someone with you for the full experience because there are a lot of items designed for sharing with two or more people, unless you are ready to shell out $20-30 to have one all to yourself.

name: Perks Advisor
text:
Inside the Westin hotel was a very good experience.  While the hotel appears older on the outside, my room and the hotel itself had an updated feel.  Most important to me was this Westin’s policy to allow pets without charging a fee - this is smart business on their behalf and much appreciated.  I also found the staff to be very professional and friendly.

There is a downside to this hotel that is beyond the hotel’s control but relates to location.  Next to the hotel is the Congress Square Park which predominantly serves the homeless population and I was inundated with requests for contributions every time I left the hotel.  Worse, the car next to mine parked inside the hotel contracted garage was broken into and the glass sprayed all over my car as well.  While this may not be an issue for some travelers it is a consideration.

resp.text:
Thanks for the 4/5 review!

We are glad you had a great experience with us! We are disappointed to see some of your concerns, and we will let our team know about them. We always work very hard to make sure all of our guests have a pleasant stay. We look forward to hosting you again for an even better experience.

Thanks again, and have a lovely day!

General Manager
The Westin Portland Harborview

text:
I honestly don't understand the higher rating. I had higher expectations from a Westin but this one felt like a 2 star hotel. From the location, to the room, to housecleaning, to the food - it was a disappointment.

First the location - it's farther away from the main tourists attractions. Hyatt is better located for sure.

The main reason for low rating is the rooms and service. First night the AC made loud noises to a point we couldn't sleep at all. Went to the front desk the next day and it seems the engineer knew about the issue but they still decided to have guests in there! While I was reporting my issues there was another gentleman showing horrible cleaning effort - he showed pictures of some gross stuff in the bathroom.

The bed too wasn't comfortable at all but the first room had extra selection of pillows that were missing in the second room.

Now on to the food. It was raining the first night so we decided to eat at the rooftop bar. Very limited selection (no coffee) and horrible food. You go there for beer, that's it. The service was decent and that's the only good thing I can say about the bar.

Thank you for taking the time to provide feedback on your recent stay with us. I will be sure to address the issues outlined below with our staff. If you would like to share any additional feedback from your stay, please reach out to me via email at lucas.laidlaw@westinportlandharborview.com.

When we got the hotel,  the desk person walked away in the middle of the sign-in process and we had to hunt him down. The whole process just came across as "we could care less." AND the sink isn't partially clogged and the heat is very weak. I cranked it all the way up and the room is still too cold. The pillow cases are either so overly starched or of such low quality it's like sleeping on tin foil. When I requested a wake up call, they didn't get th time right. And finally,  they messed up our taxi time because they didn't call the taxi soon enough. They had promised the cab would be there and waiting at 445am and it wasn't.  If there is a way to screw up, this hotel staff did it. How this dump is considered a 4 star hotel is beyond me. I've been to Motel 6s that are better.

name: Christopher Caldarella
text: My mom and dad were staying here for my wedding. Very nice place. Service was lacking. Over two days, mouthwash was never replaced by housekeeping, sheets were half-heartedly straightened (not tucked in), dirty dishes from room-service were left in the room. Overall a very nice place though. Maybe it was an "off" couple of days or perhaps they were short-staffed but for charging luxury prices there could definitely be improvements in service. I had lunch at the restaurant and waited about five or ten minutes by the 'wait to be seated' sign. I was eventually seated with no silverware nor napkin. I understand that it was slow - having worked in the service industry for six years at a luxury hotel, I get it that the wait staff was probably doing side work. But once my food arrived no one came back to see how I was doing. I will clarify that my food came with a spoon (it was tomato bisque with grilled cheese and a side salad - which was all very delicious!) So I did not immediately notice the rest of the missing silverware and napkin until after I had some soup. I just grabbed some from another table. I mentioned this when I was finally presented the check by the bartender (I didn't see my waitress again) just so he would know the table need a place setting. He was nice and thanked me, and I think he apologized too, which is nice. The food was great though. I had some of my mom's lobster slider a different day and that was also delicious. And the prices were reasonable for the type of food. But again, for that kind of establishment the service was lacking. Service was not bad, the staff is nice, just not attentive for a luxury style hotel and restaurant. Except for Amanda who works at the restaurant. Amanda was great.

text:
So this is kinda confusing, I've stayed there a few times I believe 2 in total. Well the first time was for my birthday and we had a very good time in a very nice room and and meet some very interesting people who made the night that much for enjoyable.
However, the second night we stayed there an abundance of problems occurred during check in, Which in turn would ultimately lead to other issues making the new years eve night a one to forget.  As my girlfriend arrived at the hotel to check in to the suit we had requested a week in advance, she was told that would be unavailable for us at the present time due to overbooking. Well my gf is a very quiet, respectful woman who will take what they offer her regardless If it's what she had booked or not.
Well as soon as I had arrived at the hotel I entered the room and it had to be the next best thing to the janitor closet. Tiny, one window facing a brick wall and a small little shower behind the door of the bathroom. Needless to say I wasn't happy, made a call to the front desk, spoke with one of many managers who arranged it so we could have the same room we had the very first time we stayed there but still no suite.
All in all it wasn't worth the money or the stress. And for some reason I still get blamed for us not getting the suit we were promised. But in time this too shall pass, I just wish the hotel had made right on their end and to this day im still waiting for that phone call.
Mcneel

text:
The more you pay the less you get, this saying definitely applies here.
The Good: The best part is the beds and sheets, comfy and soft. Centrally located.

The Bad: staff is 'friendly' yet unhelpful.  They don't know how to apologize for mistakes or miscommunication.  Asked someone at the restaurant to order a grilled cheese sandwich to go and was told to order from our room, so we could be charged another 20% to the cooked bread and cheese.  Then when we ordered from our room and mentioned the special on the board outside the restaurant and was told it wasn't a special.  The fact that valet has taken over all the parking I front of the hotel is ridiculous.  Morning of checkout we asked desk staff to have our bill split up for checkout and come checkout it wasn't done.

For the cost the staff could be a bit more accommodating.

text:
The only chain fried chicken you're going to find near downtown Portland.

All in all, Crown is pretty decent. It obviously has fried chicken as a staple, but they also make kabobs, burgers, and even fish sandwiches.

The interior is usually pretty clean, but the inside is drafty and chilly. The waits are sometimes long, but the staff is friendly. The best thing about Crown is the price.

I usually get their #2 special - which is two pieces of fried chicken and a side of fries or  rice (their rice is amazing, seriously) and a can of soda - all for about $8. It's a pretty good deal.

If you want to splurge, go to Figgy's - but you can't beat Crown's price, at least not unless you go outside downtown Portland for fried chicken.

I usually get take-out, but there is a dining area. It's fairly basic, but there is plenty of room and it is always clean. Off street parking is limited, but I've never had a problem finding a spot nearby. The spices they use on the fries and chicken are great.

name: Ameen Rauf
text:
Went to this place late at night on a colleague’s recommendation and tried chicken kabob over rice. I was pleasantly surprised that despite the modest price, the quality of kabob was no less that that of many high end Mediterranean restaurants in NYC. The rice were mildly spiced and not drenched in oil (what you get at most low priced places) and kabobs came spiced with herbs, were flavorful and yet not too spicy or hot. Even my 2 years old enjoyed eating them. Went back again next day, got some more chicken with kabobs and also got beef samosas (beef patties), cake pudding and their chai. Every thing was great again. The tea was out of this world, typical Indian/Pakistani chai which is slow-brewed and comes premixed with milk and sugar.
The people who run this place are very attentive, pleasant and try to connect with you at a personal level. I will definitely go there again whenever will travel to Portland Maine.
The food is halal, freshly cooked min front of you and has authentic middle eastern flavor. I am not a big fan of fried items but one must try this place’s middle eastern menu and tea/chi.

text:
This is one of those quintessential hidden gems. It's in a strip mall, adjacent to a coast guard recruiting center. The parking lot outside had two liquor bottles littering the ground. But once one goes inside, they're immediately in a place that clearly has a sense of pride. There are multiple fish tanks with beautiful fish. Art work adorns the walls and is very lovely. Everything is spotlessly clean.

This attention to detail extends to the food, which is ample, reasonably priced, and really seems to be on a different level than many other Chinese restaurants in the area. It was abundantly clear that sauces were made in-house from fresh ingredients. Aromatics, like ginger and garlic, had the kick that only happens when freshly sliced. Fried items didn't have any off flavors, telling me that the oil and fryers were in good shape. Anything that was fried or seared had a perfect crust, indicating the right temperature and not overcrowding. Lastly, the presentation of all items was beautiful. This place sweats the details and it shows.

This has become our favorite Chinese restaurant in the Portland area. That's not to say it's the only good one (there are plenty), but it offers the food quality of others without the fight to get a seat or price multiplier one pays in the city. It appears to be family run and the staff are lovely, kind people.

I received a take out meal and did not have to wait more than 10minutes to receive everything I ordered. Even though it took me 40minutes to get home and eat, it was the best food I've had in a long while. I would recommend this place to everyone.

text: Has been a fan for 10+ years.  House fried rice(ask for Brown rice) is A+. The staff recommend the Empress Shrimp and Galaxy trio. Mapo Tofu is also a good one(5* hot makes it yum).  The master chef is from Taiwan and he does make the meat, Chicken and Shrimp have a silky smooth texture  to them!

name: D. Avery
text:
Absolutely amazing, first time here and is by far the best I've ever had. We came on late in the evening during the snowstorm before valentines day, and the food was so fresh and delicious.
My GF is a crab rangoon addict and she was floored at the flavor and texture offered in these little golden treats. The beef teriyaki was to die for, the rice so fresh and delicious,  I've not a single complaint from first walking in to walking out completely full and with leftovers.
The plate representation was truly beautiful, I cannot stress enough how well decorated every plate was. If you're in the area and are craving Chinese food out of this world full of color,flavor and taste do yourself and family a favor and take them here.

I live nearly 2hrs north of here, and we WILL be back again even if it's a day trip planned here for lunch and some walks on the beach.

Thank you so much Panda Garden for such an amazing evening with my love.

I wish you and your family the BEST, I will forever remember my first visit here at your restaurant.

text: Stopped by for an appetizer and drink. Great food - made by hand in premises (the sausage anyway). The sampler platter was awesome.  Homemade chips and salsa, very tasty sausage, pickles and cheese were a delicious flavor combo. Great staff and a nice outdoor patio. Thoroughly recommend.

name: Eric Hamlin
text: I always enjoy the Thirsty Pig.  Pleasant, friendly staff, good food, and a well-curated beer selection.  I had lunch there on the 19th and tried one of their outdoor nooks.  These are nice, bent-wood enclosures with plastic over the top and back but open on the front.  Not heated, but worked pretty well to mitigate wind and keep snow off.  They also can provide pieces of flexible silver  insulation to help keep your butt warm.  If you bundle up the whole thing works well.  Looks like they are fitted with strings of little LED light... probably looks nice at night.

name: Mr X
text: Loved it. Good beer selection. Maybe a little higher priced but it's really splitting hairs n would not prevent me from going back. Great outside section so cannot wait to go back in the summer. The food (upscale hotdogs) looked n smelled amazing. Socially distanced accordingly.

name: Lindsey Ross
text:
This place was great and a real treat. The staff was very laid back but professional and helpful.

The food came out quickly and it was delicious! The portions are reasonable- Actually the first spot where we didn't feel stuffed and struggling to finish the plate. Perfect amount for a lunch.

We had the Mediterranean Gyro and Icelandic Hot Dog- which apparent was the best hot dog my boyfriend has ever had. This is saying a lot!

I would definitely recommend this spot. Atmosphere is relaxed. Decor is interesting.

text: Amazing meat. Great selection of beer and cider, good location and very friendly people.

text: I really enjoyed the atmosphere and space and appreciate the seating space. Overall layout is awesome. Bands were awesome as well. Great for a large amount of people as there is room to move about. Outdoor seating was a plus. The reason I give this a three out of five is the hot dogs are 7 bucks but they are like 50 cent small dogs. Toppings were great, chilli is pretty spicy. Price to cost just didn't match. I wish we tried some sausage though, maybe it would of got a four,next time though.

I had a brown ale which is retrospect I would have skipped because it really filled me up, but it was good! I ate out on the back porch and it offered a very lovely view of Portland.

name: Bradford Megquier
text: Well if you like great food and great beer than this is a great pick

name: Andre Ricarte
text:
We went here after a long day's travel around the city. When we walked in around 8/9PM it was packed with people.

What happens when you get there is you grab a menu first, order, and then find a table. You can open a tab or just pay upfront, like you would at any other bar.

There were 5 of us, and we ordered 5 different sandwiches. All of which tasted great in their own way. We also got the chef's choice sample platter which was 5 sausages on a plate. One sausage that really stood out was the Thai Chili, it's definitely a must try!

They had a lot of beers on tap. Many are made locally, like their Allagash beers.

When we ordered, they said it was going to be a 45 minute wait for the food due to the number of people, but luckily it was much less than that. By the time we finished, the rush was over.

Definitely enjoyed our food here, especially paired with their beers.

I do wish they carried a larger selection of beers during their cool limited edition runs, since I go there and sometimes there's just no beer for me which is a bummer. Their mustards are awesome too! Check this place out for some great sausage!

text: Over priced food for the amount of food that you receive. Crowded seating and unpleasant patrons.

name: Tyler Lund
text: The Thirsty Pig doesn't have the most friendly bartenders in the world, but the dog friendly outdoor patio is great and the local craft beer selection on tap is pretty great. The lower patio allows dogs and has several nice tables and benches. The beer menu is not huge, but has some good Portland and Maine brews on it. The service was surly and it took a while to order. No service outside so unfortunately you have to go in to order.

name: Alexandra Lynch
text: I love the atmosphere, the staff is very knowledgeable and friendly, and the food is very good. The trifecta in a good restaurant. I recommend The Thirsty Pig to all of my local and out-of-town friends.

name: S K
text:
Nice combination local ingredients, with hot dog/sausage menu.

Pretzels crispy outside, light inside.

Hot dogs not salty, crispy skin, buns were toasted just right.

Baked beans Maine style-molasses based.

name: Anita Alef

text:
Was the Italian sausage super tasty? Yup.
Was the pickle and the potato salad as well? Yes. Was it worth the price? Nope!
Old Port rents strike again. Classic case of fixed costs being absorbed into Cost of Goods Sold. Why did I get two tiny pieces of pickle and four chucks of potato and told it was a legitimate side? Who knows? Using a paper ketchup cup to serve a potato salad in is just sad and a little bit insulting. And is there a ration on pickles I wasn't aware of? Seriously, you couldn't give me at least one slice? Really? Trying to think of a reason to go back other than stumbling in by accident looking for a toilet.

name: Mac Coldwell
text: This is one of the neighborhood pizza shops within walking distance, and its always nice to have nearby shops that offer more then just an adequate meal closeby. The ingredients offered are both traditional and creative, and always taste fresh. You have a wheat and white dough to choose from as well as a decent gluten free option. You can also choose the thickness of the crust. There are good vegan options here. The vegan cheese I tried felt more like an alfredo sauce then a melted chesse, but the flavor and the  texture were enjoyable. The shop is accessible by wheelchair and parking is decent. They are doing a great job of observing social distancing. You call when you arrive and they bring your order to their door for you.

text: Starbucks are mostly the same, but this one really has great people working behind the counter. I live nearby and my daughter and I stop in often for a treat. The staff here had gotten to know my little toddler and always make her feel very special by giving her a hearty greeting and asking her about her day, etc. It's much appreciated. Starbucks is obviously a mega corporation, but when the people working there are friendly and community minded it makes it feel like an earned part of our town.

name: Evan Guthrie
text: Starbucks on Commercial Street in Portland is a great Starbucks location. I really liked the convenience of the location as it is in the middle of everything and easy to get to by walking and quick to get in and out. The service here was excellent as the line kept moving very efficiently and orders were taken care of with speed. I was impressed at how the team here worked together to accomplish everything and did it in a friendly and fun way that brought a smile to my face. I also really like the vibe and feel of the Starbucks as it has plenty of natural light and cool little extras like the free coffee grounds for your garden. Overall this was a great experience and it provided everyone with exactly what they needed.

name: F. Valle
text:
Visited for the Summer Sunsets On The Point. Starts at 4pm until sunset. Got there around 8pm and almost all food trucks where sold out.
Really enjoyed the vibe. A lot of dogs, many games, variety of food trucks and also a stand selling alcohol. Nice place to watch the sunset. Will be back earlier next Thursday to hopefully enjoy one of the trucks.

name: Jennifer Nelson
text: Beautiful night for a nicely socially distanced concert.  Almost all the food trucks were sold out by the time we arrived for the evening concert at 7 but other than that all was great.

name: Kennedy
text: This is a wonderful outdoor venue on the water in Portland. The food trucks are one of the best things about going to concerts here. They always have a bunch and they line the outer perimeter. If you are willing to nudge and squeeze through the crowd you can get as close to the stage as you want. Very intimate concert experience. There is a large sheltered area where the main drinks are served, but the lines can be long, so head to the other side where there are a couple of smaller drink serving stations with smaller lines, to the right of the stage as you are looking at it. Porta potties on site (you may have to hold your breath). Parking can be slow, and you’ll have a bit of a walk to the venue, but not too bad. If you Uber, I would just get dropped off at the lights outside the transportation center and walk.

name: Dennis Jacques
text: Great venue to see an outdoor show!! Can bring your own chairs, but seat can't be more than 9 inches high. Can bring 2 unopened bottles of water. Parking $20.

name: Jenna D.
text: Beautiful outdoor concert venue. Everything is efficient; from parking, to entering the venue at ticket check, to bar services, to portable restrooms (plenty of those, by the way - clean, no lines, and portable hand sinks). Don't forget to check out the sunset!

name: Sam Keske
text: Good spot for the home of the Maine Brewers Festival. Prone to mushy grass after rain and boiling heat in the summer sun, but plenty of room to spread out. Wise to get VIP parking.

name: Rich Stevens
text: Great outdoor venue. Just remember to check the rules on the website before arriving. Right on the Fore River.

name: Christopher Kessler
text: Nice outdoor concert venue overlooking the beautiful Fore River.  Beer on tap during concerts.  No opened bottles allowed inside.  My only criticism is that the sound is way too loud. I saw Fleet Foxes there and there was just too much volume and too much reverb. Not sure if the sound crew was in-house or not. I can always hear concerts from my house in South Portland 5 miles away.

name: Keri Thibeau
text: We went to the Paradise 2018 event at Thompson's point. The event host lost internet for a short bit, but we're incredibly great about letting us in rather than hanging out in the entrance. The event was pretty good. The music was good at the beginning. Drinks were a little pricy but expected. The only thing that I thought was silly was the $3 coat checks consider we had paid for tickets and drinks etc...overall it was a good time

name: Ryan Barr
text: This venue is incredible. Beware, shows will go on rain or shine. But if it's a night like we just had, it's pretty magical. Setting sun, nearly a dozen food trucks, beer, wine and plenty of space to roam around. Then the show starts!

name: K Zewski
text: This venue is amazing! My husband and I love it here--- open with no seats...plenty of dancing and great music. We were lucky enough to see Old Dominion in May. They were fabulous and were able to share a very personal show with their Maine fans.

text: Listen. If you're from Portland or from away, this is where you need to be. Winter has an ice rink, all other months has beautiful views. Whether concert, beer festival or just their weekly summer gathering, you should be here.

text: I had never been to a concert at the Point, but was it fabulous.  I love the variety of the food trucks that were there.  The sound system was excellent.  There is not a bad place to sit and listen to the music.

name: Katie Hatch
text: Such a fabulous place to catch a show, sunset or swirl around on the ice rink depending on the season.

name: Kate Savidge
text: I went here for a school project. There was a lot of shops I didn't realize down there. I also saw that there is a cryptology museum, a tap room and a restaurant. I have yet to attend a concert there though.

name: Paul Bennett
text: The Oktoberfest was a blast.  The venue handled the event without a hitch.  There was room for everyone with space to spare.  Having the overhead canopy was nice for when a brief shower passed.

name: Cooper Fauvelle
text: Just saw Guster there. It was awesome!

name: Justin L.
text:
Visited Thompson's Point to attend a food show and to check out Cellar Door Winery.  The venue could not have accommodated more.  With hundreds of people in attendance, parking and comfort facilities were in high demand.  I felt these details were managed very effectively.
As for Cellar Door, the wines could not be more beautiful and well presented.

name: Adam Booker
text: Thompson's Point is a great outdoor venue. It is located on a little peninsula of the Casco Bay. This gives some great views and really adds to the feel of the venue. There is a covered area used typically for beer vendors and most events have food trucks lining the back perimiter of the venue. I have gone to several concerts as well as a few other event types here and love it. I try to find at least one event to go to every year here. It is my favorite outdoor venue in the state of Maine. Definitely make a point of checking it out. You won't be disappointed.

name: Dylan Agosta
text: Street Eats and Beats 2019... the grass could use a little work!  But it was so rainy leading up to the event, so.  Sound is too loud of the stage; it was entertaining but some of the best moments came in between sets when my friends and I could actually have a conversation.

name: Jessica Thomas
text:
Fantastic atmosphere for live music. The site is spacious and welcoming. Great views, kind staff, lots of good food trucks and a nice selection of beers. Plus the lineup gets better each summer!

Another review notes that this venue has figured out how to make Portapotties work well for a big crowd, and it's true. The wait is short if at all, and you can wash your hands with soap and water at the station in the middle. They take alcohol enforcement seriously which heads off a lot of problems. We love going to shows here.

Why I didn't give it 5 stars: Shows are rain or shine, so be prepared. We've been to some real soakers. The food truck lines do get long when bigger crowds come out.  If you don't drink beer, there isn't much else here for you: they have a limited selection of canned wines that are pretty gross. But you can bring your own empty water bottle and get free refills instead of using plastic cups!

Not their fault, but still a problem: short people are hosed if they want to be able to see the band. Maybe because the ground is level rather than pitched? Whatever the issue is, it is more of a problem at this venue than at others in the area. It makes me think twice about whether I'm willing to pay $40-$75 for a show.

name: Raw Vegan Guru
text: Fantastic venue and location in the great city of Portland. The staff was very nice and accommodating each visit. It's a sweet spot

name: Roman Popov
text: There's a gorgeous view of the Fore river and a windy path through the woods that follows the river inland nearby. They also have quite a few benches facing the river. Every Thursday during the Summer, there are food trucks galore.

name: Jeffrey Pope
text: Beware the traffic jams here.Best to Uber in and jump out of the car early on Fore River Parkway. Then walk from there.  It's too slow to drive, walking is faster, and your driver isn't tortured.

name: Rory Benjamin
text: The Summer Sunsets gatherings on Thursdays are fantastic. Lots of fun activities for the little ones, adult beverages for the parents, and fantastic food truck cuisine to fill up with.

name: cwalkenisgod
text:
A great multi-purpose outdoor venue.

Most people know about the summer concert events at Thompson's Point, which are fun, loud, and exciting. However, I recently went there before the holidays to try out some ice skating.

The area was well-lit, with a comfortable warming station for changing shoes or when you get cold in general - complete with cozy chairs and space heaters. There was also a nearby fire for the same purpose. Additionally, there was a yurt which housed a small bar where you can purchase alcoholic beverages.

The price of admission and skate rentals were really not high at all - and during an intermission, the ice was smoothed over with a Zamboni. Music plays at all times over large speakers.

Would highly recommend for a family night out, a date, or a fun gathering with friends.

name: Wayne Cadman
text: They over sold tickets not necessarily to the event but to parts included in the event. Leading to money spent on tickets that never could get used or refunded. They only care about money NOT the patrons giving them money. Wont be returning anytime soon.

name: SHARMAN MAHONEY
text: Beautiful location however I felt very much on lockdown and it was a extreme bummer you could not go in and out of the venue. Ultimate location the sunset was so sweet

name: Nicholas Paulin
text: Sunset by the point--food and drinks were great. The bathroom situation is a nightmare. There was about 1,000 people on the point 8.15.2019 and they had all of the bathrooms padlocked except for two! I asked the attendant at the gate why all the bathrooms are locked and she replied "they dont want to pay the fee to have them cleaned". Consequently people waited in line 20+ minutes to use the bathroom--meanwhile there is 30 more bathrooms that could be used but are locked.

name: Anthony Sullivan
text: The concert was great. Loved all the bands. The food at the venue was acceptable. However, the port-a- potties we're absolutely disgusting. And the hand washing stations ran out of water after the first hour. The facilities are almost a deal breaker for futer events.

text:
Venue gets some great talented musicians. This is my 3rd concert here. I like the venue and look for summer concert options.

Sound quality great. Stage visible from about anywhere you want to stand/sit(beach chair/beach blanket).

Staff friendly and helpful. Police presence nice to see- glad they get to hear great music while they work. Not a bad gig!

Several food trucks available. Everything way overpriced and the few things we had weren't the greatest ( Portland pie pizza 2 slices $10- lukewarm and cardboard crust; Not your mamas meatball place also not hot, asian meatballs with a side of mac and cheese in same small dish( side was for son, but besides that the sauce from each was mixed in middle- so neither of us could eat the middle- and there wasn't much food to start with) Anyway- my fave foodtruck wasnt there (pb&me) so i was already disappointed.

A few beer choices ( allagash, which i like)
But to get not alcohol you need ro go to food trucks which had 30+ minute lines.

Parking good. Security check/ticket check quick, friendly but thorough. Portapotty area decent.

name: Janie H
text: This is a great venue!! It has a huge bar. There are lots of different areas to explore making it fun for kids. It is very scenic. People pull their boats up to it. I don't like the porter potties but at least there are a lot of them.

text: We saw Lake Street Dive at Thompson's Point. Great spot. Food trucks line the back of the venue and you pass the beer garden once you enter the place. You can either stand (up front) or sit (middle to back) but to be clear, you need to bring the chair as there is no arena style seating (rows of seats).

name: QM RK
text: Expect long lines at the food trucks. Other than that it's a great venue when the weather is nice.

text: The venue itself was a lot of fun, but the Thursday night event left much to be desired. One alcohol purchasing station for so many hundreds of people led to some terribly long lines and some of the folks working the food trucks clearly didn't know what they were on for in terms of the capacity they were serving. The event was slow moving, but still lovely, and I'd go back with the hope that some of these logistical elements will be worked at as it goes forward.

text: Beautiful views. Welcoming staff. Very short lines for quality food trucks and beer. Free water refills. Bring your own cooler with food and water bottle. Bring a blanket. Bring a lawn chair. No intrusive searches if you don't have a bag. No bathroom lines and a hand wash station outside the Porta potties. One of the best venues in New England.

text: Amazing venue!!! It was clean and well set up, there is a bar in a very large patio area so if it rains there is a place to stay dry. There were plenty of portable toilets as well as handwashing sinks. At most or all concerts they have food trucks at the back of the venue as well as people selling personalized Nalgene bottles with a free refill station to minimize on plastic water bottle waste. We brought our 6 year old daughter to a Michael Franti concert with us and the whole venue if very kid friendly with plenty of space for them to get away from the crowd if they need to. There is a designated lawn chair/blanket area for people who choose not to stand the whole time, security was tight enough to make you feel safe but not overbearing. Any bags you bring with you will be searched but they pretty much allow you to bring whatever you want besides drugs and alcohol into the venue.

text: First time having Empire since before COVID and the take out was exactly as good as I remembered it even with a 15 minute drive home. Must get the garlic greenbeans. Loved the Kung Pow chicken!

name: Chris Slesarchik
text: Empire is undoubtedly one of the best restaurants in Portland. This is one of the few places I've ever been where every single item on the menu is fantastic! Unique items and delicious Chinese fusion dishes. Expect a long wait with no option to make a reservation, so unless you're going on a weekday in the winter you'll have to tough it out but it is well worth it.

name: Jared Hall
text: Good experience overall. Funky vibe inside and attentive service. Empire's dishes strike a nice balance between authentic and accessible. We enjoyed what we ordered, particularly the pork and shao mai. The eggplant was ok, albeit sweeter/gloopier than yuxiang qiezi as you'd find it in China. Only real complaint was that the rice was oddly undercooked.

name: F. Valle
text:
Best Chinese place ever. Great vegetarian options. The green beans is a must have. I have been here multiple times and every single thing was amazing.
Don’t forget to grab some guava candy on your way out, they are really good.
The place is super cute and extremely popular. So if you plan to go on the weekend during lunch and dinner get ready to wait in line. Or try to get a table at the bar where you can also have food. I always try to do a late lunch and go during weekdays so I do have to wait.

name: Autumn Edwards
text: Food was great. The wonton soup is the best I've ever had. I also recommend the lobster Rangoon, bacon fried rice and spicy pork belly buns. The specialty cocktails left much to be desired.

name: Priscilla Arsenault
text: Our first experience at Empire Chinese Kitchen did not disappoint.  The chocolate hazelnut torte was absolutely amazing.  The spinach dumplings w/carrot, ginger & corn were fresh & soft; the ginger fried rice w/bok choy, corn, broccoli, green bean & minced ginger was delicious & plentiful; the teriyaki chicken w/bok choy & rice was very good & the chocolate(!) fortune cookies were a tasty surprise.

name: Bryan Martins
text: Upscale food with fresh flavors that do noy disappoint. Was my first time at this restaurant and was impressed by the food and the service. All items are delivered to the table as they are completed to ensure they are extremely fresh. This led us to share items and enjoy our experience even more. As a vegetarian there were enough options for me to enjoy, with options clearly marked for easy ordering. I can not wait to go back and try something else as the leftovers I took home were still delicious the next day

name: Andrew Elegante
text:
My favorite dish in Portland. The wide noodles with kale dish is phenomenal. They char the noodles somehow (wok?) and whatever sauce they use is subtle and delicious. I started with the pork belly buns but the sauce was too strong and I couldn't really taste the pork.

The dragon milk drink was a treat. Plenty buzz inducing alcohol wise and very flavorful.

Staff is professional and attentive but also fun. I witnessed one staff member "abducting" another.

name: Jason Blanco
text: Always amazing !!! Recommend go early there is usually a wait.. but I have never had bad service.. The food is always delicious!!

text: Fantastic food, such great flavors! Love their Dragons Milk cocktail.

text: This is without a doubt the best Chinese Food I have ever had. We got the Soup Dumplings and Lobster Rangoons. They were amazing! We loved it so much we went back a few days later and tried the Pork Buns and Teriyaki Chicken. We loved everything we got, but the Soup Dumplings were the best. We had excellent service during both of our visits. It is a little pricey, but definitely worth the money!

name: Simon Snyder
text: Sat at the bar which is staffed with nice folks. I ate the pork belly appetizer and then had Mongolian beef. Both dishes were very good. The bar staff was cool and they quite nicely fielded my cornball humor. The Owner was present and was jumping in to help get arrivals seated. Saturday evening was almost too crowded for my tastes but they do a nice job with diner management.

name: Henry Haynes
text: Best Chinese food I have ever had

name: Benjamin Lampert
text: Excellent spot for a cozy meal. We split a number of dumplings, appetizers, and buns to make a full meal for two. The food came out in a jumbled order and chaotic, which was fun if you're sharing all of the plates(which you should be doing). All of the food was amazing and there were a number of suprises along the way. The green beans reminded us of summer in the middle of winter and were one of the best things on the menu. The other great surprise was the orange beef. Typically orange beef tends to be overly sweet but this had enough heat to counteract and make it one of the best dishes we had all night. I cant underline how good every dish was though. I can't wait to come back!

text: Honestly the food at Empire is top 5 in Portland, Maine. The green beans are the best i’ve ever had! You MUST check this restaurant out if you like good food, plan in advance though there is normally a wait but it’s worth it!
