name: shaun harrigan
text: I always get the green beans, they are amazing. Everything I've tried has been delicious. I get the Cucumber Smash (or is it Crush?) with gin instead of vodka. Possibly the best mixed drink I've ever had.

name: Alan Fried
text: Best Chinese food in Portland. Hands down.

name: Erica Mulgoon
text: I finally made it to this hot spot, the food is great. The pork buns are delightful, and the garlic green beans were very flavorful. I found that the main dishes all have the same flavor. Plan on spending $$$ to get full.Im glad I tried it, but once is good enough for me.

name: ben mullen
text: Small plates, nice staff, the best chinese cuisine I have had the pleasure of eating.

name: Recon Byfire
text: Always excellent food.  And they carry old Rasputin's

name: Nicole Pare
text: Food was fantastic! We had lobster rangoons, pork potstickers and bacon fried rice. Every bite was delicious, and our service was amazing as well!

name: Zachary Hart
text: Excellent dining experience. Cocktails are great! Good area by the bar when waiting for seats. Really good vegan options.

name: Oliver Bedard jr
text: It's take out only

name: Jeffrey Savarino
text: Very allergen friendly. Service was great and food was too notch. Would go there again in a heart beat, but just make sure you go their early. We arrived at 6 pm and there was a 1.5 hour wait for a table for two. We ended getting seats at the bar about 45 minutes into our wait.

name: Matt Pack
text: Service is great.  Live the group style eating where everyone is open to share there food.  It's a one of a kind experience. I hope to go back next time I'm in Portland!

name: Mac Coldwell
text: I've played here and watched shows here, and it's a great venue. The sound is always well done, and the staff is ready to help. Tickets are usually reasonable. They do a lot to support local music and comedy. Good beer and drink selection. And the restaurant below has incredible dim sum. It's general admission, but you can see the stage pretty well from any spot, and there is some seating.

name: Rob Moore
text: Superlative. Well thought out. A touch too busy, a few items were in the cold side from understaffing and lag from window to table - but overall we died with every bite. Make a reservation, and get the buns. Great for gluten-free.

name: Christian Melson
text: Everything on the menu is fresh tasting and delicious. We got the mongolian beef, honey walnut shrimp and the BBQ pork buns. The place is mostly small plates so you can try a number of items.

name: thoughfully lost
text: Absolute gem in Portland and some of the best Chinese food ive ever had, duck buns crazy good.

name: Mark Hodges
text: Best meal I've had in a year. not including my wife's cooking. Great vegetarian options

name: Julie's bites
text:
Winter 2019: Empire does not take reservations. We came at 4:30 pm and were sitted at 6:00pm. People who came at 6 pm were turned away, as there wait time extended past closing.
Peking duck buns are still my favorite dish.

Winter 2018: Empire does not take reservations for small parties, and there is always a long wait.  We came at 4:30 pm and were seated a little after 5:30 pm.   Food and service were good.  We ordered 4 dumpling,2 small plates, and 1 large plate.  So many things sounded good, but that was too much food and we took a lot home.
Summer 2018:Empire serves dim sum all day long.  We arrived here around 2:20pm and despite the fairly late time for lunch this place was packed.  We were sitted fairly quickly. I liked the dim sum here better then in Boston's Chinatown which I do fairly often. The food is made to ordered, delivered to the table steaming hot and delicious.  The Peking duck steam bun is to die for.  It is just the right amount of duck and bun (it is not a typical large bun).

name: Marybeth Chipman
text: SO delicious and great prices!!! It's hard to find a place in Portland that has amazing food, good portion sizes, a nice atmosphere AND isn't over priced. Empire has it all! I highly recommend.

name: Philip True
text: Fantastic food and happy wait staff. The bacon fried rice was perfect and the pork dumplings with soup was amazing. You will not be disappointed

name: Dion Brown
text:
I feel horrible writing a bad review to a place I really enjoy but today the service I received was absolutely disgusting.
Apparently if you go in alone you're not allowed to choose a booth to sit in without being treated like absolute trash. I didn't know there was a policy in place like that.
I made a small request to sit in a booth as the place was almost empty but the hostess didn't like that. To the point of making me feel uncomfortable I had to leave.
Food is great, I recommended takeout so you don't have to deal with staff like that.

5 stars for food. Which sadly I didn't get today.

name: Paul Haskell
text:
So, we decided after several years of hearing how good Empire is to check it out. We thought a late lunch on a Saturday would be an easy time to walk in and get a table. The hour wait at 3PM on a Saturday, while unexpected, led me to guess what was to come would be worth the wait.

I was not incorrect.
4 of us ordered a multitude of small plates and a larger order of Bacon Fried Rice and Kung Pao Chicken so we all had a bit of everything. The Bacon Fried Rice was just as amazing as you're thinking it sounds! Their Spicy Pork Belly Steam Buns were a delicious introduction to the Steam Bun... I may have asked for a second order 🤫
Would most definitely recommend. Don't let the wait deter you, they will take your number and send you a text link that will let you know when your table will be ready. That way you can wander around some area shops or grab a coffee at a nearby cafe while you wait.

name: Nikola Belskis
text: Overall it gets an 8/10. When we arrived at 1:30 on Saturday we were told there was a 40-50 min  wait. We walked around while we waited. We Ordered the Lobster Rangoon, Korean pork, pork pot stickers, and Szechuan Ramen bowl. The food delicious and reasonably priced. Service was mediocre, with minimally friendly servers who were less than attentive. The atmosphere is a mixture of high end/ cheap old small town Asian restaurant. The building was clean and well lit. I will be back.

name: Alexander Blackstone
text:
Amazing food, seriously go here!

They bring plates out as they're ready which is fun and better then letting half the food get cold waiting.  This seemed to bring about confusion as two plates we didn't order were dropped off and the server was on their way before we could tell them it wasn't our food.

name: Jenna W.
text: Love this place! I've gone here a handful of times and each time my experience is great. The staff is friendly and attentive. The food is always spectacular.

name: Casey Smith
text: You will not find better customer service in all of Portland then you will here. I am not a big Chinese food fan but the food here is always well done. The atmosphere and accommodations are and have always been top notch. It is a bit pricier than other places but it is well worth the money.

name: Michael A. Wicker
text: Delicious food and great atmosphere with friendly attentive service.

name: Ben Handler
text: Excellent inspired Chinese food with a unique twist. The hand-crafted drinks are delicious. The Garlic Green Beans are a fan-favorite and one of many phenomenal dishes to split with two or a group.

name: Christine D'Angelo
text: Delicious spicy food, very different. Reasonably priced served by competent,pleasant wait staff. Will definitely be returning

name: William Evans
text: Great Veggie food!!

name: Olivia Hamlin
text: Great food, definitely can be crowded. It’s a healthier Chinese food option. A local favorite!

name: Kate Wagner
text: Travis was great!  The tempura shrimp was amazing. I will definitely be back.

name: FelineFumbles
text: I wish it was bigger. They are such a small business but have the BEST food!! I love this place

name: Gary Mayhew
text: Incredible food! Very good staff. Will return and try new dishes!

name: Matt Naylor
text: I wanted to order everything on the menu. Everything I ordered was delicious. This place was packed for a good reason. Our waiter was very good too.

name: Laura Cabot
text: Loved the gin fueled "Dragon Milk" and were comfortably seated for apps until a table became available. The biggest dilemma is what to order. All the dumplings are top notch

name: Jane Croston
text: O my. I'd been told of a few certain dishes that were not to be missed. We didn't miss much. I dislike 🦀 Rangoon - find it messy and often tasteless. Lobster Rangoon at Empire is a whole different world. Delicate and delicious, this must be how Rangoon is meant to be. O my. The shrimp with honey and walnut was superb, and I could have just enjoyed that and been quite happy. The steamed dumplings were very good though the BBQ beef had a bit too much dough for me. Everyone liked the green beans and garlic. We tried about 8 items and I can't wait to go back for more! Our server was the delightful and spicy addition to a great adventure of a meal. She was knowledgeable, helpful and charmed us all. I would add an extra 🌟 if I could. My only complaint might be that there is often a long wait for a table, so be prepared. I probably wouldn't even try or a weekend eve.

name: In Human Creation Media
text: Love the aesthetic, food, drinks, and shows that go on at this venue!

name: Dani McCarr
text: Everything was fabulous.  We did a share of 4 items- Sauteed eggplant (amazing) , spinach dumplings (melt in your mouth), ginger fried rice (very tasty) and vegetable fried spring rolls with dipping sauce. We loved everything we ate and left satisfied.  Expect a bit of a wait but it was worth it. Next time I go I am getting the flamingo drink, I saw it made multiple times and it looked so tasty! Service was pretty good considering how busy they were albeit we ate at bar to get that food faster! ;)

name: alexandra hughes
text: It's not what you expect in a relativley subtle way. Dishes here are different then they are anywhere else. Unexpected often. Bacon fried Rice is very popular. The green beans however are to die for and I'm addicted to them. A favorite restaurant of mine.

name: Jennifer Day
text: Always a great experience. Dishes are consistently prepared with quality ingredients and flavors that are not over complicated. I recommend an order of every type of buns, garlic green beans & kale noodles for the table to share. If you still have room, duck lo mein lobster fried rice for the win.

name: Peter Gore
text: Maybe the best Chinese food in the city. But be prepared to wait for a seat. Plus a small bar. But if you've got the investment of time you will be well rewarded.

name: John Guarnaccia
text: Very popular locally, very tasty food. The Singapore rice noodles are really good.

name: Evan Linger
text: Always busy because it’s always good. If you want a table for dinner make reservations. If you don’t mind sitting at the bar you’re in for a great meal and great cocktails. They have a few vegan options which are all amazing and a few more of the dishes can be made vegan upon request. I’ve been here close to twenty times and it’s always a perfect experience.

name: Fredrick Drake
text: By far the best Chinese food in Portland. There is a variety of items to suit any taste. Seating is comfortable with a separate bar area. Wait staff is courteous and attentive. My wife has had a few of their cocktails and always enjoyed them. I wouldn't hesitate to bring anyone here.

name: Mike Anderson
text: Amazing food and delightful service. Mongolian beef dish and Book Choy app. were amazing. Seated 10 of us with a hour or so notice to fit it in very gracefully

name: Joseph Gaudet
text: Small plates and big waits! Definitely worth putting your name in early and letting them text you when your table is ready. Plenty of places nearby to grab a cocktail while you dream of savory Chinese cuisine. Their vegan options are delightful, and good to share with everyone.

name: Scott Payson
text: Not the only dim sum in town, just the best. Our party of five ordered and shared 12-15 different dishes. The bacon fried rice is amazing, but other favorites were Shanghai soup dumplings, pork dumplings, walnut shrimp, pork belly buns, Kung pao chicken, beef and broad noodles, kale and noodles, and pork pot stickers. Great food, super reasonably priced and a full bar (it was lunch so we didn't partake but the house-made lemonade was excellent).

name: Jonathan Damon
text: Great food that comes out fast as it's ready. Amazing green beans and soup dumplings. Will return again!

name: Roxy LaFrance
text: Nice event space. Small venue, standing room only, everyone has a good view, full bar. Not handicapped accessible. They allow you to go outside and re-enter during events.

name: Amelie
text: Typical fare. A bit pricey.

name: sam tarbox
text:
Good food and service.  I was also impressed that they Urban Farm Fermentory, Blueberry Cider (ah) on tap.

Recommend calling ahead to reserve a table.

name: Jonathan Brockway
text: Best Chinese restaurant in Portland! Love sharing plates with my wife.

name: Jon Garrish
text: Fantastic food and excellent service! Definitely earned their popular reputation in town for excellent.

name: Patriot Lady
text: The food is fantastic! You don't feel weighted down with greasy fried food. Fresh and delicious   Always busy, crazy busy

name: Amy Jane Larkin
text: Everything here is delicious and the vibe is great.  I've had so many good experiences with one friend or many. The soup dumplings, chive and shitake, shu mai, and kale and noodles are all favorites, but I doubt you can go wrong.

name: Logan Martyn-Fisher
text: I eat here as often as I can. It's the only Chinese food I ever eat. 5 stars every time.

name: Kara Watson
text: Tasted okay but not any better than frozen Chinese food. We accidentally left the take home container on the table and have no regrets about leaving it there.

name: Sharon Lee
text: We stopped here by chance. It is not your usual Chinese restaurant.  It's small, and when my husband and I were there, crowded, though we were late for lunch and early for dinner.  We chose things to split off of the menu -- steamed pork rolls, steamed dumplings, garlic green beans, house-made broad noodles.  Everything was terrific, our server was patient and good-natured.  If we lived in Portland, I can see it becoming one of my go-to places.

name: John Osterman
text: Empire is definitely one of the best restaurants in Portland. Asian fusion. All meals come out as they are finished, so you get a steady stream of smaller things to eat while you are there. The flavors are incredible! Empire Egg Roll has salami, a definite must, along with the green beans. Staff is always fun, and it is a welcoming, child friendly atmosphere. Do not miss this place on a trip to Portland!

name: Justin Foster
text: Only 5 starts because 6 is not available. Amazing take on great classic and modern dishes. Go hungry, expect to share plates and try everything

name: Denton Weimer
text: Great tasting food for all diet types

name: Chad Butts
text:
Excellent place to share small plates. Lots of great menu items to try - duck lo mein, lobster rangoons, garlic green beans...  Very good local beer selection.

Best to arrive at opening because they don't take reservations.

name: John B.
text: Simply suberb Chinese food. Some of the best I've ever had

name: Corey Laplante
text: Arguably one of Portlands best places for lunch! We eat here on the regular! The food is very fresh, creative and locally sourced! we love everything about this place, the wait is well worth it!

name: Trevor Geiger
text:
Love this place so much! Their arrival in Portland nearly 6 years ago set a new (high) bar for Chinese food in Maine and left everyone else scrambling to catch up.

Fresh & local ingredients. Great recipes. I recommend the Garlic Green Beans and Har Gow dumplings :)

name: Myles Hebert
text:
This place is quite good. Premium Chinese food with a fitting price point. The best time to go is around 4pm just before the dinner rush (and oh boy is it ever a rush). If you go at a more normal time you may be waiting for quite some time.
Their bao dumplings are extremely tasty, the best I've had in Portland. The teriyaki chicken I got was a bit too sweet for me, but still very good.

name: Amy Briggs
text: Great food, super- cool staff!

name: Shawn Wu
text: This was a great restaurant. The food was great and the service was great. They never made the food too sweet or too salty. The dumplings were cooked just right.

name: Mike C
text: Absolutely delicious! Everything was exceptional! I’m not even going to drone on about it because it was just awesome. You will not be disappointed!!!!

name: Michael S
text:
Really great place to hang out and have a specialty cocktail or beer. This place is not small but it's pretty popular, is always busy and fills up fast.

The service is outstanding and the food is really good. I love their walnut shrimp app and their lobster dumplings!

name: Jessica Duffy
text: Food is amazing and comes out as it is ready.  Great experience for friends or business associates.

name: Troy Daly
text: Empire is an awesome Chinese restaurant It has a cool, casual atmosphere and excellent food and cocktails. Sophie was a great bartender.  I definitely recommend Empire!

name: Hannah Smart
text: Great service and AMAZING food. 5 stars and beyond.

name: Sonny howell
text: Great food and inventive cocktails. Service is always quick and attentive.   Looking forward to coming back soon.

name: Rachel Colton
text: Love this place! So unique, fun, and delicious! Highly recommend!

name: Megan Hiltz
text: One of my favorite stops in Portland. Great food excellent drinks!

name: Jeff Hawkins
text: Have made several visits now and have never been disappointed. The pork buns are awesome and most of the dishes are great to share when out with others. There is often a wait, but the host will be happy to call your mobile when your table is ready so you can go for a walk or a drink elsewhere while waiting.

name: Rob O'Brian
text: Excellent food in a small plate format.  Something for everyone.

name: Amanda Harriman
text: Took my son for his birthday. Smaller venue, but I appreciated the more intimate atmosphere.

name: Joseph Floridino
text: Amazing food, great drinks, and great atmosphere. Would eat here everyday if I could.

name: Dina Khmelnitsky
text: Just had dinner there. This place has the best dumplings I’ve ever had. We had the BBQ roast pork bao, the soup dumplings and the beef and noodles. All three were fantastic. The service was wonderful as well. 100% recommend Empire.

name: Jeremiah
text: Delicious food, great menu. Empire is always busy. The wait is worth it, but plan on stopping in to put your name on the list, then get a cocktail elsewhere while you wait. There are no reservations, and the bar is first come first served.

name: Addie Davis
text: Food is really spectacular. I would list the things you should try but really you can't go wrong with anything on the menu. Although the garlic green beans are a go not miss. They also have some really fun cocktails that are always enjoyable.  Often there is a wait right at lunch time and on weekends so plan accordingly, but it will be worth it.

name: Elvis C
text: I'm from Maine born and brought up and this was my first time. We had a bit of a wait which is expected for a Saturday night at 5 in the Old Port. But they take your name and will text you several minutes before your table is ready. So we went to have a drink at Dogfish Cafe and sat on the nearly roof top patio which is a great spot! Went back to empire and had an amazing meal. I got the Teriyaki Chicken and my friend got the Kung Pao Chicken and we shared the Spring Rolls and the Steamed Pork Dumplings to start off with. The service was great and everyone was polite and friendly! The whole experience was outstanding!!

name: Elizabeth Waters
text: Try the kale & house made noodles. The lobster rangoon will change your life. Busy spot but worth a 30 minute wait.

name: Jane Doe
text: Fast and friendly service. Very busy for lunch. Food was wonderful. No complaints. Wish it was a little bigger on the inside. But I will always recommend people to this little gem.

name: Benjamin Murphy
text: Green beans and dumplings. Good stuff.

name: Sam Jones
text: We got a ton of different dishes to share between 3 people and it was perfect! Service was great, drinks were great! Somewhat pricey, but not too bad.

name: Sara Lauter
text: Absolutely delicious! Small plates to share or hoard for yourself! Love the soup dumplings and cucumber salad but I've never had something I didn't like. Cocktails are good too!

name: Daniel Zajic
text: Holy cow, this place is amazing. Some of the best Chinese food I've ever had. Everything was perfect. I'll be coming here again and again.

name: Brent Griffith
text: Really good food small dining room

name: Justin Knowles
text: Busy.. but worth it. Portland is bustling , it's to be expected. But that Salt Cod rice... Dang. Ask for the chili paste.

name: Graylin Showell
text: Really well composed menu. I love how the safety foods (like bacon fried rice) aren't just boring features that don't belong. The menu for those looking for more exciting items are loaded with pops and layers of flavor. Long waits on busy nights if you don't reserve a table, but well worth it.

name: Jacob Krueger
text: My favorite spot for Cantonese food hands down. Truly one of my favorite spots in Portland, having patronized it many many times since it first opened. Service there has always been stellar, the cocktails some of my favorite in town, and the food--if I was cursed to only eat Empire food for the rest of my life I would probably die happier than if I hadn't been cursed at all. Go there. Eat there. Enjoy the chocolate fortune cookies.

name: Stephanie Harmon
text: Sunday evening was a great time to go and not have to wait. The garlic green beans were amazing and so were the spinach dumplings.  Kale noodles is always a delicious entree!

name: Marc Beaulieu
text: Great food, lots of GF options!

name: Chuck Staples
text: Nice folks.  Cozy is an appropriate description, though the place isn't overly small or tight.  Food is excellent and prices are reasonable for the area.

name: Candace Poirier
text: Great service! Awesome bao. So fun.

name: barry gilliland
text: Excellent food and the staff are fantastic . Try the honey walnut shrimp!

name: Ryan Barr
text: This place is amazing! Chances are good you'll have to wait quite a while to get a table, but it's well worth the wait. Highly recommend the wonton soup, and braised beef ramen bowl.

name: Tati C
text:
It will be insanely busy whenever you go, but go you must! What sets Empire apart from most other Chinese food experiences is the quality of ingredients and a lightness in preparation that avoids the common pitfalls of less mindful Chinese cuisine-- overly sweet, salty, MSG-y sauces and flavors. Here you will find nothing of the sort! Every sauce, every flavor is just the perfect balance.

Things you MUST try:
•Char Soul Bao
•Chinese Eggplant
•Hot and Sour Soup
•Garlic Green beans
•Beef and Broad Noodle
•Lobster Dumplings
•Orange Beef

Grab one of their fun cocktails, order 5 or 6 plates, and get ready to share an incredible meal with a friend in the best Chinese spot in Maine!

name: Edgar Foudray
text: Delicious cocktails, amazing flavors, lovely servers, authentic atmosphere

name: Joseph Collura
text: Had a great meal here - they handle gluten free very well, homemade noodles were great as were the dumplings.  Very satisfied.

name: Samuel Eddy
text: Superb food.  Be daring with your order and you'll get a taste explosion. Fast & friendly service. But very noisy.

name: Bill Taylor
text: Fun place to try different things

name: Ian Cravatt
text: High End Chinese food that's well worth the price. I mean bacon fried rice. Need I say more.

name: L B
text: Delicious food. Worth the wait. We ordered a bunch of different items to share and liked all of them. The lobster Rangoon were my favorite.

name: Piner
text: Flavor, flavor, and flavor... place your trust in the order and let the server time your meal. Any choice off of their creative menu will not be a disappointment... they thrive in flair and back that up with delicious non traditional tastes that will leave your test buds relieved and satisfied... delicious  dishes abound at Empire...

name: Allen Small
text: Some of the  best Chinese around. Boneless ribs and Mai Thais are fantastic.

name: Elizabeth Kordek
text:
Great food, and they are very helpful with unusual allergies
Many vegetarian, vegan, and gluten free options, and the best wonton soup I have ever had, and the pastrami rolls are a treat you won't find anywhere else

name: B
text: Yes, worth the hype plus a really fun place (& late night food option)

name: Victor Robinson
text: Food is fantastic. Family style so be ready to share.  Very hip and trendy.  Usually busy.

name: Louisa Nunan
text: Waitress was very attentive and helpful.  Food was delicious. A happy experience!

name: Aubrey Grant
text: Menu items were unique and delicious. Our server was friendly and knowledgeable about the food. I would recommend and will be back to eat there again soon.

name: Buy Local
text: Only eaten here once, good for vegetarians, very clean flavors. Addendum-now eaten here multiple times but never enough, soo good. Have you ever had green beans? No you haven’t, until you’ve had the here.

name: Davian Akers
text: High energy place with really great food.  The service is great too

name: Sarah Bailey
text: We ate at the bar. The bartender recommended food and she was spot on. The food is wonderful! The atmosphere was relaxing and the beer tasted good as well!!

name: Thomas LaNigra
text: Food is fantastic!  Ginger rice is amazing.  Favorite Chinese food place.

name: Heidi Machson
text: The food was delious and the portions were very big!

name: Ryan Gay
text: BBQ pork, pork belly bao, and duck lo mein are to die for.

name: John Kreutzberger
text: Small plates, dim sum and some large plates. I rarely order an entree sized portion because all of the smaller portion items are so good. Only down side to this place is that it is always packed, so be prepared to wait for a table.

name: bonnie clariot
text: Really good food usually, although I got the Duck lo mein and there were not slices of duck, I got mostly duck skin which was really dissapointing😕

name: Travis Agaman
text: One of the absolute best places to eat in Portland. And that means a lot in a city with many amazing restaurants. I've eaten at Empire over a dozen times and never had a bad experience. JUST GO EAT THERE NOW.

name: Andrew Mass
text: love that place.  fun.  great food

name: Cody
text: It's more than the just the amazing food here. The staff is wonderful and it has a rich atmosphere with high spirited staff. There is also a history there that I was un-aware of, I had no idea Empire had been around since 1916, that blew my mind.

name: Anthony Lawless
text: Great atmosphere, good is excellent, prices are more than fair. Make a reservation or go early and sit at the bar

name: Lauren Manera
text: Fancy casual. Sort of neighborhood but not. Small but dedicated bar scene. Food and drinks good to very good.

name: Libin Louis
text: Good food and neat place

name: Bob Leger
text: The food was good but not great.  The service was below average.  Overall, the experience did not live up to the hype.

name: Dee P.
text: The service was not good. We kept having to ask our server for more water instead of the glasses being automatically filled.  We had to interrupt a conversation between our server and another to request a second round of drinks.  Once our food arrived she never came to check on us and my date had to ask another server for silverware because I'm not that good with chopsticks.  On the other hand, the food was great but I don't think that can offset the poor service.  Personally,,  I  won't be going back.

name: Christopher Pelonzi
text:
Best food ever. Be sure to get garlic green beans and bacon fried rice!
Also, dishes are for the table... bring friends and share!

name: K T
text: We got the potstickers there as we were heading elsewhere and just wanted a quick bite. My mushroom ones where a little odd w corn in them but they were interesting. My companion got the pork and I felt they were missing something as it was just pork in wonton. The drinks looked awesome.

name: Angela Feroze
text: GREAT food AWFUL AWFUL AWFUL SERVICE. Bartender is just horrible. I ordered edamame  buns she ordered the incorrect ones with PORK. I’m MUSLIM I DONT EAT PORK. She argued. My apps, meal, meal to go was not coordinated well. My meal to go cans before my actual meal. Bartender was more interested in the hippie dude with a man bun next to me vs actually being a bartender. What a shame!!!

name: Mitchell Stein
text: Some of the best Chinese food in Portland. The Peking Duck bun is a standout but there really isn't a bad dish on the menu. For an adult beverage, try the Oolong Martini

name: Paul Cote
text: Always fantastic food and great service

name: Christa Wesley
text:
Empire Chinese Kitchen is amazing.

I could end the review right now with those five words. Do I need to say anything else? I will some day eat all of the things on menu (except for those with seafood) and consider that to be a life accomplishment. I've been here three times and each time has been wonderful. The staff are super friendly and helpful and don't seem to judge when I order one entire column from the menu.

I've tried the pork buns, the brioche buns, the garlic green beans, the lamb curry buns, the spring rolls, the soup dumplings, and the peking duck buns. I'm sure there are others but I can't remember. I would recommend that if you visit Empire, go for the small plates that you can share. The larger plates and the rice/noodle options are good but they excel at the smaller stuff and it's more fun to eat.

Keep in mind that they don't take reservations for parties of less than 4 so if you go, there may be a wait. On my last visit, we snagged two seats at the bar where they do full service. It's not huge inside and they've packed in a lot of tables but it's always busy. I've never been there where almost every table wasn't filled. That's a good sign for a high quality restaurant.

name: Rachel P.
text:
Green beans... that's all you need to know

Additional comments: Subsequent visits have proven the green beans to be a sustainable staple of this fine dining establishment. Studies have proven consistent deliciousness across all seasons and days of the week. In conclusion, they the green beans.

name: Jeff Sherman
text: The bartender on Thursday night went out of her way to get my girlfriend a tea because she noticed that she didn't have a voice. That was really nice. Thank you.

name: Matt Glennie
text: Excellent food and friendly knowledgeable staff, great atmosphere.

name: Kyle Martin
text: Love this place. They have amazing dumplings and they have pretty interesting soup dumplings to try. The drinks are quite extensive and unique, and the staff is kind and personable.

name: Susan Roth
text:
Read a recent review and felt I had to try it given that I've been searching for dim sum since moving to Maine last year. Place was packed on a Sunday night, so be sure to make reservations ahead of time. Dim Sum was very good--hargow, pot stickers, shu mai. Bacon fried rice is worth trying as are several of the main dishes--Mongolian beef and jalapeño shrimp are two. We were all a little disappointed by the teriyaki chicken. But no matter, it got eaten. Our waitress Katie was on it and provided great service.

text:
The dim sum is at San Fransisco levels,  it's as good as Yank Sing which was my favorite dim sum restaurant in SF. Its much better than any dim sum in Boston or Lowell. The selection is more limited than other dim sum restaurants but everything they offer is terrific. Our favorite was the Peking duck buns, its the best Peking duck that I've ever had. The surprise was the shumai. I normally think of shumai as the least interesting dumpling, but the flavor of their shumai was terrific. The disappointment was the lobster dumpling, I expected it to be the best of all the dishes but it was our least favorite although it's good, just not blow away good like the Peking Duck buns.

The orange beef is delicious but it's very spicy, too spicy for me.

The soup dumplings are excellent, so are the hargow. Didn't love the lobster noodles, the Walnut shrimp are good but if you need to cut down on the number of dishes this is one I'd leave off.

Important recommendation, always order the small portion, there are so many dishes to order.so you don't want to overstuff yourself.

Some areas seem to have no toppings and what was there was pretty bland or not fresh tasting. Crust should be a bit chewy but not nearly as chewy is this was. Hurt my jaw eating just once slice. There are so many pizza places around I'd say search around and find one you like and stick with it. Otto's is okay but not great.

name: Nicole Rowe
text: Stopped in for some pizza late Saturday night after a show at the Waterfront. We wanted to get out of downtown for something to munch on that wouldn't be overrun with people. Since they were open until Midnight, and it was only 11:15 we went in to sit. We felt kind of bad because they had all of the dining room ready to close up, chairs stacked in tables etc., but they assured us we'd be ok to sit down and relax. They were very nice, laughed and joked with us and had amazing wall oven baked pizza. Crispy crust and fresh ingredients. Definitely a place you need to check out!

text: This is a great spot to sit and enjoy some great coffee and baked goods. The staff are really great. The chai is a pretty sweet in case that's not your thing. I had a great bagel here.

text: When walking into this location I was impressed by the building and atmosphere and couldn't wait to try what they had to offer. Unfortunately after receiving the wrong order the barista seemed off at the fact that I wanted the drink I originally ordered. When I finally got to try my drink I couldn't get over the fact that it was more syrup than coffee. I definitely expected a more professional cup and not the sugar filled cardboard to-go cup that I received. Sadly I will not be returning to this cafe.

text: Nice place for coffee.  Staff is very friendly. Nice atmosphere.  Great place to sit and have a cup of Joe.  The coffee they serve is from Carpi Diem roasted just for them. See my separate review for them.  But the gist - some of the best coffee available.  Definitely worth a visit.  Scones and muffins are good and fresh.

name: Chris Douglas
text: Very popular spot at Oak Hill across from the town hall offices.Very easy to find, access, and exit. It is handicapped accessible. Lots of comfortable seating such as lounge chairs and coaches along with standard tables and bar. Full coffee, espresso, latte, & tea menu. Lots of bakery goods. Great service.

If you aren't in the mood for coffee or tea, they also have beer and wine. The beer is craft brew style. They have a good selection of books at a great price too.

text: Coffee is alright, food is locally baked bagels with various toppings and other baked goods and pastries. Great selection of books everything is organized. A lot of interesting things to choose from. Very cozy as well.

name: Shaun Donnelly
text: Wonderfully cozy spot with a super friendly staff. Great place to get some work done during the day, and be sure to check out the live music they have!

name: Jesse Carlson
text: Very cozy and quaint. This is the go-to spot for coffee. The service is a little slower than at some other coffee shops, but the lack of a line helps it balance out. Lots of good seating options, but Elements is usually pretty full. It's worth checking out if you're in the area.

name: Breanna Kernick
text: Elements is the place where you order a new drink and pastry to go, but end up sitting there for a while with an obscure title. Definitely worth the adventure when you wake up 5 chapters later and order another drink!!

name: William Armstrong
text: Nice place to hang out, surfin with their wi-fi, reading a book, or just chillin'out. Oh yeah...they have coffee also.

name: Cinderlu Bowley
text: Highly recommend this for anybody who loves books and coffee. Great selection of artisan coffees teas and even some little snack bites. Any kind of book you can imagine is for sale in this store. They also have some very interesting cookbooks and aprons some handcrafted jellies & Spice concoctions. If you're looking for a simple syrup this is a place to go. My best recommendation is if you've got some time to sit and relax enjoy a great cup of coffee and a good read there's no place better than Elements. Meet a friend there and enjoy a little catching up time. There's also convenient parking right next door in the parking lot period and elements does validate. That's really nice for downtown shopping.

name: Paul Garrido
text: Great place to relax and do school work or personal work. Prices are very reasonable and location is great. The Establishment is very clean in the staff are always cheerful and enlightening.

name: Megan Brown
text: Great atmosphere, friendly staff, large beer selection! Definitely a positive experience overall

name: Zachary Goater
text: Unique little coffee shop in the burgeoning downtown Biddeford offers craft beer, delightful coffee, and noshy little grab and go snacks. If you have the time I'd recommend grazing their books. You'll definitely enjoy this spot.

name: Chip Moreno
text: Best pour over coffee and best espresso, easy parking and great vibes

name: Drew Farrar
text: Fantastic spot for a chill evening.  Good drink selection.  Friendly staff.  Easy listening live music.  Open late.  They bring a good light to Biddeford.

name: Jeffrey Quinn
text: Browsing the bookstore was pleasant - they're careful about what they stock (more literary, less best-sellers list) so it's not the random pile of books you get at most used book stores (for better and worse). The beer selection is top notch, and our coffees were terrific.

name: Alex Bakman
text: Old world charm. Peace and salvation. Comfortable and cozy.  Fantastic coffee   Good selection of beers. If you area in Biddeford or heading to Portland, a must see

name: Heather Anne Wright
text: Good pour-over, espresso and craft beers in a cozy, community atmosphere. Elements has managed to make the bookshop cafe model work on Main St. in Biddeford. They are supportive of arts, good food and community. Great local flavor.

name: Jaslyn Prieto
text: Love it here. Great ambiance, prices, food and of course coffee. Wonderful place to sit, read, relax or catch up with a friend. The people who work here are kind and offer great customer service.

name: Bill Dodson
text: Expert help and good coffee in an environment designed to give coffee nerds exactly what they want. Elements, I wish you were in Portland. But you would literally have to fight 2 or 3 of the recent upstarts. To the death.

name: Paul Bellefeuille
text: Absolutely fantastic! Coffee, food and service. Perfection. Great books priced right too!

name: Your Wizard
text: If you love coffee (or beer) and books, this place.is a slice of heaven. Great spot for a date, to get some work done on the laptop, to peruse books, or just to chill.

name: Sara Donlon
text: Very neat spot. Calm environment conducive to getting your work done without much distraction yet you can look around in any direction and find something that will catch your eye and interest.  Coffees were Perfect, snacks tapas were rich, flavorful and just enough.  I will be coming back for the evening experience of draft beer and wines.

text: Loved all the books, lovely bagels and coffee, done correctly!

name: Gabriel Perez
text: Elements, what a creative and excellent vision crafted out of the simplest of ideas. Take your local coffeeshop with the quiet romanticism of the bookstores of yore, serve alcohol in the evenings with live music a-playing in the background and you have the basic elements of Elements. But, like any chemical reaction, it takes the appropriate accoutrements and atmosphere to truly make Elements what it is. When you order one of their craft coffees or teas, you're greeted with the delight of a price less than your generic swill from Starbucks. And I cannot stress enough the glory of the atmosphere. I remember when I was young and lost in the world, not knowing how to fill my time, but not wanting to go home, I would visit the Border's or the Barnes and Noble. We all know where those havens of solace went. Thanks internet based economy. Thankfully, there is one bastion of art left in this crazy, mixed up world, and that is Elements.

text:
A great place for coffee, beer, or books.

Elements has been one of the locations to pop up in Biddeford over the last decade or so to really help transform the area. It provides excellent coffee beverages, a place to use wifi and/or study during the day, and at night it's a local watering hole that is classy and delivers live music and helps support local artists. On top of all that, it's also a functioning book store.

The owner, Michael, frequently can be seen working the counter, and he's a super-nice guy.

Overall, I would highly recommend this location for all of the above reasons if you're looking for someplace to duck into while you're visiting Biddeford.

Dinner choices were limited because of the holiday and priced a little high for what was offered but still ok. Would of ordered the porterhouse steak but $39.99 is a bit over priced so cant say if it is a great steak, the prime rib was a 10 oz for $21.99 again a bit over priced but was a tender fat free piece. The place looked clean and bright but we were seated in the bar area( not my choice, just where they sat us) the noise level was extremely loud between the large parties on each side trying to talk over each other, the two tvs on diff channels, full row of bar patrons and music coming from the speakers and the place wasnt full. name: Mat Yerkes
text:
There isn't enough I can say about Bayside Bowl. The staff is wonderful. The building is gorgeous. The food is great. The beer selection is always broad but not too broad, and the service on the lanes and for the lanes is superb. Bayside has received a lot of press recently for the new addition, the rooftop bar, and the taco truck - so I won't go into great deal about those, but they're awesome.

The cocktail menu is the most un-bowling alley menu I've seen in a bowling alley. Everything on it, that I've tried at least, has been delicious. A couple favorites of mine for food and drink have been the pulled pork sandwich, they had a brisket sandwich for a bit, the mac and cheese, and for drinks, the Pinsetter and the Fixer Elixir (which is spicy, so heads up).

As of writing this, the roof bar gets extremely busy if the weather is nice, and doubly so on Fridays. If you are looking to check out the upstairs, I'd recommend getting there right when they open if you can.

text:
My friend recommended this bakery for the prosciutto croissant and as soon as she said those two words, I was already sold. We came by on a Thursday morning at around 8:30, and the line was about 15 people deep. It moves pretty quickly though - we ended up waiting only 15 minutes. Here is everything we ordered:

Prosciutto Croissant - this wasn't bad but I don't think it was worth the almost $5 price tag. I'd recommend eating it by alternating ends because one side has prosciutto, but the other doesn't. We thought we had ordered three of these (but there were two in the bag) so we went back and asked them to check if we did. Turns out we only ordered two but they gave us a third one on the house anyway. Such a nice gesture

Asiago Fougasse - this was my favorite. I wish I had gotten three of these instead. Lots of asiago flavor, toast on the outside but soft on the inside

Pistachio cookies - these were only okay. I didn't taste much of a pistachio flavor, but more of some type of spice they used. It tasted almost like pumpkin spice, but not

Blueberry scone - pretty good blueberry flavor but I'm not a huge fan of scones in general (fiance wanted this one)

If I'm ever back in Portland, I'll definitely be back for that fougasse, and maybe try some of their bread next time.

name: Perks Advisor
text: Standard Baking appears to be a favorite and offers a variety of baked treats ranging from bread to croissants.  It can be hard to find because it is part of the back end of the Fore Street restaurant.  I ordered the pecan bun and it was decent but did not taste like it was just out of the oven.  However, that was the only baked good I tried.  It has a nice atmosphere and can have a steady line.

name: William de Figueiredo
text:
There are few gastronomic delights that are better than biting into a crusty full-flavored, nutty bread. When was the last time you had that joy? Maybe it's time to pay a visit to Standard Baking company.
This is an old world bakery with scrumptious breads. Try all their breads, as well as all the pastries and cookies. Each bite will indicate that you were correct to go here for all your baking needs.

name: Heleen Raes
text: This bakery has a small selection of great pastries and bread. The baguettes are amazing and made to the French tradition, a gem to find as a European! I was disappointed in the bread though, it wasn’t any better than what you can find in a supermarket. There’s also no seating inside and only limited seating outside. There is free 15-minute parking in front of the bakery though, which is very nice!

name: Pristorn H.
text: Currently with Covid the max capacity for this establishment is just 2 in the store, so there will be a line. It is completely worth the wait. Everything there is delicious!

name: Sarah Mulcahy
text: A total dream. Brings me back to mornings in Bavaria, Germany when we'd go to the bakery for fresh pastries. Simply divine!

text: Terrific bakery to grab a cup of coffee and get fresh baked pastries and bread. Fast service and friendly staff.   This is take away place, but they do have a few tables outside - weather permitting.

text: Delicious bakery. Had the chocolate croissant. Absolutely amazing. Coffee was ok.

name: Brian H
text: Great place for baking stuff. It is quite pricy. I wish they had more pastries to choose from at this place. They should add cinnamon rolls.

text: Beautiful, unbeatable baked goods. Recommend: rye cookie, financier, galettes, marinated olive bread, fougasse. Cannot visit Portland without getting our fix.

name: Lyric Wizard
text:
This was one of the places i wanted to visit while I am here as i had read and heard so much about this place.
I was not disappointed. Being  skeptical at first me and my girlfriend got one Rubharb and raspberry tart.
It was one of the most amazing tart i ever had.I got hungry after that that went back in and got another
Baguette and a Brioche roll. The breads are constantly baked and replaced .
There is no place inside to sit but there is a small patio area covered with grape vines and big parking Lot.
This place very well deserves to be in the to go list.

text: The bread is outta this world. As a Russian, I always crave rye bread. "Miche" is the closest thing I ever tried to that sweet childhood memory of the rye bread I ate. Also of note: baguette, single pizza, asiago fougasse, raspberry galette.

name: Joseph Borowy
text:
Absolutely amazing. It's no wonder there's always a line. I think I waited 10+ minutes to walk through the door, which I debated leaving, but figured I didn't want yo have wasted my time, and I definitely didn't. Great staff, helpful, knowledgeable, very friendly and seem to love what they do (their tip cup is overflowing for a reason. Hahaha!). I would recommend this bakery to anyone and everyone.

I would suggest thru change one thing... They need to keep both doors accessible. The line in and out were funneled through one of their double doors, which made it difficult to get in and out, but that is a minor issue and not worth docking this amazing bakery any stars.

text: Always the best bakery in Portland. The oatmeal raisin cookies are the best I've ever had. The bread rivals that of San Francisco. It's an accomplishment!

text: My father was a baker for 45 years, and when I was moving up to Portland, one of his baking compatriots took me aside and told me to go to Standard. It was one of the first places I went to, and it's remained one of my favorites since! Absolutely fantastic, rustic-oriented pastries and bread.

text: One of my must vist places when I am in Portland! Scones are my favorite purchase but the selection of pastries is fantastic! Grab a coffee while you are there and you are set to explore the City. Location is outstanding and there is parking while you load up on calories. Prices are in line with their location.

name: Marilyn Massicotte
text: This bakery is a little expensive. As a Montrealer croissant are part of my usual diet and almond croissant are sold in every school cafeteria, every work place, so i was kinda surprised by the prices here as for me this is nowhere near a luxurious thing. Croissants are in Quebec what Donuts are to USA. A cheap treat but having that said here in USA a good croissant, a pain au chocolat (chocolatine) or an almond croissant are a little harder to find and theirs were very good. The almond one was a little too buttery tasting for my taste but their regular and chocolate croissant were very good. What for me really worth the 4☆ is THE CHOCOLATE CORK. Oh my this was a little piece of heaven. Call ahead cuz they don't make them everyday!

name: Eric Hollingsworth
text:
blueberry buckle temper tantrum warning... LOL

have a LOVE HATE relationship with this bakery. They make the best blueberry buckles I’ve ever  had.   Not sure what that is?   Imagine a blueberry muffin and a coffee cake had a baby....  yep, it’s that good.

The only problem is that they also make blueberry/raspberry (yuk) and raspberry (double yuk).  I’m sure there are folks that are as equally repulsed by  their blue berry only buckles.  Why rotate the flavors?  It’s not as if it would be more difficult to make.   I also know it’s not because of the lack of ingredients (another nearby bakery makes blueberry only buckles everyday.... but they are not nearly as yummy as yours)

So here’s my solution to make both the blueberry and raspberry people happy.

PICK A FRIGGEN DAY TO MAKE A SPECIFIC FLAVOR.   For example “Blueberry Monday”, Raspberry Tuesday”.

or better yet...

MAKE ALL THREE FLAVORS AVAILABLE EVERY FRIGGEN DAY!    It seems like every time I call, it’s the day that they made the other two flavors.

Ok, my rant is over.  LOL

name: William Sawyer
text: Honestly it was okay I've been to the best fairs in the country all types not just like rides and games but all types of organic blah blah blah, chickens and rabbit fairs. I think it's really light on content some solar panels some batteries where's Tesla where's like any alternative anything that is accessible to the people attending. Line for 45 minutes for a lamb kebab the ladies with the egg rolls are the ticket five bucks.  I starved till I got home and  who's going to really permafrost in their apartment in Portland Maine. A million people and a lot of dust and a mile walk.

name: Chris Pine
text: I was lucky enough to be able to volunteer for the set up and for a fair day last year, and both experiences were simply excellent. You’re not only working alongside hard-working, kind people, but you get to be a part of the warmth and wonder that goes into the fair itself. When my shift was done, I had a great time wandering around the different booths and barns. There’s SO much to see, do, and eat—and everyone of all ages seem to genuinely enjoy their time there!

name: Michael Iveson
text: A wonderful area that hosts the annual common ground mofa fair. Lots of fun cool things to see, learn, and do. Decent food to eat and lots of friendly eco minded individuals to talk to. The fair is hosted every year in September and is definitely worth the trip. We drove up from Pennsylvania to check it out. admission is pretty cheap, lots of local produce to buy, parking is a breeze. It's kind of in the middle of nowhere so make sure to fill up your tank before making the journey!

name: Sandra Horton
text: This fair is huge. There are so many vendors, crafts and demonstrations of all kinds. The farmers market is only organic. It is geared for sustainable living. There are no children amusement rides. I usually spend about 5-6 hours here.

name: Bob Brown
text: One of the best fairs in Maine. Numerous displays and demonstrations of organic farming, permaculture and alternative energy  concepts. Lots of food and vendors. A focus on children's activities, so the kids aren't bored. Large farmer's market takes up one section of the fair. Worth a visit!

name: ben mullen
text: Great family time. Exposed to knowledge. Love the  parades.

name: Devyn Potter
text: I wish there were more stars that's how amazing the common ground fair is!  I went two days in a row and I dont think I saw everything!  The craft tents were filled with amazing art, jewelry, pottery, and so so so much more!  Getting to talk to all the local Maine artists was so much fun and  very informative.  The food is AMAZING!  there was such a variety and everything was fresh and delicious, I HIGHLY recommend the chicken pot pie hand pies and the pie cones!  There was also so many talks and other events going on throughout the days!  We got to buy fresh produce and flowers at the farmers market and try samples of bread and cheese!  We also went and visited the spinners and learned how they make yarn out of sheep's wool!  All in all it was amazing, fun, and the best way to spend a weekend!

name: Steph Dee
text: We went to the common ground fair, and oh my the grounds alone were breathtaking. The diversity in informational booths, food, to all the home grown veggies is quite astonishing. I definitely recommend visiting the grounds for the fair. I will be coming back to learn more about the associated farm. Highly recommend!🤩

name: Matt Nesin
text: Great fair for family fun, food, animals, crafts, agriculture and more.  I always bring an appetite and spend at least one day browsing and eating from the various vendors.  Make sure to get a T shirt to commemorate the visit!

name: Tom Poirier
text:
Whole foods are the medicine of the healthy.
Vendors and displays are indicative of a hearty lifestyle.
One of the only country fairs dedicated to wholesome agricultural practices.
Demeter -" Goddess of the Harvest ", looks fairly on those who make the earth their Temple.

name: Ulthaedin Segerath
text: This is an amazing experience, they may not be an amusement park but they have allot of amazing things. I go every year to stock up on great spices. Aside from amazing loose leaf tea and real maple products made right.

name: Luke Rand
text: Great agricultural fair! You can't go just one day because there's so much to see. Full of interesting and unique products and experiences.

name: Debbie Gagnon
text: Common Ground fair was such a delight.  All the children looked so healthy and well cared for.  Felt like a very different environment then the usual fair....people were going around passing out water,  so much for kids, puppet shows, faire house building, hill sliding on cardboard, even a nursing tent for moms and babies. The food was clean, organic and delicious!  Can't wait to go next year!

name: Steven Long
text: We've been coming here for two decades. Aways new things to see and eat. We also enjoy seeing the repeat vendors. A great place for the whole family.

name: nick nelsonwood
text: Awesome fair with lots to offer. Great food booths + they have some of the typical fried fair food and then lots of more unique options like ravioli or farm fresh sandwiches. This fair was far more than I had expected it to be. The quality of the vendors was above that of any other local craft fair or state Fair I've been to in years. There is live music, educational seminars, and live demonstrations of everything from processing your own timbers to how to brew your own beer.
It's $15 per person to get in, and it's worth every penny!

name: Alexander Blackstone
text:
A must go to wether you're from Maine or just up for a visit!

A pleasure to walk around and see the different Maine craft; homemade wares abound!  May favorite part about all the different stands are catching up with keepers and hearing about their process.

Hands down the best event at Common Ground is the border collie hearding trials.  The two guys are quite the showmen and the dogs are brilliant!

The food is exceptional!  Every year a blooming onion is a MUST!  Other highlights include lamb kabobs, hot chaga drinks, stone oven pizza!

name: Virginia Mackay
text:
After parking, we had to walk 3/4 of a mile to get to the entrance of the fair. There is also a train that will take you there but the route to the train is not marked well.

Once there, it was packed full of people. We could barely walk around. The tent that we wanted to visit for a class was nowhere to be found on the map, and once we found it, it was too packed to sit down and we ended up standing in the back of a crowd, unable to hear the speaker.

The worst of it was the overpriced food!! Nothing was under $10.00 for a single serving. One small slice of cheese pizza was $10.00! That was the cheapest vendor believe it or not.

The area with the farm animals was wonderful though, and far less crowded because the location was away from the main fairgrounds.

Overall, a stressful and expensive experience.

name: Charles Crane
text: Hundreds of interesting vendors, farming & homesteading the old fashioned way, attracting great people with wholesome values.

Back when the fair started the people were real farmers, real rural living types, sure some hippies as well but the hippie type who actually knew how to farm... now a days... well now at the fair it is a giant left leaning political event, most folks attending are sort of cos-play farmers or as much like a real farmer as a LARP kid with a foam sword is like a real viking. It used to be an event that different types if people could gather and share and learn organic farming ideas and methods as well as sampling organic wears. But now it's a you love Hillary or we hate you type event, this real farmers who work the land for a living are made to feel outcasts.  Needless to say, it's a different crowd now a days. Sad really.

name: Roe Adams
text: Really great staff, really great food at a good price. Walked in thinking it was a takeaway place, but was surprised at how fancy it was. Very kind staff took my order for carryout with Grace and food was ready impossibly fast. Will definitely return for the Pad Thai!

name: Cc Ramone
text: Idk why I'd ever wait so long to try this place. So good and prices are good/get a good amount of food! Def 5 stars.

name: Jody Moscrip
text: We have never been disappointed! Fresh, delicious and great service. The fresh spring rolls are crave worthy. Yum!

name: Jaimie Bernstein
text: Delicious food, fast service and very vegan friendly.

name: Rick Stilphen
text:
Nice comfortable place to eat.
The food is always very good.
Service is always with a smile. The waiter made sure that our water glasses were full.
This is the best Thai restaurant in Biddeford.

name: Meghan C.
text: They have an amazing drunken noodle!!! I asked for 8 out of 5 stars for spiciness and they sure did deliver! This honestly might be the best drunken noodle Maine has to offer!

name: Cliff Allen
text: Quality ingredients, great service. The manager was super on point and if you don't like the food here you should stop eating out. There are places that basically serve sugar coated msg food and there are places that make great food with quality ingredients. Thai Me is in the second camp. My wife can be a tough cookie in the food department and if I want a happy wife I bring her here.

name: Anna yang
text: First time getting the pad Thai here! And it was amazing 🤤

name: marty schindler
text: Great place for a quick vegan dinner. Almost always enough food for tomorrow's lunch as well. Good selection of appetizers and salads, plus  entre choices for the discriminating palate. Of you're hungry and in the mood for something different... You've come to the right place.

name: Jackie
text: Amazing food! Friendly staff and the place was clean, even the bathrooms?!

name: Krista Christie
text:
Really delicious.  The crab Rangoon was full of crab (more than any other place we've been) and delicious. Mango curry was dreamy. Drinks were fabulous.  Only downside of the whole meal was the Pad Thai was a bit heavy for my taste.

Edit: Downgrading one star for consistency.  We took a friend there recently because we had liked it so much and all of the meat was overcooked, the fried rice flavorless, and the sauce on another dish WAY too sweet.  It was our first negative experience so there may be some inconsistency in the kitchen staff. Presentation was still beautiful but flavor lacking.

name: Michael Hopkins
text: Good food, fair prices. I've been taking out here weekly during the Covid shutdown.

name: Beth S
text: Best place in town!! I was delighted to finally find an Asian restaurant that wasn't disappointing.The food and service were great! Thai ME in Biddeford will be my go to place!

name: Wes L
text: I really enjoyed my meal and the ginger tea hit the spot as well. I'll definitely be back.

name: Tyler Christie
text: Straight up great food. A bit in the pricey side but well worth it. Rangoon, Gao and Mango Chicken are best in town. Mai Tai's are solid, albeit pricey. Reccomended.

name: John Marescot
text: A lot has changed since I was here 5 years ago... The food awesome I like the service.. warm environment

name: Viloria Phinney
text: Food is great and the servers are eye "candy" :)

name: Gary Kribel
text: Spicy pad-thai was great

name: Tori Macdonald
text: Great food, great service. The best pad thai around!!

name: Rolando Mejia
text: Food is always delicious

name: Daniel Christie
text: This place has fantastic food and a wonderful staff. I love it!

name: Ken Moulton Jr.
text: Great little Thai place. Awesome character, and cozy feel. Delicious food is only the start! Out of all the Thai restaurants in the Biddeford area, this is my top choice.

name: J C
text: Thai ME is a great place to get Thai food in Biddeford. It has a wide variety of choices, and has a few gluten free options as well (including some of the Pad Thai). The price may be slightly higher than you expect, but the serving size is quite large, I usually have enough left over for the next day. Thai ME also does take out, which has been a convenient option on several occasions.

name: CWW
text: The drunken noodle is the best I've ever had. The sauce is delicious, just perfect. They definitely use really fresh rice noodles. 6 stars from me to this chef

name: Mike Nicholas
text: Consistently good, big menu. Only downside is sometimes it's slow but it's usually very busy. Thai Lo Mein is my favorite, also crispy chicken pad thai! Steamed butterflies are a unique app.

name: Stephanie Lekakos
text: Great thai food and great service!

name: diana fisher
text: Fresh, delicious, lots of food!

name: Jacob Trombley
text: Try the beef of paradise.

name: Carla Martin
text: The food was fantastic

name: Sokkhann Cole
text: Best thai food I've had!!! Better then the thai restaurants in portland!!!

name: Lynda Young
text: Excellent food, great atmosphere and really good Thai food.

name: Tomi Flowers
text: One of the best Thai places in the area. The food is amazing and the portions will feed you at least two meals.

name: Jane Laika
text: This is one of my new go-to spots. Their portions are massive, and nearly their entire menu can be made vegan!

name: James Sneakers
text: Something new to try. My gluten free wife had issues with what was supposed to be gluten free. But try the ice cream. We were happy then.

name: Jason Gallagher

name: Andrew Stout

name: Ryan Boisclair

name: Bryanna Faugno
text: Have never had a dish here that I didn't love. On my most recent visit, I got the scallion pancakes (which were actually cubes) that were absolutely delicious, as well as the steamed edamame that was very well-plated.

name: Leonard Tan
text:
Love this place! My friends and I go there quite often. Their food and service is always consistently good.

Update 08/18/2013: We had a large group of people (14 people) and I was amazed by how great their service was. There were 3-4 other tables in the restaurant, but they handled our large group really well. Everything came really quickly and the waitress did a great job separating our orders and bills. Everyone ordered appetizers/sushi along with our entree and we were able to finish our meal is about 1.5 hours.

name: Holly Hitchcock
text: Worst meal i got from here. Usually very good. Not today.

name: Ann Berube
text: Best place for Thai in the biddeford/saco area. Everything I have ordered is delicious, and always good portions. Also the new remodel inside the restaurant is nice and staff is very friendly.

name: Rick Farrar
text: Yes yes yes! Eat here for fresh Thai inspired food. Large menu, my favorite is the crispy chicken Thai basil!

name: Rachel Carpenter

name: J M
text: Great food, hits the spot!

name: Karenlee Namrog

name: Amy Lucarelli

name: Lucas Patry
text: The service is friendly, the staff work hard and the food is fantastic. I've dined in and carried out over the past year and every time is as great as the last.

name: Eddie Z

name: Jason Clark

name: Victoria Ryder
text: They're food is good, but they've gone down hill recently. I like that they use recycled plastics for their take out and delivery containers, but for the quality they're heading towards the prices might not be worth it anymore.

name: Kathy King
text: Excellent food and fast service.

name: Tati C
text:
Best Thai in Southern Maine! The ingredients are always fresh and the food isn't laced with copious amounts of sugar, MSG, or anything else that doesn't belong in food that on it's own is yummy.
The curries, pad Thai, Tom kha soup, and General Tso chicken are favs.
The decor is cute and clean and parking is never a problem.

name: RACHAEL CONNER

name: John Lemieux

name: Carl Andrews
text: Live in Biddeford and tried the place 3 times, because it's close, or another place was closed unexpectedly... Anyway, I think the fresh spring rolls are over-priced, the Tom Yum has a decent broth, but other than the broth is just pieces of chicken and mushrooms... maybe that's standard, but didn't do it for me. Tried a chicken dish another time and disappointed. Tonight the place smelled. Seemed to be the bathroom which is right near the entrance.  Place has never made me sick, but it's my last favorite Thai place ever. Sorry Thai Me, but you really need to up your game.

name: Kyle Brooks
text: It took a long time for us to even get water, and the be food and whole restaurant smelled off. My friend and I could not even finish our meals before the smell made us feel sick, and we had to leave.

name: Debbie Palmer

Social distancing was in effect & I can assume if need be would have been enforced. If not for the secondary door's being closed I would have given it 5 stars.

Well organized clean store with attentive staff
Love Hannaford

name: Bill Cindy Libby

name: Sarah Dee
text: Very clean and even giving out free masks and gloves. I would have given a five but they're constantly giving out coupons for products they don't have. It's frustrating when you go in with a list and spend 15 minutes looking for a specific product just to find out they don't have it. Otherwise, it's a great store.

name: Melissa .Mckenney
text: This place is always too busy.  Not enough parking.  They always have great produce.   Check out lines are long.

name: Phyllis Plessis

name: Trevor Axelsen
text: There finally getting stuff in like toilet paper and canned soup. Stuff you could'nt find 2 months ago. It's getting better my friends.

name: Danielle Warren

name: Karen Record

name: Owen Bradley

name: Roseanna Pratt
text: I like Hannaford. I go all the time. But sad to say they are not following the Governor's directive that all customers shall wear masks. There isn't even an attempt to get unmasked people to do so. Also, there is no signage stating masks required. Not even one that Requests this. This is serious stuff people! Over 100,000 Americans dead. Smarten Up!

name: Eric Glanville
text:
The store itself is beautiful compared to other Hannaford locations, isles are wide enough for two people going opposite directions to comfortably pass each other.
The customer service was lousy, the only cashier open was non stop talking with their bagger through every customer in line. Hardly made eye contact and couldn't tell when she asked us a question versus asking her friend a question.

name: James Doyle
text: This is the Saco, Maine location of a large supermarket chain. In general, the chain is of higher quality than others and this particular location does not disappoint. Average-sized for a supermarket. Has a 2000s' look and feel. Nice selection of reasonably priced baked goods. Fast, friendly service. Ample parking in the parking lot just outside.

name: Karen Renee Record
text: Rob is always such a great guy, even when they're swamped in the pharmacy!!!

name: Eileen Coll
text: Very helpful staff. Wide variety of items. Particularly good salad/soup bar. Nice bakery items - large selection of goodies.

name: anthony wrecenyar
text: Went to pick up a prescription and a couple of other things for dinner.  Store was clean and neat.  Good selection of items.  Produce was fresh.  Prices were competitive.  Employees were friendly.  Good shopping experience.  Will go there again.

name: Robert Clark
text: I was in Hannaford's yesterday and it was cleaned out of any poultry, potatoes,  bananas, frozen foods, pasta, baby wipes, beans, rice, most anything to make a meal with. Probably a lot more items then I mentioned. For some reason they had pork? I blame all the grocery stores for not limiting people on how much food or toilet paper some can buy. If they would restrict what people could buy it would make it so everyone had what they needed.

name: Deborah S
text: Bigger then the one I'm used to. I like the fact that they have a nice alcohol section. The only downside is that they charge for paper bags because the city banned plastic bag, but that is just what it is

name: Mike Schofield
text: Nice store. Only complaint is that the food at the hot bar always looks like its been out all day. I usually am in there on the way home from work, about 5. Figure it would be a little fresher.

name: Justine Wood
text: Spend $100.00 +/- on a grocery and you better have your own bags cause you will pay for bags that is if you want to put them in bags .  Give me a break.  How low can you go.

name: Jerome Olanovich
text: Great selection, service & pricing.

name: Kat Fontaine
text: I would like to offer a sincere thank you to the two wonderful gentlemen managers who assisted me with a problem that i had regarding an issue with another store this afternoon. They were extremely kind and courteous, and I could not be more pleased. Kudos 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

name: James Duclos
text: Very good checkout service. Good selection of merchandise for an end of weekend visit.

name: Patrick Ordway
text: The best

name: Ann Hall
text: Didn't have the yogurt I wanted and didn't have the seltzer water I wanted.

name: Jeanette Dantuono

name: Stewart Shuster

name: David Emery
text: Always find what you need very helpful people

name: Rich Cormier
text: Well the parking lot was nice. Waited for roadside to fix my flat tire.

name: The Crushingtons
text: My wife loves shopping here! I enjoy snoozing in the car while she shops!

name: jamie sandefur
text: Love the employees here. They are always so nice.

name: Justin Titus
text: Very clean store very outgoing managers employees are very outgoing I'm telling you they have the best seafood department you could ever imagine all the produce or fresh the fish are picked fresh and caught daily and they have the best deals on all the free and vegetables you could ever ask for 100% satisfaction guaranteed hands down this is the best place to get your groceries in awesome deals

name: Tim Sweeney
text: Plenty of parking and a very friendly and helpful staff

name: Elizabeth Coburn
text: My regular food shopping center. Nice size store, not too big. The food is always fresh and great quality. They also have drive up food shopping now! The pharmacy inside is convenient too.

name: Thom Lessard
text: There is nothing quite like showing up at the supermarket as soon as the doors open. I enjoy brewing a cup of coffee on their Keurig and then heading towards the bakery to smell the bread being taken out of their ovens. You'll find a very wide variety of produce and products here. I also enjoy self-checkout staff is more than helpful and friendly.

name: Becky Barker
text: I like it except they are always stocking the shelves which yes I know it needs to be stocked but you are constantly waiting to be able to get to the shelves to get what you want also the sales thing that hold stuff in the aisles are always in the way so you can't get to the things you want on the shelf behind it

name: AndreaL Farrow

name: jeff bnnett
text: Makes shaw's look like a gas station

name: Joe Bagodonuts
text: I feel as if this supermarket has the best values on cold cuts. I have gone to other places and everybody wants eight nine or ten dollars a pound for everything. For that reason I do my shopping here

name: Tammy Williford
text: We love shopping at hannaford but you've gotta remember your bags

name: Jeremy Grady
text: Good experience. Found a new low carb snack to try. (I hope it's good! Lol) I like that they moved the beer, liquor and wine to a "Spirits" section. Please add in 18 packs of Twisted Tea. It's about all I can drink because of stomach issues.

name: Linda Crowell
text: Went there the other day to pick up a prescription and the pharmacy staff they are so wonderful and helpful

name: Heather Anne Wright
text: Always over-crowded, nearly impossible to shop in summer, poorly stocked bread (which is horribly over-priced) and under-staffed with inexperienced summer help. Despite living locally, I go out of my way to avoid this particular Hannaford. The price of food staples like bread is ridiculous. The fresh-baked sourdough is $4.49 and is always sold whole which means a customer needs to ask for it to be sliced. In other parts of the world, people can at least buy a loaf of bread for $1. Not in the United States.

name: Allura Morneau
text: Good selection. Love self check out. Manager was helpful

name: Kayla Andrews
text: Prices are high, the self check out screws up every time I go in, and I end up waiting 5 minutes or longer for a manager. And as a former employee, your company does not care about their associates, nor the families that work and shop there. Those of us on a budget shop at Market Basket and dollar stores

name: J Holmes
text: This is our go to stop when my family is visiting the area. We generally stock up on water, snacks, and other groceries. Last time we were in, there was a large variety of hot foods, and a salad bar. There are several isles stocked with hygiene products, and other convenience products, making it a perfect one stop shop for a travelling family. Location is also very handy and easy to find.

name: Shauna Johnston
text: I returned avocados that I had purchased last night. The store clerk who helped me and polite and timely in taking of me, and I got my money back as well as a bonus.  I shop here all the time. They are awesome.  The store is always near, clean and the staff is so very helpful.

name: Scott McElyea

name: Carlene Cyr

name: Nick

name: lisa morrison
text: Completely reorganizing, but enough knowledgeable​ staff to help guide and locate items needed. Although always busy with tourists in summer, shelves are always faced and neat. Easy access in and out of lot and carriages usually where they belong.

name: Shawn Tibbetts

name: Mac Coldwell
text: This is my local grocery store, and the staff is always helpful and friendly. Good selection of local produce year round considering we are a four season region. The liquor, wine and beer after was extended, and offers a fairly decent selection. Would like to see some of the local whiskeys and a deeper variety of local breweries represented.

name: Rick P

My physician actually told me to switch pharmacy's once she found out that's where I wanted my meds sent and recommended I go anywhere else. Said she's had nothing but bad experiences with Carol nightingale

No communication on meds. They were to fill yesterday now when we show up and say they are out of the mental health med and the child will have to wait! B...S... ! They could have called yesterday when they knew they were out or they could have gotten some from another hannaford.
NO they wait till we travel in then say " by the way we can't fill this script." Of course it's a med they fill every month for the last 3yrs. ARGGGGH rant over.

The least they could do would be to put the organic food back the way it used to be to make it easier for people with allergies. I spend enough time cooking everyday and now i have to go from store to store and isle after aisle which is very time consuming and frustrating. Its hard to live like a normal person does.
