excelente

resp.text: Hi Joshua, we’re sorry you didn’t have a good experience at the brewery. We’d love to how to make it right. Please let us know what we could’ve done to improve your visit!

Hi Kevin, thanks very much for taking the time to leave us a review. We always try to provide a memorable experience for our guests and would really appreciate it if you wanted to let us know how we could have improved your time with us!

Thanks very much for taking the time to leave us a review. We always try to provide a memorable experience for our guests and would really appreciate it if you wanted to let us know how we could have improved your time with us. Thanks!

name: Jessica Cyr
text: What a fabulous experience! You order online and pick it up at the window. I had a specialty drink (London Fog) which was piping hot and delicious. Our bagels looked burnt but weren't! The Buff Chic and Spicy Salmon sandwiches were AMAZING. Run, go!

name: Troy Hollihan
text:
A bagel I can bite into! I can enjoy almost any bagel but not when it's so tough and chewy that you're getting a workout. This was NOT a problem here. Think of an average bagel like a hot air balloon and these are the most beautiful and exquisite balloons, just without the hot air.

Look at me go on and on about the density. Holy smokes the flavor is gooood. I got the everything bagel with plain cream cheese and it felt like a gourmet experience.

Order online and they'll text you when it's time to come to the pick up window.

name: Elizabeth Pockl
text: Amazing! Ordering was online, did say it would take an hour, however that was luckily just the app saying that. I went to the window to check after a few min and it was done!

name: Aaron Solet
text: Good. The wood fired oven makes for a unique bagel. Not a typical bagel shop though. Expect a hipster/artisanal wait and price. Nice, laid-back staff.

name: Thomas Farrington
text: Their wood fired bagels are delicious.  The soft and chewy texture with the light smoke flavor puts these bagels at the top of my favorites list!  The photo really does not do it justice!

name: Ryan Moore
text: So good. So nice.

name: Rick Stilphen
text:
Bagels were perfect! They did not disappoint us. Wide variety of flavored cream cheese. We tried the LEMON/THYME.  IT WAS AMAZING!
The CHIVE Cream cheese surprised us! All of the cream cheese's had just a perfect hint of lemon and chives.
We highly recommend Rover as an excellent place for breakfast and lunch.
Rover has indoor seating (smelling the wood fired stove) as well as take out.

name: Mac Coldwell
text: What a great new spot for Biddeford. I had the anadama bagel with cream cheese, and it was delicious. Coffee is really good, and there is a really nice atmosphere. Service was helpful and friendly. They have local artists, artwork for stale on their Walls. They will start serving pizza in January. Can't wait.

name: Abby Baker
text: I got The Classic bagel that has the smoked salmon and all the fixins on a sesame bagel (which is the only way to go in my opinion) and my boyfriend got a Shift Lunch which has bacon, avocado, sauteed onions, and hot honey on an everything bagel which was also super delicious. The atmosphere is really nice to go and have a relaxed breakfast and people watch out the big front windows. And the coffee is really good too.

name: Joel Bilodeau
text: Awesome bagels!

name: Colin Becker
text: There's nothing quite like Rover in southern Maine.  The pizza oven fired bagels have this crisp crust and this amazing chew.  The staff is also super friendly, which is always a plus.

name: Andy Martin
text: I finally had a chance to check this place out. I had heard good things about them but was surprised as to how good and different their bagels were. I didn't realize they had a wood fired oven, it gave the bagel such depth of flavor. You won't find another place around here that will compare. The atmosphere is pretty cool as well even though I had mine to go I could see myself hanging out there and enjoying future bagels 😀. This is precisely the type of business Biddeford should be growing on. I would recommend this business to anyone wanting to try a unique and delicious bagel...

name: nicole lewis
text: Delicious! I had the veg special on the seat salt bagel...amazing! Daughter had the sticky bun...best cinnamon roll ever.  This is our new favorite spot when visiting maine! I could eat here every day!

name: Danielle Floyd
text: You have GOT to try this place. You would think the bagels being wood fired would make them hard, but it is just the opposite. Nice and crunchy on the outside and light and airy on the inside. The flavors are so tasty and with vegan and meat options there is something for everyone!

name: Alysse McCann
text: This place is some of the best bagels you'll find. They guys that work there are always friendly, they have great cookies and sticky buns, too. I wish they could be open all the time so I could have a great lunch and dinner place where I always knew I'd get such amazing food.

name: Briant Gaudet
text: Love their bagels! Go there soon, closing in a few weeks.  They are moving back to MA.

name: Lauren Rantuccio
text: “The Classic” (smoked salmon, fresh dill, capers, red onion , cream cheese) was amazing. We’re huge fans of this style bagel. This was our favorite. The bagel isn’t too dense and too chewy. Usually the sandwich is too big and falls apart within the first few bites. Rover makes it where it’s proportional. In my opinion, it’s better than Rose Foods, Highroller, and the places we’ve been in NYC.

name: Joe Conte
text: I'm from New York and this is the best bagel I've ever tasted

name: Donna Ponce
text: Wish I could rate it higher... Came across this place today for the first time... best sesame seed bagel I have ever had.. Definitely going back to try their sandwiches...

name: Jennifer Day
text: First time @ Rover and The Shift sandwich ensures we'll be back again.

name: Scott Anderson
text: Never cease to amaze.  Amazingly friendly staff and amazing food.  I am never disappointed when I come here.  Due to my  lifestyle change to keto I dont come here as often as I used to but occasionally I'll cheat and come here for a treat!

name: The Maine Criminal Defense Group
text: Best bagels in Maine.  Super creative and delicious sandwiches.  Best cinnamon buns I've eaten anywhere in my lifetime.

name: Crystal Harriman
text: The bagels are amazing!!  I've had coworkers ask what's so great about them, but couldn't explain it - so I brought some to work and everyone agreed that they were the best bagels they had ever had!  Bonus: the employees are always friendly!

name: William Bly
text: Best bagels and sticky buns on the planet.  Incredibly creative sandwiches and unique cream cheese spreads.  Biddeford is luck to have a place like this.

name: Your Wizard
text: Simply the best bagel I've had, ever. I've had bagels in New York City and many a Jewish Deli, but the fresh, warm, well-dressed bagel from Rover topped them all. I got the spicy salmon on an everything bagel and nearly lost my mind. The avacado was perfectly ripe, the spice mild and pleasant, adding substantially to the flavor. I also got an iced Vietnamese coffee and found the strength and flavor of the coffee to be unusually high. The service was excellent. I enjoyed the free foozball table in their dining room. The only complaint I could make would be that their prices are a bit high, but the food and drink are well worth it.

name: Amanda Kimball
text: Great wood fired bagels. I didn't care for the vegan cream cheese. Sandwhiches were excellent. Sometimes they sell out so get there earlier for more bagel options.

name: Janie H
text: Great bagels. Nice atmosphere. Plenty of seating and parking. Lose 1 star because they are sold out of bagels by 10:30 and no eggs on breakfast sandwich. Have been several times and will continue to go back.

name: Jesse Carlson
text: My favorite bagels, and my favorite place to eat bagels. Love the atmosphere, music, and people.

name: Bob Swain
text: I had the "shift meal" bagel sandwich for lunch.  HOLY COW!  The bagel was incredible, and then the avocado, hot honey, and bacon were a perfect flavor combo.  I also tried a sticky bun and that was also incredible.  I hate a dry sticky bun, but this one was as gooey as you could ask for!

name: Yew4eya
text: My bagel was great and I was super bummed that the lady in front of me took the last of the freshly made cinnamon buns!

name: Sean Mokler
text: I love their bagels. Great selection of toppings and amazing sandwiches.

name: michael wood
text: Amazing bagels and excellent service I got the breakfast sandwich plain bagel with sausage very tasty!

name: Dori Rogers
text: A delicious, unique bagel. Enjoy!

name: Amy Jane Larkin
text: Really tasty bagels in a comfy spot. The anadama bagel was great with smoked salmon. I really dug all the veggie and other topping options. Friendly staff and a lot of great bar seats by the window.

name: Anne Baltren
text: It's not a place to pop in a quickly grab a bagel. But i it's worth the wait.  I highly recommend any kind of sandwich on a bagel.

name: Michael Hopkins
text: The bagels are delicious. Only a few tables. Oriented to takeout (they will not toast a bagel?!). Very very busy on weekend mornings.

name: Derrick Mallar
text: Rover has been a great add to the area. The bagels are delicious. Staff is very nice.

name: Heather Anne Wright
text: Overpriced small bagel shop with moderately authentic Italian style wood-fired oven pizza. The location could use some ambiance. Would love to see outdoor seeting in the summer.

name: Mike Nicholas
text: Maybe not a hidden gem anymore and that's because these bagels are always fresh and unique being wood fired. A big reason younger people are hanging out and moving to the Saco/Biddeford area.

name: Friendsy Farm
text: Great new business!  Friendly staff, great bagels... Go early for the cinnamon rolls, they're to die for!

name: Christopher Fritzel
text: Awesome bagels, nuff said.

name: Sandra Golash
text: Good bagels.  Whonky open times.  Have to be a local and have patience to learn the ropes here.

name: marty schindler
text: Best Bagels ever. Great choices of baked goods and sweets . Wood fired pizza to die for. Get on in there.

name: Valerie Nahorney
text: Bagel was not toasted as requested.  Bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon (not the sandwich) for $8?  Way too expensive.  And wood-fired means burnt.  Not my kind of bagel.

name: Paul Fournier
text: Great bagels - we finally got to try them

name: Paul Bouchard
text: Delicious wood fired bagels. We had the special sandwich with roasted tomato cream cheese, roasted onions, fennel.

name: Greg Smiddy
text: This place has made me gain almost 10 lbs. Five stars.

name: Roland Moore
text: Excellent choice of bagels and spreads. Places to sit! Worth a trip to Biddeford.

name: William Evans
text: Best bagels this side of Portland. Try their specials can't wait for pizza

name: Sandra White
text: Amazing sourdough bagels , flavors and topping choices!! Or bagel sandwiches!!!

name: Thomas Palmer
text: The bagels we're very good with a ton of flavor. I ordered an egg sandwich which took 10 mins to make and the egg wasn't even fresh and it was spongey. Highly recommend the bagels but not the egg sandwich

name: Mexi l Booboo
text: Great bagels but weird hours of operation.

name: Brian Harvey
text: The bagels here are just as good as they were when they were popping up in Salem.  Would like to try their pizza too!

name: AnnaMaria Morano
text: Delicious bagels and best Margherita pizza I've had in the states!!

name: kee love
text: Friggin fantastic!

text: Tasty bagels and good topping selection.

name: Whitney Billett
text: The best bagels around!

name: Daniele D'Accardi
text: Keep it up guys.

name: Debbie Bartlett

text:
Best bagels
Great service

name: leslie peele
text: Great place

name: Chip Haver
text: There was a little bit of a wait to get in...sat in the diner car...had a great breakfast and pretty good service

name: Taylor Wilcox
text: The food here is veryyyy good. The service seems slow, but the line was also very long. Adorable little spot though. I’d definitely come back.

name: Cory Morrison, CHS, CHRM
text: Stopped for breakfast in the historic dining car. Marie provided exceptional service and the Bayside Breakfast was amazing. Kudos to the chef as everything was expertly seasoned (didn't need any salt, pepper or ketchup) and was presented at proper temperature. It is evident that Miss Portland Diner is complying with Covid-19 precautions, allowing them to continue serving great food. I encourage everyone to support this local icon, especially during these difficult times. Keep up the great work Miss Portland Diner staff! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

name: glenn bell
text: They are well known for their fantastic breakfasts.    Good portions and great service

text: I would describe this as upscaled classic lunch options at a very reasonable price. Fresh and delicious chicken salad on marble rye won me over even more with homemade chips! Staff was friendly and efficient as well.

name: Mike
text: Since 1949 this diner has served the greater Portland area. The building itself if a classic old diner with an attached modern-ish addition for extra seating. The staff is very nice and helpful, the coffee was good too. One thing that really stood out in the meal was the pancakes. These were some of the best pancakes I’ve ever had and they took this place from a 4 to a 5 rating for me.

name: Alexander Merrill
text: Great staff,  classic diner food and excellent outdoor seating situation with tent and heaters!

name: Shawn Mcfarland
text:
One of my favorites for a hearty breakfast. The place is divided into two dining areas. One more of a cafe setting with tables and chairs and then another that is more of the classic rail car style diner with booths and counter stools. I always choose the latter. I used to go to this section as a kid when it was a stand alone diner at a different locale. The food! Classic diner breakfast and lunch. I ordered a Shamrock omelet which was stuffed with homemade corned beef hash. It came with classic grilled, skin on home fries that are perfectly seasoned and marble rye toast. More than I could eat... it generally is over there. Bonus: They actually serve good coffee too.  Previously I dropped in for lunch. Again, great experience and food. A big ole fresh fried haddock sandwich and a cup of chowder. Fantastic! The counter service is always pleasant and attentive. Price point is on par with most other diners in the area.
Easy 5 stars.

name: cwalkenisgod
text:
A historic Portland diner experience.

If you're a fan of greasy spoon diner establishments, you need to come to Miss Portland Diner. Located near Bayside, it's not very far from downtown Portland or Forest Ave.

They offer traditional diner breakfast foods at reasonable prices (most dishes are around $10 or less), as well as lunch. The interior is deceptively large - and it's generally clean inside.

The only downside of the place is that there aren't usually a lot of servers, and the waits tend to be on the longer side. Still, the food is great, and the atmosphere is fun as long as you don't mind a little noise.

Would definitely recommend for breakfast, brunch, or even just lunch.

text: This is my favorite place to grab breakfast in Portland. It's on the Back Bay, which gives you a little less traffic to contend with and the food is VERY good. I am a particular fan of their scrambles. They generally have a pretty eclectic menu so there should be a little something for just about anyone.

name: Sylvie Bailey
text: Amazing food and extremely friendly waitstaff. Very comfortable, relaxed environment. I loved everything on my plate. Reasonably priced for the Portland area.

name: Terence Roder
text:
This diner is a rare find!  Worcester Lunch Car No. 818.

The food is exceptionally good, way above average and what you would expect from a long established (Since 1949) fixture in the Portland landscape.  Very clean, well maintained.  I had sausage and eggs, cooked to order and they exceeded my expectations.  Wonder if Diners, Drive-ins and Dives have shot this location yet.  Perky, attentive and bubbly waitstaff.  A diamond and a jewel.  If you’re over in the Old Port and stuck for parking and long lines at Becky’s Diner, by all means cross over the hill to here.  It’s conveniently located between Whole Foods, Trader Joe’s, and Eastern Mountain Sports.  Make a day of it.   Easy access to I-295, exit 7.  Definitely coming here again and making this a regular stop.  Good prices, open Mon - Sun.

name: Adam Edwards
text: Good food , nice breakfast lunch joint

name: Aaron Leong
text: Local and fresh ingredients play a key role in this diner's draw and popularity. It was our first time here and were pretty impressed by the taste of much our food, which ranged from their burger, Bayside breakfast, fish and chips, hotdog, and milk shake. It gets busy at lunchtime, but you can usually get a seat pretty quickly. Only downside I can think of is the kitchen can be slow in producing food. It's a breakfast diner - food should be flying out of there.

name: Colby Geoffroy
text: Nice quaint little diner with most of its seating in the back behind the actual train car front facade. There’s a good chance of a wait but the wait is worth it for the incredible breakfast food you get. Everything a ordered came out great and the specials all sounded amazing. The price wasn’t bad either, with my total being much less than I originally expected going in.

text: Miss Portland Diner is a great old (coach car?)diner that has been moved, refurbished, and expanded.  Great place for breakfast or lunch, and Sunday Brunch!  The food is always good, the staff is friendly, and always busy during peak times.  I would recommend being seated in the old diner section of the restaurant!

name: Hannah Olson
text: There is parking, which is great. The wait at peak brunch hour on Sunday was only about 20-30 minutes, but they definitely did not have enough staff working and service was understandable scattered and slow. I had the corned beef hash Benedict, since the menu made a point of calling out how good the house-made corned beef hash is. While it was fine, I would not order it again. The hash is shredder, not chopped, has not real color, and was very bland, not even particularly salty. The English muffin was fluffy and tender but the hollandaise sauce had split a little. The side home fries were well seasoned but a few bites were slightly undercooked. My friend had the Thai omelette and liked it. Prices are very reasonable and the atmosphere is unpretentious.

text:
Been coming to the MPD for a lot of years!

This place is a must stop for a cool place to have breakfast or lunch...never been for dinner, and not sure they even serve it. It has an old railroad car for the original diner. The seating is at a counter or in really small booths..think late 40’s early 50’s small. They have a more modern style section, that was built on several years ago, that is much larger than the railroad car section with booths as well as table and chairs.

The food is what you'd expect for breakfast and lunch and is priced reasonably. The service is always friendly and quick...been here at least a 100 times and not once been disappointed!

Parking is easy, either out front on the street or in a no cost parking lot right next to the diner. Enjoy!

name: Rhomni St. John
text:
We were so disappointed when the pandemic hit and we couldn't visit the Zelda themed restaurant we'd just discovered via twitter. Fortunately, Yeto's was happy to negotiate with us for delivery outside their normal radius if we ordered from the catering menu.

We're 30 minutes away so the food was a bit cold when it got here but it was still amazing.

The Ganon sandwhich feels powerful, with plenty of umami and a hint of spice; it's a meal fit for a Gerudo king.

One bite of the Chicken Francese had us immediately addicted.

The Mac and Cheese was perfectly creamy. And the pulled pork that went with it had a wonderfully unique flavor that was still delicious for a bbq sauce fan like myself.

The herb dressing for the Princess Salad was the best salad dressing I've ever had and matched perfectly with the peaches in the salad.

The Yeto's Soup was all of the joy of eating a wonderful homemade soup made by a loving husband for his sick wife without all the nonsense of searching for the ingrediants ourselves.

Finally, the cotten cheesecake we had for dessert was the perfect finisher for the meal. It was light and creamy and melted in your mouth with every bite.

Overall wonderful, nerdy experience. Great service and great food. I hope I can visit Yeto's someday.

My boyfriend and I absolutely adore this restaurant!!! (His dad does too! Goes once a week!)
The food is unique and the decor is so perfect for its name! If you love Zelda, you will fall in LOVE with Yetos !

I had the caprese salad, it was the best I've ever had, truly. Genuine home made food, we will always come back here!

text: This place is amazing. You walk in and the atmosphere is light and relaxed. The lights arent too bright, the music not too loud. They have a shelf full of games so you can pick one out and take it to your table to play while you wait for food. You seat yourself and stay as long as you like. The place has a lot of character and charm. Mismatched furniture, a mix of booths, stools and tables. The food is delicious! The prices are reasonable and the owners are amazing. The man is Italian and the woman from the south she said. Both places really know food. It shows. That was an all around great experience. Highly recommend. It reminds me of my favorite resturant from back home paddy murphys. Though they are Irish and 3 hours north of here they both have great food, fair prices, games and a home atmosphere.

name: Lee Demers
text: Restaurant has a Legend of Zelda theme to both the dining room and the menu. Hanging in the dining room was a big painting of the Legend of Zelda. Lunch came out quickly, and you can view the kitchen from the bar. The Yeto's Superb Soup was the right balance of fishy and creamy, everyone should try it if they can. The golden potato salad was thick, while the baked beans had a nice spice and tang to them. Enjoyed both the Ganon and the Life's a Peach sandwiches; both were big and were hefty. Have not had any of the pasta dishes or cocktails yet as this was an early lunch, but I think it safe to say they will be delicious. They do offer take out. The owner was super nice and service was great. I hope to see this restaurant do well and will be back for more soup.

This is an enjoyable smaller venue! The stage is nicely raised above the lower floor and there also is a higher area around the perimeter, so all had a nice view of the performers. There is a bar along one wall. The evening I was there, there was limited seating, so if you need to sit, plan to get there when the doors first open. Very spacious with high ceilings.
There is a parking garage right next door on Temple Street, $5 an hour. Although be aware that the garage closes at midnight and if the security guard has to come let you out after midnight he will charge you an additional $35. Debit or credit only at the garage.
My only downside to this particular evening was that there were two beer swilling millennials next to me who thought it was okay to dance to the up-tempo songs and then turn their backs to the performers and chat during the slower songs. I could handle the dancing, but really got peeved when they were interfering with my ability to hear. They were indignant that I politely asked them to not talk and also told me they would not stop talking and would not go talk in any other location in the venue. I didn't complain to management, I just tried to ignore them... Maybe if I had danced between the two of them it would have chased them away, LOL.

name: Matthew LittleFarmer
text: The Aphohadion is a tiny live performance venue located in a profoundly unfashionable neighborhood in Bayside, Portland Maine. There is minimal signage identifying the place, I finally spotted a hip young lady having a smoke near an open door and slipped in. The place is maybe 30×40 feet or so, with room for a generous stage, 5 or 6 cocktail tables and a small bar. It would be easy to get a wheelchair in here. A comfy couch and a few more chairs are available.  The bar is beer, wine, tea and coffee. No food is available.  The large and I think, wheelchair accessible bathrooms are down a long hallway. The overall vibe is cool without being exclusionary. The  minimal decor includes a changing art exhibit. Shows here tend toward drone/noise/improv/ experimental. I know they have also held film screenings and there is an upcoming VHS "swap meet". Street parking is plentiful in this utterly deserted industrial neighborhood.I plan on making this pad a regular destination. Enjoy it now before some yuppie developer demolishes the whole area to build condos to sell to rich people who can sit on their balconies and talk about how great Portland used to be! Yay!

This is an amazing small venue that hosts the most eclectic of bands - every so often I will pick a random night, not knowing the band, and be always, pleasantly surprised. This place exudes coolness and, if you want an intro to musical genres you aren’t familiar with, this place is the place to jump off from. I’m not cool enough but, watching from the wings, I experience ‘musical radness’.

I only had a card with me and they didn’t charge cover, only asked me to get something from the bar.

❤️

name: oh ma
text:
Babylon Restaurant!!
We had the most amazing experience last evening trying all of the amazing foods in the dinner buffet. Each dish was one we noted as our favorite, until the next. We have four new items we plan to order through takeout next time.
The price was incredible, 14.99 for a fun evening of experience and complete pleasure. A spacious comfortable dining area with comfortable seating that further encouraged us to relax and enjoy the trip through Iraq through this cuisine.
One note, preparing all of this incredible food definitely impacted the air in this restaurant - we have a slight cooking smell now in our clothing. Reminds me of when I studied in the cafeteria in college, hitting up the cappuccino machine and endless sliced veggies from the salad bar but coming home with a 'kitchen parfuum'.
The dessert was our big surprise - home made dahin, which alone had us going back for a third try even after being full. An absolute must.
A kind friendly young woman hosted us and tended our table. Thank you so much for our lovely evening.

name: doug horseman
text: We have been going to Rose Foods since they opened. The customer service has always been weak even though the food is always good. On a impluse we rode over today at about 130PM. We figured we'd get a bagel and lox to take home. My wife who just wanted to put the order in and wait but was rudely told by a worker that orders had to be called in or made online.What harm would be created if have the worker took the order while my wife waited outside?  Especially since there were no customers there or waiting the half hour before closing.The poor customer service and lack of common sense will always keep Rose Foods from achieving better success in the Portland restaurant community.

name: Max Upp
text:
I’m conflicted. Awesome bagels, cool spot, fun stuff, but this is one of the worst experiences I’ve had in a while. The person at the window was actually pretty mean/annoyed that we were there and made us feel bad for coming, which is weird with a place that felt as cool as this.

We ordered online and when our food was up they acted like it was a huge ordeal to find it in the back even though we could see it sitting right there. When we got finally got our bag of food, half of it had been substituted for other stuff (which is whatever, it’s a bagel shop) but we didn’t even get to choose our alternates and ended up with with a half bag of their weird bagel of the day.

But wait that’s not all, we also ordered some swag which is dope as hell but that was a whole other ordeal. It wasn’t included with our food even though it was part of the same ticket and the lady was trying to tell us we’d have to wait for it to be shipped to us until she “got her manager to get it figured out in their system”.

I’m sad to walk away from this spot with a bad taste in my mouth, please be nicer to folks, especially when they have to wait 30 minutes in the cold for their bag of bagels!

text: Words cannot describe how delicious their bagels are. I mean, not only is their cream cheese incredible but their bagels, I mean, c'mon! A nice, soft, moist inner with a crispy outter. name: Jake B
text: I really like this place. I only discovered it a week or so ago, but I've already spent several lunches there with my daughter (who loves bagels). The people are friendly, the prices are good, and the quality of the food is absolutely first rate. I haven't gone too wide on the menu, just a bagel sandwich or two, and a few lightly adorned bagels. However, I feel like I have enough experience with the place to say that they really care about the quality of the food they serve. There's usually only a few varieties of bagel available: a good thing, because they're all fresh. I have no doubt that the more elaborate sandwiches and salads rise to the same level of care and quality. It's just a basic deli, nothing is spectacular about the menu or the decor or the service, but it's a very high quality stop off for a quick bite at breakfast or lunch. It is one of my favorite places in Portland, and one of the first places I'll bring visitors from here on.

text:
Not as good as I expected based on Bon Appettit review.  We stopped by before noon yet they were already out of two things we ordered.  There is only one soup option - the maza ball soup.  The maza balls were good, but the soup a  bit thin.   The sandwitches options are limited, but if you like lox there are a lot of options.  I love lox but turns out having so much of them at one time was hard to handle, I had to leave some.  I was not impressed with the flavor of the bagles, I had better ones.

Finally, the bathroom facilities are totally inadequate.  There is one  unisex bathroom shared by patrons and staff, there was always a line while we were there.  I had
to wait 9 minutes and the saw the person go back to the kitchen. That's how I know this one bathroom is shared by all.

Two soups, two sandwitches, two soft drinks  were 57 dollars.

I was in NYC a month ago and had the opportunity to try Russ and Daughters. I have been craving food of that caliber since. I was so happy to find Rose Foods and say that I actually found it better than anything I’ve had in NY. This place could easily open in NYC and have a 45 minute wait any day of the week but instead we have it all to ourselves up here in Portland.

I tried the everything bagel with herb CC, pastrami nova, onion, tomato and dill. I will certainly be back to try whatever else they have on offer.

name: Henry Quinn
text: Very good bagels and appetizing. Plenty of seating. Oooonly thing that gets me is that the patina of NYC deli falls away because the counter service is too patient and Mainey. You go in, you say what you want, you step aside: that's a bagel place. This is a Maine takeaway with subway tiles. I get it: no one wants this but me. And maybe it's even better this way. But it's a break in authenticity that for me, I mean, standing in line behind a couple with a stroller starting agape at the menu while they wonder how bagel stores work -- the facade crumbles and it all turns precious and cute. So yes, five stars for food. But if you know what a place that looks like this is actually like & how great that is, you're going to get cranky, as I just have.

text: Great bagels. All the usual things you would want for them as well. Keep and eye out for Pizza Bagel night! They were unexpectedly amazing. The service is fast and very friendly. Keep in mind, it is not the cheapest place for bagels. That's not what they are about. You are paying for, and getting, quality.

name: Mac Coldwell
text: Bagels are amazing. I tried the egg, cheese, and salami with hot sauce sandwich. It was a great combination of flavors. On ground floor. Handicap accessible. Very friendly served. Best bagels in Portland.

name: Steven Sidman
text: A bit pricey, but very very good. Excellent bagels and lox, good coffee, fresh squeezed orange juice. Friendly people, simple but comfortable place to eat. The main issue is finding parking. They're right on Forest Ave, but some of the side streets generally have spaces.

name: David Richards
text: Pricey, hipster hangout with undeniably great kosher deli fare. Prepare to take out a second mortgage for a truely great hand crafted Ruben.  Worth it?  Not everyday, but boy is it good!

name: Evan Linger
text: Bagels are 10 out of 10. I’m vegan and they even offer a vegan spread despite having a predominantly meat/dairy heavy menu. If Mr Bagel is like Olive Garden this place is like going to Italy to eat. I love this place.

name: Mitchell Stein
text: Great bagels and everything that goes with them. A little pricey but worth it.

name: christina hattaway
text: The lox bagel is so yummy with the herb CC. They sell out of bagels early, so by noon time you are at slim Pickens. Matzah ball soup (with chicken) broth is very flavorful- I'm not big on the matzah ball texture in general.

name: Jenn J
text: So good. Great atmosphere. Feels like you are in Los Angeles!

name: John nauyokas
text: Bagels are good. Workers were friendly. It's a cool spot. They have tons of merch to sell. I'd visit again if it wasn't out of the way for me. I do like it tho

name: West End Village School
text: This is my new favorite breakfast spot and place to do a little computer work when i have a few hours to kill. I a addicted to the "good deal" lox bagel sandwich. It is so great to have an authentic Jewish deli in Maine, definitely check this pace out! The dark rye bagels are so good!!!

name: Jen George
text: I hve never been inside a bakery that didn't sell sweet pastries. But the food was excellent, and they had vegan cream cheese. Woohoo!

name: Jeff Howe
text: Busy Sunday morning at Rose Foods, first time visit for us. Simple theme: bagels, in many variations. Order, and find a spot to sit, and they'll come and find you with your order. Had a classic everything bagel with cream cheese and lox, very nice. They serve coffee and other beverages, too.

name: Meggan Dwyer
text: Yummy deli foods and great bagels.

name: Evan Caprari
text: Great Bagels. A little pricey (bagel, cream cheese, and a coffee will run you about $7) but all are very good. They do a special daily bagel flavor, the pastrami flavor was awesome.

name: Alexandra
text: Good food, fast service.

name: Vincent Aceto
text: This place is 5 stars for one reason...because this review can't put in 10 stars. Seriously, Rose Foods is the place to go for a breakfast sandwich that is out of this world. I had their newest "L Train" which has pickled jalepenos and oyster mushrooms on it. Locally sourced from North Spore Mushrooms out of Westbrook. These shrooms make the sandwich amazing. And yes, the bagel was the best I have had. Make the trip, enjoy the personable staff and relaxed surroundings.

name: Nick Wilson
text: Yum! Good addition to Portland, great addition to neighborhood. Family friendly spot

text: I was excited when I heard that there was a new bagel place opening up in town but I left today feeling a little disappointed. It's one thing to have high quality fish on a bagel for a high price but that doesn't mean they have to charge high prices for the simple stuff too. 8 dollars feels steep for a bagel with cream cheese and an ice coffee. Basically this isn't the place to go for a simple breakfast, as you need be prepared to drop some serious dough - some sandwiches run as high as 16 dollars. Additionally the concrete floors and stark white walls of the cacophonous dining area left a lot to be desired. And in the end the prices stack up a little too fast for me to visit this place with any regularity.

name: Steven Jefairjian
text:
This lunch was not good at all... two people sharing two sandwiches and a side of potato salad... one Pastrami on rye, the other Corned Beef on rye... served on stale, dry bread no less!!

I knew something was WRONG when asked if I wanted the bread toasted... an old trick to disguise old dry bread...  Ha!! The meats were just OK... sliced way too thin, not outstanding as advertised... there went another star... 🌟💣💥

I'm a New Yorker, living in Portland a long time, but one does NOT forget NYC fantastic deli food... this is not it! THEY should not make claim for being in that category... they can't cut it, reputation or otherwise... ick!! 🌟💣💥

The potato salad was awful... the potatoes were NOT firm yet tender... they were hard and chewy. Then, it was at least one quarter celery... a bit too much. The dressing was watery and tasteless. Instead of classic style pickle spears, they served chunks of rolled cut dill pickles, three small chunks per sandwich... totally stingy... I was embarrassed to ask for more...🌟💣💥

I had a can of Dr Browns Cream soda...a NY classic drink with this type of sandwich for $3.50... ridiculously expensive and warm. The celery seltzer was a good brand, but for $3... Noooo waaaay.

Oh, one OTHER THING... at the register, there were refrigerator magnets, I thought they were gratis, like most businesses do... they wanted $2 each. I mentioned they need a sign stating the price... the cashier caught an attitude for questioning the matter... then showed me a tiny price sticker, like you find on canned foods, barely visible on the display, but not on the said magnets... not obvious in the least... she and her demeanor need to go.

As a Native New Yorker... I could have READ HER THE RIOT ACT AND LET HER KNOW HOW SHE WAS PISSING ME OFF... but I remained a gentleman...  THIS PLACE ISN'T SO UPSCALE, THAT ONE WOULD EXPECT BS ATTITUDE FROM A CASHIER!! 🌟💣💥

Lastly, the ambiance and attractive decore are nonexistent... it looks like a dump!! It wasn't very clean and neat... looks like furnishings from Mardens clearance basement.

INITIALLY, I was so excited to go there, we talked about coming back for the fish platter, bagels and cream cheese...At $32.... but it's not going to happen after today's Fiasco.
The nice woman that brought us our lunch was the only enjoyable part... she smiled, was friendly, a very nice touch.

This was NOT WORTH THE $40 WE SPENT.  GRRRRR 😖😨

text: This is the way a theatre experience should be; comfortable seating in recliners, clean, great acoustics and great views from every seat in the theatre. With 12 theatres the viewing areas are smaller than older theatres which I liked as well. The concession stand had a good variety at the infamous movie theatre exorbitant pricing. I had a large Coke along with M&M peanuts which were good for about $10. Ouch!!! When all is said and done, if you're wanting to see a movie I highly recommend Cinemagic & IMAC in Saco.

name: Rory Benjamin
text: Without a doubt the best option for IMAX viewings in the greater Portland area. The reclining seats are comfortable and roomy. Being able to buy your tickets at the kiosk and select exactly where you are going to sit is a huge plus. Concessions are the usual level of mildly absurd pricing, but that's what you're going to see at every theater nowadays.

text: This was my first time seeing a movie in IMAX and it was absolutely incredible! We had so much fun! Their seats are unbelievably comfortable! And the popcorn was yummy.

text: Absolutely amazing and will definitely go back. Anyone who's rated below a 5 star for this cinema is only salty bdays they couldn't get decent seats. Ignore the negative comments, use this theatre anytime!! Will definitely be back.

name: Matthew Calder
text: Love the seats and the setup in the theaters. Love that you choose your seats when getting tickets. Prices on food are a good bit higher than other theaters.

name: Tarah Blakeslee
text: Love this theatre. Super comfy reclining seats, most of the seating has a good view. Very clean as well. Not too busy that you can't see something last minute. Food is pricy but it's a movie theatre so that's to be expected. Also attached to a pizza place so you can grab a bite to eat and only need to get a small sized popcorn :)

name: cwalkenisgod
text:
The only IMAX theater in Southern Maine.

I come to this location whenever there's a huge movie event I want to experience in IMAX. We came to watch Star Wars: The Last Jedi.

I had a good experience. The line to get in was handled well, and there didn't seem to be any chaos. The employees all seem really nice and professional.

The parking lot is pretty big, but it was still overcrowded. People were parking elsewhere and walking over. Our car was hit by someone trying to park in a spot that wasn't actually a parking space.

The interior was about as clean as a theater could be - but I feel bad because people just dump their popcorn everywhere and leave trash. Pick it up, people.

The bathrooms are small, and the lines usually begin forming directly after a movie is finished. On top of that, their food is insanely overpriced ($5.00 for a hot dog) and not prepped well.

Still, the movie-viewing experience itself was great. Would definitely recommend if you want an IMAX experience.

name: Briant Gaudet
text: Went to see Mr. Rogers last night.  It was a great movie.  Now the theater, I have to say wow!  Haven't been able n awhile, seats were wide and luxurious. They even have motorized recline (helps to make you forget all the commercials before the movie)!  Only wierd thing is full recline next to someone you don't know... Great experience non the less

name: Steve Donovan
text:
A great experience once again at One Longfellow. Robyn has been a great influence on the music scene for over 40 years. The fact that he could be here in our small town in such an intimate room was remarkable. The fog of emotional ambiguity that hangs over his deeply poetic lyrics was partially lifted by the banter of his "transparent mind" between songs. With the help of Longfellow's amazingly talented and attentive sound engineer, Chris, the depth and richness of his enduring music was presented on one acoustic guitar, one harmonica, one fabulously intricate and unique voice and vision.
Major kudos to management, staff, and volunteers for their commitment to maintaining this valuable venue.

name: David Clark
text: Saw NY band "Upstate" tonight. What a fantastic fun upbeat young band. Original music sung in beautiful 3 part harmony by three women, backed by three men on bass, sax/keyboards, and Cajone (drums in a box). I didn't know anything about this band, and that speaks volumes about how great this venue is. Small, intimate, not a bad seat in the house. One of Portland's best venues, if not the best. And definitely see Upstate if you get the chance.

resp.text:
We agree, Dawn. However we are only complying with existing state laws for breweries. Many of us have been fined for allowing dogs in the past. Even without the addition of a kitchen we are regulated by the Maine Department of Agriculture as a food production facility, and no animals are allowed indoors or outdoors.
Trust me, we regret not being able to allow dogs as well, but as all breweries move forward it will become more risky/difficult to bend the rules in this way.
I hope this helps.
Cheers!

I was excited to see that on the menu since I just had kolsch in Germany. Pizza was amazing as always. If you didn't think mashed potatoe and bacon could be awesome on a pizza you are wrong. name: Will Kessler
text: Been going for ages.  Recently, they have eliminated the perennial favorite with roasted garlic-kalamata olives and red peppers; replaced it with newer over-cheesed cauliflower-mushroom pizza (way too much).  Plain cheese and tomato pizza is still OK.  They literally had someone cleverly write up a disclaimer for the menu: "Our pizzas a crafted each individually, we do not offer 1/2 pie topping options."  They just want to sell you more slightly-overpriced whole pies.  Last time we went in, the service was fawning and disruptive, with unnecessary check-ins every 2 minutes.  Our waiter referred us to the 1/2 pizza legalese, and it sounded pretentious as soon as it was read out loud.  Otto's seems to be getting more and more precious each time we go.  This restaurant has, perhaps jumped the shark.

text: Excellent, gigantic slices of pizza. It’s really more like really good soft bread with toppings than regular pizza. It’s amazing. We also got the meatballs as an app and they were wonderful. Would be 5 stars except all but one of their five types of pizza were “out of stock” when we ordered, yet the table behind us and some phone orders were able to order and get different types before we got ours. That was frustrating, but I suspect it was just bad timing on our part. Oh well! Will definitely make this a regular stop every time we are in Portland.

text: Great value, and the Sicilian crust pizza is unmatched anywhere I've been.  Thin crust (neapolitan) is also quite delicious.  Staff is down to earth if a bit surly from time to time, and not at all precious about their kitchen; while the atmosphere is surprisingly low-key -- perhaps why they've stuck around so long. text: Amazing Pizza! The crust is both tasty and unique, great flavors!

name: MC Cheddar Bob
text: Live music at the slab pizza parlor today. They are setting up as I speak. This place is off the chain. Come on down and grab a pie. Hang out side and hear live music. I may see you here. This place is so fresh and so clean clean.

name: Kim Crabb
text:
Slab's thin crust is our favorite pizza in Portland. I think the sauce makes it the best.

We usually get take out, but the best time to go is during the summer when you can sit outside on their huge patio, often with live music. Inside is pretty small, but the ambiance is great. The only bad experience was during one inside visit. When we arrived and asked for one of the booths, we were curtly told we couldn't sit in one of them because we only had two people. Then they sat two people there by the time we were done with our dinner. It wasn't a great experience.  :/ Otherwise staff is pretty good.

name: Lucas York
text: Love love love it! 💘

name: Martha VanHorn
text: Love it! Both thin AND very think pizza done well.

name: Jay Ferrante
text: Still delicious even in a pandemic. I'm glad they made the flavored slabs the same size as the cheese. Ugh I'm soo full. But there's still more delicious pizza. Call the ambulance for me 🤣

name: Jeremiah
text: Slab is incredibly unique and delicious. Their slabs (pizza) are one of a kind and cannot be compared to any other pizza place in town. Wonderful tap list for beer drinkers. They introduced a thin crust pizza which is wonderful, if you're looking for a pizza that's more in line with "normal" pizza places.

name: tarek BIZRI
text: The place has one of the most tasty pizza I ever had. A slice of pizza weighs 1 pound. cant complain. Perfect toppings.

name: Kevin McNeil
text: Delicious 1-pound thick crust pizza in a Sicilian style but with a hint of sweetness and extra cheese. Thin crust tomato pies also available but require 20-25min lead time. Sandwiches, Sicilian “street food” starters and sweets round off the menu. Beautiful interior and spacious patio with communal picnic table seating under the lights in front of a small stage for live music. Twenty tap rotating drought menu with an excellent selection of local and non-local breweries. Good for kids especially in the outdoor area and on the earlier side. Highly recommend.

name: K MM
text: Best pizza in Portland hands down, so good.  The thin crust pizza is amazing, there is no better pizza joint around.

name: Josh Reali
text: Great food, nice atmosphere, prices make you want to cry. BUT definitely going back. What's up Steve (the owner), glad you got away from Micucci's, killing it man

name: Joanna X
text: The food is amazing! And the staff is great! I had to stop on a very hot summer day and the bartender did a random act of kindness that I really appreciated. The food is really fantastic!

name: Mac Coldwell
text: This is one of my favorite doughs for a pizza. Like the sauce, there is a sweetness to it. It is a perfect lunch for me and priced right.  I normally order to go, but the service whether I'm sitting at one of the booths or grabbing a slice on the quick is always pleasant and on point. They also support local music with their patio in the summer.

name: Nelson Mondale
text: We got takeout because if pandemic, and it was pretty good, but the dough was incredibly cakey and the sauce was a little sweet (for my taste) - I cannot speak to the atmosphere of the restaurant. From the outside - the restaurant seems like a sports bar. Slab is very descriptive of the pizza.

name: Karen Gilbert
text: Awesome pizza spot, This slice was the My Big Fat Greek Wedding $9.5 you can't tell by this pic but it was huge. Took half of it home. Yummy!

name: Mike D
text: Probably the best tasting pizza in Portland. Dense dough, great flavor. Outdoor seating area is nice, recommended!

name: Donna Sheffield-Greene
text: Came late, choices of pizza limited, shredded salad with lime vinaigrette and curried chicken, excellent. Good choice of beer.

name: paul pizzimenti
text: Food was pricey, but good

name: Mark LoGiurato
text: Authentic Sicilian food - pizza is very good!  nice variety of beer and cocktails.  The staff is friendly and accommodating.

name: James Ganley
text:
Really enjoyed the white pizza w garlic and pesto, and their wedge salad is probably the best I have had.
Good service, enjoyed the patio and overall atmosphere.

name: Keith Gosselin
text: We had great service from our waiter and the food was excellent, as usual. The draft board on this visit was not too exciting. Hopefully next time it'll be better, at least from my perspective.

name: Savannah Carlson
text: Holy moly this is good pizza. Kind of different but incredible. Super pillowy. The cauli crust was insanely good. Really fluffy, and gluten free

name: Robbie King
text: Delicious food served alfresco.

name: K Jacobs
text:
Awesome! Stopped in for happy hour special. The pizza is really good and unique, a hand slab is a very generous portion and will more than fill up the average person. We also had (Crisps and dip) which were also fantastic.
We brought our 9 month old with us and they had high chairs all ready to go and are clearly kid friendly. The space is really nice and has a hip yet casual vibe to it.

name: Jill Banks
text: Hand slab is the best deal and delicious!

name: Johnna Sheppard
text: The pepperoni slab was legit. Good amount of food for a decent price. Definitely will be back!

name: Mark Maguire
text:
Peperoni slab pizza is awesome,  arrive hungry.
Great selection of local beer as well.
Great atmosphere and great service.

name: Miles Stanton
text: Hands down the best pizza I've had since moving to Portland. The slices are HUGE and the crust is super fluffy. I can not say enough great things about this place! Side note, the staff is wonderful and very friendly, especially the guy at the register! He deserves his own 5 stars!

name: Troy Tracy
text: Don't get me wrong, the pizza is amazing, but I went with the BLT today and was glad I did. It was a great balance between the salty, the savory, and the peppery greens. The bartender was friendly and our food came out fast. Another great experience!

name: Cedric Fredrickson
text: This is the best place to go for parties or if you want a huge slice of pizza with a beer. I have always loved Slab, their pizza never ceases to amaze me

name: Michael Hopkins
text: Delicious hand slabs and other Italian items. Simple and well done. Good beer selection too.

name: James Denz
text: I had the spicy meat wedge and it was delicious. My friend had the 1/2 slab with pepperoni. The dough is think and tastey. They have a great selection of local craft beers and spirits.

name: Jess Segal
text: The hand slab pizza is the best! Delicious crust, sauce, and cheese! If you want a lot of carbs, this is the place to go.

name: Nancy Sheppard
text: Delicious food, really cool atmosphere

name: Rebecca Flaherty
text: Nice small diner. Larger beer menu over pizza menu. Crust is awesome. The servings are great. They are over-the-top on toppings. Bathroom is not handicapped accessible because need to go down stairs. Brick oven cooked pizza. Outside seating available.

name: Jason Talbot
text: Amazing food, delicious beer, amazing dessert and an epic team of people. They have all the things! I love just grabbing a meatball sandwich or slab of pizza and a drink before heading out to the book store or Arcadia across the street.

name: Dennis Rosenshein
text: The Hangover Slice the sfnich or even just the Classic Slab LOADED with Pepperoni absolutely worth it, they have amazing flavors and Pizza here if they have a special running you MUST try it.

name: Brandon Foster
text: This place in a must of u r looking for pizza and around the block.

name: Cody Doyle
text: Pizza was undercooked, but you do get a lot of pizza for a small amount of cash. We got the classic "Slab" pizza, and it wasn't too bad, but like I said, it was doughy and undercooked in the center. Not sure if it's supposed to be like that because the it's so big, or if we just got an off batch.  I may be back to try the "normal" pizza instead of the Slab.

name: Shaughnessey McArthur
text: Massive slices and one of the best slices of pizza you can get around Portland

name: Kristen Fissell
text: get the sfinch. we live in south Portland and this is our favorite go-to pizza spot to pick up some pizza (one slice is a lot!) and it never gets old. love this place.

name: Pamela Duplissis
text: Absolutely perfect!  From the comfortable modern atmosphere, the carefully crafted menu items, cocktails, mocktails, and knowledgable staff everything here is A+++

name: Herb Warren
text:
Pretty casual place with excellent food and a nice selection of beer.
The pizza is excellent - the crust is thick, chewy, and yeasty without being too dense. They claim a slice - a "hand slab" is about a pound, and I'd have to agree. It's more than I can easily eat in a sitting, but its still good the next morning for breakfast.

name: Joseph DeMartin
text: Amazing thick crust and a great selection of beers on tap.

name: Glory Gomez
text: This place was AMAZING !!! Best pizza I’ve had since I left NYC seriously ! Don’t get fooled though! I ordered four slices thinking they’d be regular triangles to my surprise extra giant pizza. Supper yummy, it was fluffy but dense dough. They had the option of thin crust too. We had chicken wing appetizers as well. It was very little quantity for $7 they just gave us tree prices of chicken but honestly the sauce was delicious and it came with bread. They serve you water in the words smallest cutest cups and they leave a giant jug of wanted for you to refill which is kinda fancy. I would come back if this was closer to me daily.

name: Fred Bopp
text: Great pizza overall, their vegan pizza is out of this world!

name: DENISE GRIFFIN
text: Delicious 🍕 great employees!

name: Ed Kimlin
text: Outstanding Sicilian style deep dish with high quality crust and toppings.  Recently ordered pizza for 50 (office lunch party) and the Slab team came through on time with delicious made-to-order quality pizza (e.g. no drop off in quality for a large order).  You can't go wrong with Slab, and you definitely won't leave hungry!

name: Dillon Ballweber
text: Great service, huge "slabs" of pizza. Took one home and reheated it in the air fryer 😍

name: Jill Falkenberg
text: Slabs are fluffy clouds of heaven.  Not your typical pizza establishment- there are only a few preset topping options on the slabs/wedges, but there are lots of other entree types available and an excellent craft beer selection. A cozy atmosphere inside, and a nice patio outside with the occasional live band.

name: Patricia Little
text: Good prices nice atmosphere and even better pizza

name: Sina Skates
text: So much gluten, so good... just sayin'. Reminds me of Pinocchio's in Harvard Square. This place is the real deal. Wish there was better parking, especially for take out. They do deliver. Pizza warms up great in the oven. We cut each hand slab into 3 peices at home, serve with salad and lots of dressing, to dip the extra bread into... wish they had a simple ceasar salad to go along with the pizza. That would be perfect!

name: Hailey Young
text: It just wasn't my thing. Staff was very nice but for pizza that expensive I felt very disappointed. I love pizza and it was the first time I've ever not eaten it because I just didnt like it at all. My dough tasted uncooked and like it better after they cooked it a bit longer. It was just a strange experience. I will likely not be back.

name: Andreas Schöllmann
text: One of my favorite pizza joints in Portland!

name: Hannah Kliphan
text: The pizza is so good!

name: Chriss Sandling
text: Such a limited menu. It's really a sit-down draft beer restaurant that you can order a few kinds of pizza at if you want. It advertises the slabs of pizza as a main attraction instead, though.

name: Scott N
text: Awesome

name: Kyle Martin
text:
The pizza is phenomenal and sandwiches are good, but the salads with the meats is phenomenal. The dressing is delicious and the Italian meats are out of this world. The balance is wild.

Enjoyable space and bright.

Staff is helpful and friendly. Definitely a nice lunch or dinner spot.

name: Esley Leda Sonnikson
text: Not impressed. It definitely wasn't bad and the staff is very nice. Just not fantastic and I'd rather go somewhere else for pizza, especially when considering the price.

name: Mufaddal Jafferji
text: Got the thin crust and it was tasty.

name: Sharyn Lincoln
text: Food was amazing. Slices are HUGE but delicious. Beer list is fantastic. Good number of draught selections and a lot of local choices.

name: Jessica DeLisle
text: That's a big pizza.... It's not great but it's good. And there's certainly bang for your buck in portion size.

name: RickC1916
text: Slab pizza (basically sicilian) is excellent. The sauce gives it a distinct flavor.  Careful ordering beer. Some of it is sour beer, the new trend. I don't care for it but wasn't warned when I ordered it.

name: Michael Cassidy
text:
Pizza had very good flavor, could have used a little more sauce and toppings though. We had a half slab and the dough was a good inch thick was very good and well cooked.

The service unfortunately was horrible. I think we got the bartender not sure. He seemed bothered with us from the first interaction. We had 3 adults and 4 kids in our group, all good kids so that wasn't the issue. We had never been there and had to ask about the size of the pizzas to figure out how much to get. He first looked at us like we were crazy to be asking the size. Their round pizzas had the size on the menu the rectangle slabs did not. After he asked me what I meant I said that about the round pizzas and again had to ask how big are the slabs. He held his hands in the air and said the single was like this big.. and offered no more. After waiting for him to tell us the next 2 sizes I asked how big is the half slab was. He said like the size of 4 heads??? What does that even mean.... My wife's head is much smaller than mine.. I asked can you just give me a size inches by inches?? He held his hands in the air again and said like this big.. Keep in mind we are sitting at a rectangle table and he could have showed us on the table this wide by this long for the 3 different sizes and cleared up the whole thing very quickly. We decided on the half slab anyway and asked about it being cut into more pieces than the 4 it comes in. He pointed out there were plastic knives and forks on table.. I said yes I see them, but can they just cut it in to more pieces in the kitchen?? Again I got the crazy person look, but then he said oh yeah they can. This review is to long already and this is only about half of the dealings with this waiter so I will end it with this. The food we had was good and restaurant was nice, but if you choose to go here avoid the bar area so you can hopefully avoid this guy.

It was a Sunday evening so not overly busy.

name: Justin Costable
text: Very happy with the service. Staff were very helpful with questions about gluten free options. Excellent choice of craft beer on tap. Can't wait to go back

name: Allen Bourassa
text: It was good ,The slices of pizza are very big,the beer was good,nice atmosphere,the service could have been more personable.

name: Nick Guerriero
text: Best Sicilian pizza north of Boston. Best meatball subs in New England. Outstanding craft beer selection from Maine locals to Colorado. An outdoor patio with ample seating and live music. A must try if you're in Portland.

name: Scott Payson
text: Not awesome to me. Their idea of pizza is like a loaf of bread with some sauce and toppings - a truly massive amount of dough for the money. I might be better with it if they used organic flour but they definitely do not. And happy hour is 3-5p? Who's done with their day @ 3p? The Portland High school kids around the corner? Super popular place but I won't be among those legions again.

name: Michael Falzone
text: Excellent

name: Benjamin Moore
text: A hand slab can cure anything here.

name: Erin Doyle
text: This is my favorite place for pizza in Portland. The slabs are made with super thick chewy crust and the sauce is just perfect. They have other great things on the menu as well for meat lovers and vegetarians alike. The prices are really affordable as well.

name: Robert Jorgensen
text: Best pizza , huge slices, fair prices. I love it.

name: Callahan Bryer
text: A really great place. Food is amazing, and setting is light/full. 5/5.

name: Gregory
text: The pizza and sandwiches here are fantastic. Staff is always helpful as well. Truly one of the best pizza spots in Portland.

name: Adam Carpenter
text: The best pizza in town by far!

name: Shaun Gilbride
text: Great vibe. Awesome beer list. Rayshella was fantastic! She was a great local guide. Fight your instincts for pizza and grab a sandwich. They are epic.

name: Lucas Snyder
text: Great drinks and pizza

name: Scott Nutting
text: Everything was delicious. The basic "slab" pizza is incredible. The staff was incredibly friendly and they had some top notch beers on tap. Personal ax to grind: pizza joints should offer turkey pepperoni among their toppings.

name: Maine CarGuy
text: Love these folks! Nice people, great food, huge portions (slabs) at $6 for a one pound slice. $3 happy hour if you eat in instead of take-out. Some of the best tasting pizza anywhere! And... They let me stand in the arm entryway while I was locked out of my truck on a freezing night, waiting for AAA.

name: Ryan Fitzgerald
text: Good was great, awesome music, had open mic night for Monday's, really great service and inexpensive, tastey pizza and beer.

name: Tina K
text:
Slab pizza is the BEST around.
Thick
Fluffy.
Oh so good. You will not be disappointed.

name: Brandon Hepler
text: Really nice location. Not crowded. Decent pizza.

name: Aaron Solet
text: Not a typical pizza joint. The simple "slab" is a meal in a single slice. Doesn't sound all that exciting but it-is-delicious. Look further for interesting combinations and beer options. Don't expect to build your own pie combo. The menu is very good but it is set.

name: R .P.
text: Great thick crust pizza. Nice beer list. A happy hour deal that can't be beat. Very nice staff & always a great atmosphere. Especially when they have live music outside.

name: Benjamin Hickson
text: One of the best pizzas in town. On the higher side for price but worth it. Not an everyday pizza snack though

name: Joe C

name: Gavin Barbour
text: Service wasn't the best, was a little slow but the pizza was very good.

name: Azizah Alawadhi
text: Thick dough & yummy pizza

name: Wendy Haltom
text: Had the cauli Gf dish. It was amazing! Others had the slab & said it is to die for.

name: Daniel Doucette

name: Sir_ Fowler
text: This is a very great place to grab some thick crust sicilian pizza, every time I've been here i've had a good experience and thoroughly enjoyed the pizza.

name: Debbie Siegel

name: Deborah Penham
text:
I really don’t see the big deal about this place. The “pizza” I got was more like a Sicilian, so I think they should call it that. There was a tiny shred of cheese on my slice, which was disappointing. The bread itself was good, but I paid for pizza, not just bread with a little marinara, which is what I got.

Went once, I probably won’t go back unless someone I’m with is determined to go. I just don’t get the hype. There’s better pizza out there.

If you want poofy bread with a little sauce, then check it out.

The LAST item I want to talk about is the street orange chicken.. seven bucks for two drumsticks. Kind of threw me off balance. The taste was great - but 2 drumsticks for $7 seems off. I was going to give Slab 4 stars, but with the upbeat, friendly, and attentive service, it deserves a 5. Try it out.

name: Seth Page
text: Great food and beer selection. Two Slab salads and a split hand slab is enough for two people and it is under $20.

name: Ryan Anzaldi
text:
As a newcomer to Maine, my first priority was to find out where I could get the best bang for my buck when it came to eating out. I was overjoyed to discover The Slab met all my requirements and more!

Featuring a host of delicious local draughts, and the famous sicilian-styled "slab" pizza, The Slab is a local favorite. The quality of the food is matched beautifully by the quality of the service. The staff is extremely knowledgeable, and very friendly, often checking waters and insuring that the dining experience of their patrons is second to none.

The prices are very agreeable, especially when you consider the quantity and quality of each entreé offered, the most famous of which being the aforementioned pizza on which the restaurant bases their name.

The pizza is absolutely incredible, and I maintain that it's the best pizza I've ever had in my 27 years of living. The slices are roughly the size of a full grown man's hand, and THEN some. Delicious spices and a heavenly tomato sauce compliment an assortment of melted cheeses layering the top. Alongside, one can always find a rotating selection of local beers, ciders, and wines.

I love bringing friends and family here when they come to visit, and I eagerly await my next slice!

name: Jordan Zoretic
text: Great thin crust pizza that is easily customizable.

name: Robert Benn

text: The sauce is incredible and if you like thick doughy crust then you'll love their pizza.

name: Teresa Vaubel

Pretty disappointing.
I ordered the mushroom wedge and got a HUGE hunk of BURNT bread (everyones crust was black) with about an inch of sauce, cheese and a couple mushrooms.
How anyone could send out food obviously burnt is strange to me.
Wait staff was unprofessional, burdened, and hung around in groups at what was a station outside, just barely checking in on folks.
Waited 20 mins for a glass of water, and everything was over priced.

I enjoyed the ambiance, the music I was there to see, and our company.
I wouldn't go back, overrated.

I love sfincione, so would have loved a more authentic version (more breadcrumb, onions, anchovy, less tomatoes) but that is really a minor quibble.

Can't wait to try their thin crust.

text:
Absolutely great. My work has me delivering food from various restaurants in Portland and the staff at Taj are always the most friendly and nice people to work with.

On top of that, their food is delicious, I've never had a bad experience here taste wise. It may seem a little pricy, but the cost is more than worth the high quality cuisine that they provide.

If you do decide to stop by, I recommend the Chicken 65.

Overall, Taj is a place to go for simply good food made by good people.

name: Ashlee Smith
text:
My absolute favorite place to get take out. Ive been struggling with celiac disease for the past 6 months since I found out. This restaurant has a majorally gluten free menu and little cross contaminación.
I miss deep fried foods and "street" type foods. Instead of wheat flour, they use chick pea flour. They have deep fried onions and spinach- yes please.
You can get a pound of food here for $10, and still have left overs for tomorrow's lunch.
Their menu can be a little spicy, so i accompany it with a side of ranch and/or cream cheese.
*is currently available for delivery on doordash*

name: Rate Maine
text: By far the best Indian food I've ever had. Everything I've ever ordered is delicious and I just want more and more. I usually get the Biriyani with some naan and its to die for. The spices on the food are on point and the taste of the food is something I have only gotten at this restaurant. The next time you are craving Indian food, or looking to try something new, you should go to Taj, and then you will keep going back for more.

name: Joe Presser
text: Not to sound like every other local (hint hint, locals like this place that’s a good sign, bub) but Taj is where it’s at! Once quarantine’s over, you can bet imma hit up that lunch buffet again, it’s delicious and was my last lunch before all this Covid stuff happened. Did having the Taj lunch buffet right before quarantine make it easier to handle the drudgery of everyday life? Maybe, because now I can pick it up whenever I’d like. If you’ve read this far, just order from this place already!

name: Longbow Gaming
text: Got awful butter chicken that was way to sweet and tasted like tomatoes and sugar. My friend and I also got veggie curry and both of them were disgustingly sweet as well. I am not very picky about food but the people at this restaurant put way to much sugar into all the curries. Hi Bombay in Portland has good curry that is not sweet and actually has Indian spices in it. The curry here literally tastes like half sugar and tomato paste. A few bites of it made my stomach sick.

name: Tyler O'Brien
text: This is my go to for Indian food. This place is fantastic and the staff is super pleasant. During Covid they are take out and delivery only.

name: Samuel Pierce
text: Pretty good lunch buffet. Most dishes quite enjoyable and only sine with the telltale signs of buffet-sitting. I would enjoy going back for a night meal based on the quality of the food. The bread with the buffet was a real treat and or is very well priced.

name: Kristy Wagner
text: The best Indian food we've ever had in the Portland area. This is our go-to place for Indian food in the area.

name: Tom
text:
I hate to edit this review down, but it took two hours to get our takeout the other night. There was no discount or refund, no free naan thrown in, they just kept telling is it's almost ready. I get that it's a hard time to be a restaurant owner right now, but if you're slammed but can't turn away the business, at least be honest with customers, or do something for them.

Otherwise always a good choice. Affordable with a varied menu.

name: rishi lad
text:
I only ordered Samosa.
It was disgusting. They added Masala Dosa’s stuffing in it and the out-layer was soggy too.
Thats not Samosa!!! Change the name from samosa to fried masala dosa!
I do not recommend this place at all as they cant even make this basic dish properly!!

text: It's hard to find good Indian food out here, but it's worth the 35min drive it takes me to get to.

text: This is a favorite for Indian cuisine in Maine. I have not been disappointed with any dish I've ordered yet either in the dining room or to go. The staff is always warm and welcoming. As busy as I've seen the restaurant, I have yet to have an order messed up. They are on the ground floor with lots of free standing tables allowing for wheelchair access. If you are ordering to go during lunch or dinner, I'd call ahead because they are really busy and it will make sure your food is ready closer to when you need it.

text:
It's very reasonably priced and the service is good.

They also have really great food. I've been here at least 5 times and ordered different things each time. It's always been delicious. I haven't tried anything other than the Indian food yet.

The lunch buffet comes with naan and a ton of vegetarian and meat dishes to choose from.

text:
A great variety of good Indian food. The tastes and spice level options were perfect. It was nice to see a variety of patrons from India as well. I do have several small criticisms which can be remedied easily
1. The Masala Tea was off taste completely.
2. The amount of  lamb and chicken in two different entrees were miniscule.
3. No chutney were offered for free. 1st time ever.
Yet, the tastes of the sauces were exceptional and almost completely made up for the shortcomings.
Next time I will try the lunch buffet. I WILL BE back.

text: This place has excellent Indian food and service. Highly recommend, and even better they will sub coconut milk for dairy on request for us vegans!

It was only at the very end of the meal that we were told that the oven was broken. No apologies or explanations were given beyond this. Adding insult to injury were the severe stomach issues I suffered as a result of eating this food.

They have a sizable menu with a full page of vegetarian entrees. Located very close to stores and movie theater, very easy to find and ample parking available. It is on one level with no steps and would be accessible to those with special needs. I will be in the area again next week and plan to eat there again.

You might have to wait a while for a table depending what time you come but the wait is well worth it. Naan may also take a while if the place is packed, but oh is it so warm and good.

name: Lee T
text: Alert: Avoid Saturday night around 6pm. Very busy with people waiting. Long wait to have order taken, the staff seems a bit overwhelmed. Also with the opening and closing of the entey door the cold breeze comes in making the place less then cozy. So we will see how the food is. Also the people in line look don't look happy and are looking at us perhaps hoping we are done with dinner.  I am sure the wait will be worth it. It smells so good and it's only been about 50 minutes since we were seated. So cold here. Well the tandoori chicken is here. Ordered half tandoori chicken. Funny the menu said breast, thigh and two legs. Unfortunately it is only half a breast to fit on serving plate. The rest of the food arrived about 5 minutes later. Forgot the beer and chutney. My recommendation: tell the customer that the wait for dinner will be an hour or more and then offer some nan bread during the wait. Then the restaurant filled up all the tables.  We said well good thing we got here when we did abd got our order in.  We then talk for roughly 10 more minutes and noticed almost everyone else had their food before us.  So my friend got uo and asked about our food.  They said it will be 5 minutes till its out.   We waited 10 more minutes and nothing came to our table.  At that time we said if we dont have our food at the hour mark we are leaving.  At the 1 hour mark my friend went back and told them we are leaving because our food is not here.  They said it was coming right out and it would be 5 more minutes.  So after checking in around the 35 to 45 minute time wait they said 5 more minutes.  Then telling them we are leaving due to no food they said 5 more minutes was the last straw.  Noone came to us to say they made a mistake and they forgot us.  All they did was say its coming out soon.  No offers of taking some money off the bill due to the mishap.  They have horrible service and i will not be going back to this place ever.  P.S . Go to Pom's Thai instead they were packed and had our entrees out in 15 mins max. name: cwalkenisgod
text:
A great place for Indian food in Portland.

Hi Bombay is located in the "Cinamon Building", down the street from Brian Boru's and near the statue of the director John Ford.

The interior is cozy, clean, and the staff are very friendly and accommodating. There is a large television that constantly plays Bollywood dance routines, which is nice to have during lulls in conversation.

The food is amazing and pretty decently priced. They give you free papadum (very addictive spicy/crispy bread, almost like tortilla) at the beginning of the meal and their garlic naan is to die for. My favorite dish is pretty basic - chicken Tikka masala - although I love most of their dishes I've tried.

Would definitely recommend for a night out if you're in the area, but they also have carry out.

text:
I ordered a lunch special over the phone to pick up.  The old man on the other end of the line kept trying to up-sell me to the dinner portion.  I had to refuse more than once.  Then he kept asking, "What else?"  "I just want the lunch special", I said.  "Not even bread?  You aren't going to get anything else?", he said.  "Is that a problem!?" I asked.

Rude.

When I came to pick up and pay, he made a comment that I was paying with "big money", a $20 bill.  It came to $8.51 after tax.  He gave me only $11 back and kept the change.  I can understand if it were a couple pennies or something, but 49 cents?  I just walked out, not wanting to get in an argument over 49 cents.

I open the bag, and I have a measly cup (literally one cup) worth of vegetable korma and a container of rice.

So, I basically just paid $9 for horrible service and a cup of basmati rice.

It has been a few years since I've been there.  I remember it not being bad, but I am never going back again and I recommend people go somewhere else.
