text:
I want to like Time and Tide. I really do.
The quality of everything I've had there is definitely good and there is no arguing that! However, sometimes their prices seem steep for what you get. $4.50 for a maple latte that's looks like it's about 8 oz is a little much for me when other places offer similar beverages at a better price / size ratio.

My actual only other complaint is that as a coffee shop downtown, it's a great place to sit and work and hang out. However, there is literally only 1 outlet for customers to plug into. So make sure your laptop or tablet is charged before going.

I've seen a couple of coffee shops pop up and close within the year in Saco/Biddeford area and I'd love for Time and Tide to stay open! Pretty cozy place but I think they have a lot of space they aren't working with. Adding some couches or comfier spots to relax would be great.

resp.text:
Thanks for the review, Daniel. We’re glad you like our coffee and appreciate your business!

Our maple lattes are 12 ounces - iced or hot - and use premium espresso, milk, and real Maine maple syrup. We never cut corners with ingredients and that is reflected in the price. We know our 12 ounce iced cups appear small (the shape is definitely strange) and are working on changing vendors.

We have two outlets available for customers, and often have people reconfigure tables to make it work for them. There are limitations in an old building.

We hope to see you again soon.

name: Ryan Anzaldi
text:
Listen: it's a Chinese food buffet place. You should know what you're getting into.

The food is great when it's fresh! I recommend going around 12-2, or 5-7. When it's not fresh, it's very bland and overly chewy. Usually fresh sushi, a lot of desserts, and a copious amount of different chicken dishes. Cocktails are wonderfully priced and usually generous.

Atmosphere is nice enough. It is a very large building, so there's almost never a wait time. The staff are extremely friendly, very attentive, and considerate.

If anything, the only qualms I have are as follows:

I feel like if they served less food initially, there would be a higher turnover, resulting in a more consistent stream of FRESH, HOT food, as opposed to 1-2 hour brackets of good food.

Lastly, the music selection is awful. Kenny G and "My Heart Will Go On" do not make for pleasant background. It's like being in the world's slowest and largest elevator, except there's food inside.

But again. It's a pretty good, relatively cheap place to get food, especially if you want a lot of food.

The food wasn't kept hot enough (which is likely why I got food poisoning), it seemed like almost every dish was primarily seasoned with sugar or corn syrup. I really like mediocre Chinese food, it's a comfort food for me, but this wasn't simply mediocre, it was utterly unacceptable. The price was very low, and it's obvious why.  I won't go back, I will warn others to avoid it, and I hope you take my warning seriously.

text: The food is great. The beer selection is pretty solid and there's bowling!

name: Jacqueline Mahoney
text:
This is the cleanest bowling alley I have ever been to. The inside of the building itself is beautifully designed. I felt like I was at a high class bowling alley made for the queen.
There is a restaurant in there that people were actually eating at.
The fact the people went to the restaurant at a bowling alley and didn’t even bowl says a lot about the establishment.

I didn’t get any food because I decided to get a few drinks instead, but the menu looked delicious. Next time I go I will drink less, enjoy the food, and bowl more.

If you aren’t a sad lonely person like me then you should go here on a date! Perfect atmosphere for it. Romantic lighting, what I assume to be great food, good prices, and booze. BAM your welcome.

name: Jacob Buttarazzi
text: Want to grab a beer with the guys? Go here. Want to go on a fun date? Go here. Want to get the kids out of the house? Take them here. Want a great dinner? Go here. This is a great place to go with a group of friends, I could hang out here all day. It has a slightly upscale vibe to it. It's really the only place in town that offers food and something to do.

name: kyle brown

resp.text: Thanks Kyle!!!

Haven't ten pin bowled since I was stationed in Montana (USAF) 1985 mixed doubles with my wife. Our friends and my wife and I had a great time.
For not being regulation lanes it was okay. Quite a bit pricey compared to other area alley's. Paying by the hour is not a choice I'd make again. Pushed the by the hour play, wasn't offered a by the string option, $30.00 for 1 and a half strings.

name: Michael S
text:
If you LOVE specialty drinks and a wide variety of beer selections this is the place to hang out in the Kennebunk area. I would highly recommend to anyone coming down from Portland or up from Portsmouth to give this place a try. It is very much worth the trip!

And if you enjoy bowling that's an added bonus. While it is a bit loud while you first arrive (think bowling alley noise levels) it soon fades away to an average noise level for talking within a group. I don't let it hinder me and this coming from someone with hearing problems but with assisted hearing aides.

Whether you love to bowl or not, this is a fantastic venue for small or large parties or just to hang out and enjoy the drinks, food and ambiance!

text: Really nice & friendly place - even the customers were friendly! It's very popular here, so be prepared to not have a place to sit. People like to work on their laptops and camp out at tables, so be aware. The coffee is excellent, and so are the Italian sodas.

text: They have the best hot chocolate I've ever had so far

name: Ashley McCollor
text: Super tasty. Gotta love those locally owned rosters. They brew and sell single origin roasts, which are probably the smoothest I have tried in Portland proper. You can order any number of coffee or tea drinks, which are all tops. A black coffee here does not need to be drowned in dairy (or non dairy, of which there are plenty of options)to be palatable. In fact, don't. This place looms large over the corporate mermaid across the street, that's for certain.

text: Extremely good coffee, great location, nice assortment of pastries to choose from.

text: The coffee was good and we enjoyed this place. Wish we had stopped here the days prior since it was our favorite of the trip. Park right outside is very nice as well and a good spot to sit and relax with your coffee or food.

name: Rob S
text: A great local spot for coffee. Make sure if you order online you check in, because they don’t start your order until you check in at the window.

name: Jeremiah
text: The best coffee shop in Portland's Old Port. Incredible staff, they are extremely knowledgeable, friendly and helpful. Would recommend going here over any other coffee shop in the Old Port. Great space to work, hang out and read, or just for a quick stop. Outdoor seating available in the summer months. Large open space with great natural light.

name: Michele Dixon
text: Great service. Snacks were good. Coffee was hot. Service was ok. It was clean. Need the key to use the bathroom. Needed a refill-- I'd like better service walking around cleaning up, and refilling coffee for more of a cafe feeling.

name: Anthony Vanaria
text: Dark roast’s are precarious. There’s a fine line between being thorough and burning the coffee. Many roasters understandably aim just shy of that line and serve a medium dark cup that maintains a certain level of acidity. If that’s what you like, great - but if you’re looking for a true dark roast, they do it right at Bard. I tried Coffee By Design, and Tandem. Both were great businesses, with thoughtful spaces: Bard just has a better dark roast. I can’t speak to the light-medium, but here in Portland, this is coffee the way I like it.

name: Nadine Thurston
text: Great latte and and awesome staff

name: Chris Taylor
text: Great pour overs, baked goods, and some amazing chai. The place is an awesome spot to sit and just be, or grab a great drink and head out. I like the openness of the space too. A definite stop whenever you're in the city

text:
Girl at the front counter taking orders (she was wearing an aloha shirt). Very friendly even though our interaction was short ☺️

I ordered an Iced Chai. Very creamy & made quickly. I feel like it could have been shaken more because a lot of it was at the bottom.

The interior was hip & warm💕

We were recommended to come here for the Nitro Cold Brew which my husband ordered and enjoyed 👍🏼

name: Zachary Goater
text: I've been to Bard a number of times. I find that the space can be, and often is, quite packed and the vibe leans mostly in the hipster-y direction. The coffee is good but doesn't carry the hype for me.

text: Nice place. Good coffee. Perhaps an extra restroom won't hurt 😊

text: Capuccino and service both great. Long wait for the bathroom, which was less great.

text: Bard Coffee is quaint and cozy, and their delectable food and drink is pretty good typical boutique coffee shop stuff. I do like Bard, and I would go more often if it weren't so crowded. It's been hard to find a seat inside for a few years now, and I'd rather go to a nearby coffee shop where there's room for me and my little laptop. But if you're walking by and want a Starbucks alternative, Bard Coffee is great for on-the-go!

name: Ryan Fortman
text: Great tasting coffee in cool mugs

name: The Maine Criminal Defense Group
text: What more can I say then the coffee is superb. Bard coffee is well known for their excellent beans and pour over preparations. They also have a wide variety of Bakery Goods like croissants and cookies. They get these items from some of the best local sources in Portland. You really can't go wrong with anything here. The only negative which I can find, and frankly doesn't affect my rating, is that you can never really find a seat. If you want to sit down and drink your coffee you'll need to come in, in the off times.

name: Paddy McCarthy
text: Excellent coffee shop a few blocks up from Commercial Street. The cortado I ordered was made with care and had bright flavors. Nice atmosphere -- so many coffee shops have loud retail drink coolers in the waiting or seating areas, and those are absent here!

text: The coffee at Bard was honestly as good if not better than my favorite shops in Seattle or Brooklyn. The space is large and nice and bright and has plenty of seating. The staff is super friendly and pretty quick. The nitro cold brew is smooth, creamy, and delightful. It's definitely an iced coffee you sip and enjoy rather than suck down. It's a great place to either sit and enjoy or close enough to downtown and the water to head down to the water for a nice view and relax. And they even have a couple of outdoor tables for nice days and enjoying your drink with your dog.

name: cwalkenisgod
text:
A reliable and affordable comfort food joint.

Located on busy Forest Ave, Stavros is one of my go-to spots for greasy sandwiches, pizza, and calzones. Sporting a decent-sized menu with many different options, you're sure to find something you like. Salads, pizza, hot and cold sandwiches, calzones, pasta, and even baked goods are available and there is even a parking lot which is rare for Portland.

The only reason I didn't give it five stars is that, as far as taste goes - some of the food is sort of bland (looking at you, fried mushrooms). But, it does the trick, especially on cold days.

Would highly recommend - and if you can, you should check out their cheese bread sticks because those are delicious.

text: I went in for an inspection, of which I failed and then went to the dealership the next day and passed. While I was there, I asked for and paid for an oil change. Based on the sticker, I should have another thousand miles to drive, but my car is saying I have 0% oil remaining.

resp.text: The inspection on Samantha's vehicle was done last October, so we're a bit confused as to why she is only now, in late February, making us aware of this situation.  According to our records, we identified a part that did not meet Maine State Inspection guidelines, so we had to fail the vehicle for inspection, and we recommended the appropriate service.  If another technician "passed" this part, then we would be very interested to know why.  We would also be happy to have Samantha bring the vehicle in for a re-inspection, and we would invite the Maine State Police to join us for that inspection.  If a mistake was made, we will be happy to correct it.  Otherwise, we stand by the results of our inspection.

name: Daniel Myers
text:
Good atmosphere and service. Our waiter was very friendly and helpful with questions about the menu, and the location of the restaurant combined with the comfortably small interior give it a cozy, small-town feeling.

The food left something to be desired. Appetizers were brought out quickly, but the entrees took close to an hour to arrive at our table from when the order was placed, and that's just for a party of two on a night that wasn't particularly busy. The rare steak I had ordered had a bit too much charring to ignore, and the person I was with had to go with a seafood dish because there are no vegetarian or vegan options anywhere on the menu, something that would be far more inconvenient to a more staunch vegetarian.

Not a bad location by any means, very comfortable location, but better for an event where you know you'll want to be in the restaurant for a long time, like a family gathering. Not as great for a casual dinner out.

text: The food is absolutely wonderful. A nicely curated menu, with a selection that will appeal to every palate (pork loin, beef shank, trout, mussels, and vegetarian options were on offer tonight). For an appetizer, I had the special of grilled broccolini with lemon and procciutto, and my companion and I shared mussels. My entree was buttermilk oriechette with wild mushrooms and delicioso squash. Everything was divine. The only reason for 4 vs 5 stars is the decibel level. While Blue Spoon is a tiny restaurant that fits about 20 diners, it is unbelievably loud! I could not hear my friend across the table and had to lean in to catch her conversation. The noise level really took away from the dining experience. I'm not sure I will be back despite the excellent food.

name: Samantha Bassett
text: Island Dog is my favorite brewery.  They are hidden on the back side of a building near the mall, but what that really means is there is always FREE parking.  They have games, you can order pizza to be brought in from Ottos, some nights they have entertainment too.  That’s not even the best part, they have fantastic beer.  They have quick and kind service. They give back to their community. Less than six months after they opened they started collecting for homeless veterans. They invite dog rescues in etc. You will find great beer, a smile and open hearts.

resp.text: Samantha, thank you for the awesome review. We are glad you enjoy our beer and taproom.  Jim

I would say if you want to dine in, look for a day with not great weather or away from normal dine times.  Picnic syle lobster roll is my favorite.  Food is worth it!

name: Hayeon Haylee K
text:
Classic Maine seafood restaurant!
Humungous fresh oysters
I killed lobster scampi which was a big portion and very savory.
Seafood casserole was a perfect match with fresh beer.

Loved waterfront view and the service was outstanding.

I wasn’t sure why my friend from Maine recommended this place in a tourist saturated area, but now I know why!

name: Justin McDowell
text: On busy, tourist saturated Commercial St., there is something for everyone when it comes to food. Lobster rolls are a dime-a-dozen (ok maybe like $20 each but everyone's got em). Us locals like the waterfront too ya know! We want great food at reasonable prices and if it's gotta be seafood, J's Oyster is my throw down spot. First off the service is always outstanding, we sat at the bar this time and the bartender was just great. She checked on us often, offered us her thoughts on the entrees, and didn't mind that we weren't ordering alcohol (were both sober). I veered of my usual path of lobster and steamers for dinner to try the broiled scallops casserole done in a honey butter reduction and sparsely topped with crumbs. Perfectly cooked and so good. My friend Tom got the lobster scampi which was flavored just right. Both scallops and lobster are mild mannered and the full flavors of both were present in the dishes. Haddock chowder for me to start and clam chowder for ole Tom Q. Both were good, although the haddock chowder was a bit bland and needed some additional salt and pepper. Both chowders were loaded with their namesakes. There are more hip and fancier places to eat in the Old Port but why be so extra?

name: Mari Sol
text: What a special place! I saw the episode of Anthony Bourdain in Maine and figured if it was good enough for him, then it's definitely good enough for me. The wait was a bit long but it was worth it. The Market Price for lobster was very reasonable that day. I feasted on lobster, steamed clams, fresh oysters and corn. The lobster was so tender, the shell so soft you could break it open with your fingers. It felt really special to be there. The staff was so friendly even though they were running around helping so many people in the bustling restaurant. For a little I was so enthralled by it all that I forgot that we're in the middle of a pandemic. Thank you so much!

name: Katie Hatch
text: A Portland institution. A great taste of the local waterfront scene. Very real - not contrived and full of locals! Great service, awesome local seafood and great value.

Also had crab stuffed mushrooms, again no flavor. Ordered the whole lobster dinner. The clams it comes with were very flavorful, the lobster was not. Service was average, no convo, just brought us our order. Had to wait on check. We were seated next to bar inside, a loud drinker guy was throwing loud F bombs one after the other and nothing was done about it. A couple seated close by were also bothered by it. Food was excellent and our server Amy was the icing on the cake! What a treat 👍 Lobster stew was simple yet succulent (and yes loaded with lobster), same for clam chowder. Crab melt was perfect - served w/ mayo on the side, and the haddock sandwich was another winner. Worth the trip!

text: J's Oyster on Portland Pier in Portland is a great choice for all things seafood. I really liked eating here and was able to try a couple of dishes and each one was tasty and delicious. I really like that this restaurant is on the water and offers beautiful views that really add to and enhance the dining experience. The service here was great and they went out of their way to make sure that we had everything that we needed. Overall this was a special and memorable meal.

Ok everyone! It took 3 years, but we made it back and brought our kids. J's is just as delicious as we remembered! This time we came in the summer, July 2019,  and during lunch.
We ordered the lobster meal with steamer clams, a side of raw scallops, the kids ordered Mac n  cheese and blts. The view of the boats and the ocean is gorgeous in winter and summer. The weather was warm and great!

The steamed clams did not disappoint. My wife got the seafood casserole. i got the scallop casserole. I was surprised the scallops tasted so sweet. My wife enjoyed her entree. We got the casseroles because we were seated outside and they did not have any heaters going. So we figured the entrees would stay hot to the end of the meal if they were in a ceramic dish. The service was very good.

Large steamers $22.50. Scallop casserole $25.00. Seafood casserole $28.00

name: mjtplayer
text: 2.5 Stars.  J's (or the "J-O") has been a Portland local spot for over 40 years.  I've walked past the place many times but had never been, so we decided to give it a shot - myself and 2 others.  What a disappointment.  We started off with the clam chowder and lobster baked stuffed oysters.  The clam chowder, or more like clam soup, was good (3.5 stars).  Full of clams and had a nice flavor, though a bit runny for "chowder".  The baked stuffed oysters were terrible (1.5 stars - pic attached), they look good in the pic, and when they were brought to the table, but wayyyy too much breading (which was soooo dry and flavorless) and you had to really look closely to identify lobster - at least I think it was lobster, more like small lobster flavored red dots in the breading.  Entrees we ordered were the cheeseburger (4 stars), which needed seasoning for some kind - very plain, but good.  Baked haddock with rice and veggies (3 stars - just meh) and lobster stew - which sucked (1.5 stars).  For $18, the lobster "stew" was more like lobster chowder, with a few mid-size pieces of lobster, but mostly shredded meat - such a disappointment.  If you're going out for seafood in Portland, there are much better options than J's.

text: J's is a fine local bar and a decent seafood restaurant, but don't expect anything special in terms of food, service, or atmosphere. The outdoor seating has a nice view of the piers and water, but also is essentially in the parking lot. Service was fairly slow and a bit grumpy. After ordering, we were told after 5-10 minutes that they were actually out of the lobster stew and got clam chowder instead. This took 30+ minutes to arrive, came after the other food, and was below room temperature when it arrived. It was good with nice chunks of real crab and other seafood, but the temperature was poor. The steamed clams were delicious, and require a little planning to eat, but with the butter, are awesome. A small bucket of them was more than enough to fill me up. The beer menu was just sad for such a great craft beer town. The most craft-y beer on tap was Sam Adams. I'd give them the benefit of the doubt on the food, but in a town with so many awesome seafood restaurants, there are so many better options. Dog friendly at the outside tables.

name: Trevor Chenoweth
text:
Feels a bit like a hole in the wall down on the docks, but it was recommended by a local bartender and the bar was full when we came in around 6. There is sparse decor but it feels authentic and the staff is friendly and jokes around with you a bit.

The menu is almost entirely seafood, I'm not sure why you would order something else. No fried seafood either. This is all pretty fresh stuff. The lobster dinner was solid although not the best lobster I've ever had. The steamers were quite good and served traditional. Clam chowder was very rich and good. Lots of ingredients, including bacon. We also had the scallop casserole, which was less a casserole and more some baked scallops in butter and a light breading. This was probably the best dish although it was a small serving. Delightfully sweet and very nicely cooked scallops.

Biggest problem, surprisingly: the oysters. Poorly prepared and bland and rubbery. Not good at all. And it wasn't because no good oysters were available. After dinner we went up the street to a different restaurant to quench our thirst for brine and found some incredible oysters. They weren't even separated from the shell, as any good shucker should do.

Service was also completely overwhelmed even though the restaurant wasnt full. She took about 10 minutes before even coming to our table for the first time and forgot one of our Cole slaw sides after two reminders.

Overall, pretty good seafood but didn't live up to its name or location. Very poorly executed.

name: Elizabeth Richardson
text:
Really comfortable hotel-like inn with unobstructed views of the bay, and maybe out to the ocean depending on your room! The Reading Room restaraunt in the main building was very good with excellent service, delicious food and a relaxed atmosphere with fabulous water views.

New infinity pool and jacuzzi tubs make for a relaxed environment out of the room but not off the property. The spa space provides the self-care solutions you deserve while enjoying the beauty of one of the nation's most visited national parks, Acadia.

The facilities could use minor upgrades, but otherwise it's clean, comfortable and the staff are available to meet your needs.

The gardens feature some beautiful seasonal blooms. 💐🌟🛎️🍸🐟

name: Girish Dhameja
text:
Amazing location in the heart of the town; amazing views from the balcony - that sunrise is from the balcony;  great people. The breakfast was perfectly packaged to pick up and head to your room, or sit by the pool.

There are a couple reasons why I gave it 4 stars rather than 5:
1. People don't follow social distancing while grabbing breakfast and the management doesn't provide any guidance
2. Coffee could have been better. They do provide coffee 24 hours by the reception. They have a better tea selection.

name: Dennis OBrien
text: Beautiful day for an outdoor lunch. Had the Covid special. Lobster roll sandwich. Good drinks good service splendid view. Definitely will come back. Unfortunately we had to run to early.

name: Anysia E.
text:
My new husband and I stayed at the Bar Harbor Inn and Spa for 7 days and 8 nights for our honeymoon at the end of May 2017. We could not have been happier with our choice! We knew we were going to feel right at home when we walked into the inviting lobby with a wood-burning fireplace. We loved everything about the Bar Harbor Inn! We stayed in the main building in a room with a king-size bed, overlooking Frenchman Bay. The view was amazing, and the room was so close to the main lobby and dining areas. Our favorite features of the room were the gas fireplace and the sitting area/porch.

The staff were all friendly and helpful, and even went out of their way to make sure that my new husband got a package that was sent to him (which was waiting at the post office over the holiday weekend) before we left at the end of our stay! Our room and bathroom were very spacious and everything was always neat and clean! The restaurant, lounge, and spa were also wonderful; the coupons for guests to eat breakfast/dinner in the Reading Room were a great incentive! The continental breakfast was more than adequate and very well maintained. We especially enjoyed the fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee cake!

For a full Bar Harbor experience, you definitely can't beat the location of the Bar Harbor Inn! The grounds are lovely and the views are breath-taking. Being able to walk to town, to the pier, and along the Shore Path was so nice! The weather was definitely cool (perfect for all the hiking we did), but we loved coming right before the summer season. The town definitely got more crowded over Memorial Day weekend, but the rest of the week was nice and quiet for our honeymoon. We already know we want to come back!

text: Very nice hotel. New infinity pool which is heated and great, with two adjacent hot tubs. They are upgrading the landscaping and doing an excellent job. The guys who work the front door are all exceptionally nice and professional.  The room was nice enough.  Nothing particularly negative to write, except two things: (1) the food/beverage service at the pool is spectacularly bad. The servers seem like they are hiding by the restroom. Once you place an order, it will take forever for the food to come out. The food, once you get it, is decent, and (2) the outdoor restaurant (which has spectacular views) serves mediocre food. Definitely do not get the lobster roll.  It is very dry and tastes quite poor.  On the other hand, the bar and table service inside is top-notch, and the charcuterie plate is delicious (although you will need to request extra bread). We had a minor maintenance issue which was never resolved,  but since it was minor,  I won't elaborate.  Easy access to downtown is a definite plus.

text: Only reason I am giving 4/5 stars is because they kept the doors open so dining inside was very chilly. Our server, Alex, was very nice. The corned beef sandwich was divine, the cabbage wasn’t too strong at all. Mostly, we were enamored with the truffle fries. They were SO good. Worth the visit for sure!

text: We've eaten here several times and have never been disappointed. Tonight we had a fish sandwich and Irish shellfish stew. The sandwich was good but the stew was outstanding. There were dogs allowed in the outdoor patio seating which was nice and they will give you a water bowl for your pet.

text: Paddy's is my favorite place to eat in Bar Harbor. The service has always been super great and friendly and the food is awesome. The prices tend to be high but you are certainly getting a good meal for it. The presentation of this place is great and usually has plenty of space wherever you sit. The bathroom is crazy nice! Highly recommend stopping here when you stay in Bar Harbor or even Ellsworth. Parking in Bar Harbor kind of sucks but it is kind of expected when staying in Bar Harbor.

text:
Went there this weekend and the food was good but not spectacular. Had the Fish Sandwich with fries, it was delicious. Husband had the Fish and Chips, said it was good. We had a Mojito that was to die for -but- it was $13!! The drink was around the same cost as our meals - should have been $8 for the drink but whatever, it was a fabulous Mojito.
I guess I didn't learn my lesson so we went there again the next day and had two Mojitos! lol
I do have to say the Nachos need a lot more cheese.

Parking is dang near impossible, you have to pay to park if you do find a spot. It is a wicked touristy area so good luck!
Downtown shopping and the restaurant has great views of the harbor.

I get to check-out and there ringing in as $3.99 and $5.98 . I ask the lady at self check-out to please adjust the price and she said that they were ringing in correctly.. I explained where they were and  that they were on clearance so she  had the other gentlemen follow me over! I show him the whole shelve of masks, all that were on racks with a yellow clearance stick showing $1.00 ( the big long shelves that are atleast 7 ft. Long and the whole thing was nothing but masks) He states that he can't honor the price because stickers are putting things in the wrong area, so I showed him a $1.00 tag that said mask on it and he still denied to give me that price.. I guarantee if anyone goes there tomorrow or the nexted day, they will see nothing but clearance stickers showing the $1.00 ..... ludicrous !!!
Floors always seem to be clean. All employees are wearing their masks! The Door greeters are always polite and friendly.  The cart collectors deserve a raise for collecting the carts in the winter... cold and there really cleaning them, due to covid!!

Buyer beware. Prices displayed are often not correct and you will be charged more at the register. Not the first time this has happened and I do not memorize each item I place in my cart, so it may happen more often than realized. Latest incident: photo memory stick for smart phone. Price on sticker was $9.97. Get to register and I happen to notice that it scans a price $14.97. Mistakes happen, but I was disappointed in staff response to such a 'mistake'. I asked what price the item rang through, cashier stated the higher price. I stated the item was listed as lower price. Her response "Do you want them to go find out?" (In a tone like she was put out).
"Heck yeah, that's $5" was my response.
Supervisor (female) looked me up and down (I'm wearing medical scrubs) and states "Ok, just give it to her". (Again the tone was palpable). Cashier re-rings in the item at a lower price and supervisor states " Huh, she must be right, it didn't ask for an override. "
No efforts appeared to be employed at fixing the problem of bait and switch pricing as supervisor went on to small talk with other employees. I will now decrease the number of items I buy here at one time and will more routinely take pictures of prices of my items to compare with what register rings in.

text:
Although I prefer to shop at WM Falmouth, I do have occasion to get to WM Supercenter once in a while.
The larger WM has many more choices in products, larger varieties of most dept items... and of course, groceries.
The assortment is phenomenal, the prices excellent, and the array of ethnic foods is wonderful.
I enjoy finding interesting alternatives to enhance my pantry and satisfy my culinary curiosity.
The deli department has been as good as the delis at Shaw's and Hannaford... and competitively priced.
The bakery dept is nice and produce area is convenient.
It's worth an occasional visit... but it can be very busy and crowded... there are usually enough employees at the registers to avoid congestion, but you need to be patient. Check the website to determine the peak hours and work around them. Enjoy!!

name: Kara R
text:
The Walmart Supercenter in South Portland/Scarborough is one of my favorite Walmarts. It's huge and has a selection to match its size. Even though it is bigger than the one I usually shop at it is well laid out, signs are visible to tell you where things are located, and the layout is easy to navigate.

There are restrooms at the front of the store and near the back so that you don't need to walk all the way to the front.

The fruits and vegetables are usually in great condition and the selection is good too. They do have some organics to select from and unique fruits like dragon and star fruits.

The lawn and garden center usually has a good selection of flowers in the Spring and Summer with the usual mums and sunflowers in the fall. They also carry bulbs for Fall and Spring planting. They also have soil, mulch, and other gardening items.

I definitely give this store 2 thumbs up & thank the employees for all their hard work in keeping this place clean and tidy! Of course holidays and storms can make things a bit hectic but maybe if people would put things back and not make such a mess the employees would be able to keep up all the time. Just say'n ... if ya unfold it ... it takes just a moment to refold it. Retail is hard enough.

text: Beautiful quintessential picturesque views with lots of benches and green space. You can walk or sit and just take in the ocean view. Bring a blanket and sit on the grass with a little picnic. It gets chilly so bring a long sleeve something.

text: This trail wraps around the coastal side of portland and connects the upper neighborhood and the walking path. name: Jeff Howe
text: The Eastern Prom is a little gem of a park, at the Eastern end of Munjoy Hill in Portland, overlooking Casco Bay. It's open to all, a nice place to sit, picnic (there are food trucks in warmer months), take a walk or run on the trail that runs along the shore, or even walk into Portland's Old Port (Standard Bakety, yay!). There's a mini beach for brave swimmers and dog owners. There's no fee, it's free for all. We went there often over the COVID  months for walks, a lifesaver.

text:
A manager publicly shamed me for not donating to the Ronald McDonald fund, after I made my purchase.
On a recent visit to this McDonald's, after paying for my order and  waiting for my food, the manager asked me if I would like to make a donation.
I politely declined, "not today, sir"; as he walks away he yells out "I'll remember that" I said "excuse me" and the manager replies "I'm gonna hold you to that next time!"

Never shame a customer for declining  to donate! He didn't know if I had just spent my last dollar or if I had in fact made a donation already. He's not the person who took my order.

What if it's an organization a person doesn't believe in, or maybe I am a philanthropist who donated a ton of money already this week. You don't know,  you can't know and it's not anyone's right to ask.

This was embarrassing for me, I felt like I was shamed in front of other customers. And what hurts the most is I do support the Ronald McDonald foundation. I take my 4 year old to these establishments quite frequently and donate my change to the cause.

I would like to see some sort of training come from this. I will not name the manager. This needs to be a lesson taught to all employees. Other then this experience I think this is a great restaurant and would certainly rate higher if my concern was addressed.
Thank you.

text: Always a fun time. Very reasonably priced seats -- definitely don't go for the GA ones though! name: Todd Healy
text: The box seats were incredible, very comfortable and easy to see the field. Food choices are just like any other typical sporting event. They have some good beer choices, not just your typical piss water. Pricing for food and beer is nearly the cost of a pro game, so that's the biggest problem I have with this stadium. The staff was very friendly, and helpful. Everything was very clean, no sticking to the floor as you walk, trash cans were not over flowing.  You may also want to get to the field an hour plus early due to the limited parking in the area.  So over all a great place to bring ther family and have a good time.

name: Nathaniel Terpening
text: Go Seadogs! The staff here are great. They make seeing a baseball game so much more fun, which is hard to imagine. Right on the grass next to the dugouts for less than $20 and conversations with the players as they warm up. Double A baseball is a great way to experience the great American past time at a reasonable price, and with the atmosphere here you will always leave happy regardless of the outcome of the game.

name: Vanya Caron
text:
It's a beautiful,clean ball park. The rest rooms would please a germophobe like me. Good beer. Different kinds of fast food,some of it good. Nice souvenirs.
Don't bring in water bottles or metal objects much larger than your keys. You will be nicely asked to bring them to the office where they may be picked up when you leave.
Choose seating carefully if you love the sun or not. Sit westerly if not. you will get some  to lots of sun otherwise.
It's a fun place for the kids, entertainment between innings and sound effects as well as snippets of rock music.
For me the game was incidental (not a big sports fan)but I had fun anyway with my family.

text: Love this place!  Great food.  I like the fisherman's platter which comes heaped with a combination of seafood (clams, shrimp, scallops, fish) that is battered and a choice of 2 side items.  The twice baked potato is good.  My hubby had the prime rib, but didn't like it fried, so next time he'll order something else.  Overall we really like the food, and our waitress was great.

name: Andy Martin
text:
I've been hearing about this place for years but this was my first time eating here. Everything I heard has been confirmed.

The crab stuffed mushrooms were on point, I would have been happy with a double order of those and calling it good. My buddy and I split the mushrooms and an order of crab cakes, they were excellent as well.

For my entree I got fried scallops and shrimp with hand cut fries and coleslaw, both were excellent. They use a simple light batter so the seafood shines and it's not overly greasy.

My buddy got the lobster casserole. We got lunch portions and we were both surprised by the amount of food they gave you for a reasonable price. We are both big eaters and both of us were stuffed, no desert for us, which is unfortunate because the few items I saw looked delicious.

I liked the atmosphere, a real simple decor and very clean. If this place was closer to where I live I would be in there all the time. I will definitely be returning soon.

text:
Hostess, erred seating our party, we were actually last to be seated after a full lobby that came in after us. The worst was a member of our party was served a one lb.to less lobster, when a 11/4 to 1 1/2 was ordered. Worse the lobster had a fishy smell. It was not fresh
The floor manager was called and she said it was impossible as their lobsters were fresh daily. She was insulted.  There was close to 300 plus years of native Maine experience at the table. Our families spend a lot of money here but with new management we will be spending  less.

name: Kate Savidge
text: The two people in our party are seafood eaters. One had the fried shrimp with cole slaw and fries. The other had a combo of fried shrimp and fried clams with fries and cole slaw. Both of them said their food was perfect, light breading and perfectly done. Flavor was great and I think they polished off the huge bottle of tartar sauce given to us. I chose the chicken broccoli alfredo pasta dish and I have to say I was incredibly disappointed. The sauce was about as far away from being an alfredo as it could possibly be. If there was any cheese in there, I couldn't taste it. There was no seasoning whatsoever. I could have sworn it was just flour mixed with water (badly, as it was lumpy) and sprinkled with a hint of garlic. The broccoli was just this side of cooked and all the pasta was completely stuck together. I was able to pick the entire mess up with my fork  For $15 worth of dinner, I expect far better than this. So if you are looking for a good seafood place, go for the seafood. If you are unfortunate to have to eat something other than seafood,  I recommend going somewhere else.

name: Madison Kirby
text: This place is heaven-sent for any seafood lover that suffers from gluten sensitivity. They have so many accommodations available, baked items, along with GF FRIED shrimp, clam strips, fish, chicken strips, you name it! text: All I can say is OMG!  I assumed it would be good, but hadn't been in about 25 years...The quality and the taste of the food far exceeded my expectations..... taste was better then 5 stars!!!! Grandchildren had the adult portion cheeseburger instead of the children's menu...fresh, cooked to perfection....homemade fries and salads  that even 3 and 7 year olds loved....  I had the luncheon portion which was huge.. between the meals and sides we couldn't eat everything,  and it made for a great lunch the next day.  Also, to have a perfect ending homemade strawberry shortcake,  with a hot homemade biscuit and a scoop of vanilla icecream...again so large the three of us couldn't finish it.  The service was prompt and very pleasant...and was very child friendly.  Not only was our waitress  great, but the other staff members were, asking if everything was fine and if we needed anything.  I have eaten in may places around the country and will say the food and our experience was one of the best!  Oh and now I should let you all know the cost of this 5 star meal.....$ 40.00 tip included and with a home cooked family  establishment you can have your leftovers to enjoy later.  Highly recommended,  if you do not go you are the only one missing out... just waiting to ho to Lewiston again, because the Chick A Dee is on my list for a necessary stop!

There is a tumbelow from the beach to Fox Island. Be careful you don't get caught out there when the tide comes in again. Then have a meal at Spinneys at the end of Rte.209.

name: Tracy F.
text: Popham Beach is spacious with an island you can walk to when the tide is out. It does get very crowded. We arrived 30 minutes before the park opened and there was already a line. Mosquitoes were vicious this year, but they disappear once you're on the beach. Rest rooms, areas to rinse sand off, and lots of parking also.make this one of our favorites.

name: Troy Ancona
text:
The State Park, at Popham Beach, offers great swimming as well as an opportunity to stroll on a sand bar at low tide, plus plenty of opportunities for sea shells and sand dollars, at the right tide, of early in the morning.

There are picnic tables, a nice bath house, changing area, and plenty of parking. But beware as on hot days this big lot fills up quickly!

This is not to be confused with Fort Popham, which has free access but is not a great swimming spot!

The State Park does have an entrance fee!

text: Gorgeous wide open sandy beach, a locals secret, with bathrooms, lifeguards, & food trucks. Beautiful place for sunsets too

name: Kyle Bognatz
text: Loved it here.  Was very windy but fun walking the sand bridge during low tide.  Would be a great spot in the summer.

name: Nikki Smith
text:
Love this beach so far. Just relocated to Maine and have been waiting for warm weather to finally enjoy a beach day. We visited this beach on a chilly day in May and although it was a nice little walk on the beach and the rocks during low tide, it was freezing.
Recently went back with my kids for a beach day and it was beautiful, still slightly chilly with the breeze but there was barely a cloud in the sky. We went during low tide again so that they could climb on the rocks and attempt to see some sea life (no luck). It was pretty packed when we arrived around 11 and we had to park along the over flow parking outside the parking entrance.
Silly me, figured this would mean we would not have to pay to enter so I didn't mind the walk in. I was wrong, they still charge you full price to enter the beach area which I find absurd but oh well. It can get a little pricey the more adults you have with you but if you are a veteran, you can get in for free.
Also, Watch out for the seagulls. They are pesky little thief's and will creep right up on you to steal your meal/snacks and then go tell their friends who will them swarm you waiting to attack.
The downside, I did notice that many people that attend this beach really lack consideration for others and will walk right on top of your belongings, kicking up sand and what not all over you. I am not sure if they are locals or tourists since it's a pretty well visited beach by both in the summer but just be warned. The lack of respect for other peoples property is not really there.

Overall, it's a great beach with so much space and the little water pockets left during low tide in between the sand bars is great for kids to play in. You have amazing views all around and can head just down the street towards the fort for Ice Cream when you are done for the day.

name: Chris W
text: Really fun place, great beach right next to the fort.  The kids loved it abs it’s free, so despite my criticism msg below I still highly recommend.   -Downside is the fort isn’t as well maintained as we’d like (graffiti and the stink of urine run some areas).  Also difficult to Find parking so be prepared to walk a bit.

Lots of seagulls and hermit crabs and even a couple islands you can walk to ( tide permitted). It has some crazy waves with some dangerous undercurrents so be careful!!

text: Our favorite! Dynamic beach...different experience every time. Walk out to Fox Island during low tide and search for sand dollars and explore. Seagulls are brutal! Pack your food in coolers or closable bags. They will go through your bags if left open... food or no food.

text: Awesome state park beach! Go at low tide so you can walk over to the island and sandbar. Even if the place is busy, the beach is plenty big enough! Wonderful sandy beach. Beautiful and the perfect place to spend a summer day.

name: ervin brown
text: It's a great beach and on a lucky day you might find tons of sand dollars like did!

name: Erica C
text: A great beach for a family, people watching, swimming, reading a book, beach combing or sun bathing. Popham beach is quite large and is often crowded during the summer. It's definitely a nice, clean beach. There isn't a bunch of trash which you will find at other beaches. There is a lifeguard on duty until 16:00 during the week. (Any form of Military ID; active duty, retired, reserve) senior citizens or government employee(s) gets you in free! There is a small fee for the entrance otherwise. Parking is free although it can be quite a walk if you end up parking on the road side. There is accommodations for handicap/van accessibly. It's a clean, beautiful beach! At low tide there is a sandbar that is walkable to this tiny island! I have found quite a few sand dollars there. In the "off season" it's a great place to find sea glass. They do offer public restrooms and changing rooms- which are actually clean. They also have a washing off area with fresh water which is great to remove sand from your body, feet or any items. Watch out for the sea gull's, they can be aggressive and will try and steal your food if they can. Over all a really beautiful, clean, nice beach!

name: Michael Serrano
text: Awesome beach, great for kids. Love coming here.

name: EJ Fortin
text: Big beach, plenty of room to roam. At low tide you can walk out to one of the islands. Great place to spend the day with family

name: Laurie Rich
text: A beautiful sandy beach. It is well off the beaten path but worth the drive. Walking around the beach is Pleasant you can go from tidal pool to around to the surf of the Bay. In different seasons you have to be aware of the nesting Birds and staying off the beach vegetation to prevent erosion. There are bathrooms picnic area and during the height of the Season lifeguards are on duty. There is a fee for using this park but it's not terrible. Well worth of visit for the beach itself and the scenery.

name: Ashley Malinowski
text: Nice Sandy Beach with an island you can walk to within a few hours either side of low tide. My little kids love playing in the tide pools but waves are big enough for the older kids, too. Tons of parking and nice bathrooms.

name: arlette Andersson
text: Very beautiful peaceful and quiet this time of year.  People were actually respectful and nice especially with covenant 19.

name: Joseph Marin
text: Great place to watch the water and climb the rock if tide is out. Rest area and snack bar, not sure of hours.

name: Mindy Allen
text: One of my favorite places in Maine! Walk the insanely large sandy beach, scramble on the rocks, pick shells, surfing and gorgeous.

name: Joe Douglas
text:
Absolutely beautiful beach, very clean facilities. We were here at the what seems like the perfect time and weather. It wasn't crowded at all. I suggest bringing some mosquito spray while at the parking lot and bathrooms while it's fine at the beach. There is a somewhat long walk to the water if the tide is remotely out if you have small children or elderly folk with you. Very beautiful spot and you can even see a light house in the distance.

SIDE NOTE: WE WERE FOLLOWED AROUND BY A DRONE FOR A SHORT TIME WHILE ON THE BEACH, I'M NOT SURE IF IT WAS FUNNY OR CREEPY BUT I HAD MY DAUGHTER WITH US WHICH MAKES ME CAUTIOUS. I DON'T KNOW IF THIS PERSON LIVES HERE OR WAS VISITING SO THIS MAY HAVE BEEN A ONE TIME OR RARE EVENT BUT YOU MIGHT KEEP YOUR EYES OPEN FOR ONE WHILE HERE. THIS DRONE CAME WITHIN LESS THAN 5 FEET FROM US WHILE "WAVING" AND "DANCING" AS MY DAUGHTER THOUGHT IT WAS ALL FUNNY AND REACTED AS A CHILD WOULD. JUST FOR GOOD MEASURE A REPORT WILL BE FILED WITH THE AUTHORITIES.

Clean beach, with a moderate walk to the sand. The perfect place to gather seashells and sand dollars. Picnic tables are near the parking area. Restrooms are clean, and located at both ends of the parking lot. Seagulls are hungry and bold.

name: Shirley Humphrey
text: We waited in the car queue about a half mile from the entrance gate this morning for 45 minutes when it came to a halt. People started getting out of their cars, cars were passing and cutting in line. Finally walked to the gate to find all in front of us left their cars to attempt to walk in. Was told by park staff they were at full capacity and closed to further visitors until noon, including pedestrians. Yet the traffic director a half mile or more away kept waving cars through, like they could get in. We gave up and left, having wasted our 45 minute commute (1 way). Dozens, maybe much, much more cars were still in queue thinking they'd get in. Why can't the park have a digital sign or someway to let folks know they are waiting in vain? What a mess.  Guess I'm giving up visiting my state's parks until capacity restrictions are lifted.

Lots of beach room so you won't need to worry about being to close to other people. Staff are great,friendly and very helpful. Enjoy your day at Popham Beach!!!

name: John C. Madden
text:
Popham Beach State Park is home to one of the most beautifully unique beach landscapes in Maine, if not all of New England.  It sits between the Morse River and the Kennebec River and is straddled by Morse Mountain and the ancient civil war era garrison known formally as Fort Popham.

The beach itself has taken a battering from Maine’s truest versions of Mother Nature over the last few decades and, as a result, erosion has whittled away a great deal of its shoreline and its naturally occurring dunes.

Luckily, there is still ample space to enjoy this unspeakably gorgeous place where you can stake your umbrella and lounge on the sand for a nominal fee.  You’ll be grateful that you did.

Oh, and a little tip to those making their first visit ... Plan your day around the tide times, with the most optimal arrival window being the one that’s closest to low tide.

Fantastic little market. They manage to pack in an astonishing amount of goods on offer into a relatively small space.
