text: Absolutely lives up to the hype. Tried so many of the vegan flavors and not one disappointed. My boyfriend and I joke about driving here from NJ for some delicious donuts.

name: Dustin Thompson
text: We missed the Maine hash browns this morning, but the donuts made up for it.  The chocolate peppermint donuts were awesome, and the texture of the toasted coconut chocolate covered donut was amazing.  The drive-through personnel were friendly and fast!

name: BeantownEater
text: Fast service here. Bigger then the Portland location. Look like a bigger selection too. There outside seating to enjoy the weather. Staff are friendly and helpful. I would suggest this place over the Portland on.

name: David VanLuke22
text: Doughnuts were great! It's not Sweetwaters doughnuts but I am sure y'all know nothing about that place. But if you are ever in Michigan and enjoy these doughnuts Sweetwaters should be at the top of the list!

name: Damian Watson
text: Delicious. Tried six different flavors-all were yummy but the toasted coconut was absolutely fabulous!! Drove thru service was friendly and efficient.

name: Denton Weimer
text: Went to this location for the first time, this is a must have every time you visit Maine love the variety of flavors, they also have vegan options.  These donuts are dangerously good!

name: William Tuttle
text: I drive 20+ miles for the vegan donuts. Exquisite.

name: Kaitlin C
text: Fresh made potato donuts that melt in your mouth. What's not to love?! Chocolate sea salt and old fashioned are always favorites.

name: nikki bulmer
text: Super friendly service, beautiful building and delicious donuts! They even have my puppy a treat!

name: Scott Anderson
text: Staff is friendly enough but the girl that was working in the drive thru was very flighty and not paying attention.  Donuts are amazing, tasted great, very fresh.  Speed of service was good.  Overall not a bad experience, would have been 5 stars had it not been for the issue with the girl taking our order

name: Melissa Rappleye
text: Our whole group was absolutely shocked that this place was rated so high. First, you had to wait a while. The cars were lined up into the street. We got out of the car and waited in line. They were out of half of the flavors. But we both got maple, and they were so bad. Not only the texture of the donut weird, but you couldn't even taste the flavor of it. The hot chocolate was so room temperature warm, not hot and very syrupy liquid chocolate tasting. We were very disappointed. No one even finished half their donut. It's a cute place it looks like it should be awesome, but huge fail.

name: Melanie Champniss
text: Friendly barristas. Good coffee. Unique donuts.

name: J Thomas
text: These donuts are out of this world.  Some funky flavors but worth trying!  They are large in size and quite filling,  so be prepared!  😋

name: Dakota Brackin
text:
We came to the Holy Donut and have been pleased to try their many flavors and experience the friendliness of the staff. They will greet you with a warm smile and happy faces. One great plus to coming here is that they get the public involved in social media and put the choice in the public’s hands on new flavors for the coming seasons.

I personally was not a fan of some of the flavors however with the professionalism of the staff and the cleanliness of the establishment I recommend coming to see if your taste buds approve.

name: Barbara Dozet
text: Wonderful family-owned donut shop using real ingredients

name: Chris Slesarchik
text: Awesome donuts and an all around great company. They use a unique dough made with potatoes that gives the donuts a dense and hearty quality I haven't found anywhere else. Holy Donut has several locations in the Portland area and the donuts are consistently fantastic at all of them, but the Rt. 1 location is the newest, nicest, and most spacious (also features a drive through). Chocolate sea salt is the go-to choice but they have a bunch of other flavors that are all great.

name: N M
text:
Their gluten free donuts are okay. There are honestly much better but not in this area. It’s disappointing that a company that is known for their gluten free donuts but only has 4 or 5 options, all plain cake donuts with some sort of dried out flavored icing, but tons of non-gluten free options.

It’s also pretty consistent that they do not have any gluten free donuts in the morning at the Scarborough location. They open early but I’ve gone more than once and they’ve had no gluten free donuts available at 7-8AM. I get that they receive the gluten free ones from another facility but this option is what you’re known for. At least have some of them available in the morning for people before work.

name: Jordan Guy
text: Best donuts and awesome flavors!

name: Samuel Pierce
text: Decent potato style donuts, exotic flavours. A little empty tasting dough but not as sweet as other cake donuts. Expensive. Tony's still the best around.

name: Kevin McNeil
text: Tasty Maine potato donuts in classic and inventive flavors. Light filled location with ample seating and parking. There is also a drive thru. Coffee ice cubes for the iced coffee drinks is a nice, inventive touch.

name: Wha Atrip
text: Visiting from Virginia to Acadia and all points in between, your coffee and donuts were theee best! The cashier in the drive thru was SUPER NICE and hilarious..."hope you get your velour track suit for your birthday honey"!! BTW, this track suit had BELL BOTTOMS!!! Your comment is going in my travel journal!! ❤🍩❤

name: Jennifer Bragdon
text: It was really good! Plan to wait in line but they are very efficient and the line moves fast. So don't be discouraged to see a long line, it was well worth the wait. My daughter liked watching them dip the doughnuts into icing and then the toasted coconut. We got a variety to try. We plan on going again if we are in the neighborhood.

name: Miss Tish Creates
text: Always a treat, we got a whole dozen and oh boy, it was a LOT of donuts!!!! Lol They are huge!!!  But so delish, it's fun to try all the flavors - they won't disappoint!!

name: Cindy C Chesney
text: We had heard of this place on The Food Network. It more than lived up to what they said. We were in there on Saturday morning and it was busy. There was a long line that moved quickly and efficiently. Although the donuts were a bit pricey, they were worth it. Fresh, moist and flavorful. Many flavors to choose from. Not your usual run of the mill. Good coffee and we'll worth the stop. If you're in the area, I highly recommend it.

name: Allison Emmons
text: Holy donut is a great local Maine business. If you want an amazing donut get yourself over there and order one. 🍩

name: Nehru Enerio
text: I literally went to all the holy donut places in Portland. They're so good, you really can't go wrong with any of the flavors.

name: Matthew McGrath
text: Crazy delicious donuts!!! Super friendly staff. Highly recommend the MAPLE BACON donut, HOLY MOLY its beyond good.

name: Cliffs_of_Rover86
text: Absolutely incredible. Not overly sweet either, like so many donuts are. The Maine Blueberry is a must have, as is the sweet potato coffee cake!

name: Anthony Stewart
text:
I don't want to overstate it... but this is my favorite thing to eat on planet earth.

That is all.

name: Deb Hichborn
text: Got a raspberry glazed/frosted donut. Yummy

name: Rebecca Prewitt
text: It was so delicious!! A little pricey but tasty!!

name: Dave Stiles
text: Product was super, really enjoyed.  Employees very polite and prompt.

name: Stacy Foster
text: Excellent we got there around noon and alot of flavors were sold out, gotta go early!

name: Edward Parks
text: Parking seems to confuse people here for some reason.  They're very quick and taking your order and the donuts are fresh and delicious.  Pretty expensive but the donuts are super filling and tasty.  Highly recommend at least trying these.

name: Shawn Surma
text: Good doughnuts. Great chai. Definitely a place to stop by and try. Large seating area as well

name: Lee Demers
text: Always a delicious treat to get Holy Donut and I love sharing them with others. Coffee is always fresh and there's a good selection of beverages for those that don't like coffee. My personal favorites are the sweet potato ginger and maple bacon, but seasonal lemon and apple donuts are great too. I do agree with other reviews, parking seems to be a struggle most of the, but that goes to show how good they are.

name: Patrick Fagan
text: Triple berry holy cannoli is one of the best donuts I’ve ever had. Grapefruit juice is the best I’ve had outside of Florida. Coffee is really good and they use frozen coffee for the ice, so it’s never diluted!

name: Aaron Wiggin
text: Great donuts decent coffee.  If you are going in the afternoon call ahead.  They close before the listed hours if they run out of donuts

name: Scott Linscott
text: Fans LOVE these donuts! Made uniquely with mashed potatoes included in the recipe, they have a different consistency. For my liking, they are too heavy and not my preference.

name: Kiki Reno
text: The Holy Donut is absolutely delicious! We always stop on the way back home to bring some donuts back with us. Our favorite so far is the Blueberry Maple Bacon donut!

name: Mac Coldwell
text: Fantastic donuts. I usually hit the shop on Park Ave, but needed to pick up a couple dozen donuts for a special event and the route 1 Scarbarough shop is on the way to my home. The efficiency and friendliness of the staff was amazing. Their chocolate glaze with sea salt is a classic favorite, but they have some creative donuts as well. Their gluton free donuts are also really tasty. Nothing lost on the quality.

name: Kayla W
text: We love every Holy Donut location, we would love for them to come up to Bangor some day! Donuts are delicious, coffee is great, service is fantastic, a must stop when we're in the Portland area!

name: Brooks
text: My wife says these are the best donuts in the world.

name: Monica York
text:
Awesome gluten free donuts! They had six flavors and I tried five over the course of two days. I didn't try the Chai donut as I am not a fan of that flavor. The donuts were just as good on the second day.

As someone who has been gluten free for over 13 years, having the ability to get donuts while traveling was just awesome. I was so overjoyed with the whole experience.

Service was quick and friendly even on a very busy Saturday morning!

I wish I lived closer so I can get more of their gluten free donuts. Wish they could overnight them to me. I would pay for it, they are that awesome!!

name: Cedric Minkin
text: Ok ... don't quite get all the hype

name: Gus Alivizatos
text: There's a line down the street for a reason ♥️

name: Jake B
text: I do not understand the hype. These are better than the donuts from a big chain but they're not as good as the other donut shops in Portland. I get the potato thing, but honestly this is probably my third or fourth favorite place to get a donut around here. The donuts are dense and crusty, and unless they're very fresh (which, to be fair, they usually are), they are quite dry. They have good flavors though, and the people at all the locations are friendly. I just don't get why people wait on line for these.

name: Justin L.
text:
I'll pick up donuts for work.  We typically get about 12 dozen.  Driving about 45 min to get there right before they open at 6am.  It's always a hit.  Anyway, Justin their manager is very professional and helps me get the order out to my truck.  I recommend getting their coffee as well.  The coffee brand is Coffee by Design.  But somehow their coffee maker is better than all other coffee makers as it makes a really superior cup.
Thanks Holy donut!

name: Ronald Cote
text: This place is crazy good.. very busy but the donuts are awesome. If you have not tried them make it a point to plan a visit.

name: Allie Rose
text: Always quick and helpful service. Great selection of donuts too.

name: Anastasia Nor
text: Delicious locally sourced potato donuts. The drive-through in Scarborough is really helpful if you don't want to get all the kids out of the car, lifesaver on a weekend morning.

name: steven doughty
text: Not impressed.  Donuts were very heavy, somewhat flavorless, and not fresh.  This was our first and last time coming here.

name: Katherine Earley
text: DELICIOUS! And they even had Maple Bacon still available in the early afternoon. :-))

name: Jennifer Whitten
text: We loved this place. It is more than just going to get a coffee and a donut. It is an experience an adventure. Something to cross off your bucket list. 🍩 we're great and so soft. Who knew potatoes were meant to make yummy 🍩 s.

name: Andrei Menchikov
text: Local staple. Excellent donuts!

name: Ghassan 'Gus'
text: Love the holy donut! Love of tasty and delicious choices. The dark chocolate sea salt is my favorite!

name: Lindsay Whitmore
text: Smells amazing when you walk in. The coffee was good and doughnuts are to die for!☠️

name: Krista Christie
text: One of the best if not the best donuts I've had.  Made with local Maine potatoes. All kinds of great flavor combinations. Moist with crunchy exterior and delicious.  Definitely s donut deserving of the devine title.

name: Alex Funicello-Paul
text: Amazing donuts. They practically melt in your mouth. My favorite is the chocolate donut with coconut. The potato pocket with cheese and bacon is amazing as well. For coffee I've only had blacked iced coffee so I can't really speak to that. Wife loves the triple berry and pomegranate frosted donuts.

name: Steven Sidman
text: Great donuts, Coffee by Design. It's all good.

name: Michael V
text: First time having a potato donut. Definitely a different experience. Not impressed with the donut, but their icings were amazing — plus the seasonal Maine apple donut was great! Friendly service. A bit overpriced.

name: Dustin Bonk
text: 11/10. Amazing potato-based donuts. Fun flavors, very unique. You can't come to Portland and not eat some Holy Donuts.

name: Justin Britton
text: Best donuts you’ll ever have. 100% Maine potatoes.

name: Stephanie N.
text: I too used to think that a "potato donut" sounded weird - then a coworker insisted that I stop on my way through Portland a couple of years ago. One bite and I was convinced. They are dense, flavorful and moist. A little worried that they're not as niche and secret as they used to and therefore getting too big,but I'll stop anyway.

name: Lisa Dennis
text: Love this place. Potato donuts have a unique texture and taste (which I like better than your traditional Dunkin offerings). Coffee is good, hot, strong. The team is friendly and fast. The merchandise is pretty clever.

name: Thomas Tj
text: Excellent donuts. Good variety as well.

name: RON GRECO
text: awesome, delicious and almost better than ...

name: Susan Cashman
text: Ginger cannoli is out of this world!

name: soo-eun Song
text: very friendly efficinet and pleasant!

name: Becky Barker
text: The apple doughnut was delicious the hot chocolate also is good however I am not impressed with their customer service!!! we looked online to see when  they closed it said 5pm we met some friends there at 4pm to spend an hour visiting before they close at 5 so we got our stuff and sat down next thing we know they were locking the door so we asked why they said the lobby closes at 4pm the drive thru is open until 5 so we stayed a few more minutes but finally gave up they were slamming the chairs and tables around to clean if they do "close" at 4 then they should say it online!!!!

name: Samantha Weck
text: This particular spot is a lot bigger than the other locations which is super nice. I didn't feel squished while waiting in line. The donuts are fantastic as always and the girl who prepared our order was super nice.

name: The Donut Guy
text: 5 Stars cause the service was great. 4.5 for the Dark Chocolate Sea Salt donut..

name: Chuck Hayward
text: If somebody told my wife she had to pick either me or Holy Donut, I’m pretty sure I’d be single.

name: JiDii O'Alowra
text: Wonderfully Yummy Homemade donuts in Maine!

name: Roger Greenlaw
text: Friendly staff and interesting donut choices. A little higher priced, but worth it for fresh donuts made on site.

name: Em
text: A friend recommended I come here while I'm visiting Maine and I'm so glad I listened! The donuts are delicious with a wide variety of flavors. I'm going to miss Holy Donut when I'm back home!

name: Dave Houck
text: Donuts are great but seriously $26 a dozen? I guess I should have paid more attention! I will say that the Bacon Maple donut is Heaven with a hole in it! I got the donuts for my tram so they are worth the extra but it would have to be special occasion for me to buy these donuts.

name: Courtney
text: Delicious donuts and excellent customer service!! I went through the drive-thru a couple days ago and ordered one donut for myself. Come to find out, they were out of my favorite kind. After making a suggestion for another I should try, the employee at the window offered me a second donut for free just because they didn’t have what I wanted. Definitely unexpected and appreciated! Thank you to the employee who did this for me! I found out that my grandfather passed away earlier that morning and was having a rough day. Your small act of kindness seriously made it better!

name: Stephanie McIntyre
text: I love the holy donut! I just happened to stumble across the one in Scarborough on my way back from Massachusetts and I am glad I did! The donuts are so fresh and delicious and their is a huge selection of flavors as well as drinks and coffee. The building is clean and fresh and in a great location. Will stop in the next time I head to Mass.

name: Vicky Mccully
text: These are the best donuts! Great variety. Favorites are chocolate sea salt and pomegranate. A must place to stop when visiting Portland.

name: Kelsey Towle
text: The vegan donuts are perfect everytime 👌

name: Rachel B
text: Faster than Portland, same amazing donuts & coffee. #potatodonuts #theholydonut #scarborough

name: Jason White
text: Who knew potatoes would form the basis of addiction-inducing doughnuts? About once a month, my wife and I make the trek to Holy Donut -- she loves their vegan options, I inject my diabetic self with the maple bacon. Good coffee, quick service, tons of options if you drop by early enough (including filling, scrumptious breakfast sandwiches). Staff is great, too, although the downtown location is a bit too into itself (we prefer the one in Scarborough, which offers ample parking and is strikingly ego-free).

name: patti cuva
text: Super friendly staff, Vanessa was wonderful!  I had the Ginger Holy Cannoli and it delicious.  This was my first visit and I'll be back!!.

name: Patrick Pilvines
text:
Delicious! So many delicious (and unique!) flavors. This is definitely a great place to go before a road trip or next time you need to bring coffee and donuts to the coworkers.

The wait can be a little long if you go inside (depending on the time of day) but the like moves along well, just be patient :-)

Potato based donuts, so they're a little different but we love that. Highly recommend checking this out! Especially the cold brew iced coffee (they use coffee cubes! Genius!)

name: Jonathan Hilton
text: The best donuts in Maine!!!! Love them and the service is always friendly. Mist stop when I am in Scarborough.

name: Luke Holmes
text: The donuts are quite different and they make some cool favours like maple and bacon. Overall though the donuts didn't blow me away and the service was fine but not great. There is a toilet and they have a little area with some of their merch which is actually all very nice.

name: Katrina Flanders
text: Unique shop with good coffee and even better donuts! Quiet setting to chat with friends.

name: Kiera Emerson
text: The owner of The Holy Donut was working the cashier, and she was kind enough to offer me the option to have a hot chocolate w/ soymilk. Definitely recommend because of her kindness and the staff attentiveness of the whole place!!

name: Sammy Antinoro
text: Worth the drive! Potato donuts are epic, I have tried almost all of the flavors. Lemon is my favorite and the sweet potato ginger glaze is my number two! If you go in the summer snag the blueberry donut! I will keep coming!

name: Greg Marchand
text: Impressive donuts. Wasn't a huge fan of the flavors but the donuts were impressive for potato donuts - very light. Friendly staff and tons of customers!

name: Bronwyn Held
text: Really really good doughnuts. A lot of doughnut places stand out because of their toppings. But here, even a one without frosting would be excellent. The drinks here are good as well. They have savory doughnuts too so you can stop for a complete breakfast.

name: Jennifer Molloy
text: Best iced coffee around. Donuts are so good. Love the space.

name: Tom Sing
text: Great Donuts, service fast & the people were smiling !

name: Victoria Rose
text: 2 WORDS- HOLY CANNOLI

name: Lauren Cabral
text: Loved my first experience. Great donuts

name: Peter Kuczynski
text: Love the variety! I try and bring some home to CT when I can.

name: Jess Farley
text: Amazing cappuccino. Had the apple donut for the first time today, it tastes like apple funnel cake and heaven.

name: Isaac Stroe
text: This place rocks, i love there donuts, they have the best selection of delicious and inventive flavors, i got the vegan pomegranate!!!

name: Elana Castiglia
text: You can't go wrong with any of the flavors of donuts that they have to offer. All are delicious and there are gluten free and vegan options as well. The Scarborough location is spacious with a great amount of seating. Friendly staff and simple check out. This is always a must stop for us when we travel near Portland!

name: Christian Overton
text:
Must visit! I never thought a “potato donut” could be the BEST donut but now I realize every other donut is just an imposter. I went to Holy Donut in Portland a few years ago and now every time I’m in Maine I make it a point to get Holy Donuts. There staff is amazing, the shop smells wonderful, there are so many awesome flavors, the whole thing is just a great experience.

Pro tips:
- Go early and get their first. There’s usually a line, sometimes even before opening! But here they tend to move quickly.
- FIRST TIMERS: Go with friends and get a dozen (trust me it’s worth the price) and sample all the cool flavors you think you’d like and maybe even some you don’t. Then just have quarters and save the rest for later, they keep well in the fridge.
- Definitely try the Chocolate Sea Salt and Maine Blueberry (my personal favorites are: Chocolate Sea Salt, Dark Chocolate Cinnamon, and Lemon)

name: Stephen Robbins III
text: Excellent service. Exceptional donuts.

name: Yvette Dilallo
text: Holy Moly what a Great idea: Maple Bacon Donut and Wide Awake Coffee. This place is in a Category of it's own! An absolute must try! It's Wicked Good.

name: Michael Mackesey
text: Busy, a bit of wait, pricey

name: Kenneth Spinney
text: Delicious donuts. Not cheap but delicious.

name: Scott
text: HOLY DONUT is not an oxymoron...when in the Portland area this is definitely a must stop!  I recommend the maple bacon!

name: Alicia Tenney
text: Just came from Texas and went to rt 1 location!! Bought my sea salt chocolate ones and my socks!! I will love to take a picture of the owner!!

name: Alexander Kontoleon
text: Warning, consuming any of delicious donuts from here may lead to the consumption of more donuts than you think humanly possible. Every flavor they make is incredible, one is not enough. The chocolate sea salt donut and the lemon are my personal favorites.

name: Chris Stedwell
text: Blueberry bacon is delicious and so are the rest. Best fathers day donut ever 😁

name: Cherie Johnson
text: It was my first experience here. The donuts were huge. We got several different types,  they all had an old grease flavor. They were moist but tasted like they were fried in used up oil. Probably won't be returning.

name: lauren ditomaso
text:
Its great, but watch out because they switch out the vegan dough after a few batches and still label them vegan when they are not any more.
*we went at 12:45 on July 28th

resp.text:
Hi Lauren, Thanks for the review.   Were you at the Scarborough shop?   And what was the date of your visit?   While we do change the flavors periodically, they should be updating the wall to coincide with the flavor variations.

Thank you

name: Amanda B
text: So many people rave about these donuts, so I figured I would try.  The line was LONG (testament to thier popularity), prices were high and I didn't care for the potato texture... seems on the drier side.

name: deborah eaton
text: Great donuts. Unusual flavors. Not your same old thing. ♥️♥️♥️

name: David Cloutier
text: They have donuts. The donuts are very good. Rich,  savory, melt-in-your-mouth good. The bacon and cheese stuffed donut is particularly indulgent. Just make sure to eat them right away, these donuts are nowhere near as good the next day.

name: Brian m
text: Very good.  My first thought was "are these going to taste like potatoes?"  They dont.  They taste like other higher end (non corporate) donuts.  They also cater to vegans which is a big plus since vegan donuts are hard to find.

name: Drew Team
text: Sooo good, just try them. Not a bad donut on the menu.

name: Karen Hammond
text: Awesome.  So good and many different kinds...too hard to choose just one!

name: Susan Bohnet
text: The old fashioned donuts are the best...great go dunking!

name: Julie Cooney
text: Best donuts around! Friendly staff, amazing customer service. Stopping here is an absolute "must" when visiting the area!

name: Maura Jones
text: I went here on a Saturday morning before going into work.  It was early, around 7:30.  No lines.  Excellent customer service from staff who actually smiled and chatted.  I'm thinking they have tried the donuts and coffee they serve.  It will put even the grumpiest person in a good mood. Take it from someone who doesn't care for donuts, these are "da bomb'.  This is my most highly recommended place for donuts and coffee in the area.

name: Chris Taylor
text: These doughnuts are great and I understand why there is always a line. They are definitely something to be shared because they are huge and filling.

name: Anthony Edwards
text: What can I say....my inner fatty loves these things.

name: Douglas Goodman
text: A local shop in the Portland area for doughnuts with a twist.  A first time there, arrived late.  There was a limited number of selection.  Parking is tough, but worth the effort.

name: Anthony Stohlberg
text: Donuts were pretty good but not as good as all the hype surrounding it. A little overrated but a good coffee and donut shop none the less.

name: oh ma
text: Friendly Staff, clean inviting space. I enjoyed trying a selection of 6 donuts. I really enjoyed the coconut ones (my fav donut across the board anyway). The plain (~vanilla) donuts with the variety of frosting flavors (maple, coffee, lemon, berry), beyond being very pretty, didnt really hit the spot for me. The frosting is messy and crumbles off, and is intensely flavored against the comparatively bland donut. This made, for me, an unbalanced, fun-dip kind of experience. Perhaps the plain donut alone would be the more fair way to enjoy tasty fried sweet dough.   A comment on the lemon and berry donuts- they have a very intense citric acid flavor.  There is lemon and berry flavor too, but its so amped up with citric acid it ruined my enjoyment of them.

name: danielle mccabe
text: Amazing donuts!! You have to try the dark chocolate sea salt one.

name: Mike Whitten
text: What can I say best donuts regular and gluten free. Little pricey but a real treat

name: Swizzle Stick
text: It's ok if you like greasy food.

name: T S
text: You can actually taste the potato in it which adds a little something

name: Rod
text: If you love donuts .this is the place for you lots of frosting.

name: Roger Madore
text: The best doughnuts around! Fresh, soft, delicious!

name: Amy Taylor
text: Absolutely fantastic donuts! Great flavors and so amazing!

name: Max Boston
text: I have never had a donut here, that being said my friend's wife is gluten intolerant and this place has gluten free donuts. She loves them. So 5 stars from me. :-)

name: Ryan Eling
text: Busy place... Expect a wait. But the donuts are better thank they used to be. Not as heavy and oily as they used to be. Don't worry about all the flavors... Just get the chocolate Sea salt.

name: Trisha Marie
text: If you're willing to pay $3+ dollars for a donut, you won't be disappointed.

name: Debbie Clark
text: Picked donuts up for our son..We thought they were pricey but big donuts our son loves them

name: Glen Lord
text: Potato doughnuts,  gluten free a definate must doo

name: Gregory Hogan
text: Delicious donuts but the price if a dozen will scare you

name: Merrill Robbins
text: A little pricey,, but the place was packed donuts are the best, no compition, even from the big boys

name: Greg Goodwin
text: These hardy potato donuts come in a wide variety of flavors, some quite unique. Come early in the day to select your favorite flavor before it sells out. This freshly renovated location has both stool and table seating. No time to walk in? Make use of their convenient drive-thru.

name: Kit Johnson
text: The gluten free cinnamon glazed donut was delicious! The staff was super friendly and helpful too. I would definitely come again.

name: A Moose
text: Maine potato donuts.  Creative and tasty flavor combos!

name: Tina cummington
text: HOLY SMOKES! Donuts made w Maine Potatoes. We drove by several times on different days and the place was BUSY. Si we decided to see what the fuss was all about. Now you have to also.

name: Ruth Bondi
text: Holy Cannoli is my favorite but everything is great there! Staff is attentive.

name: JP Seabury
text: Best donuts, period! So glad they're not just down the road from Higgin's Beach!

name: Joseph Boland
text: Love the new location but the staff are pretty rude here. Every time I've been I haven't had a great experience like the original locations in Portland. I thought it was just because they just opened but it's been a few months and they haven't gotten any nicer. The drive through is kind of a gimick but there's more space for dining than the Portland locations

name: Frank Fuller
text: Donuts are hours old in the afternoon if you want fresh donuts you have to go in the morning otherwise they stop making them around noon

name: Amanda Hedge
text: So many vegan donuts! The texture of these are amazing, and have just the right amount of sweetness. The coffee is great too. New favorite!

name: Christina Kaslow
text: Delicious local donuts though I've had a few visits where they fell short on quality. Closing time is fluid as they run out of donuts early.

name: Kate Savidge
text: I grew up behind the Cookie Jar in Cape Elizabeth. The Holy Donut is a very different doughnut. We tried the Maple Bacon doughnut today and I have to say I was pleasantly surprised by how good it was! There was a Triple Berry Holy Cannoli that looked interesting as well. All of our store managers are trained to verify pricing and if something is not in our image they are able to adjust the prices, but they do need specific items to be able to do a comparison.

Prices will vary based on the quality and where the stock originally came from, the discounts are intended to provide a true value to the customer and be less than they can get that exact item anywhere else. We do make mistakes or prices change in the digital age, our managers are trained when brought to their attention we will make it right (or explain why it is a deal at the price).

resp.text: We do sell items from insurance claims.  Often they are in perfect condition, but at times, they can have smoke and/or water damage. When they do, we deeply discount them.  If you ever see something in a Marden's store that isn't priced as a a true bargain far below what other sell it for, please bring to a manager's attention and they will address it promptly. Biddeford location is a dirty store which is not a very positive first impression in my opinion. I understand it's surplus and salvage but clean it up a little.   Customer service is lacking as well. No one seems to want to help the customer.  Big Lots has similar items which are not salvage and prices are similar or better with superior customer service. Ocean State Job Lot is a better choice as well.

resp.text: Jennylee, Thank you for your review of our Scarborough store. Our typical discount runs from 30%-60% off retail (and even more in some cases). If you are looking to purchase an item from us and find that we are not the cheapest, please bring that specific item to management’s attention. When comparing identical items, we want to be the lowest price! We do our best to price all items accurately, but it is near impossible to keep up fluctuating retail prices that are out there. We buy all surplus, salvage and closeout. So at times we could have "very expensive" items and other times, we could have items that are incredibly low cost. Please try us again as our store changes daily.

Bruce, thank you for taking the time to review us. On the heels of our reopening after the COVID-19 shutdown, we tried to reestablish our relationship with the bakery, Labadie’s. Unfortunately, they raised their prices on their baked goods.
Giving our customers real values is the core basis of our business. We felt that with the price increase from the bakery, the baked goods would no longer be a real bargain.
We wish we had better news for you, but our negotiations have just not panned out. We are still actively working with the bakery to get their items back so that we can offer baked goods once again at Marden’s bargain pricing.
Sandy - Customer service team

name: Stephen Hoy
text: When you're dining at a restaurant on a Portland Wharf, especially one as famous as Boone's, you expect great seafood. We ordered Shrimp scampi & Salmon a la plancha. Both were very good, completely satisfying. We didn't order appetizers or bread, so we had just enough room for dessert. You can eat outside, but we sat inside at table not far from the entrance. Great atmosphere!

name: Brian Hunt
text: Outstanding atmosphere, food, service and drinks.  Good craft beer selection and creative mixed drinks.  The seafood popover I enjoyed was one of the best seafood dishes I have ever indulged. Outside dining is a perfect Maine coast setting with lots of coastal night life swirling around. This was a true 5 star experience, worth every penny, without completely breaking the bank.

name: April G
text: Boone's is a great place to eat, but it is pricier than suggested on Google. We went for drinks and appetizers, had an app, 2 drinks, and 3 oysters and it cost us almost $60 before tip. This is not to discourage anyone because the atmosphere, service, and food was incredible. Super romantic for a special night out, perfect for our anniversary. We look forward to a full meal in the future!

name: Cindy Howard
text: From the moment we walked in this place was more than welcoming! It's very cozy and has wood fireplace. We had the lobster stuffed lobster. It was a bit pricey because it was out of season but out server let us know ahead of time so there where no surprises. The food ha so much flavor and the portions were more then filling.  They also have a great local beer selection

name: Mike Jeansddgvhjj
text: Excellent food and service. Be sure to see if you can reserve the igloo. Fresh oysters are the tops. Dont forget to order the bread basket!

name: Mars
text: Delicious food, pleasing atmosphere and great service!

name: Lorraine Hirdler
text: Had great meals. Salmon and stuffed haddock. Wine to start and ordered a great popover with blueberry jam.

name: Martha Crockett
text: From the moment I walked in, I knew this place was special.  The sweet hostess greeted me and was accomodating.  Everyone we interacted with was friendly and provided excellent service. I met the owner and she was lovely.  The food was incredible.  Absolutely fantastic, how many stars can I give? Every bite was decadent.   The atmosphere here is fabulous, inside and out.  My new favorite restaurant in Portland.  It's been here forever- my 1st opportunity to come and now I will come again and again. Great date spot, too, BTW.  1st date or 50th anniversary, birthday or just because... this place is wonderful.

name: Dustin Bonk
text: I love the igloo! Great food and atmosphere, summer or winter.

name: Rayleen Tritt
text: Impeccable service. Our server knew the best beer and wine pairings, was knowledgeable about the menu and was on the ball. The food was perfection. We had oysters to start which were fantastic. Perfect combination of brine and sweetness. Zero grit or sand in them. My partner had the stuffed lobster which was the best we've had and I had the cold lobster roll. It was a cozy environment with a crackling fireplace and the music was awesome. We will be back next time we are in Portland!

text: Baked stuffed lobster is to die for!!! The oysters were sub par compared to other food there.

text: We were all blown away by the great food, no stingy portions here either! So nice to have the huge fireplace on a chilly day.  We loved the staff! So friendly and fast! If you haven’t been to Boone’s in awhile you are missing out!

text: Everything we ate was delicious but there were unusually LONG gaps between courses, and service was OK. The two of us started with cocktails that took +20 minutes to arrive. By the end, our 3-course dinner was bordering a 3-hour experience… which did not jive with the loud, casual & smokey setting of Boone's. Plus, sitting at a high-top table for a long meal was not comfortable. Luckily, the food saved the day with fresh oysters to start, a spicy Thai shrimp appetizer (I could eat a whole bowl of that over sautéed vegetables!), and a wonderfully buttery baked-stuffed haddock that featured large pieces of lobster & scallop. Over all, good food made up for lackluster service in a semi-uncomfortable setting.

We ordered appetizers and dinners by 8:45pm. Appetizers arrived at 9:15, dinner arrived at 10 pm. And when it finally arrived, two meals were missing. Instead of apologising and trying to make good, a) the waitress went unseen for 20 minutes and b) the meals were not delivered until after everyone else was finished, c) the temp on the two meals (medium well) came out medium rare, and (medium) came out rare. We attempted to ask the waitress to rectify the situation, but she disappeared again for 20 minutes, only reappearing to try to upsell desserts, and then ultimately dispersing checks. name: Hannah Olson
text: A wonderful place for a fall walk. There are several woods trails through the park. On the day use side, you can pick up the loop by the beach. It's a little under 4 miles if you do the full loop, all very level and easy. The beach area has plentiful picnic tables, including several which are designated handicap accessible. It was very quiet on an late October Monday and we only encountered a handful of other people, all of whom were practicing good social distancing/mask wearing. The gate was unmanned/honor system fees.

name: Dwight Corning
text: This campground is one of the nicest, and quietest in the state. The beach is very nice for all ages, and there are geat playgrounds for the little ones. The tenting intermixed with other camp vehicles is well spaced in most areas, with plenty of trees for shade.

text: Another boating adventure: 12th year anchored at Sebago Lake State Park, but outside the roped off swim area on the sand bar. Very nice for the State Park attendees, but glad our kids had years of playing there when young. You can still access at end of sand bar to get snack shack food😋.

text: Probably the coolest boaters hang out in the whole state of Maine IMHO. The well known Sandbar @ Sebago Lake State Park. Luckily the water is like 3ft deep for half a mile off the beach so you can drop anchor and wade... Pure Summer Awesomeness!!!

The lake is perfect for swimming, canoeing, kayaking, boating, and fishing. The park rangers are friendly and dedicated to their job and to the environment. text:
A clean, scenic beach and campground with lots to do.

I've been coming to Sebago Lake State Park since I can remember, and no matter how often I come, it's always a pleasure.

It can get pretty crowded on days like the 4th of July Weekend or Memorial Day Weekend, but overall there is ample parking in the lot and lots of space once you're in the water.

There is a convenience store at the head of the road leading to the park where you can buy sandwiches, drinks, snacks, or ice - but during the peak of the season, the park runs a food booth.

The bathrooms are clean, there is lots of shade, and there is even a boat launch if you have one. If you hike, there are also a few trails in the area and lots of opportunity to view wildlife.

Would highly recommend for a summer day trip.

text: I'm a pretty regular customer at this location, and I'm always pleased how clean and well-kept it is, as well as the friendliness of the staff. they have great deals on lunch foods like pizza, hot dogs,chips, soda and such... You can usually get two slices of pizza with chips and a soda for under $5, and it's always hot and fresh, and honestly whatever brand they use is REALLY good lol, I prefer their pizza over anywhere else... They also have a great selection of fresh baked goods, many of which are much better quality then similar ones I've paid three times their price for from bakeries and or shopping centers. The Hersey muffins are actually delicious! They also have a great selection of fountain sodas, with all sizes priced under $1. This location also serves the f'real shakes and smoothies, which my kiddos absolutely love. They have a wide selection of refrigerated canned amd bottled drinks, including sodas, juices, flavored milks, beer, wine and other alcoholic beverages and spirits like Twisted Teas, Mike's Hard Beverages, single-serving bottles of Mudslides, Kahlua, White Russians etc, as well as your everyday convenience store items like lottery ticket, cigarettes, lighters and little do dad's. They also have a small isle of both household and grocery items like toilet paper, paper towels, dry cereal, and canned goods;automobile needs like engine oil, dry gas, air fresheners, tire gauges and such....and of course gas pumps. In the winter during the heaviest snow storms are parking lot is always one of the first ones on Commercial Street cleared and accessable. This location is also a 24-hour store.

Neon green, dripping a liquid that has a real "battery acid" tang to it, like pure malice in spear form.

text: I'll tell you what, I'm a bit of a "foodie" and I have pretty high expectations but I was absolutely blown away by Amato's lobster roll. Just imagine the freshest lobster meat you've ever had tossed with a little mayo and served on a soft Italian roll. I have had lobster rolls all over the city and I would rather pay $12.95 for the lobster roll I had at Amato's than the smaller $16 lobster roll at Eventide. Don't get me wrong, Eventide's brown butter lobster roll is delicious but it's a distant second compared to the one I had at Amato's. Just saying. See for yourself. On another note there was a new cashier who wasn't quite up to speed but the gentleman making the sandwich was super friendly. I ❤️ Amato's.

name: Michael Lewin
text: The basic Maine Italian sandwich -- ham, cheese, sour pickle, onion, tomato, green pepper, olive, s+p+oil on a soft almost doughy sub roll.  Some places do it slightly better but Amato's is everywhere and fairly consistent. They do pickles right, but the slicing of the veg onto the sandwich out of hand sometimes leads to unwieldy piles of large chunks that slide onto your shirt and pants when you attempt to eat, even if you unwrap the wax paper a little at a time.

name: Kimberly Brown
text: This was my first visit to Ken's Place. Friends have encouraged me to dine there for years. I shared the Fisherman's Plate, a side of Onion Rings and Clam Cakes. The Haddock was excellent. I was expecting chunks, but was served 2 large fillets. The Scallops were the best I've ever eaten, tender and juicy! Just melted in my mouth. Fries were good, but needed salt. Clams were big, Shrimp were tiny and not very flavorful. Onion Rings were very good and crunchy. The Clamcakes had decent flavor, but on the small, thin side and I thought a bit gummy.  Regardless, it was a wonderful meal and good value for the money. I'll definitely return.

name: Kevin Brown
text:
One of if not the best place to get seafood! Literally the only place I will eat out at when I want battered Clams, Scallops or Shrimp:) It is located in a beautiful area with lots of picnic tables on grass with lots of beautiful pine trees for shade if you want to stay out of the sun.

Everything they make is GOOD:) The portions are big!! They also have an ice-cream window- yes!!! they actually have a window for ice cream service. The service works like this: the order windows are inside..you put in your order and they call your number. You pick up your food when they call your number..you can eat inside ( there is a small family friendly bar area if you want an adult beverage ) or you just carry your disposable tray of food outside to one of the picnic tables. PS: When I say family friendly bar I just mean that it is very low key and actually blends right in with the total family friendly atmosphere of Ken's...you might not even notice it:)

Service is quick ( considering they seem to always be busy ). The staff is professional, well dressed ( in white and with aprons ) with lots of young summer hire associates who are friendly, sharp, on their game and focused on customer service. I love how they seem to always have an associate walking through the dining areas with a broom and dustpan keeping the dining area well maintained.

The building has lots of wood and is designed along the lines of classic style Maine Diners. Lots of parking and trees and grassy areas for kids to run around and have fun in. I just at their today and ordered one of my favorites..battered clams and shrimp combo. I also love the clam and scallop combo but I had that last week so I went with the shrimp today. I hope this review helps:)

name: Bruce Marstaller
text: Had lobster stew and lobster roll plate, both very good. Had fried shrimp, small gulf shrimp not as tasty as Maine shrimp however, suggest the home made tartar sauce. Had egg salad plate, comes with slice of cheese, roll, two each of green pepper rings, sliced tomato, sliced dill pickle and two sweet gerkins, egg salad, potato salad on a bed of lettuce. If you like your potato salad tasting like mustard you'll enjoy Kens, and maybe this was opening weekend issues, but the potato salad pieces, half were raw and half cooked completely. It also has green pepper and dill pickle pieces in it.

name: Joe Hall
text: First visit of the 2019 season...placed my order at the window and then chatted with friends who had also stopped at Ken's Place for a fantastic meal. The hustle and bustle in the kitchen is always the same and the food smells great! I felt a genuine sense of satisfaction when my number was called. My plate was filled with fresh seafood, a dinner roll, coleslaw and french fries - Yum! I had just visited another local spot last weekend and thought, "they really load you up on the fries". At Ken's, I thought, "they really load you up on the seafood". Much better in my opinion!

text: What can I say it's Kens! The food is great, the staff are friendly, and regardless if they are busy or not you never wait long! Sometimes it takes a minute or two to find a seat, but well worth it! The food is always excellent and it shows by the volume of cars in the lot. An inside joke in my family is when we drive by Bailey's down the street, we ask if they are open due to no cars in the lot. Or, oh Bailey's has no cars there Kens must be packed haha. If you are looking for good seafood at very reasonable prices, please consider spending your hard earned money at Ken's Seafood you won't be disappointed!

text: So I have to admit this place holds a special place for me - as a local we've been going here all my life and I have wonderful family memories. Their ice cream should be avoided at all cost, but their food is always good. But I have to admit that my visit this year was a bit of a let down. While it is always crowded, it felt like their kitchen and counter staff didn't have it together and it was really scattered. People were there in big groups with lots of food, and the flimsy trays (used to have large reusable plastic now cardboard that you have to throw away) aren't up to the challenge. I saw many people having to make multiple trips which just slowed the process down and made it hard for people to know what was theirs and what wasn't because the counter girls weren't paying attention. Also, the prices have gone up... a lot! We got a lobster roll (on a regular frankfurter roll), a cheeseburger, fish and chips, and fired clam dinner, and 2 watered down sodas. $56 later, we ate outside at a picnic table by the road, had to carry our own food and take care of own trash. Still good food, but with the prices being charged now, the place is looking a bit rough around the edges (no longer rustic, just shabby and dirty).

They've even got outdoor restrooms for patrons who choose their abundant seating area of picnic tables.

resp.text: Thank you for your review, Ken. We take a lot of pride in our staff and customer service has always been our number 1 priority. We are proud to hire young employees who are, perhaps, entering the "real world" for the first time. We feel very fortunate that we have the opportunity to help shape these young individuals into productive members of society by teaching them the importance of good work ethic, team-building, and an all-around general responsibility for themselves. name: James Siler
text:
There are two very similar eateries very close to each other on Pine Point Road.  One is Bayley's and the other is Ken's.  Bayley's maintains hours throughout the winter while Ken's opens in April.  It is a local tradition to to to Ken's on their opening day.  After Ken's opens for the season the comparison between the two is stark.  Ken's parking lot is always packed while Bayley's is sparse.  Once the season takes off they are both packed with out of state plates, but during the shoulder season Ken's is the hands down local favorite.

The fried seafood and lobster rolls are uninspired but fresh and tasty.  The  fish chowder, though, is a stand-out.  On a nice day, grab your food and head for an outdoor table.

name: sam tarbox
text:
Ken's is a long time staple of the Pine Point seafood restaurants.  Many folks are polarized by the restaurants that are in the local area.  Simply put each family or clan waves the battle flag of who they feel has the best of the best in fried seafood. 🦂 Be careful when asking a local who's clams are better.

Ken's has not changed much over the years.  This not a bad thing...it's a nice throwback of simple dining out.  Food is ordered at a window from a simple menu.  The toughest thing to remember is whether you want crumbs or batter.  The food is served hot and fairly quickly.  Remember once Maine's summer season hits peak the lines at the counter get longer and the chances of finding an open table decrease.  Get there early or tailor your visit to the off-season.

Be wary of cougar corner AKA the "rawar" bar or just the bar. Some locals and outta towners hang here.  The bartenders are freindly and drinks served in plastic cups.

All and all it's a must stop in the group of Maine's local seafy restaurants.

name: Taryn Simmons
text: The salon was clean, the staff is polite & friendly, and they got me in last minute with out issue. Those things are important. I was disappointed in my service. I went in for acrylics and a simple nail art design, only on my ring fingers. My nails were Very thick, uneven in places, and unbalanced; they flared at the tips. The polish coverage was streaky as well. But with all of that , what was most disappointing, was I didn't feel as if I was listened to. There was no language barrier either. I showed the woman a photo of the design I wanted, it was very simple and rustic. She asked if she could modify it a bit, I agreed bc we had discussed using more muted colors and placement of the art. Not only was the nail art bold colors, the actual design looked nothing like the photo, and the placement was not where we had discussed. I honestly feel as if she just did whatever she wanted and just did a standard, older looking, design. I had another place to be that afternoon, otherwise I would have asked for a fix. Instead I won't return and will not reccomend this salon to others. I would never refuse payment, bc I understand that this is their livelihood and it's just rude to do so. I was just very disappointed with the outcome of my nails.

name: Theolonius Dutton
text: Nice midweek blockbuster flick with plenty of space in the theater to relax minus the crush of a crowd. First movie in theaters in many months. My kiddo & I were so stoked🤙🏾

name: Pam Cleaves
text: Mixed reviews: The bathroom was clean (thank you), movie was clear, and sound was good. The lobby and theatre were not clean.  The crew was leaning on the counter and there were no customers besides us.  We were in the lobby 15 minutes and they never moved except to talk to another employee. Popcorn all over the lobby floor, straw wrappers on the dirty tables, etc.  ("If there's time to lean, there's time to clean"). Our cupholders in the theatre had crud in them.  We certainly did not use them.  Who knows what's in there! I doubt we'll be returning.

name: Bonnie
text: The leather recliner’s are HUGE and clean and you have so much space. You also get to reserve you seats when you buy your tickets online, I love that! Can’t wait to get back!!

name: Mac Coldwell
text: The renovations were well worth the wait. The stadium seating with recliners is so luxurious. The bar is gone, but I rarely saw it used. There parking lot is also in better shape. Service is usually great and quick. You can purchase tickets at any register now and get your snacks at three same time. I miss the football games.

name: Maj
text: Comfy chairs. Very comfy chairs. I usually go here instead of the Westbrook one. Because of comfy chairs. Did I say the chairs are comfy, because they are VERY comfy. Like a little butt pillow.

name: Matthew Cochrane
text: The best theater in the area, very comfortable. Nothing stands out otherwise, no unique snack or beverage options, the snack bar tends to close early which sucks if you're trying to squeeze in a popcorn refill before they are supposed to close. They could clean the theater a little better as well, but we tend to go to the last showing of the day, arguably the worst time to go in terms of cleanliness.

name: Shawn Tardif
text: This theater is fantastic. Lazy boy recliners, spacious, an all around cozy experience.  This will be my new place to watch movies.  I would recommend this theater to anyone looking for comfort in a movie watching experience.

name: James Iezzi
text: Due to covid-19 movie theaters are going to be opening soon and I have to warn people if u to go to the movie theaters be warned that you may get covid-19 covid-19 is here to stay people you've been warned

name: Robert Blow
text:
I love the comfortable seating.

The restroom are clean and the place is what you look for in a movie theater. Game machines and temporary tattoos!

name: Rory Platt
text: Good movie theater. Comfortable chairs. Nice that they have cult classics shown occasionally.

name: Davis Daniels
text: A nice quite theater with great reclining seats. My regular go to theater for a quick afternoon or evening movie. Bathrooms need an update but the rest if the facility is great.

name: Jen George
text: The auditoriums are really nice. The bathrooms, however, are atrocious. The family bathroom is torn up and in disrepair. The men's room has non-working urinals, and the women's room has several toulets, soap dispensers, and a hand dryer that are out of order. Ticket prices are not going down. Why aren't they keeping up the restrooms?

name: Branden Keller
text: This is my favorite movie theater in the area. Comfy reclining seats, always clean, tons of parking, lots of bathrooms. Whenever possible I go here and I buy my seats in advance and show up a few minutes before the movie starts. Highly recommended!

name: Bonnie R.
text:
I had a wonderful experience there, the chairs were very comfortable. When you walk in the doors so clean , notice they had a mini arcade and a photo booth. The movie and sound effects was awesome.
If you go on a Wednesday the tickets are discounted. I haven't been out for a while and have to say it was worth it! great theater day!

name: Nathan Cermelj
text:
Sunday afternoon with my son. I spent $36 on tickets, popcorn and a drink. I ask them for a cardboard container. They ask why and I say so my son can have own container. They said that WILL NOT give me a 5 cent piece of cardboard BUT they would sell me an empty small bag for $1.

I will have a hard time returning to this theatre. Family friendly? $1 for an empty bag?

Be a place where people want to go again because they feel appreciated or keep losing customers to people staying at home to watch movies.

name: Jessica Simpson
text: Love their wide, spacious and foot reclining seats. Always have a good movie experience here.

name: Fredrick Drake
text: The theater had just had some pretty substantial renovations. There are now wide, comfortable recliners to sit in. Also tickets are sold through the automated kiosks which makes for a short wait buying tickets. Theater are clean and well maintained. There is also a nice little bar if you are early for your movie. Popcorn is really good. The staff has always been friendly and the loyalty program gets you some decent rewards over time.

name: Kevin Remsen
text: The large, comfortable recliners are a real treat!  This is my go-to cinema!

name: Russell Sprague
text: I love the recliners, but I am too tall so my feet hang off the end of the foot rest and it gets uncomfortable.  At least the seats are big enough I can pull my feet up some by sitting at an angle.  Everything thing else is great here, the sound and picture quality are great, and I love being able to reserve seats online, so you don't have to show up 30 minutes early to get a good seat.

Very nice upgrades to this location.

This was after a five minute conversation between a manager and concessions worker on how to handle a large soda that was accidentally rung up as a medium. After much deliberation they reluctantly just gave me a large soda. The trip for four of us cost a little over $85.00.

text:

The seats were insanely comfortable. They are recliners. Plenty of leg and arm room. The seat allowed me to watch the movie without my sciatica driving me insane with pain.
This is my new favorite seating style and theater.

name: Daniel Rios
text: They update this location, better seats!

name: Kenneth Vouvounas
text: I have been to this theater many times for the past 26 years with three different names: Hoyt's, Regal Cinemas, and now Cinemagic.  I never had a problem with parking, because I don't drive and I never even had a license, but I never needed one.  Just a bus ride to Hannaford and only takes a ten-minute walk from there.  Great movie selections and wonderful staff.  Whenever I go to Cinemagic, I always make sure to buy a medium popcorn, a large Coke, some nachos, fries, and two hot dogs.  The only problem however is the tickets and the food being overpriced, like my personal menu selection would cost at least 35 bucks.  Despite the price of tickets and concessions (they should reduce the price to help reduce the crime rate, LOL), it was well worth it.  It was definitely worth it.  The first time I ever went to that cinema (known at the time as Hoyt's) was my then-favorite movie, Terminator 2: Judgment Day.  But I guarantee it won't be the last.  Plenty to offer for movies.

They changed the ticket system to assigned seats, now you HAVE to buy your tickets hours or days ahead of time to get a seat, and good luck trying to watch a film with friends. text: I find myself sort of... looking forward to going to this Hannaford, which might seem weird. But it’s genuinely a great store with an amazing selection that you rarely see at other Hannaford locations. I’ve found things I was looking for at places like Whole Foods for a much better price. I’ve found things I wasn’t looking for but absolutely needed. (like a giant fish plushy) I’ve found diverse products from multiple cultures and religions that were reasonably priced, especially considering the price of import for some of the items. The only drawback to going to this location is the baggers/cashiers tend to be either downright rude and insulting, don’t do their jobs, or basically non-existent. It’s kind of weird, especially when the staff in the other areas of the store are generally pleasant and professional. Overall, though, this is a good store to buy a good verity of food as well as your usual staples.

There are case workers here who are assigned to clients and help them follow through and up with providers housing agencies opportunity employment mental health and substance abuse services and so on and so forth. It's located and extremely close proximity to both the soup kitchen the overnight shelter and the City of Portland general and emergency assistance offices which makes it the go to place for people when they're down and out and needing a hand up.

text:
Have not dined at Rosie's, but just had a horrible interaction with staff on the phone.  I called in to ask whether they could accommodate guests with peanut allergies, to which he said "That would be tough...but yes, we can."  And then he said "Well, it would be more on you than on us."  When I asked what that meant, he said that they don't have peanuts in most of their dishes but they wouldn't have a way of ensuring that things were safe.  Then I started to say, "Okay never mind." and he hung up on me.

Yikes.

name: R B
text:
I don't know what to say about Rosie's. The hostess was nice to us. He was a shorter guy. Things went odd when we met our server. She seemed nice. She said she was A couple days new. We did not get the friendliness we are used to in a restaurant.  We felt rushed and it was like, once you ordered something off the menu,  you didn't have a chance to say what you wanted or didn't want with it. She just grab the order and "Boom", she was gone.  At one point,  you felt like you were doing something wrong by trying to get her attention. First time I felt almost intimidated to ask her for anything.

The steak was ordered medium well, but it was more well done. I must say my burger was perfectly cooked. Didn't like the fact they threw a juicy pickle on the fries. I hate pickles but didn't get a chance to tell the waitress that because she fled so fast. Tried the Rosie's punch.  It was like fruit water.  So that was disappointing.

It could have been an off night.  Other patrons seemed annoyed in our section. We did see other waitresses and had to ask them for a thing or two.  They were nice and friendly.  Idk what the heck happened. We might go back to give Rosie's another chance.  But as of this moment, I can't say I'd recommend Rosie's and that makes me sad.

name: Kennedy
text: Solidly in the realm of pub food. Not baaaaad service, but average, at best. Seating outside during COVID times, and they have warmers to extend the outdoor season. Had the tenders—they were out of their house special Mac & Cheese at 2 p.m. on a weekday 🤷🏼‍♂️. Tenders were unremarkable. Don’t expect much table side attention. Maybe I’m nitpicking but how do you delver food to your one table (of the two you have) and then say, “Oh, yeah, I’ll be right back with your silverware and napkins.” Maybe put this place on the list for beers, but not food. Or just expect average pub food and average service.

Rubbery lobster, so although you are in Portland, you still are at a pub....so pub food wins! Enjoy some free popcorn as you wait (my kids did)

Pros

text: What can I say that hasn't already been said. It's a Walmart. It has a decent grocery section that segues into the clothing which then leads you to office supplies and electronics, from there it's a jaunt through the home department. Make a hard left towards the front of the store and you arrive in the land of liniments and arthritis relief. Continue and you voyage past hair products, makeup, and arrive in the pet department. A short hop and you are in the outdoors section, i.e. BBQ, bug spray, lawn paraphernalia. Unless you have hung a right past the bike display which will usher you to the trash cans, paint, and auto sections, in almost that order. As you proceed past  home repair, look to your right and observe the toys. Beyond this you should now see at a tiny but moderately stocked craft section, on your right, opposite the auto necessities. Now you have arrived in the outdoors department which will provide you with the raw materials for hunting, fishing, camping and a modicum of other sports related outdoorsy stuff. If the urge strikes you there are bathrooms located at the back and the front of the store. At the front entrance you will find a New England staple, Dunkin Donuts. Which should really rename themselves Dunkin Coffee etc., because I would rather buy donuts anywhere other than a DD. There is another entrance which  boasts a hair salon. So there it is,  this particular Walmart in a nutshell.

text:
I have to say that it is okay. (Which means two stars.)
I decided to rate it because today I stopped by on my way to the library downtown. Yeah, they have great deals on some basics that I know I might want to grab sometime: a belt, undergarments, socks, household supplies, etc. But when I was looking at their shirts and pants it was not in any decent order whatsoever. Looked like decent deals, but I couldn't find sizes properly sorted.
I did come across a couple items I thought I might try on. The changing room said no backpacks, which I understood. So I asked someone that was working near-by where I could leave mine. "Oh, just on the hook next to the door." Wait. What? You don't trust your clients because they may steal YOUR items, but you expect us to assume that others won't steal a bag that may contain computers, books, etc. from us? "Alright, no thank you then." Was my response, and I placed the clothing down and walked out. If a store worries that we may steal from them, then they should care for us to prevent other clients from stealing our belongings.
I only go here for essentials, which they do often have. But if I ever need to buy anything more than some socks or a box to store my books, I'll go to a decent store. I highly suggest ignoring those that love it just because it is solely based in Maine. They're being very irrational.

name: Melozi Scott
text:
This is my favorite liquor store in Portland proper - possibly because of its close proximity to me. I generally go in straight for beers or whiskey which they have plenty of options for both. Their wine has nice, quality selection for varying price points.
They're easy to talk to if they don't carry something you're looking for. Kyle was really helpful with me in that regard and even gave accurate estimates when they would get back to me.

name: Hannah Phillips
text: A convenient place to go coming or going from Portland. The store is right across Commercial Street from the Casco Bay ferry terminal.  Inside is a wide selection of numerous Maine-brewed ales and lagers, many offered in the very handy 4-pak 16+ oz size. Also hard liquors and chilled wine...perfect for BYOB windjammer cruises offered nearby.

name: Jennie Walker
text: Wonderful spirits location with amazing staff! The guy at the register was very eager to help me when I was searching for craft beers without an ounce of knowledge, and he helped point me to his favorites as well as others. Giving him categories (made in Maine, sweet) didn't slow him down any, instead seeming to aid him in pointing out the best beers for my purposes. So many beers, all stacked around in and out of fridges with every flavor profile imaginable. Plus it's right on busy busy Commercial Street - so easy to get to! If you want any sort of alcohol for you or someone else but don't know where to start, I highly recommend this location.

text:
Roundtrip ticket to Peaks Island was $7.70 for an adult, which you can buy the same day at the window (credit cards only). It was a nice, 15-minute ride over. The ferry is big enough to allow proper social distancing. The cool thing is that residents from the Casco Bay Islands can bring their cars onto the ferry (not sure how much that cost), which is something I've never really seen before.

I would just note that the ferry times are limited now due to Covid (which is understandable). So that's how we decided on Peaks Island - because it was the only one that fit with our schedule. Would I come back the next time I'm in Portland? Probably not but it's nice if you just want to take a ferry ride somewhere.

Tip - you can see Portland Head Lighthouse in the distance!

text: Took the ferry to Long Island for a day trip. The locals were so friendly and the island was peaceful. The round trip ticket was just under $11. There's a little market on the beach that has a good selection of beer and wine. They even have a large cooler where you can get some chilled beverages. The ferry experience was lovely. We caught the 730pm ferry back to Portland and were able to see the sunset over the water. Remember to bring your mask and wear it on board!

text:
Hop on board! You'll be glad you did!

What better way to see the beauty of coastal Maine than from the deck of a ship! The Casco Bay Line company offers a variety of cruise lengths and prices. We opted for the day long cruise to Bailey's Island. For $26 dollars per person we spent a wonderful day listening to the captain describe the history of Casco Bay. We cruised pass lighthouses, forts, and 19th-century summer colonies, and saw some great wildlife.

This trip included a two hour stop over at Bailey's Island. This allowed us the opportunity to enjoy a really beautiful spot. With clear weather and lots of room to move around, what better way to see Maine. So hop on board, you'll be glad you did!

name: Tyler Lund
text: Casco Bay offers several ferry lines as well as a great mail boat that takes you around several of the nearby islands. You can either get off at any of them or stay on for a 3-ish hour tour of the harbor and surrounding areas. This makes for a great orientation tour of the area when visiting. They are also very dog friendly, you just need to buy a $4 or so ticket for Fido. Hershey loved the fresh air and sights of the bay, bird life, and especially that they let you bring your own food and drink onboard. Stop at duckfat for a great sandwich and the craft beer cellar for some liquid refreshment while on board. The boat makes longer stops on a few islands as well so you can get off for a few minutes and stretch your legs. Boarding is a bit stressful as they don't control the lines well, but there are more seats than you'd think and it clears off after Long Island where many people go to their island homes.

Thank you for visiting Best Buy in Portland, and for your feedback when trying to price match. There are a few key things to know when looking to do a price match.  The product must be the identical model and color; it must be immediately available from a qualifying online retailer or local competitor, and not be on our exclusions list. You can view our full Price Match Guarantee here: www.BestBuy.com/PriceMatch. If you feel your requested price match should have qualified, please email us at ReviewSupport@bestbuy.com, referencing my name and your information. Thank you for being a loyal shopper.
Best Regards,
Jen *Best Buy Support

name: Richard Snow
text:
The Best Buy store in South Portland is just your typical big blue box.  They have a good selection of everything you'd expect at Best Buy - TVs, Home Theater, Speakers, Appliances, computers, and Phones.

This store does have a small Magnolia section where you can experience their higher end Home theater products, although many products are special order only.  Steer clear of the high end HDMI cables, though.  They're overpriced and offer no picture quality increase over Amazon Basics HDMI cables.

Staff here is typical Best Buy.  One or two specialists that know what they're talking about and the rest just read the product cards and don't understand what they're reading.

Since Best Buy actually stocks TVs and Electronics (and Amazon charges sales tax), I find myself purchasing here on large purchases rather than Amazon.

Oh yeah - this store is really good about price matching Amazon, so you're not spending anything more and you can take it home today.

Pro: The Root Cellar has good intentions, they try to help with social, economic and health issues for the community. If you and your family are immigrants of African origin, or from the Middle East, they will help you as best they can.
Con: They prefer to help and assist the immigrant population, but make no bones about turning away natural born Americans, Seniors and in general, needy Caucasian residents. The basic services offered, are prioritized to CERTAIN INDIVIDUALS... the rest of us get the excuses, lies and literally pushed to the end of the list.
I desperately needed dental work as a disabled senior with no insurance or DHHS help... repeatedly filled out paperwork THREE TIMES IN THREE YEARS AND KEEP BEING passed over, never contacted, or always told some b.s. that they (conveniently) never got it/can't find it. Tell me how fair and equitable that is... more likely ISN'T.
SHAME ON YOU GUYS.... 👎😝😷

text: My 5 and 10 year old went here for a birthday party. This place is HUGE! Amazing fun at every turn, an observation deck with couches and TVs overlooks the entire facility, and the staff was very welcoming and attentive. The obstacle courses and the jousting pit were way better than their competition in Portland.  Not to mention how incredible the ginormous jungle-gym was. I did have a hard time keeping track of my kids though. After they went it the jungle-gym I swear they didn't surface for 20 minutes; and they came at me from an exit I couldn't see. The under 7 jumping area was pretty good for my little guy, too. Pads on everything. I noticed a few people get put into weird positions and hit their head on things, but no one was injured the whole time there. Impressive.

text:
So on a positive note, it is a good size facility with lots to keep kids entertained.  That is really where the pro's stop and you get to the con's.

1st off, its "company policy" that you have to use their proprietary socks.  This is the 1st trampoline park I've encountered this and the staff readily acknowledges that their socks arent any different than other facilities, its just to milk you for another $20.

2nd, it is not nearly as cleanly as other trampoline parks ive been to.  The floors were dirty literally everywhere. Also there was a noticeable unclean aroma that ive not experienced at similar parks.

Lastly the sign in and waiver process is fairly asinine.  There's 3 touch pads setup off to the side that arent readily apparent, so once you wait in line you find out you need to go to a seperate area only to wait in line again.  During school vacation week, having one of the three touch pads functioning made for a less than fantastic 1st impression.

Recommendation - drive 10 minutes north on the highway and go to Get Air in Westbrook.  Cleaner, cheaper, and overall better facility.

We got the Ultimate Party Package for our youngest. We bought extra dipping dots, pizzas, and the powder puckers things.

First off, it was so DISORGANIZED!! We had to host when things were going to be done (cake, pizza, etc).

Secondly, the host kept forgetting things. She forgot the t-shirt, which I reminded her. Looking back at the package we were suppose to get 1 trip to the candy drop station and scratch offs for all the guest and they didn't provide us that!!

Worse of all, the private rooms were all upstairs and the air conditioning wasn't working. It was 85-90 degrees upstairs and everyone was sweating, including the hostess. One of the guest parents said she notice that the host kept wiping her sweat with her hands and they used it to hand off the pizza to the kids. They also did nothing to remedy the issue. I mean they should have gotten portable fans for the room. Another party was going on in the other room and it was empty also cause no one wanted to stay in the room. One of the guest brought a baby and we had to go downstairs cause we were worried the baby would overheat

Honestly, having the host was useless. She basically just handed off bracelets when the kids arrive and went off to do her own thing and occasionally checked in with us. We could have done all the stuff she did.

Also, we had to tip the host, which we gave a decent tip even though we though the hostess role was kinda useless.

All in all, save yourself the trouble and book your party somewhere else. For the amount paid, it definitely wasn't worth it!

name: Deborah Penham
text:
This is a fun and different place to come for a drink.

The food is surprisingly tasty! The servers were funny (we were in a jokey mood and they matched that, which is a skill) and very helpful when I couldn’t decide what I wanted to drink.

And of course the view is amazing... That’s what it’s all about.

The charcuterie board for $24 was extremely generous, and the variety of meats and cheeses, crackers and crostini, nuts, olives, etc, was quite filling. We also got the wedge salad, which, oddly, had already been cut up a bit. It was very good though. I got shrimp on the salad for $9 extra and received 6 large juicy shrimp; that’s a pretty good deal for a hotel bar in Portland... Other places might easily charge quite a bit more.

Don’t hesitate to pop in for a cocktail to start off your evening. If you’re in the mood for something slightly fancy, but not snooty or whatever, check it out. And try out some snacks.

I haven't been at the Top of the East for at least a couple of years. I obviously have been waiting too long to go back. This is a high-end Lounge that is wide and spacious and has spectacular views of Portland Harbor & downtown Portland.

We only had a cocktail, we did not have any food as we had just visited another restaurant and wanted to catch the sunset on a beautiful early spring evening. I will tell you that the cocktails are a little pricey, however, you're paying a premium for the view for sure.
