Located on Middle Street in Portland, Maine - this location can be hard to find parking for. Out of the three or four locations around, this one has the biggest collection of music and Magic Cards, I'd say (though I'm just guessing) - barely any books and a decent selections of movies and games and collectibles.

The staff are friendly, the store feels cozy, and since you're close in proximity to Anthony's Kitchen and Casablanca Comics, you could easily spend an entire afternoon here if you're at all like me.

name: Perks Advisor
text: The Portland Observatory is of historic significance.  The observatory was built in 1807 it served to communicate with ships providing two way communications.  There were both a telescope and signal flags that were used in the day.  The observatory is worth a visit as it is iconic to Portland.

name: Andy Novikov
text: This observatory is a very interesting restored building in Portland. There are many interesting displays explaining the history of the structure. Amazing 360 degree views from the lantern at the top. A must-see when visiting Portland and be ready to the stair climbing.

name: J Philli
text: I worked as a tour guide (docent...volunteer) a couple years ago for a summer and a bit after Labor Day.  I REALLY enjoyed it.  As time on I did a lot of research and had access to an historian. Since you have a 360° view of Portland, Casco Bay, out to the ocean, you can spot many interesting sites, research them, and then add to the tour narrative.  What history!  Wow! In 1807 Captain Lemuel Moody (1768-1846), ordered construction of this octagonal, 86-foot high tower on Munjoy Hill to serve as a communication station for Portland’s harbor. It was a venture designed to give a competitive edge to ship owners who paid Moody a subscription fee to alert dock workers, 'their ship had come in'.  JeffP

This is a typical fast food place. There are actually two stores here a Taco Bell and a Kentucky Fried Chicken. The food is as expected. I had the Kentucky Fried Chicken. I like Kentucky Fried Chicken but I rarely eat there. Maybe once every two years tops.
This is a really great location for a store. The inside is small but clean and there were ample spaces to sit even for larger groups.
Because there are two restaurants  here there is a fairly large selection of food from which to choose. This makes it nice for a family that might like different types of food To get what they want. All in all it's a decent place, good location, decent food.

text: Friendly wait staff, very good food with ample servings and great prices!  Only reason I did not give 5 stars is the noise.   10/01/2016.  Back again and again satisfied.  Noise level better this time.  Food was hot, tasty and timely.  Lesley, our waitress, was cheerful and on top of things.  Even though the place was very busy, our wait was no more than 30 minutes from door to appetizer.  Entrés were 45 minutes.  Not bad at all for the volume.  Nice meal.  Great staff.                                 Update:  06/01/17.                     Just ate lunch here.  Ordered our favorite meal, seafood stuffed mushrooms and chicken tenders.  Both were dry, dry, dry.  Related to waitress who related to manager and they did not charge for one stuffed mushroom entre.  She did offer to make another set but not enough time for us.  However, if I was to have time to stay, I would have challenged this more.  I found no seafood in mine and friend found one shrimp in hers.  Does not qualify for seafood stuffing in my opinion.  Again, it was dry.  The buffalo tenders tasted ok but, very dry.  I am down grading due to managers unwillingness to not offer a no charge for mushroom entres that were not easily eaten and not as advertised.  We did not eat more than a couple bites.

name: dennis apotris
text: Sad but I used to love it here. They used to have the best sandwiches.  Portland has seen alot of these types of stores disappear over the past 30 years. Growing up every neighborhood had at least 1 if not 3. Now I camt even find one that has fresh bread fresh veggies and decent cold cuts. I bought 4 large Italians Sunday and we got home to find that one had the tomato top on the sandwich. Who the hell eats the tip piece of the tomato and the bottom was on the other one. The other two were odered no onion extra pickle and labeled as such. Both loaded with onions and no extra pickles. . The bread wasn't the freshest either. This is first time that I've had a problem with bread at this location. I've noticed that chain stores like to freeze their bread and you can always tell. I've noticed a big difference in quality since they franchised the name. It's too bad because they are the inventors of the Italian sandwich. I'll have to try the other store that recently reopened since remodeling after a fire. Hope to see better quality next time I take a chance at this location. This as far as I know the original family running it since I can remember. They used to be the best.

text: When you feel like having breakfast at Wendy’s and notice there is no line think about why this must be. I ordered 1 simple sandwich, sausage egg and cheese biscuit..did not even complicate it by ordering the value meal and the guy still couldn’t get it right. No egg, week old hard biscuit and cold...when I took it back to get my egg put on it the older man working Tuesday mornings at 9:45 began arguing with me. What a way to start the day..a simple apology and an offer to fix it for me would have been just fine, instead of starting my day with a smile, I gave him the sandwich and was so bothered by how I was treated that I just pulled away with my sandwich paid for but no Sammy in my tummy not really feeling like eating it anymore if this is what I have to go through. From the apparent lack of business it appears others feel the same way. :(

text: I went there last night on my way home. First,  it's a pain to get to and I almost missed the entrance due to lack of proper lighting in the parking lot/entrance area. At the order window,  I cannot hear the guy taking my order and ask him several times to speak up. My radio is off and my vehicle is quiet. There is a lot of traffic noise. I get up to the window and the guy tells me to just leave my truck and he'll give me the food. Ummm,  yeah that's a hard no Buddy. He asks again,  laughing,  then tells me he's asked other people and they told him to buzz off. He's an older gentleman missing a few informal gnashers. I told him again,  not happening. Pull up to the next window. I sit there for a good five minutes watching a skinny jean clad kid wondering around aimlessly. I can see the dining room is deserted. I do suppose that should have been my first clue,  the utter lack of other diners. The kid finally pours some drinks and walks away again. Another minute goes by. (Yes,  only another minute but those things are eternal when you've been on the road all day,  you've got a grumpy teenager in the backseat with the wet dog and your co-pilot is giving these guys the stink eye.) I see a taller,  older man walk by, that due to his oversized,  untucked, button up shirt,  gives the distinct impression of an umpa-loompa. Yep. Still no drinks,  not even a hi,  sorry about the wait. The kid finally squeezes an unholy amount of strawberry sauce into a cup and makes my strawberry lemonade (it was sickly sweet). We finally,  at 9 minutes get our drinks. There is surprisingly,  only one car behind us in the drive through and no one in the dining room. Another 3 minutes and we get our food. Two baconater meals and a bbq cheeseburger meal. Only one of those was supposed to be a special order,  plain with only ketchup. It wasn't. I didn't touch the fries,  drank not even half of the syrup drink and my burger tasted gamey. I didn't think anything of it. Until four hours later,  I was in horrible pain,  burning up and puking my guts out. No,  I was not sick prior to this and I cannot remember the last time I've vomited. Overall a bad experience and I strongly recommend avoiding the Wendy's in the South Portland Mall area at all costs.

name: Just Me
text:
A neighborhood strip mall with an eclectic variety of stores, including:
Maine Hardware, Portland's largest hardware store
Save-a-Lot, a large discount supermarket
Buckdancer's Choice, Portland's oldest store selling musical instruments
Coastal Trading, a large,diversified pawn shop
A (so-called) Dollar Store
A laundromat
a pool hall
A fast food sub sandwich shop
A chicken restaurant
Also in the immediate area are a Greyhound Bus station, Mexican, Asian, BBQ, and pizza restaurants, a smoke shop, Asian food stores, bars, an Italian Sandwich shop, misc. chain fast food establishments.

text: I went there to purchase an item that was on sale for Christmas dinner. After several fruitful attempts to get assistance to get them item I wanted I went on , found some other items I needed, checked out and left. I left a review through the website on the receipt. The next day the manager called me, apologized and after discussion he assured me that there was plenty of the product I was looking for in stocks. Some days later I went back to the store to purchase the same item that was still on sale. I was advised by a worker in the depth that they did not receive delivery that day of any of the items I was looking for. He suggested that I try again in a couple of days. How can an item be on sale when it is not in stock? I'll try again but if the item is not in stocks I'll shop elsewhere. I've been shopping at Shaw's since 1985.

text: Shaws is not my favorite grocery store. The prices are much higher than the other local chains. The stores generally do not seem to be well stocked. I heard customers having verbal altercations and it was a bit scary while management well management did not seem aware. I will say the "Store Director" spoke with me at length about my concerns which I appreciated, but he did seem controversial to me and not a great listener. I will shop elsewhere and in the big scheme of things right now I guess my individual concerns don't matter much. But stores other than this Shaws seem to be limiting the number of customers at a time, spray disinfecting the carts and for some reason more shoppers seem to be wearing face coverings.  And with the loud argument between 3 customers I could hear three aisles away I did not feel completely safe in there. text:
I can find some good deals here when they have specials and 10 for $10. Items that are not in some special I feel are more expensive then other stores I go to in the area. I very seldom see any workers out on the floor especially in produce area. There is seldom workers in the bakery also. They seem to use the red $5 stickers pretty heavily throughout the store no matter what it is and how much there is of the item. The self checkout always need help from cashier's and most times talk about items in the package area then they shut down and blink red. There are never many cashier's and really not many people in the store.

Update 1/8/2020:
I was at Shaw’s today to get light hamburger rolls by the Shaw’s signature brand. I brought them home and used tonight for burgers. My wife bit into hers just as I was getting mine from the bag and noticed green tint on rolls. I turned the bag over and they were all covered with mold, but to late she already bit into hers. I am taking them back tomorrow and show Shaw’s that the bag said fresh thru 1/8/2020 and they were all moldy. Better check what you buy here! Beware of the red $5 stickers in produce. You can get a pound of strawberries a dollar cheaper in the regular packaging than the $5 bowls.

Update 7/23/2020: This Shaw's has signs saying masks required to shop in their store. I saw at least one lady that I guess thinks that it doesn't apply to her. Why isn't the front end manager standing right there not enforcing it. The lady also had her own bags which by other stores are not allowed right now. I would let them know people are not abiding by the state mandate.

You may have to wait a little bit to get in sometimes, but it's worth the wait.

Doris had their awesome She Crab Soup, Crab Cakes and their infamous Lobster Mac and Cheese. I also had the She Crab Soup but ordered their mouth watering Lobster Pie. All to die for. Good thing we walked about 10 miles today. The place was packed when we dined here for lunch a couple October's ago as we traveled throughout New England. text:
Maine Diner has a nice covered ramp for wheelchair access. The food is good basic fair that is the hallmark of Americana dining. In the summer they offer food right from their own garden at the back of the restaurant.

Our personal favorites are the Red Flannel hash available only on Saturdays while it lasts, and the DownEast Benedict.

The service is superb! You won't find a better wait staff. When you combine great food and great wait staff, you have the ingredients of a top-notch restaurant. Therefore, the waits can be long during peak hours, and the restaurant can get noisy when it is full.

If you are a coffee connoisseur, you may find their offering just a little disappointing.

text: Prices are good. Food is excellent.  Had the clam cakes. Delicious!

name: Matthew Calder
text: We had crab cakes, lobster Mac and cheese and seafood chowder. They were all delicious and at good prices. Service was very good. Love eating here.

name: George Thayer
text: Wasn't bad at all. Filling. Get there early!!!

name: Linda Evju
text: So glad you are back,delicious as usual, thank you for all your hard work!

name: Gus Wolf
text: You will love 💘 it here.

name: Kathy Contarino
text: Favorite for breakfasts. Love the Irish Benedict!

name: Daniel Porter
text: This place is the best diner ever. Absolutely no comparison.

name: fred earle
text: Food was good but it was barly nuke warm

name: Tricia McDougal
text: Our waitress dropped our order some of the fish fell off and all of the clamstrip roll. Kim the waitress put my fish plate on table and ordered another clamstrip roll 11 minutes later ask if that was all the fish on my plate and Kim said nothing fell off my plate which it did because I have picture of the food on the floor. I'm with my 98 year old grandmother, I'm not going to eat while she has no food in 11 minutes my food is cold. I ask to pack up food that I never touched and Kim took it away 8 minutes later she returned with packed up food. I payed the bill left that food there and left with my grandmother. Do you think I would take that food after I complain and who knows where it went!!!? Should of ordered 2 new lunch items when it was dumped so we could eat together. I payed for bad service and no food. In the picture this is what $9 worth of fish looks like. I saw 3 other pieced on floor. Not happy and poor service!!!

name: Kevin Tappa
text: Always consistently good. High quality food at reasonable prices. A plus to go in February for lunch and walk right in with zero wait. Seafood chowder is the mist have item, you won't be disappointed.

name: Linda Kozak
text: Home town feel. Great food and big portions!!

name: Ellen Rudert
text: Food was outstanding, service as well I stop worth making..yum !!😁

name: Michael Lheureux
text: Service was great. Food came out quickly and correct. Everything was delishious. Much better experience than I expected for such a well known and busy venue. They lived up to their reputation.

name: Ismael Olmeda
text: The food was great. The service was good. Had the meet lovers omelette was stuffed with meat. My wife had the vegetable omelette she said it was great also. Very busy place.

name: B Christopher
text: The best baked lobster ever!

name: Sean LeVine
text: Very good but prices are kinda high for breakfast. I understand it's a famous place but there are so many other choices for breakfast that are better and less money. We still enjoy visiting once each time we visit.

name: Deborah Lambdin
text: The almond encrusted French Toast is awesome!!!!

name: TJ Grundler
text: Waited 20 minutes holding my purse and card in my hands waiting for the check and she came up and asked would you like any desert we said "No. But we would like the check." And after she heard the word no she went and served another table. Still no check.

name: david mispel
text: I would have given it 5 stars except for the fact the place isn't big enough to  handle the amount of people that go there with 20 to 40 minute wait for breakfast however if you don't mind the wait the food is great. Also if you go early am or brunch wait time is much shorter if at all. I would also mention that lunch and dinner I never had to wait. Staff is friendly waitresses are very competent of the many times I have eaten there never once did I have any issues with my order. Plenty of parking also has a very nice gift store right next door. Happy travel

name: Crystal Dow
text: Could not ask for better food or service. Biscuits and gravy are worth the drive!!

name: Leslie Welch
text: I give the Maine Diner five stars, and I give their gift shop five stars . Their staff is friendly and helpful. They have a nice menu and their food is delicious. When I was at the Maine Diner I enjoyed my experience there immensely. The Maine Diner is very popular, the Maine Diner is a really nice place.

name: David Sager
text:
This place is fantastic.
The portion sizes are good, and if you get one of the breakfast burritos you better bring the appetite. Because it's big. And filling.
Also the corn muffins are good enough that five Iowa boys raved about the corn muffins for days. They would tell you that it is the best corn muffins you could ever have.
Really this is the place to be. And it's usually busy, which is another great sign. Plan ahead because for breakfast you may have to wait a bit before eating. It is worth it though! So stay, chill, eat your fill, and mark it in your maps to never forget it!

name: Stephen Harrison
text: Top notch breakfast yummy

name: Stacie Kivett
text: First place we went when arriving in Maine. Breakfast was great!

name: Christina Levitan
text: When we arrived, the place was packed. We were given a pager and we were told it would be a 20 minute wait but we could head over to the gift shop  to pass the time. But luckily, it was just a few brief minutes before a table was ready for us. It is really tight in there and would be difficult to get someone in a wheelchair into the back but the Maine Diner does make it as wheel chair accessible as possible so perhaps it would be easier to be seated in the main dining room. Anyhow, we ordered our drinks and breakfast and despite being incredibly busy, our order was out quickly. My only complaints are that because they are so busy, they must make sides beforehand because I had ordered specifically one thing, but received something generic instead. However, they fixed it for us easily. They had also piled the entire breakfast on top of the pancakes. Over easy eggs, bacon, sausage, and toast on top of pancakes. I'm not sure who likes yolk in their pancakes but not me. Anyway, because the plate was so full, my sausage had fallen off the plate because there was no room. Again, they fixed it super fast but maybe just put food on 2 plates like every other restaurant in existence? Had also bought a coffee and asked for a refill but it never came. Again, they were busy so I get it. It just could have been a lot smoother but we do look forward to visiting again in the future when they aren't as busy.

name: Bruce P. Maeder Sr.
text: best lobster roll in Maine

name: Angela Blount
text: Blueberry pancakes and BB muffin absolutely delicious! A must have when in Wells.

name: MARK MULLICAN
text: The best soups and chowders I tasted on the entire journey through Maine!  Fast service and a few famous dishes also. Highly recommend!!!

name: Dawn Haberman
text: Delicious as ever... service was excellent!!

name: Stephen Lareau
text: Our waitress was very friendly and helpful. The food was very tasty and fresh especially the salad bar. I'll be back.

name: Erin DYER
text: Great for breakfast, lunch, dinner or dessert!

name: Marcelino Perez
text: So much memories about this good restaurant so much good food there but service not that great they need to work on consistency

name: Jason Cesari
text: Busy but worth the wait.  Reasonable prices and great food.  Staff friendly and desserts to die for.

name: jean paul arsenault
text: Great Service, Good Food and a Very Clean Establishment! What more can one ask for? Certainly recommend them 👌!

name: Krystine Ouellette
text: Super waitress and the food was very good

name: Damian Watson
text: First stop and it was great.  I own and operate The Brookside Inn, in Smyrna, ME, and have followed The Maine Diner on Facebook for sometime now.  So happy to finally make it in!!

name: Kiki Reno
text: Maine Diner is one of our favorite places to go in Maine! Always absolutely delicious food and great customer service!!

name: UDT Jr
text: ALWAYS Great meals, comfort food. Great staff. Diner atmosphere family friendly place. I make it a point to stop here. Worth waiting for.

name: Madeline Coats
text:
Meh.
I was disappointed with most of what I got, however, the pieces of lobster that I overpaid for were very good once I uncovered them from the soggy, unnecessary, crumb topping. The rest of the items were lackluster, unfortunately. Also, the service wasn’t top notch. We had to ask for water refills and she wasn’t very attentive, although, she was nice.

name: B.F. Maine
text: The food here can be hit or miss, but the atmosphere and history makes it a 5 star place every time. I have been to the Maine Diner a couple dozen times over the years, and there are certain dishes that I get on a regular basis. The seafood chowder for one is amazing. Go for the atmosphere, reasonable prices, and to be a part of history. On top of that, you will probably get a great meal as well - except for the times you get a mediocre one.

name: David Glazebrook
text: I LOVE this place. Great biscuits and gravy. Friendly staff and great food.

name: Lisa Bilowith
text: Great lobstah roll and strawberry shortcake!!

name: LaLa !
text: It's usually our first stop when we get off the highway I love some mac and cheese and cod fish cakes. Amazing food great staff very clean

name: Diana Baker
text: I have not been though this diners doors for at least 3-4 years now....My family and I were repeat customers......my family no longer goes as well......went in for breakfast, (off season) asked for over medium eggs and got barely over easy eggs.  Told waitress right away and she said: " if you want over medium ask for over hard"????? She argued with me about how to order eggs.... Being a professional short order cook I know my stuff....its taken me this long to give this review as I hate bad reviews, but if it's earned, it's earned.   I hope they have improved.....and got rid of that waitress.

name: Bruce Locke
text: Great food.

name: Kathy Woodman
text: Maine Diner never disappoints! Always good food and service ❤

name: Heath Leavitt
text: One of the best places to eat in Maine.

name: erin libby
text: Blueberry ice cream was amazing

name: kc193
text: Everything is delicious! I am never disappointed and the service is always excellent and friendly. Gluten free bread available as well!

name: John L
text: Seated almost instantly, food came out quickly. Coffee better than expected. Friendly staff, will be back!

name: Bruce Giroux
text: Great food.

name: Jake Harvey
text: Yeah the place is great. But the staff is positively unbelievable.

name: Susan Rodrigues
text: Must go to place. Food is excellent. Top rate seafood chowder.

name: Geoff Quick
text: Great food for a good price....

name: Bill Copeland
text: As usual, Maine diner has a great selection of food. From seafood to meatloaf and the famous Eddie Andelmans hot dogs and macaroni and cheese dinner. And, oh yes, most meals come with corn muffin !

name: Stephen Leeman
text: One of the best Diners I’ve ever been to,really gonna miss it

name: Debra Browne
text: Excellent, excellent ... excellent. Was actually too full to finish my dessert...hmm that never happens!

name: Ariel López
text: The best cornbread I have eaten to date.

name: Gabriele Manganaro
text: Great new England seafood. Lots of lobster dishes and homemade plates. Friendly and efficient service. Absolutely recommend it

name: Mary Swerdon
text: Cod cakes are a must try.

name: Joseph Nolette
text: Looked a little dated from outside but have to say the food was amazing

name: Therese O'Brien
text: Love the food. Staff is  great. You never know who you might run into (L.Tiant).

name: Cory Curtis
text: Good food and great hospitality

name: Coco's
text: Always great food

name: Kim Mariner
text: Home cooked food style.. Great seafood chowder!

name: Christopher Blaudschun
text: The service was friendly and efficient. We felt the food was good, but not great.

name: Scott Anderson
text: Waitress was friendly, food was ok. My wife and I visited the restaurant for breakfast, it was our first visit. I wanted to go because I am a huge fan of Diners, Drive Ins, and Dives and they had been featured on that show.  I am a little torn with my review though.  I liked the food but it came out way too fast.  I ordered an omelette with toast and home fries and a single biscuit with sausage gravy on the side. My wife ordered the 2 egg breakfast with corned beef hash. It took no more than 5 mins for our food to come out.  Don't get me wrong I do enjoy prompt service but when food comes out that fast it can only mean that mean that sides are being pre-cooked and held in warming trays. I understand it's a diner, and diner food is what is it is but there is no way that my order came out that fast with everything being cooked to order.  Corned beef hash was canned, nothing to write home about.  Wife said it was cold and not cooked properly.  Those things aside, food was good. I challenge them not to utilize pre-cooked food and step up their game, I will try one more time.

name: Dale Herman
text: Great food, friendly staff.

name: Darrell Stam
text: Great comfort food, with large portions and local seafood favorites.  Ordered the lobster melt and it was delicious!

name: Benjamin E. Skelton
text: Great restaurant breakfast all day. Second best turkey dinner ever in any restaurant

name: J
text: Used to be very good. Today clam chowder was lukewarm, blt was mostly l very little t and one slice of b for $6.00. Bread was not toasted. We had two different pies and we couldn't cut the crust without a knife. It was like cardboard. I don't think we will go back. You can't live on your laurels unless you live up to them.

name: Bill Bowes
text: Little bit of a disappointment,  food was average,  our server took our order, and we never saw her again, until she brought the check.

name: Amanda Shin
text: Love this place, great food. Taste like homr made, helpful and friendly staff. Get there early during the summer

name: Danielle Duckworth
text: Every time I come here I'm never disappointed. The seafood chowder is delicious. The best I've ever had. All of the food is great and reasonably priced for the portions you get. It's a local gem. Service is always fast and friendly.

name: Jessie Paradis
text: Maine Diner is a great place to get a good  meal.They have All Day Breakfast. The people are so friendly and fast getting your food to you. They are Iconic.

name: Ronald Reilly
text: A little loud,  but good food and service. Our waitress, Jennifer, is very knowledgeable about gluten free options and what you should not eat off of the menu. Made a big difference for me.

name: syn edgē
text: Stopped here for breakfast the other day upon a hotel clerk's recommendation. Wasn't disappointed. The crowd waiting outside (on a very frigid Maine Morning) and the online reviews kinda prove this doesn't need a 5 star vote from us. Wow! This place is what all eateries should strive to become. A grand slam review coming soon!

name: Don Winterhalter
text: I'm a big fan of the Maine Diner.  The food is good, especially the breakfasts, the lobster pie and the chowder.  Even the coffee is good and you can't always count on that in Maine.  The only thing that isn't terrific is that the place isn't much to look at, but I think that's actually a good thing because it can get awfully crowded inside, especially in the summer

name: Cam M
text: There were 3 adults in my party and one had heard amazing things about this restaurant from someone, so he wanted to check it out. Well, 3 of us didnt like it. The appetizer was very overcooked. The main course lacked flavoring of anything except butter. Very surprised to see that Diners, Drive ins and Dives had been here. We just were not fans.

name: Ryan Michaud
text: This place was awesome. We were sat maybe 10 minutes and our food came out. The food was great and affordable. The commercials actually tell the truth about the place. If you are in this area check it out.

name: Andrew Jenson
text: Fast service good food. My sweetheart and I was able to share a meal and have more than plenty to eat between the two of us at a very good price

name: Trisha Watson
text: Always a great meal. We stop here for cod cakes Benedict every time we're in Maine. Doesn't get any better! Classic diner food with a great Maine twist.

name: Todd Doody
text: Talk about good food!!

name: Bill Thomas
text: Regular breakfast fare. Good coffee. Friendly fast service. Nothing special about the food but the service is always great. This place does an enormous amount of advertising throughout New England so they get huge crowds in tourist season, but there are much better breakfast venues at more reasonable prices just down the road. As my friend from Texas said when we ate here, "this place is all hat and no cattle."

name: Mark Levensalor
text: As popular and perfectly located as it is they should really consider treating it down and building something much bigger and more modern. I felt very cramped and the place was packed at 3pm. They're doing something very right I guess. Maybe I'm just getting old.

name: Brenda Grimes
text: Love this dinner. Excellent food and service. Lots of choices to pick from. Great prices too.

name: Mark Addis
text: Yes!  It was all that and more!  We've been travelling throughout Maine over the past month and experienced some of the best seafood.  The Lobster Pie was amazing, along with the seafood chowder.  Even our 3 children with them loved the homemade mac/cheese, and their Roast Beef.  The service was great also with an attentive waitress.  We took some homemade Blueberry pie to go...and it was awesome!

name: Gary Ovitt
text: Friendly atmosphere great and reasonably priced breakfast. Always had a good meal with top notch quality and quantity.

name: Anne F.
text: I had the Lobster Benedict and it was great!!! My husband had the eggs with ham and he said it was very good!! I am sure that we will be coming back. 👍👍

name: Mary Shannon
text: Solid food. Lots of great menu choices. Breakfast was amazing. One really nice aspect is their ingredient book - everything they make is in there, so if you have allergies or sensitivities, you can read for yourself. Much easier than hoping the wait staff gets it right. Fun stop.

name: Gregory Davidson
text: Delicious breakfasts served up hot!  Something like 4 million people served since 1971.

name: Melinda K
text: My first time at the Maine Diner.  We had breakfast and it was very good and filling.  Service was great and the coffee and food were hot.  We will return.

name: Paul L
text: Fantastic diner scene, we ordered out and all meals impressed. Would love to sit down here next time but this time it looked like it wasn't an option unless you waited a long while.

name: Mg 0
text:
Loved this Wells diner. Open year-round. Down-home restaurant, local, welcoming to all. Good food and a no-pressure atmosphere.
I loved my lobster salad and the accompanying corn muffin was ideal : tender, corn-mealy, flavourful without being outrightly sweet, nor was it greasy.
I went on a Friday in early May at 2.30pm and sat down immediately for lunch.

name: denise Gamester
text: The waitress was so very nice and the food was great!

name: Meg Bragdon
text: Good homestyle food and friendly staff

name: Matt C
text: So so good! The seafood chowder was out of this world. Going back for breakfast tomorrow morning

name: Bill Robinson
text: Food was just okay services great atmosphere was nice but food was just okay

name: Kim K
text: Sweet breakfast and lunch options. Friendly family run. Highly suggest you check it out.

name: Malayna Shiels
text: Not quite cracked up to what it is supposed to be. The service was great but the food was very bland. And the seafood plater was expensive for what was actually served. There seemed to be not much fish and just a lot fried junk; it also did not come with a side or even a pickle. No offense, but I can make much better food at home for cheaper. The breakfast items seemed to be a lot better than the lunch and dinner options. If you do go there, I recomed going for breakfast.

name: Sue Heaney
text: Exceptional diner food.  Lobster roll was stuffed full and offered many different sides.  Dessert was wonderful also.  We had chocolate cake and Indian pudding with home-made ice cream.  Expect to wait in line but it's worth it.

name: Danielle
text: Good food... busy, touristy diner..  always a wait but if you've got patience it's worth it.

name: Michael Verde
text: Allie our server was so friendly.  The food was home-cooking scrumptious!

name: Trina Rojas
text: Went here with my friend Ella. She raved about the seafood chowder, said it was her absolute favorite. I got a Reuben, one of my personal dinner faves, it was pretty delicious. Service was very good!

name: Gi na
text: Love this place! Used to come here as a child with my family and now my husband and I bring our daughters here. Sometimes it’s a full house and wait can be a bit but the gift shop attached to the restaurant helps the time pass as there are lots of treasures to look at/buy there.

name: STRONGER Michelle Long
text: I love the Maine Diner, their seafood is always fresh and they have an amazing selection of food to try out.

name: Donna Merrill-Walls
text: Very good company Tim and I. Good eggs beni,and today the home fries were perfect!!!And the girls were terrific!!!

name: Lynd Blatchford
text: The Maine Diner is very popular with tourists and the lines can be long during the tourist season. It is also popular with local tradespeople who are up and about early. The menu is long and has a large variety of items. The breakfast menu is available all day and is also comprehensive. I find most items to be more salty than I prefer but it should be noted that I use very little salt when I cook and I normally do not put salt on the table. I also sense a high level of fat in most dishes, i.e., typical of diner food. During tourist season the noise level can be quite high. The servers are terrific even when the diner is mobbed. In summary, for tourists the Maine Diner is a place to be experienced. If you are a local I recommend going very early to enjoy a tasty and filling breakfast.

name: dana jackson
text: Love the food and great waitstaff but expect to wait due to popularity

name: Rick Hyde
text: Great food, 5star service very affordable

name: Richard Jones
text: Great food, fast service and fair price.  A favorite place to eat.

name: Mike S
text: Very friendly staff and good selection of diner food or of what Maine is known for.  The seafood chowder was very good, along with the rest of our meal.   The house dressing for salads is a creamy dill, which we wish they bottled to sell.

name: H. John Herzog
text: We have never had a bad meal here and the prices are great! Tons of delicious food fills you plate.. great friendly wait staff. Favorites include: corn muffins, grapenut custard, red flannel hash, lobster roll... every special I have ever had there.... the list goes on.

name: Heather Peatman
text: If you're on Rt 1. stop in. If you want large delicious portions for a good price go here! I don't think I have ever left wanting more or feeling unsatisfied. The staff is spectacular and the food is wonderful. The place is clean and has a "diner" feel but harbors a good family atmosphere too. It's family tradition to stop here.

name: James Hamelin
text: Good food, good service, reasonable prices. Clam cakes not that good.  Chowders are excellent.  Popular spot on route 1, count on at least a 15 minute wait to be seated.  Part of a Maine vacation experience.

name: Bob R
text: Good food. Fast service.  Busy diner.

name: Gary J. Winthorp
text: This place is banging. Great food portions, got the chili and have been eaten it for three days now. And at this point I'm taken a bite a day to see how long I can go. Haddock so fresh I swear I saw it move, and workers so nice I thought they were up to somthing.

name: Rylee Pellegrino
text: Such a cute little spot! I got the 2 on 2 on 2 and it was a lot of food but the blueberry pancakes were absolutely delicious! Highly recommend for something more local driven.

name: jordan goodwin
text: Fairly decent food.  I think the prices are a bit high for what your getting.  I suppose that's not outside the norm in a tourist area like this though.

name: Jen Warner
text: Great food. Wonderful service, the 3 servers we have had so far, Emily, Bethany, and Jennifer are exceptional servers with wonderful, pleasant, and fun attitudes! The food comes out fast too

name: oneredeemer lives
text: Nice diner environment and quick service.

name: Nelson George
text: I had breakfast for brunch. Eggs, toast, pancakes, sausage, bacon, all times two for 10 bucks. Very good.

name: Nicholas Abell
text: We called ahead for takeout, it was ready on time. The lobster roll was delicious , the fried haddock sandwich the oil could have used to be changed. It was good regardless

name: tawny_one
text: Quentisential Maine dining experience. Fresh, hot, home cooking, with seafood dishes that are pretty good. Very, very fast, friendly service everytime.

name: Susan Williams
text: Always delicious! We are never disappointed with the food or the service.

name: Lyn Hodgdon
text: Very good for diner food.. I got to full on the corn muffin..

name: Deanna Friedman
text: Best chicken pot pie EVER! Also great onion rings. Clam cakes were premade and just ok otherwise I would give it 5 stars. Been coming here for 28 years, MD never disappoints with a good meal.

name: Lee Demers
text:
Classic diner food to be found here with an almost overwhelming menu. Chunky seafood chowder hits the spot. Breakfast is indeed served all day and you will see pancakes and eggs along side burgers and soups emerge from the kitchen if you sit at the counter. Runs like a well-oiled machine.

They have dessert to go! The diner is well prepared to pack up a slice of cake or pie for later. We got the chocolate chip cookie pie to go, very rich and sweet.

name: P Keithly
text: Great Diner atmosphere, terrific food. Can get busy at peak times if the year, but other times no problems!

name: Valerie Pinkham
text: Great  food. Great service.

name: Michael Dagenhart
text: Excellent food! A Must stop every time we visit Maine.

name: Kevin Santom
text: Fast efficient service, good price, have the blueberry pancakes

name: David Bilodeau
text: Food is general comfort food at an okay price.

name: Joe Harris
text: Great food and great service. This is one of several reasons that this restaurant was featured on Guy's Diners, Drive Inns and Dives show.

name: Swizzle Stick
text: Food is out dated and not at all what Maine has to offer. Wait staff is not attentive and could use some retraining. If you go here remember your wallet. If you see the restaurant while driving, keep driving.

name: J H
text: The lobster pie was even better than I remembered... but, the mashed squash was way too sweet.

name: David Eldredge
text: Was actually across the street at the Bull and Claw. Had a delicious maple glazed Salmon dinner.

name: Christopher O'brien
text: Friendly staff and food very good.

name: Katie Kearney
text: Food is so good! Portions are huge for the price!

name: Brigit McCallum
text: A busy summer Friday night but the wait was just less than the predicted half hour. A friendly, Diner atmosphere and excellent service brought us a delicious full turkey dinner and some yummy clam cakes. All in all Maine summer evening and a comfy place to have a good meal.

name: Tracy Miller
text: Excellent food and service!

name: Emilie Vashion
text: Great food excellent service. Big portions, but have a Senior menu

name: Helen Lamb
text: Food was delicious and plenty of it friendly wait staff and atmosphere  and prices were good

name: Bret Casella
text: Family tradition to go here every year and I love that 4 generations of my family have all been able to eat here and have so many fond memories

name: James Dawson
text: Great place! Good food, reasonable prices, clean establishment, and great service. We will definitely be going back. Nice variety and a great kids menu very large portions!

name: Robert Corwin
text: Great food fun placr

name: Alan Brearley
text: Great food and friendly staff.  Will return for sure.

name: Valerie Arbour
text: Love this place! Breakfast, lunch,and dinner! Waitress very professional.  Clean,and great prices!

name: James Grasso
text: Been coming to the Maine Diner for years for the best dinner food you can get anywhere! Is a reason all the local folks come here in the winter and summer - The food and service is great!

name: Christina Michaud
text: Service was lightning fast! Food was excellent and can't wait to go back!

name: Shawna Lei
text: Food is actually pretty good. It feels crowded in there sometimes, but the food is so worth it. Huge portions, and the pancakes are ridiculously huge. But I dont mind the leftovers. Prices are fair, especially for the amount of food you get. If it wasnt for the 30 minute drive I'd be here every weekend getting breakfast.

name: Arn Heggers
text: Great food and service, large groups need to make reservations.

name: Phyllis Powers
text: It was great as usual. They were having a benefit blueberry pancakes for childhood Alzheimer's. I think that's awesome. I was glad to participate in that.

name: Allen VanGuilder
text: Prices way to high ,portion not enough food !  Food was good

name: Marta Gaines
text: The fries are incredible!  The rest of the food is very good.

name: Edwina Hudson
text: Best lobster rolls, they also have home made Indian Pudding with Vanilla Ice cream

name: Anza Beldon
text: Food and service the best. Fun night.

name: Joan Cook
text: Great food cozy place but is a bit noisy..well worth it though

name: Joe Malinowski
text: If you are within 50 miles of this place, plan a stop. All meals are worth it but the always on breakfast menu is REALLY worth it. The country breakfast with ham, a biscuit, baked beans, eggs and home fries is hard to beat. Only regret when ordering this is leaving the blueberry pancakes behind. That alone is worth a second trip. Not crazy about the upcharge but the extra dollar for maple syrup is worth it. Bottom line is GO! Breakfast, lunch or dinner doesn't matter. Just go.

name: Vicki Matthews
text: OMG still a fabulous meal. We had a bowl of seafood chowder and a corn muffin. The corn muffins aren't  always moist but the flavor is so there. We have traveled from VT to the Maine Diner just for LUNCH,, many times

name: Donna Day
text: Best Maine diner.  Great service and food.

name: Jennifer Downey
text: Breakfast burrito was perfect! Every bite was everything I could have asked for. Its no california breakfast burrito but they certainly did it well. Thank you

name: Deborah Shipp
text: Really good comfort food at reasonable prices. On the summer when there are almost always a wait I order take out and either eat at home or go to a picnic area overlooking the ocean near Wells Harbor.

name: Patty Webb
text: Well worth the visit.  Good ole home cooking!

name: Bill Perry
text: As always, this is my favorite of all places to eat when in Maine. Excellent food, excellent service. The friendliest staff. Good people! Great food and there are so many choices, from diner food to all day breakfast to excellent seafood... I could eat here every day for a year and have something different to eat! Thankfully, there was open counter space and my party of 2 adults and 1 child were seated immediately.

The service was quick to get us our sins and efficient at providing our orders to us promptly and with minimal fuss. Our server, Jessica, answered it questions and provided great recommendations: lobster rolls were well-portioned and the almond-battered Texas-style French Toast was a touch of home here in Maine.

The children's menu is fairly priced with the typical offerings (for us, the options for either a grilled cheese sandwich or mac and cheese were greatly appreciated!). Children's-sized drinks also were available.

For dessert, the chocolate chip cookie pie (served warm with ice cream on the side) was a sweet conclusion to this meal! For a more local experience, the eyes drooled for the Maine blueberry pie as slice after slice left the counter.

Affordable pricing, quick turnaround, friendly service, and diner food done right, here at the Maine Diner!

Though the interior is on the smaller side and can get cramped, it is also very cozy and feels like you're sitting in the family dining room. There is an attached gift shop to boot, if you're looking for a souvenir from Maine.

text:
This is a classic place to visit on any trip to the region, although visiting in the "off season" makes for a much shorter wait for a table (or none at all) and a much quieter and saner dining experience. The food I've had has always been delicious, and the portions are definitely hearty, leaving plenty to take "home" for an entire second meal. My only "complaint" would be that for some reason the pancakes seems to end up with a somewhat chemical-ish taste on the outside that I would only guess would be the result of some sort of spray or something used on the griddle when they are cooked (I don't know for sure what the cause is). It is a rather off-putting taste, but let me just say it never stops me from eating as much of my pancakes as I can there, and taking the rest to finish later. Of course, only real maple syrup will do!

Even in the height on the tourist season, it is still worth waiting to eat there. I'd go nuts dealing with those crowds, but the wait-staff are some of the friendliest people you'll ever meet.

name: Warwick Varney
text:
Living in Maine, the vast majority of businesses in the hospitality industry rely heavily on the summer tourist season for the majority of their business. Maine Diner definitely falls into this category. It's small, cute and typically New England, so obviously draws tourists aplenty to try authentic "clam chowda and lobsta rolls". If you want a quick meal don't even try coming here on a weekend in the spring/summer, unless it's first thing in the morning while the tourists are still asleep.

Rather come here on a weekday afternoon or evening, out of season, when it's quieter. You can order off the breakfast menu any time of day, and there are plenty of tasty options to choose from, however, it's in the typical diner type meals that the Maine Diner excels.

There's a lot to choose from on the dinner menu. Sandwiches, burgers, soups, salads, seafood, comfort food (meatloaf, chili and so on) and bakes; it's very extensive without seeming overwhelming. I don't know how else to describe the food, besides good, honest, wholesome and tasty diner food. Nothing has the flair that you'd expect in a Michelin starred restaurant, where presentation is as important as flavor, but everything looks hearty and tasty. There are no delicate flavors that subtly play off of each other with each bite, but neither is anything over seasoned or spiced to the point where one flavor dominates. It's just good food.

Food aside, there is one thing that REALLY impresses me. The phrase "a place is made by its people" doesn't usually apply to restaurants, but in the case of Maine Diner, it is really true. The wait staff are among the best I've ever dealt with. Everyone knows what they need to do, where everything is, what everything on the menu is made from, and how it's prepared. Sometimes we think of wait staff as people who ended up doing that job because they just "ended up there", or they're students. Maine Diner's staff are there because they WANT to be there. They like what they do, they do it well, and it shows in their service. There is a good mix of younger less experienced wait staff, and older career women who are ruthlessly efficient in what they do.

I love sitting at the counter of Maine Diner and watching how everything operates. Every item has its exact place behind the counter, from the creamed butter, to the mugs, plates and silverware. Nobody ever has to search for anything, and everything is kept in good supply by the bus staff. You know that cup of chowder is going to be served exactly the same way with its bag of oyster crackers 100 times over, just as the delicious crab cakes I had will consistently come out of the kitchen perfectly cooked and seasoned time after time.

That's what differentiates a good place from a great place. Consistency. You know it's ALWAYS going to be good, you're ALWAYS going to get wonderful service, and you're ALWAYS going to leave feeling satisfied.

name: syn edgē
text:
We were in the midcoast area, taking pictures of snow-covered stuff and pulled in here mainly because it was the plowed out place in the area. Took some pictures and video. Will be back because I bet the view is Amazing in the summertime and the place has been serving food for 70 years!!! Wow!!!
See ya when it's warmer or at least when this 3 feet of snow is gone!

As promised, we returned in May and yes, the view is awesome at this spot. The service was adequate and fast. The terriyaki chicken sandwich was just ok. But the burger was delicious and the fries were pretty good.

But the 2 things that stand out about Bagaduce, is the years in business. 72 years, that is impressive. In this world of fast food, big chains and even faster restaurants turn-over, it’s a great to see a local place, still making burgers, fries and seafood for that long.

Second, the view. I guessed it when the snow was waist-high. This place must be a great place to eat outside in Summer. Check out the new pictures, I bet this place gets rocking with Summer. Not even memorial day , and we had a nice lunch experience there

The atmosphere caught my eye right away kind of pieced together type of layout that really worked for these kinds of establishments. Decorated with many retro signs and many, many pictures and models of fish. Lots of interesting things to see.

The place was medium busy, which was a good sign since it was blistering cold outside and biting wind. The food was pretty decent, I had a blackened grilled chicken sandwich, which was about a 7 out of 10…(I like real spicy food). My partner had a french dip, which her only review was “Damn, I should have gotten the Calamari!”. The adult beverages were average.

I haven't been able to return as much as I wanted to, but plan on going back soon and do a FULL review at that time.

text:
Best Fried Clams in Maine - Bar None.

For a serious fried clam junkie, I can say I've scouted far and wide in the State of Maine to find the best of the best, and the Lost Gull is it.  It's become a much-enjoyed ritual for me to trek over from where I live to have fried clams at the Lost Gull at least once a year.  I look forward to it all year, and just thinking about it makes my mouth water.  Trust me on this...these are the most tender, sweetest, freshest fried clams you'll find.

resp.text:
Hi Joe,

We are sorry that you did not enjoy your experience with us. We just want you to know that we have not cut down on our portions, and weigh each plate out to ensure consistency. We also use fresh Maine haddock, which is what we have always used. We never use cheap or garbage fish, and we cut it daily. Some pieces may be cut different than others, so you may get different cuts of haddock at different times, and haddock chunks are not as perfect as filets, which is why they are chunked up for the fish and chips. We appreciate your concern and feedback!
