text: Great atmosphere very relaxing wide variety of food drink.staff is fantastic

name: Diane Simmler
text: I like their menu and the food is always good. They view of the river is nice. The charm of the old architecture is a plus. This building has become iconic. It's yellow stands out against the landscape of the river and the rocks. There is patio seating when the weather is nice.

name: Cheryl Anderson
text: The food was delicious.  The service was excellent.  We sat out on the open porch and saw two bald eagles swooping across the river and a seal feeding in the river near some rocks.

name: Gabe Rumoro
text: I've given this place an honest run. I had the unfortunate experience of a waitress tipping herself more than $50 with my debit card. The manager helped me get the money back - and I thank her for that. The other disappointing experience is I ordered a large chicken tender to go. 4 tenders for $20+. Is this normal here?? Disappointing. I called but it was late. The other dissatisfying experience was getting a chicken ceasar salad with no chicken. They do have some good food, and some of the waiters/waitresses are very nice. My first mentioned experience is probably the most dissatisfying. That's NEVER happened to me before. Please be careful when writing your tips here, there could be a lowlife about.

name: Dan Mclellan
text: We stopped here for a lunch break with Minis if Maine. It was our lunch stop.

name: Kimberly Rollins
text: Good food but not worth the price in my opinion. My 8$ salad was the size of a side salad

name: Jim LeClair
text: Good pub food in historic mill on the river. Good selection of Seadog  Beer. Large facility accommodates groups easily. Fun place to gather with friends.

name: Martha Logan
text: Miss this restaurant since I moved.  Friendly courteous service. Good menu. Can have long wait so make reservations.

name: Jef Snipe
text:
I had a "special " a $14 pastrami sandwich. Someone needs to teach the chef on how to slice pastrami properly. Sandwich was tiny, perhaps 3 oz of meat.
Service was fine but nothing happened that would make me return or recommend this place. Buy a slicer for heavens sake.

name: Martina Hairston
text: The atmosphere was good and our server was great! Certain classic recipes should remain as is...baked stuffed haddock should not have a sweet creamy sauce. Onion soup is usually a beef broth base with red wine and purple onions....chicken broth, white onions, and rosemary change this too much. Maine is famous for blueberries, was my blueberry ale made with artificial blueberry flavoring?

name: Jo-Ann Christian
text: Love the food and atmosphere.

name: Peter Gore
text: Local plane with good beer, good food and a friendly atmosphere. In the summer lunch, dinner or just a cold beer on their outdoor deck overlooking the river is a true treat.

name: Marc S
text: Great menu. Food executed on a consistent high level. My go to place in the area👍

name: TFM
text: Had the lobster roll but it tasted like it had not too much flavor. This could be because of season changes in lobster or just wasn't prepared that much with seasoning. The potato wedges were great, and the coleslaw and pickle complemented the dish overall. I've been here 2-3x so far and it never disappoints. Their specialty beer is fantastic too.

name: Emily Smith
text: Four stars almost entirely for the location, which is right next to the falls. Definite sports bar vibe, loud and packed. Good on tap brews and large food selection. Food was okay, but nothing stellar.

name: Michael Henderson
text: Food was good. Server was attentive to any concerns. 1 thing not really a place for sashimi.

name: Mark Pettingill
text: Love this place year round. Always have good food and service. We often meet up with friends.

name: Ron Lusk
text: Good beer, good food. I had Cobb Salad with blackened haddock, and it was all excellent. My wife enjoyed her meal, although I can't recall what it was. Beer was good, too, as one would expect.

name: R Boday
text: Fabulous beer, cool venue, *exceptional* menu -- even having a grumpy server doesn't take any stars away from my rating.

name: Amber M
text: Used to be one of my favorite restaurants, but the recent menu is lame (unless you're a huge seafood fan) and way over-priced. The atmosphere is nice though and service was good. The last time my husband and I went in we got an appetizer then left as there were so few dinner options available; the whole menu is mostly sandwiches and burgers. I really expected more entrees from a high end place like this (maybe a decent steak, or even a few chicken meals? Heck, I would have even gotten pasta).. especially for the prices they ask.

name: Nikki Smith
text:
Took my kids out for what I thought would be a quick lunch with a view. This was our first time to Sea Dogs after moving to Maine and I have been wanting to come here just for a beer and a view if nothing else. The interior is great and decorated well. They have outdoor seating that gives you a great view of the river and bridge.

We requested to be seated outside, even with the wait. We didn't get a table for to the side so our view wasn't anything special but being outdoors in a sunny day was nice, especially after all of the rain we've had since we moved here.
The service was super slow. We waited way to Long for our beverages at the start and then waited another decent amount of time just for a refill. Our food took almost 45 min to get to us from the time we placed the order. Simple items such as, peanut butter and jelly, tortilla chips with a hint of melted cheese and a side of Pace picante (which is called nachos on the kids menu) and the hardest of them all, a cheese steak sandwich. I don't told by my waitress that they had dropped my first sandwich and had to make another one and she apologized for the wait. I'm fine with that but I don't understand why it took that long for my kids items to get out?!

I wish I could end this review with a bang and say that the food finally arrived and it was well worth the wait but, it definitely was not. The nachos were stale, the fries were not hot and my sandwich tasted more like a shredded beef sandwich soaked in oil. I'm sure the PB&J would have been decent if it had been brought out when it was made but it came out with slightly hard bread so that only received a few bites as well.

We left with more than half of the food on our plates, 1 refill in over an hour and down $45 in my checking account for overpriced, overrated food.

I may return for a drink or two but I'll pass on the food that go around. I had high hopes for this place being a brewery and somewhere to bring our out of town guests too.

name: Dustin Ouellette
text: Delicious food and great location. Will definitely visit again.

name: CM Brock
text: This is my absolute favorite must go to place for Sunday brunch buffet!  They use farm fresh foods, a great selection, breakfast favorites, carving station, omelette and pancake station, nice cold salads and shrimp, desert station, mimosas and bloody Mary's..  what more can you want?! during the summer is beautiful to sit out in the back and just listen to the river flow by!

name: Zac Angotti
text: First time going and had a great meal!

name: jessica chubbuck
text: Good food nice service

name: Bruce Nelson
text: Great staff and great location.  The food was good, well prepared.  The fun part was looking around for clues of past inhabitants.  This is an old mill on the androscoggin river so there's a lot of history here.  Go see for yourself, you won't be disappointed.

name: Kelli Tome
text: We got here Evey time we have a family outing . The menu is kid friendly and it is such a relaxing place

name: Keith Greaton
text: Great food and beer

name: Jason Prout
text: Food was really good. Service was a little slow, but there were a lot of kids in the restaurant. It was prom night at several schools. Will definitely go again.

name: Samantha Gogan
text: My friends and I had the opportunity to eat lunch here this past Sunday and it was worth the drive! The staff was friendly and attentive despite the place being very busy for brunch/lunch! When I asked for a gluten free menu they listed off all of my options. They were also very accommodating to my dairy allergy. The view from our seats of the river was lovely as well. An overall great experience, we will definitely be back!

name: TMS SMT
text: Took a long time to get our food to us even though it wasn't super busy. Pretty average food, nothing super memorable about the visit outside the wait time

name: Drevik
text: Ordered the steak tip poutine. It was pretty obvious they let it sit a long time before it came out. The gravy had soaked through the fries, making a rather unappealing goo. My wife ordered a salad that managed to be so over dressed that the lettuce has become a soggy mess. All this after a 90 minute wait. Do yourself a favor and skip it. There is way better mere minutes away.

name: pete bernard
text: The absolute best cheese burger and fries by far ! Great atmosphere along with friendly staff. This place is a must for stopping by 😁

name: Mike Kohut
text: This is a great location and space so I was really hoping it'd be good. Service was fine, bit the food and beer weren't great. I had the house IPA, which was described as "hop forward," but I could barely taste them. If I had wanted something watery and tasteless I wouldn't have ordered an IPA. I also had the fish and chips. They were the worst I've ever had: somehow both dry and greasy. I am not a fan of salt, and yet they didn't put nearly enough in this batter. It was heavy and tasteless. The fries and cole slaw were pretty good, though I think most people would expect the slaw to have more sugar or vinegar or mayo. It was pretty much just chopped cabbage. My son liked the Mac and cheese. And my spouse's seafood pie was decent, though too salty and with poorly distributed fillings. We won't be going back, unfortunately.

name: Steve Mather
text: Food was very good. Service was fairly good(very good for 8 of 9. One person had their order arrive 20 minutes after everyone else). It was a bit noisy hard to hold a conversation along a long table.

name: Ross Watson
text:
Went for the brunch. It was amazing! Food was spectacular and the price was fantastic! Was absolutely stunning, can't praise it enough.

Didn't try the regular menu or the beer. But man.... that BRUNCH.

name: Brian Michaud
text: Our food was great. The kitchen really screwed up our 8 burgers (medium when was supposed to be well done, wrong combination of sides etc) but the waitress was fabulous and very attentive.  She made everything right and was on top of everything.

name: Julia Johnston
text: Great setting right on the river. Nice atmosphere both inside and out on the deck.

name: Hawk Dobrich
text: Great blueberry beer. The blueberry BBQ wings are ready mouth watering. The burgers are full of flavor .

name: Hob9200
text: Came in 30 minutes before they closed on a holiday and was treated lovely. The new cheese sticks are delicious and food was good as normal. Beautiful view as well and very scenic building.

name: Rebecca Perron
text: Terrific location in Brunswick with gorgeous views of the water from inside or on the covered porch. The wait staff were attentive without being intrusive. The cider was superb and our dinners were mouth watering, done perfectly. We are now fans, we will return for more!

name: Michael Estes
text: One of the best brunch buffets I've had. Would reccomend.

name: Kelly Heath
text: We went during lunch and received very good service (Though the restaurant was not busy). The atmosphere was nice; the restaurant was quiet. The decor was tastefully done (I love the dog pic wall) and the view was enjoyable. The food was average; nothing to rave about but it wasn’t the worst I’ve had. The restaurant is definitely overpriced for the quality of the dishes they are serving.

name: William Wright
text: Great food, beer, and people!  Fairly kid friendly, but if there was a dedicated kid zone like Bucks Naked BBQ or Gritty's in Freeport that would be awesome.  Nice outdoor seating by the river.

name: Dorothy Sheehan
text: It's not as good as it use to be.  Menu needs work as does the cooks. Great atmosphere though and location.

name: Frank Wozniak
text: Great food and drinks and a nice cozy setting.

name: Nate Hoy
text:
I'm a Mug Club member and have been going regularly for years.   The dining area is open and the ceiling is the original beams and wood from the mill with some funky and interesting nautical equipment hanging from the ceiling.   So it can get pretty noisy when it gets busy.

Service has been consistently attentive and polite, food is invariably very good. Beer is tasty, all of their beer on tap is brewed by Shipyard in Portland.

name: Christopher Clayton
text: This is a great place for families, good food and great staff.  The beer is good and the space is an old Mill on the river.

name: Reynold Bergquist
text: Great food and Service!

name: Eileen Miazga
text: Loved it! Great food. Great service!

name: Shawn Butler
text: Drinks were deep and food was tasty

name: Laura Hatfield
text: Always good food, atmosphere and service

name: Trevor Brown
text: Oh my God. This place is AWESOME! Their food is delicious FAR beyond imaginable, the service is perfect, everyone serving was very kind, the atmosphere is a combination between an old fashioned style restaurant, and a newer style restaurant. I personally LOVE this place. I give it five stars.

name: Ron Gio
text: The beers are sub-par given the choices in Maine.  The food was OK, but not worthy of another trip.  Neat space.

name: Jamie Wall
text: Great food and drinks nice views of the river and bridge good service

name: Ryan Nelson
text: This is a great location for a meal, and the food selection is pretty good. (And I think the quality has improved over the past couple of years.) However, I've never been a huge fan of their beers, which are pretty much all they've got on tap. In the summer, though, sitting on the deck over the river makes it all worth it.

name: L Richardson
text: The Sea Dog is right on the river, beautiful view. If it's warm enough there is outdoor seating. It is in an old mill building. The floors are hardwood and the setting slightly rustic. It was VERY busy when our party of 18 walked in. We were having a birthday party...along with 3 other parties happening. At first I thought it would be overwhelming but I was surprised at how smooth and comfortable it was to talk with family while other parties were happening. There is a diverse menu from onion soup, veggie dishes, gluten free food, burritos, salads, and cornbeef to steak sandwiches. The service was great and the staff were accurate. The bathroom was clean. There is a bar and they have a buffet on Sundays. I liked it!!!!

name: Justin Norris
text: Great food, great drinks, better company 🤪

name: Matt Porter
text: Good menu selection. Service was ok.  Our order on two occasions was messed up. For the price doubt I will return.

name: Christopher Pelonzi
text:
Always love this place. The sunday brunch is, in a word, outta-this-world. I could not believe how good the food was. Not only is is a buffet, but a speciality designer buffet. Incredible.
Their regular fare is top notch and reasonably portioned/priced.
And of course, they have beer. And cider!!
Favorite line from the restaurant:
Beer = hops. Hops = plant. Therefore, beer = salad.

name: Lan Demly
text: Phil's the man.

name: Chris Douglas
text: Easy access and exit, easy to see from the road. Broad menu to satisfy most. Full bar with plenty of craft & commercial beers. It's in an old mill building with antique wood floors and beams with old brick exterior walls. This is popular spot for couples and families. It gets busy, yet not too noisy.

name: SanDra
text: Been frequenting this place since they opened waaay back at the Bowdoin Mill, Topsham... service and food has been consistently very good! They always have good weekend events & music, very casual, Sunday Brunch is excellent! The deck is beautiful in the summer! Great spot!

name: Ash
text: Awesome views of the river. Great food. Beer is not bad either.

name: N F
text: Jambalaya is incredible!!

name: Denise Boucher
text: Pricey and food was not great. Service was very good tho

name: Fred Kenworthy
text: Always stop here on our trip to Maine (at least once) for a beer and fish and chips. We usually get in quickly this time of year (early October). Great Brussel sprouts. Fish and chips are very good as well.

name: Chris Cole
text: Good food, nice atmosphere.

name: Chris Taylor
text: The location of the brewery couldn't be better. If it's a nice day outside you would be doing yourself a disservice to NOT get a table on the deck. The food here was great, the staff behind the bar were all very nice. The beer's are great, but I was surprised by how good the cocktails here are too (if beer isn't your thing).

name: ed rolfe
text: I dropped the rating 2 stars after my last visit. It was busy but we watched 2 tables who came in after us get served their meals well before our simple Shimp Tacos and Burger arrived. Shrimp taco's were popular that night as we saw several orders being served. Our waiter pretty much ignored us after bringing the appetizer, showing only once to ask if we needed a refill on our iced tea, and stating our meal should be there soon. When our dinner finally arrived 45 min after our appetizer was gone. The Tacos were good but the Burger was old and dry. It was obvious it set under a warming lamp a long while, even the plate was hot to the touch. Yeah not so impressed with the food or service now.

name: Allen Bourassa
text: Food and atmosphere was good.

name: Arn Heggers
text: Great atmosphere, selection of beers, great Sunday brunch!

name: Allen Oakes
text: Have their own brewed beer and prices are reasonable. Good family atmosphere.

name: Jill tibbetts
text: They have delicious food and great employees. Friendly.  I had the calamari appetizer and friend haddock sandwich with fries.  Yummy yummy.

name: Justin Henderson
text: Trivia Tuesdays. In direct competition for best lunch view in town with Frontier.

name: Villa Anderson
text: The staff were very nice and my chicken was not microwaved .

name: Charles Spear
text: Enjoyed the food and atmosphere. Service was excellent.

name: Leah Griffin
text: I have never had a bad meal here.

name: John Revilla
text: Great food,beer and service

name: Caitlin Geishaker
text: Food was delicious but service was on the slow side.  There were 6 of us dining and two of the four burgers were extremely undercooked and then it took even longer to get the new burgers back to the table.

name: Julia P.
text: Found this place randomly and couldn't be happier! $3 sunday mimosas and bloody Mary's all day! Beer is pretty good and the view is spectacular. Get the lobster soup! Lots of good chunks of lobster meat.

name: Patt Bothel
text: Microwbrewed beer at it's finest. Great menu with creative ingredients.

name: Benjamin Turlo
text: Took mom for mother's day.  They delivered her food wrong with gluten allergy being known.  Waitress comes by 20 minutes later,  says sorry for the late check in and asks if I need a box, brings my box to the table next to me another 20 minutes later. Finally gets my box to me 10 more minutes later with the unadjusted check. Up there for worst service ever!

name: Chris and Amy Boivin
text: Good but not awesome, food is average  and so is the service.

name: Michael Hutchison
text: Super easy place to bring the kids and enjoy dinner over the water or views out of the windows while eating. Its inexpensive with large portions and of course amazing beer. A local favorite and a tourists "must try". I always recommend Seadog.

name: Devyn Potter
text: Seadog is AWESOME!  We always get the pub burger because it is so amazing and it is always exactly what we want!  They have a great selection of beers, I personally love the blueberry one!  They have a couple ciders.  wish they had more options but they have downeast cider which is the best! I have never been disappointed here, however, sometimes the wait for a table is longer than I would like and it get loud occasionally.  The outside seating is beautiful and looks over the river.  They do have seating that us quieter and they were able to seat us there when we had elderly people with us!  All around a great place to eat, drink, and watch the water!

name: Jason Walker
text: Great food and service love the atomsphere as well. Its cool eating in an old mill

name: gary roberts
text: Great food and service

name: Brian Butterfield
text: While there can be a wait my opinion is wait. If it's a nice day a deck seat gives a great view. The beer and food are always great. I recommend the fisherman's pie especially on colder days. Lots of history in that building and I'm not just talking about the pictures posted on the walls.

name: Michael Schmidt
text: I had dinner at Sea Dog in Topsham Monday night with my boyfriend and his friend. We received two checks. One check was for my boyfriend and I, the other was his friends’. I gave my debit card to the server and told him I wanted to pay HALF of the bill for my boyfriend and I. My boyfriend paid in cash for the other half. We both provided the server with a tip. When I got home I checked my online banking to see that my card was charged for the ENTIRE bill and then again for HALF of the bill.  I immediately called your location to have this matter handled. I asked to speak to a manager about the situation and I explained the whole ordeal. She said that I would be contacted about this Tuesday by the General Manager since she was unable to do anything about the situation.  I was not reached out to Tuesday and I sent an email to the contact address provided on your website.  I have not heard anything back STILL about this situation.  I am extremely dissapointed with the lack of customer service on the Sea Dog in Topsham's behalf.  I would appreicate being contacted ASAP to resolve this situation. I love paying a $75 dollar bill twice and giving a $20 tip to be Ignored for a total of $170 👍 I guess I got the Veterans deal. When one person fails you all do as a team but multiple people failed from your staff all the way to your management.

name: Brogan Teel
text: Charney is an awesome server and bartender! I haven't met a staffer I didnt like. Fun environment and good food!

name: Brandon Giarratano
text: Food was an 8/10. Very good but just average. The view is amazing if you get to sit outside and the service was very good!

name: Brenda Mondor
text: Very clean, awesome clams

name: Cynthia Edmonds
text: We've been coming here for many years and often get our favorite Blueberry Ale at the bar while we wait for our table. Erica, our charming bartender, was so delightful that we decided to stay at the bar for the very delicious Cuban Reuben on special and later split the BBQ burger. Consistently good food and if you're in during the day Friday, look for Erica at the bar. (She was just subbing last  night.) Seadogs hasn't  had someone that friendly behind the counter since Ben moved on.

name: William Snyder
text: Good food and atmosphere.

name: Laura Hopkinson
text: Great variety menu. Huge selection of drinks and appetizers. Live music on weekends.

name: Kate Hanley
text: Excellent food and environment. Service was a little under par for me this time.

name: Mick Daigle
text: Aways a great time at the Topsham Sea Dog, the deck is awesome in the summer but sitting inside is almost as good. Great beer, food and desserts. Live music acts that I have seen there are always good as well. Always a place that I recommend to others.

name: Lindsey Ho
text: We waited around 20 mimutes for someone to take our drink order and then an additional 30 for our food. We had to wave to other waiters because we couldn't find ours. The salmon was dry, but the steak sandwich was good.

name: mainegirl
text: Everything was very good

name: Ed Talanian
text: Great food, good atmosphere, but I've been here probably 10 times and had something wrong with my party's order 8 of those times.

name: Susan White
text: Great place to have a party.   Food and service were excellent.

name: Patricia Millett
text: Great brunch. Variety is awesome

name: Joseph Tomm
text: Always friendly staff, always running into old friends and great pubfare and brunch

name: Wayne Sansouci
text: Excellent food and atmosphere.

name: Deb Brug
text: Portions small, long wait but love pub atmosphere

name: Katherine Le Favour
text: The customer services was ehh. Ordered the fish and fries. The haddock was pretty good, the fries were just odd. Little, and I mean very little fried pieces, almost shavings of potato that were way overcooked. Would have preferred plain old fashioned fries, or at least an option to decide if I wanted thier "version"of fries?

name: Tania Briceno
text: First restaurant in Portland I'm not impressed with. Got clam and haddock chowders and they were just a bunch of cream with rubbery fish. Even the side of broccoli tasted old. Maybe the hamburgers are better but you can do better in Portland. Service was good though and beer not bad

name: Jennifer Pendell
text: I love this place. The food is always fresh and delicious and the viewing always lovely be it summer or winter. The rustic interior is warm and inviting. This is my favorite local restaurant.

name: Kristina Hill
text: Karaoke Saturday nights!!!! Woot woot!!!$

name: M.A. O'Brien
text: A very. Good Sunday Brunch. Their regular menu is even better.

name: Jameson Hobbs
text: Food is good... Not so much the beer. Shipyard owns seadog (enough said) but the location and the views are worth a visit.

name: Ted Hersh
text: Gorgeous location, solid menu. Beers are good, but not great.

name: Nick Bull
text: Okay for chain food. Servers were friendly

name: Henry Bingham
text: Drinks are good but Saturday night karaoke needs to be worked on as far as length of time and organization

name: mark diterlizzi
text: Excellent food and fast service

name: Brent Atkinson
text: Relaxed atmosphere, good drinks and rich food.

name: Tyson Reissfelder
text: Great food in a fantastic casual setting with riverside views and amazing beers! The Blueberry Amber ale was light, smooth and delicious with a pleasing blueberry finish.

name: Sara
text: Food is delicious, staff is friendly!

name: michelle amato
text: The Sea Dog Brewing Company surprised me. The drink specials were quite good and the food all freshly prepared. Even though it gives off a corporate vibe, the food was real.

name: Rick Grenier
text: Great views from the outside deck. Love the old Mill setting. Good food good beer!

name: Jeff Audet
text: Good food an drink with a view of the river

name: Lauren Busby
text: The Sea Dog is my go to place when we are in Maine. Awesome food and good beer can't be beat. I love their chicken tenders with buffalo and fried pickles. The only problem is the wait. It's always 30-45 at lunch, even at 8:30 pm on weekends.

name: BoB
text: Their food and drinks are great.  I almost always get a full flight of their beers every time I go to enjoy a lot of different flavors.

name: Stephanie Thomas
text: Very pleased with the food! Service...not so much. Party of three, turkey sandwich, crab & havarti, and a beer burger. We all were quite happy with our meals. Our server, hmm, what was her name? oh that's right she didn't introduce herself,   was not familiar with the menu when I asked questions and for basically three sandwiches took well over 1/2 hour to get our food. Will return since it's a neat venue, great location, and good food,  but would probably sit at the bar and check out the service there.

name: George Smith
text: Great beer and food. Scenic and historic mill on nice falls.

name: Adam Hall
text: We loved the atmosphere, this location is in an old mill and you can look out at the river while you eat. Everyone enjoyed their food, beers were tasty too.

name: Bill Hunt
text: Great wings! Great food, great family place!

name: John Moore
text: Excellent food and the service is great.

name: Teg Griffiths
text: Great beer and although the food looks creative, the chicken tacos we're totally dry. I will go back and try again, the setting is awesome and a nice.pub atmosphere.

name: PatriciaRileySmith BalancedLifestyleSolutions
text: Amazing location nice environment good food!

name: L̶e̶g̶e̶n̶d̶s̶ N̶e̶v̶e̶r̶ d̶i̶e̶
text: Excellant  food but slow service check back to see if your table needs drinks.

name: andrea milotte
text:
Pretty darn good brunch! Way more options than i expected.  All breafast stuff, omelet bar,  sandwich fixings, tons of desserts, seafood and chicken and meat.
Brunch goes until 2p. Easy parking if youre leaving going  right ...lol. Lots of seats and the deck in summer is awesome, right on the water with a cool view.

name: Erik Ross
text: The lobster roll, clam chowder and fried calamari are out of this world!

name: Roxanne Armstrong
text: Love this place! Great food, great location, always something here for me.

name: Denis Giard
text: My baked stuff haddock was awsome . Our waiter did an awsome job. Thsnk you Brian. My wife enjoyed the French onion soup.

name: Kate Mueller
text: Great service and food, and some great options on-tap.

name: T K
text: Loved it! Good beer & food! Great service.

name: SmokeytheBear66
text: Great atmosphere and beer. Loved my food and service was good.

name: Marianna Sargent
text: Used to be a great place to go with the family but the quality has decreased and it takes far longer than it should to get anything from the bar. I've never seen bartenders so annoyed that someone sat at the bar and call ahead if you're hungry because they stop serving food at random times.

name: Michael Kelly
text: Good Food..great service

name: PIANO PIPER
text: Very pleasant. Food was great. Great variety.

name: Jessica Lavoie
text: I simply LOVE Sea Dog! Best artichoke dip anywhere, and believe me I've checked/searched! Great drinks, food, and staff. Decent prices and good specials menu.

name: C C
text: Went to dinner with our club and sat outside on the deck. The service was excellent and the food was fresh as well. Very happy with the restaurant and the location is easy for parking.

name: Zac
text: Great place for dinner drinks and an evening on the patio.

name: James Estabrook
text: The steak tip poutine dish was a real disappointment.  For $18.00 you get 5-6 pieces of steak, some thick cut french fries with gravy and a few cheese curds.  Better off buying an entire steak that comes with a side of fries for less $$$.  Total rip-off.

name: cody nelson
text: Decided to stop in for a late night drink seeing they were open until 1am, came in at 11:45 only to be approached by some of the least personable people I've ever met in the hospitality business to be informed they are closing @ midnight. Only my second time here and not sure I'll want to come back

name: Jeremy Grady
text: Drink was pretty good, much better than Ruby Tuesday's, and the food was decent. Competitors have larger chicken strips that are juicier and more tender and they give more for the money. Your fries are "meh". You should use thicker cut and pre-season or salt them before they reach the table.

name: Frankie Klajbor-85
text: Ok food and service last night

name: Molly Berberich
text: Awesome restaurant with amazing views of the Androscoggin river

name: Mary Granade
text: Reliably good food, nice atmosphere and friendly wait staff.

name: Christina Michaud
text: Food is good but not a WOW staff and service was fast and friendly. Very affordable!

name: Samuel Brown
text: The food is good, but tries too hard, and the prices reflect this. There are reasonably priced menu options, and the staff is friendly. If you're looking for that micro-brewery restaurant feel, you've come to the right place. The overall experience comes off as a bit pretentious.

name: Adam
text: Normally it's a great place to eat and have a drink. Last night seemed to be an off night for all of the staff. The seemed stressed very short. I asked how long the wait was when I walked in. The gentleman at the podium sighed and said "outside will be about 45 min and inside is less if your to impatient to go outside".

name: Valerie Flanagan
text: Good food, decent service, variety of beer.

name: Shaughnessey McArthur
text: Best pub nachos in town and awesome service. Beautiful location as well!

name: Kyle Green
text: One of the best pubs around, awesome food, atmosphere, drinks, and staff. I can't recommend this place enough

name: Kurt Toothaker
text: Excellent service and meal. Definitely got my money's worth.

name: Matthew Carr
text: Mediocre beer, but nice big venue with good scenery and predictably decent food. Temping burgers not the strong suit but otherwise pretty good. Nice spot for a big group. Good service.

name: Lori Shackley
text: # love that sitting at the bar you can get right in and the buffet is great!! Food, fun, and great people!!

name: Jeff McGivern
text: We eat here every year during our stay in Bath.  Food is better than your average brew pub and  they offer a nice selection.  Can't miss!

name: Susan Bizier
text: Medium well ordered burger was med rare..but still ate the whole thing.

name: Anita Robinson
text: Love the drinks and food

name: Cassandra Kenney
text: Great place to go with friends, also my favorite brunch place.

name: Maddison Pfaff
text: The food is meh. There are other places to go to get seafood.. this place is a little touristy, but the beer is amazing and the view is probably the best in town. The outdoor seating is absolutely the greatest around.

name: Peter W Elvin
text: Pub style dining.  Micro brews.  Great food.  Reasonable prices.  Great outdoor deck dining overlooking the River Falls

name: Teri Zrioka
text: Was a little disappointed with my fish and chips. Was hoping for a nice piece of haddock and what I got was small 2bite nuggets that were over cooked. Usually better than this.

name: Doug Light
text: Good food and excellent views from the outside porch overlooking the falls. Friendly service and accommodating for our large group.

name: william watson
text: Very good place to eat. Has a good selection of of adult drinks

name: Donald Verrill
text: Popular spot is along the riverway/falls in Topsham across Androscoggin River from downtown Brunswick.  This brewery has the full bar with a wide selection of great food on menu. Meetings, parties, big n small indoor or out.

name: JA Shaw
text: Hopping place. Good crowd on a Friday night, live entertainment. Friendly service, good craft beer. Flight of tasters available.

name: Paul Thomson
text: Excellent food, great service!

name: Joanie Naigle

name: Ellie C.
text:
Usually the food there was good, and the servers on point.  But not last night!
I had planned my husband's birthday celebration there again as last year.  A bunch of friends get together for dinner and a visit.  We arrived the table was in place and partially set.  A knife and napkin, but no forks.  As our friends joined us we ordered our drinks.  The waiter came over and sort of took our appetizer order.  Skipped right over 2 people in our party. (There was 10 of us) so we had to hail him back. We waited quite a while, then the appetizers came out haphazardly.  I had ordered a salad instead of the veggy, and another friend ordered  a salad to split with her husband.  The salad came out in 2 plates as he thought they wanted a full size  salad split in 2 bowls?? My salad did not come and I asked the waiter and he said oh that will come out with your meal.  Well that's a first.  I have always gotten my salad first even when ordered in palace of a veggie.
So we ordered our food.  The waiter asked who was on what checks and proceeded to take our orders.   This poor chap was definitely in over his head and obviously not getting much help from the kitchen.  One of our friends ordered a salad with quinoa and shrimp.  Just before our food started to arrive, the waiter comes back out and informs her that "the quinoa went bad so they didn't have any more" well...first of all a trained person would have just said that they ran out to save face for the restaurant. So my friend said just give me the salad with shrimp only.
All our food started coming out in waves...and I didn't get my salad yet again.  We all had our meals, my husband's was cold...and still no salad for my friend.  Finally it came out.  It was a bowl of kale.  No shrimp just a bowl of kale.  She didn't eat it and at this point I was mad.  They should not have charged her for it as we we're practically done eating by the time she got it and it was not what she ordered. When the checks came, we had someone else's order on our check too.  Beware if you eat here.  Watch your checks.
I can tell you the food was tolerable at best and we will not be back.  The service was bad.
This place really needs to train their Waite staff to LISTEN TO YOUR CUSTOMER! I am all about customer service and to have your waiter ask you to repeat yourself and still get it wrong...
Wake up your kitchen staff to be a little more on the ball and make what is ordered all together.  Sorely disappointed. I could go on about our experience here but I think you get the idea.

name: Alex Seise
text: Love this place!  Recently visited with a big group, and we enjoyed the vibrant atmosphere overlooking the river.  Even though were arrived somewhat late and had a big group, the service was fairly good (if a bit slow, though the busy Saturday night crowd very likely played into that).  Our drinks and food were great, from the lobster rangoons to the fried pickles, and everyone enjoyed entrees.  My pub burger was cooked perfectly, with a to-die-for brioche bun and thick slabs of bacon up top.  The whole thing was slathered with hearty beer mustard, which only made it better.  Equally fun was the karaoke crowd crooning by the bar!  This place has character, great food, a perfect location...  What a treasure for the Topsham / Brunswick / Harpswell communities!

name: Deborah Ripley
text: When we woke up on Sunday morning,  February 19, 2017, it had snowed, obviously without wind, because every tree trunk, limb and branch were covered with a white sticky snow! The scenery was just so gorgeous. A winter wonderland! We had a great fun day instore for us . We were invited by my husband's brother and wife, to attend an old fashion ice cutting party on a local pond near my huband's old summer stomping grounds, Damariscotta, Maine.  Ice cutting at this pond started in the 1700's. We were all going to see an example of early history repeated. People, mostly men, were cutting ice blocks with old fashion long ice cutting saws. It was really easy as long as I kept the saw upright....AND only if I had one block to cut loose! The blocks of ice were two feet thick and extremely heavy. First the men used a tractor to push all the snow off the small pond. Then a scarifire, big cutting machine run by diseal or gaseline. The machine'' blade was huge...mabe 5 to six feet in diameter. The machine was very loud and cut gauges into the ice. These cuts were long going in both directions.  After they took this machine off the pond, it looked like perfect size rectangles. The rectangles would then be cut off the blocks of the long floating logs of ice. The men, of all ages, would float the blocks over to a pulley system using a chain pulled by a truck. The driver would pull the pulley with his truck as it backed up, which would hoists the ice onto a ramp. The A-frame conveyor belt would haul the ice almost 20 feet upward onto the A-frame structure. The ice would reach the tipping point then fall onto the long ramp on the other side. The ice would fly down the ramp and hit the other blocks of ice in the cold shack/barn.  The ice would then sit in tight stacks and saw dust. If there were any pockets of air or cracks between the blocks, they would melt too quickly. Hopefully, the blocks would stay ice cold until Spring. After this great afternoon outside, we headed to Sea Dogs, a great resturant in Tompson Maine! Sea Dogs is located just off the highway. We were really hungry! The scenery was spectacular!. Sea Dogs sits right on the Androscoggin River. We had a window seat. It was so nice looking out onto the river. There were ice houses looking down to the left which made me smile. Anyone who has gone ice fishing in Maine would smile too. It is being outside on a sunny Spring day with the sun burning brightly and the cool or cold wind blowing and making everyone have very pink cheeks. Sea Dogs reminded me of the Lewiston area with all the old red brick mills being refurbished for businesses, condos and apartments. Sea Dog looks like the old Warehouse Restaurant which use to be located on the same street in Lewiston close the famous Victor News. The Sea Dogs Restaurant felt like going home to visit the  history and remember the many many men, women and children, whose lives were a bio part of the building. The building has wonderful arch headers over the windows. There are beautiful red bricks with, what looks like grayish/white concrete on the walls. The window are huge and there are many in every direction. The foo! Oh my gosh! The food was fabulous. Everyone's dishes were delicious. In our group, we had  griiled salmon, deep fried huge baby shrimp, haddock fish and chips and searde Ahi Tuna sandwich. All our entres were cooked perfectly. The coleslaw was so good. It reminded me of my mother's and she from the South! We did not have dessert. We were too full from all the generous portions! What an incrediable Saturday in Maine! Now this is the truth...when we were getting up to leave, we looked out our window. There was a huge beautiful male or female eagle sitting on a frozen piece of ice right out in front of our window.I couldn't help but think, if the eagle was a past generational descendent from prior eagles who visited this mill and our people years before. God bless America!

The greatest outdoors shop I've ever been in! And that includes BassPro, Cabela's, and many more.

Kitty Trading Post has three levels: ground floor is predominantly clothing, the lower level is entirely fishing, and the upper level is everything else. Anything you're looking for, they probably have 10 variants.

Budget extra time if you're coming for a visit, because it's going to take longer than you think to get the whole family out of here!

name: John Painter
text:
I was able to find a new Springfield Armory 911 Alpha chambered in 380ACP, for a very reasonable price.  I would give five stars except their service is very bizarre.

While anyone just looking, could walk to a counter and ask to look at a firearm, look and just chat, if you knew you wanted to purchase something, you needed to take a number and wait.

My wait time? 1 1/2 hours, this made no sense despite having a number system. I lost count after 20      people came and left just looking while I was waiting to purchase a firearm -  I had already called to verify was in stock and saw in the case.  Again, from the time I took a number to the time a sales person spoke to me was 1.5 hours.  Once I spoke with someone it took about 5 minutes to pull the box from storage, the background check took maybe 10 minutes, and there was not a line of people at the register for the whole 2 hours I was there.  Why there was so much emphasis on showing, versus selling I do not understand, but it certainly will make me think twice about going back.

name: Andy Martin
text:
I like Kittery Trading post, I only get down there a couple times a year because of the drive.

I  went down today because I received a flyer they mailed to me.  They advertised a sale on Ammo and other rueger products.

Ammo has been in short supply lately and I needed some and figured i would look at a new gun while there, they have also been hard to find but Kittery usually has a very good inventory.

Well ammo was very very limited and none of the advertised Ammo was in stock. The inventory of guns were maybe a quarter of which they usually have.

I don't really have hard feelings about the guns because I knew they have been selling out everywhere but I was expecting Ammo to be a little more available as they advertised it.

Well i at least able to pick up a box of less lethal 12 Guage shells. They had plenty of fudge so I was able to buy a couple pieces of that, and it was excellent.

text: Tried to purchase a nice shotgun in the over $1200 range. But the systems were down (understandably they were busy and it took alittle longer than usual) i have no problem with that. My problem started at the background check stage they told me it would be about 30 mins. I waited and waited over an hour later i noticed no one was actually picking up the guns behind the booth. I finally asked when i could get someone's attention to find out the system was down and they did not know if it was going to be back up today....... why would they not tell all of us so we could go on with our day? I said what do we do now they said oh we will call you when it comes back up whenever it was. So i left not so happy had over a 2 hr one way journey on my way out i hear another person telling their friend that they put a deposit down so the gun would be reserved for them. I walked back over and asked if i had to do that knowing that i would not just be able to jump right over the day or time they called. They tell me yes you have to or they would not be able to hold it for me. How can you not tell a customer that before i almost left? So did the deposit and requested repeatedly to give me a call as soon as it goes back up to see if i was still in kittery and save me a 4+ hr trip again. I called back house later after shopping around before leaving the town and they tell me yes it is back up and ready to go. WHY DID YOU NOT CALL ME? You said you would. Over all not my first purchase there and i love the store but the help i recieved was way below quality there was only one helpful person there and i think it was a manager trying to fix the hold paperwork. They did not even give me the usual how to breakdown and clean and oil explanation which i was expecting.

name: Daniel Martell
text: Found a great little room here in the flea market, Anns's Corner. It's just a small room with a door that is gone to some of the neatest and beautiful antiques and more. Well worth a visit!

name: robert knight jr
text: Very friendly people and great stuff.  Me and my daughter can't wait to go back.

name: Nobuteru Hirata
text: Hey I am giving this review is not because the place is bad or anything!!! This place is really awesome!!! Until Me and my wife meet an old guy. We were looking at staff he ask us “do you wanna know the price?” We said yes he told us then we started concerning and holding item he told us “if you don’t buy that and keep holding it price is going up!” And he literally start to count upper price! He ruined not even experience there he ruined our Sunday. I also read a lot reviews like this so be careful and not go to his junk place!

name: Rachel Merriweather
text: Something for everyone and it's easy to spend hours there.

name: Anne S
text: I love browsing around.  It's big, airy and well lit.  I have purchased a few antique objects over time.   I feel the prices are generally reasonable.  All my interactions with the dealers have been good.

name: ROBERT WEILAND
text: One of my favorite places to go to find old tools

name: craig carey
text: This is usually a fun place to browse and find interesting things you didn't know you needed. We always stop in to browse as we pass thru Brunswick. It is worth the stop and spending an hour or two.

name: Jõsęph Rèêď
text: Allot of the booths weren't open and it's always the same stuff. The inventory doesnt seem to change.

name: Amanda Goodall
text: Always love a good flea market. Some great finds. Some overpriced but so much fun to look.

name: Dawn Toth
text: I got all the ingredients for a hearty soup and some sticky buns too!!

name: Max Corwin
text: Stop by the atm before visiting because there isn't one nearby. The first room you enter makes you dig deep for good finds, but the second room has organized stalls. I have only been once but I had enough good finds to warrant a second visit the next time I am in the area. Also, I'm not even into vinyl, but there was a guy with a long term booth with old records who was awesome.

name: Amberlee Edgerton Moriarty
text: There's plenty of room for lots of vendors and wares, however, it is not organized and the vendor for the item that interests you may or may not be on the premises at all. a neighboring vendor offered to accept payment on behalf of the absent vendor, but then I received no receipt from him, and I was left unsure if it was a legitimate transaction. Additionally, this and other vendors there seemed either disinterested in actually transacting business - others were desperate and pushy. It was all a disappointing experience for me.

name: Alecia Wenslow
text: I love going to this flea market.  It's indoors so you can go year-round.  There's a small concessions stand if you get hungry or want to sit and chat.  The vendors all carry a variety of items.  Make sure you bring cash because not all of the vendors take checks or credit.

name: Amy Simpson
text: Indoor flea market with many booths offering an array of flea market finds. Some nice antique items. Some of the sellers give off a weird vibe, but otherwise it's fun to walk through.

name: Enchantment Positive Energy News Media.
text: Find the hidden treasures if you like looking for all kinds of items ...come see for yourself.

name: M. Eric Carr
text: Lots of good deals to be found here. CDs for $1 etc. The flea market is only open on weekends.

name: Tyler G
text: Will not be returning to this place abunch of grumpy old men with over priced nicnacs would not consider this place a flea market

name: Thomas Riley
text: Good farmers market Saturdays

name: J B
text: The prices have gotten too high to be considered a real "flea market." anymore. This place was awesome back in the day.  All the fun is gone.  Half the stuff in the place is owned by 2 or 3 dealers.  It is really just a messy, dark antique shop.  I think it caters to out of state tourists who want the flea market experience and don't mind spending their money.  Don't bother.

name: Sabrina B
text: This is more of an antique market with a bunch of old junk. Vendors that have permanent booths. Not what I expected.

name: Alison Lee Freeman
text: Our favorite flea market. Always something unique. Today it was sheet music from the late 1800s.

name: Bill Eugley
text: Lots of areas that look like an episode of horders! Some booths are neat and clean, some are not. Piles and piles of innaccessible stuff. If you can't get to it you cant sell it, so why is it there? Even the food place looks grungy. Not much positive for me.

name: Benjamin Bernier
text:
good luck ever getting all the vendors here at once. half the booths are closed depending on what day you go. not the friendliest place i've ever been.

all that being said, i have certainly found some gems here

name: In Human Creation Media
text: I always end up finding something great every time I go.

name: Jennifer McCray
text: Fun and packed full of good stuff!

name: Kevin Maybery
text: Indoor flea market that has a little of everything..vendors always changing good place to browse on a rainy day

name: Jamie Spier
text: I love this place! So many anitques

text: Topical fleemarket

name: brenda richards
text: Xyz

name: Mike Grill
text: Fantastic local flea market

name: aric odone
text: You never know what you may find.

name: Jonathan Waldo
text: Lots of treasure to find

text: Go find yourself a bargain!

text: Needs improvement

name: Eaghan
text: Hate it

text: Always interesting

name: Bradford Megquier
text: You don't need it but you can find it here

name: David Bolling
text: Mysteries around every corner

name: Doug Campbell
text: Good picking

name: John Serrano
text: Great views of the coast. There are a couple walking paths, however, when we went one was closed. The lighthouse is not accessible to the public or at least it wasn't when we visited. If you're in the area its worth a stop, though no need to go out of your way to visit.

name: Summer Cornetta-Webb
text: Lovey little walk. Pathway to lighthouse itself is accessible-ish, a bit steep if you’re in a wheelchair. And old asphalt. Other path, into the woods is nice and the stairs down to the beach seems very nicely kept/brand new.

name: James Pettit
text: Bass Harbor Head Light is listed on the National Register of Historic Places in Acadia National Park.  Absolutely worth seeing!  Parking is less than adequate; however, the bathrooms are clean.  The hike down the stairs to the ocean observation deck is difficult for some people and the view of the lighthouse is much better from the rocks off the deck.  The rocks can be very dangerous, so most don’t leave the small deck.  Best at sunset.

name: William Slaughter
text: Beautiful spot to take your hunny to catch a breathtaking sunset. Wear boots there's a small path thats takes you down the rocks to the water. Depending on when you go bring a jacket.

name: John R.
text: Gorgeous scenery, peaceful, and picturesque! The weather can change drastically without notice.  On cooler days, fog rolls in pretty quickly.  It can roll out just as fast as it came in, but it can linger for a couple hours or so.  Plan your visit accordingly if you intend to take pictures!

name: Nikhil Jain
text: Nice place to view the sun set behind the lighthouse. Reach well before time asthe parking gets full pretty early. Make sure you find the trail at the far end of parking to see the sun set behind the lighthouse. We ended up on the front side near the fence at first as a lot of people were gathered there but that is not the right place. There is a short trail that leads to the rocks behind the lighthouse.

name: K-Lap
text:
We went here just before sunset one evening to check out the lighthouse. We climbed down into the rocks to get a great view of the lighthouse itself and we spent a little time watching the sun go down. You need to get there early because as we were leaving, it looked like the local authorities were no longer allowing people to enter the area. This is purely  speculation based on the squad car blocking half the road when we were leaving.
Anyway, it is a cute little lighthouse and a great spot to watch the sunset.
Very picturesque...
We purchased tea in Bar Harbor and this lighthouse is on the back of the packages.

name: Label Grafik
text: Nice place to hike and get a better view of the light house.

name: Andrew Muttiah
text: A must visit location when in downeast Maine. The lighthouse is amazing and historic. Lights up after sunset. Watching the sunset behind the lighthouse is an amazing sight to see. It gets very busy in the summers when photographers from all around New England drive up for the view. Free parking on site but it fills up very fast.

name: Robbie Littlefield
text: Amazing Lighthouse, highly recommend checking this one out. There's also a cool little path down the back side of it that has some stairs to get you down to the beach. Definitely makes a great afternoon. Gotts store is right down the road for some great food & ice cream. Perfect 👌

name: Amber Ewing
text: One path has easy access and close up to the light house, and then another path has stairs that let you climb on rocks n get another view of the light house, and family friendly.

name: Nancy Hulme
text: Remote but beautiful.Lots of trails around the lighthouse

name: Andy Callens
text: It is a beautiful lighthouse, and the coastline is amazing, but at the end of the day, there's not a lot here and it can get a little congested at peak times. We had no trouble parking in mid morning, but by the time we left there was a line of cars waiting to take some pictures of the lighthouse and leave.

name: Divideby4 Tarnation
text: Pretty cool place, worth a 30-45 minute trip. Bathrooms are less than desirable. But other than that cool little place.

name: Sarah Collins
text: Beautiful location. Go in the winter and you have the place to yourself.

name: Corey
text: A great light house to stop at. Part of Acadia national park you can quickly visit and take in the sights and read about the history of the light and the keepers obligations. Be polite and do not knock on the door or otherwise bother the coastguard Family who lives in the keepers house.

name: Joseph Kunder
text: Kind of lame till you climb out on the rocks to get the iconic picture.

name: pmwartel
text: Very interesting but a little unkempt. Needs some TLC maintenance attention, but worth the visit!

name: Darren Hoevel
text: Beautiful view of the pictuesce Maine coast line and a picture perfect lighthouse.  There is a small parking lot, so be prepared to wait on the weekends or busy summer weeks.  There are a few small hiking trails around the lighthouse but all very short.  Small walking path to a scenic view of the lighthouse.

name: Charles McGinnis
text: Great place for viewing a picturesque lighthouse setting and a great sunset, if you time it right. We visited today (off season, always) and were lucky enough to have the sun come below the cloud deck for a great sunset. The light is fantastic and the short walk to the rocks from the far end of the parking lot is a must see. Beautiful water, landscape and of course, the beacon itself...4 seconds on and 4 seconds off of a red light is all great viewing...worth the drive and time spent there.

name: Bob Benson
text: Nice views, pretty much a 1 lane road in, not much parking.  Nice spot on low tide.  Follow fence to small trail.

name: Jeff Palmeter
text: Classic New England lighthouse and a must see. Easy to get to and at lower tide you can get some great pics from the rocks below.

name: Judy Kutt
text: Very pretty and great views. If doing the hike to the left of the light house, expect lots of steep steps. And for a better view you will need to climb over rocks.

name: Ken and Alicia Lund
text: When I visited, the fog was beginning to roll in. It was a perfect Maine ambiance. The lighthouse's surrounding coastline is spectacular. This is a must-visit location if you are in Acadia National Park.

name: Michael Stephens
text: Interesting facts but nothing spectacular to see, in my opinion. But this low-set style characterizes most New England lighthouses. I was dying to see something grand, like in Michigan. FYI, there are two vantages, one on each side.

name: Justin Engstrom
text: Beautiful and historic. Info graphs could be updated. Has a nice walk down to the rocks.

name: Master iOqY
text: Still an active lighthouse manned by the US Coast Guard, it goes to show the importance of this location for nautical navigation and safety then and now. From the small parking lot, it's a short walk to the path's end for one view of the tower but the main viewpoint is down a set of steep stairs on the other side. It's worth the stroll down the stairs to get up close to the water. We saw lobster boats coming in when we went down there.

name: Irsan Sutanto
text:
Came here to take pictures.
Nice view

name: Katie Davis
text: Super cool lighthouse with fun little trails around it!

name: Ashley
text:
Hopefully this review might help some people. I have been to this light house 2 times, 2013 and 2019. It's always a beautiful sight and picture worthy, but things people need to keep in mind.

Sunrise and Sunset this place is a madhouse during peak season. There is only enough parking for maybe 20 cars (thats even pushing it) in the lot. I have seen people walk down the road from parking at the very beginning of the road just due to the traffic waiting to park is insane. We went on a Sunday evening, during peak sunset time. It was absolutely insane. I turned around and left instead of waiting in line for a parking spot. This is a little spot that people tend to want to hang out at and there isn't much spot for people just to hang out down here.

Finally I managed to get down to see the light house on Tuesday afternoon, still a bit busy but not as crazy. So, pack your patience, or go during the mid morning/afternoon hours. It is scenic, but I would say if you have a chance to see it by boat... Take that option instead.

name: Jon Kraeuter
text: It's well worth the hike to the shoreline to climb over the rocks to get to an area to take some nice photos of the lighthouse.  The wooden stairs on the trail are steep, well worn, and can be slippery when wet, so be careful. Our kids has a blast exploring the rocks near the water.   Parking lot is small so get there early.

name: Joseph Silva
text: Beautiful views of the ocean, fishing boats and islands.

name: Toxic Doll
text: Such a beauty to be seen from 2 sides, path to the left will give you an opportunity to take that famous shot. A treasure in a quaint little area

name: Stan Levenger
text: The lighthouse itself is unremarkable but the coast like is especially memorable. Trail that exits the PL near the restrooms has two options. One trail is rustic and traverses along the coast with remarkable views and multiple access points. The other is the steps that go down to the water with a very nice lighthouse view. Not handicap accessible to these two sites. Paved path to other side of light house is accessible. Visit is highly recommended for access to water and views.

name: idusevich
text: Everything in Acadia is beautiful. This lighthouse is cute and located in a gorgeous spot.

name: David MacIndoe
text: Beautiful views and a nice walking trail nearby. There are some informative plaques too for those who are interested in the local history. Definitely worth the drive to get away from the busy Bar Harbor side and enjoy the more relaxing west side of the island.

name: Trisha Merrill
text: Love the coast of Maine and it's Lighthouses!

name: Jason Christenson
text: Neat place.  Awesome spot to watch the sunset by the ocean.  Worthwhile!

name: Vicki Johnson
text: The Lighthouse was beautiful. It is a smaller one and you can't tour it because it is still active. Their is a Coaster Guard family that lives in the house and man's the light. It only takes about 5 minutes, but it is well worth it.

name: L.J Goldstock
text: Wasnt on any to do list in the bar harbor site maps very nice but no one is there and really wasnt much to see spent 30 mins took some pictures and left

name: Jamie Lai
text: It's hard to photograph the lighthouse and there's not much to it from the presentation of the cultural experience.  But headed to the side there is an easy path to the rocks (and some walking paths) that's worth checking out.

name: John S
text: Great place to take pictures of rocks or the lighthouse. The paved trail that leads to the lighthouse is just OK, you really want to take the trail to the right of the bathrooms to get the best view and pictures.

name: Melissa M
text: Unique lighthouse. There is another trail along the fence that leads to wooden stairs.  Small area, but a real sweet taste of Maine.

name: Google Account
text: A classic lighthouse. While they have added pathways, you can still get down to the rocks and take some amazing pictures and explore

name: Mark James
text: Very beautiful place . Go see it

name: Brittany Knight
text: Pretty cool area. The path on the right leads to the lighthouse, and a path on the left leads to steps to go down to the rocks

name: Shakeel Ahmed
text: Nice sunset , not too crowded and also there is additional parking while you drive towards the light house which can be used in case the main lot is full.

name: Kim Donica
text: Lighthouse isn't spectacular but the setting on the pink granite rocks jutting into the ocean is. Worth a visit, especially towards sunset

name: Max P
text: Well kept spot- but there isn’t really a whole lot to do besides hanging out on the rocks by the lake house (there aren’t any trails within walking distance and you understandably cannot enter to tour the inhabited lighthouse).

name: Owen Bradley
text: Nice lighthouse but very busy around sunset time, best to walk there instead of drive

name: Dinesh Gundu
text: It's an amazing place for sunset. Walk over to the boulders by the shore... there is a path by the corner of parking lot to reach there and enjoy the ocean view..

name: Kev Bot
text: Kind of cramped area if you go to the main side of the lighthouse. The trailhead to the left will provide a better viewing area for photographs, however it wont be wheelchair accessible.

name: Joyce Currier
text: A definite must go-to location when vacationing in Maine. The sunset are beautiful, but you should arrive early to find a parking area and a spot to view and/or take photographs.

name: Damon
text: Nice little lighthouse

name: Dan Nordmeyer
text: One of the only lighthouses on the mainland, it's kind of off the beaten path. Hike around the east side and go down the rocks for some great cliff shots of the lighthouse.

name: archibald claus
text: Beautiful view with very discriptive signs. Beautiful view and nice atmosphere. A bit too crowded for my taste.

name: Linsi Locks
text: There is a path to the right that takes you right down to the lighthouse so you can get an up close and personal view. The path to the left gives you a bit of a glimpse of it from the side as long as you are willing to climb over some rocks. To get that iconic lighthouse picture you must have to go at low tide, the water was too high and strong for us to go out.

name: Erin McCabe
text: This light house gets over one thousand visitors a day during busy season. After visiting then you should read the ghost stories about it! There is a lot of history that is not posted, much like the rest of the Mount Desert Island! You can find a lot of rich history here!

name: Andy Novikov
text: The Bass Harbor Head Lighthouse is a part of Acadia National Park. We came around 5 pm there trying to catch sunset, but it was very foggy. Anyway we enjoyed the place. Definitely this lighthouse is a cute one! If you have the time to make the drive, we highly recommend.

name: Andrea Lopez
text: Beautiful, quick visit with many photo opportunities.

name: Jim Harings
text: Nice little walk and some great views if you take the trail down to the Cliffside. Lighthouse is not open for tours inside.

name: Loyd Dennis
text: Nice Lighthouse needs more parking.

name: Katina Doty
text: Cute lighthouse at the top of a lot of stairs

name: Arch Stanton
text:
Beautiful and iconic location
It’s an honor to visit

name: Henry Watkins
text: Beautiful scenery

name: Kenneth Weaver
text: Nice light house to visit in Maine.

name: Robin Damstra
text:
For a “quietside” Acadia excursion destination spot, this is a great one... not as crowded as other places in Acadia, with a gorgeous lighthouse to stand under and watch as it beams out red light to seafarers or lean against the gate and stare out at the open ocean with the salty air on your lips, and make sure to stop and read about the making of the lighthead on the stone information slab, which is easily missed on your walk down to the main attraction, but well worth reading. (And afterwards, you can head over to Thurston’s Lobster Pound — the hot lobster dip, lobster roll, and an Allagash White brew are my recommendation there — which is only a few miles away, letting you sightsee the town while you drive, getting a glimpse of how lovely life is on this quiet & mainly non-touristy slice of the Maine coast.)

Because it’s a working Lighthouse (or lighthead), there’s actually a Coast Guard family living in the place, so please stay within the boundaries that the signage states so as not to be a bother to them.

name: Thomas Brown
text: Beautiful view and access to lighthouse!

name: Vijay Alagarraj
text: Drive to Bass Harbor is fun also. The light house looked big in the photos but it is small when you are there in person.

name: chris farthing
text: Picturesque lighthouse perched on rocky maine coast. Direct access cut off by homeland security but there is a pathway down and around to view from oceanside. Bathroom in parking lot.

name: Todd Casey
text: Beautiful view, if you can hit this spot at low tide during a sunset you wont be disappointed.

name: David Borger Germann
text: Nice place for a quick visit to a working lighthouse. Try to visit not at peak times as the parking lot is very small.

name: larry cooper
text: This is a small site but a very popular one. It gets lots of visitors.

name: John Durham
text: A craggy piece of the Maine coast that's easily accessible, iconic and wickedly beautiful!

name: Heather Wendel
text: Wish parking could be easier to navigate but absolutely amazing

name: Meg Brodie
text: Beautiful but parking is drama

name: Nathan Deremer
text: An iconic emblem of Acadia, this lighthouse is beautiful at almost any time of day.  Be sure to take the path to the left of the parking lot to go down to the rocks and view the lighthouse from below.

name: Michael Johnson
text: Beautiful location to come visit, I even seen a large deer on the road coming up to it when visiting. The lighthouse is well kept from the looks of it and the trail is really scenic in the area.

name: Pamela Cyr Mercier
text: Beautiful lighthouse and beautiful views. Need to do a little hike and climbing on rocks to see the nice view.

name: CSH123
text:
Love the views, history and Downeast Maine!
Thank God people had the vision to protect it 100 years ago.
Bostonians protecting natural resources.

name: Dave's Adventures
text: Sunset views are absolutely incredible here! Take the little path at the end of the parking lot and walk down the steps onto the rocks. You will face West with the lighthouse right in front of you on the right of the frame. The parking lot is small so arrive early to try to secure a parking spot

name: Meredith Raphelson
text: Awesome part of Acadia National Park. We were able to arrive early enough for the sunset and before it got too crowded with people so we had a good spot. It gets crowded during sunset and sunrise so if you want to view during these times arrive early. There is a lot of rock climbing to get down for a good spot for viewing but you can see from other more accessible locations as well. Definitely visit if in the area.

name: Christine G
text: Cute lighthouse but crowded like everything in the area. Still worth visiting though.

name: Rae Ann Gustafson
text: Very picturesque. The setting is beautiful Maine.

name: Jacob Day
text: It's quite small, actually.  Not really that impressive, but kind of cool I guess.

name: Blair Wright
text: No the typical Maine lighthouse, the views of this one are limited and it's smaller than most. The trail to the left side of the light provides the best views but can be a bit dicey once you get down to the rocks

name: vidalia jewel
text: Cool place. Very scenic.

name: Heath Larson
text: I have visited a lighthouse or two and usually been disappointed by the view, crowds, or both.  But thus was the best one yet!  We loved listening to the buoy bell, crawling on the rocks, and getting the perfect lighthouse photo.  Not too crowded during the Wet evening we were there, too.  From the rocks, we saw HUNDREDS of porpoises in the harbor, and multiple seals out hunting too.

name: Patrick Lawler
text: Just absolutely beautiful and serene !!!

name: Nate Gross
text:
Beautiful, but at peak season it is a nightmare to wait in a line of cars for a parking spot to open. Very small lot.
If you must see it, it is beautiful, but I recommend researching some of Maine's other lights. They are all unique, historic, and picturesque--but not all as crowded as this one.

name: Taylor Clark
text: Pretty light house right on the coast. Has a trail down to the rocks if you want a front view of the light house.

name: IG: Journeying.Johnsons
text:
Cool place
Also a Pokestop

name: Adam Chang
text: The iconic spot of Acadia

name: R. Fitz
text: Wait is too long.  People are stuck on the road waiting

name: Chen Chi
text: Take the trail near the restroom you will find the spot for the second picture.

name: Zach Locks
text: Cool little Lighthouse, but there's no way to get a good view of it without going on on rocks right at oceans edge and risking a big wave knocking you off to your death. You can walk right up to it from otherside, but don't expect to get the view you see most people take without exposing yourself to some danger.

name: Ron Osborne
text: Well worth the visit.  A picturesque spot within a short walk from the parking area.  We also spotted a seal or two in the harbor.

name: Regina Sokolinski
text: Easy access, parking us provided

name: Tamara Plimmer
text: Beautiful view of the sea. Two trails give you a view of the Lighthouse from opposite directions. Dog friendly.

name: Jennifer R Vernier
text: It's beautiful. When we got there on Thursday June 20, we waited 15 minutes in a line of cars to get to the parking lot. In this area, you take a bit of a walk down to the right to see the lighthouse sorta at the side. Not the best view. Then from the parking lot, walk over to the left for a trail & wooden steps down to a rocky area. There's a decent side view for those of us who aren't brave enough to get a real photographer's shot. Still, beautiful area.

name: Myles Brown
text: Can not go inside lighthouse or keepers house.  Due to Coast Guard people still live there, since lighthouse is still functioning & in use to this day.

name: Jean Beaulieu
text: Great short walk located on MDI

name: Christa L
text: Beautiful

name: Ryan Parker
text: Beautiful..no more to say

name: Dave Roche
text: BEAUTIFUL. There really isn't much more to say about it. Definitely check it out if you're in Acadia, and don't forget your camera!

name: Grace Silva
text: Beautiful, worth the drive to see !!!

name: Barbara Bainbridge
text: Enjoyed seeing this Maine lighthouse, different from those in NC. Parking lot not very big. In summer, could see back ups

name: Cody Daniels
text: This is a beautiful and well up kept light house. There is also a little trail that enables you to see the lighthouse from a different angle other than the one that leads right to it. Beautiful to see in almost all types of weather.

name: Randy Harrell

We went here when we first arrived to Acadia National Park and got some great information from the friendly, knowledgeable staff. There are bathrooms here, which are handy.
You would be wise to purchase your tickets online and print out a copy or two before you arrive and you too can become part of the 2%...

name: Corey
text:
Hulls cove is a great place to get park information and learn about on going activities as well as to get park passes, maps and small trinkets. Recently re-built the facility is fantastic and you will find the rangers waiting at the desks during business hours ready to help you plan your time in the park and recommend things to do.
Hours vary by season so look it up on their web site to be sure but typically run 8 to 5.

Staff is super friendly and be sure to pick their brains to figure out what to do in this fantastic park. There are also alot of informational postings on the park, safety and wildlife. Definitely check it out as you start your park visit.

name: Carolyn LeCroy
text: Acadia NP is so BIG and has something for everyone.   We hiked the Carriage  Roads, Stoney Man with a park ranger and Upper & Lower Doyle Waterfalls (moderate, beautiful), Fox Hollow (3/4 mile) where bears hang out around dusk.  I wanted to do another portion of the Appalachian Trail this visit, but hubby''s arthritic toe wasn't cooperative. Also, have to plan another trip to see the fall foliage in NY, PA, VA, Skyline Drive and Blue Ridge Parkway.

name: Sean Faison
text: The rangers are all friendly and fun to talk to. The Visitor's center is 52 steps from the parking lot. If you don't like climbing stairs that can be an issue otherwise it's a wonderful place.

name: kevin Bell
text: All the information you need about Acadia National Park starts here. We parked at the end of the parking lot and started our day here with a 7.5 mile (1 1/2 hour) bike ride straight to Jordan Pond House via Eagle lake carriage road. Here we had our lunch and enjoyed pop overs and a sandwich. We left our bikes there and hike along Jordan's Pond around South Bubble up to North Bubble. We proceeded over to South Bubble and straight down to Jordan Pond trail back to Jordan House. Total hike was about 4.5 miles (2 1/2 hours). We hopped back on our bikes and headed back on the carriage trails to visited center. A great day and workout in Acadia.

name: Richard Hunter
text: Very serious about Covid precautions, but the lack of folks in the gift shop makes it nicer to be there.  Bathrooms were good.  Staff was friendly.   Get your year pass and help the park system and potentially save yourself a couple of bucks if you go to some other park or monument.

Start your adventure with the @AdventureKrewe #AdventureKrewe tip: while Cadillac MTN at sunrise Maybe a thing. Then, stop at the gift shop to get the National Park Passport Stamp, that you can't get at any other visitor center, along with hats, pins, blueberries, hiking sticks, and much more. On the way out, stop by the Junior Ranger table to get a booklet of activities for your kid to get engaged into Acadia National Park. Definitely stop here and Thompson Island (small island on bridge to Mt. Desert Is.) before heading on the park loop road, and into Acadia and Bar Harbor.

Many stop here for the lobster roll which always seems overstuffed (with claw and knuckle meat) and definitely ranks up there with the best in Maine. But I'm more likely to be there for the all-you-can- eat fish fry (check to be sure it's on the menu when you plan to go; the schedule changes seasonally). The haddock is lightly battered and fried perfectly leaving the fish moist, flavorful, and perfectly done.
It's been a while since I've had enough appetite to make it through the initial serving and ask for seconds; mostly I take home enough leftovers from the first plate for at least one more meal at home.
There are certainly lots of other choices and make sure you check the specials board. Portions are very generous but prices are on the low side.

name: Steve Page
text:
Consistently good food. I have always been pleased with the quality of the food served at the Eagle's Nest. Their portions are large, and I have enjoyed the flavor of every meal I've eaten here.
Also, their wait-staff are exceptionally friendly and prompt.
There is only 10-15 tables in the dining area, but that lends to a cozy, more intimate setting. You can see out to a beautiful section of the Penobscot River from every seat in the house!
The dining atmosphere is comfortable and relaxed, with the feel of a 20th-century diner, which is a good thing. The folks at Eagle's Nest have found the perfect combination of food, value, service and size, and they shouldn't change a thing!
