name: Lee Crowell
text:
This is a comparison of 4 breakfast restaurants all located in downtown bar harbor. I rank them in the following order with a possible rating of zero to five stars.

2 Cats  5 stars

Jeannie’s Great Maine Breakfast  4 stars

Jordan’s Blueberry Pancakes 3.5 stars

Cafe This Way 3.5 stars

2 Cats by far is the best place for breakfast. Their mildly spicy home fries are pre boiled and cooked to perfection. Scrambled egg mix was fluffy and not greasy. Excellent corned beef hash. The spicy country sausage was grilled not greasy and delicious. Fresh homemade biscuit and excellent coffee.

Jeannie’s Great Maine Breakfast excels in service. They’re just plain nice people. The blueberry pancake was delicious. Homemade oat toast outstanding. The home fries need improvement. They seemed to have been pre cooked in a fryer and then left too long in a warmer leaving them too dry. I much prefer grilled home fries vs fried in oil.
Coffee was a little bland.

Jordan’s Blueberry Pancakes confused me. Their name suggests good pancakes but if I had to guess I believe they’re made from an instant mix vs made from scratch because they’re bland. The blueberry sauce was superb but wasted on a stack of disappointing pancakes. The coffee and grilled home fries were very good.

The surprisingly best thing about Cafe This Way was the blueberry pancakes with a rich and crispy texture.  The coffee was also excellent and their dining room very comfortable. I got there early they appeared to be over staffed the dining room only half full but they sat me and never came back. After spending about five minutes watching the staff stand around talking to each other I finally walked over and asked to be waited on. The service never got better. My issue with Cafe this Way is their overuse of oil. The fried home fries and the scrambled egg mix were greasy. The sausage was actually deep fried. Definitely not my preference.

text: Tried for the 1st time 2 weeks ago and went back a few times.  Overall solid pizza, decent ingredients, good mix of flavors, staff was friendly.  We had the Supreme, Bohemian, Cowboy Kick, and BBQ chicken.  Enjoyed the Supreme the most.  Liked the use of black pepper on the Bohemian, have to copy that at home.  I'm dinging them 1 star for rushing the BBQ chicken.  They were busy, it was just cooked and a bit blonde.  Still, I will definitely return based on the other pizzas and the overall experience, and will encourage others to check them out.

name: Clayton Mixer
text: Yikes. We ordered one large bacon and pepperoni pizza. Over $21! Then, we waited over half an hour after they said it would be "six more minutes." Then when they brought the pizza to us (this was a pick up order), they gave us a $10 gift card and told us, and I quote, "We are giving these out randomly." Suspicious. Turns out our pizza was burnt to a crisp. The crust was black as can be and we ended up throwing most of it away. It was inedible. Even the small parts that were less charred had almost no cheese and mounds of sauce. They could have been honest with us and told us they ruined our pizza, but instead they underhandedly gave us a gift card and concealed the charred nature of the pizza. Thanks! What a waste of money. 😬

name: Unschooling Mama
text: We've been trying every pizza place in Ellsworth recently. Being a former pizza cook for many years, I am fairly picky when it comes to Pizza and often make it at home myself. Sometimes we like to go out. We decided to try finelli's this time. Despite the one hour wait time we were going to give it a shot. Any decent pizza place is going to have at least a 50 minute wait time on a Friday night anyway. After an hour and 5 minutes we went to pick up our pizzas one small cheese pizza and one medium carnivorous Rex Pizza,we still had to wait another 10 minutes because they literally put the pizzas in when we walked in the door to pick them up. Now I still understand how the business works and it was busy. the carnivorous Rex was delicious albeit the same size as my small pizza so I paid extra for a medium size and got the size of the 12 inch cheese. again it was busy so I'm sure the Joe didn't have enough time to get warm enough to stretch and stay at the size not the worst thing in the world.the cheese pizza however was burnt to a crisp with two large bubbles that pretty much took the cheese of the entire pizza. it was already 8:30 at night by then and I wasn't going to wait for a replacement that night. I ended up having to make something else for my kids who did not want to eat the cheese pizza. We called right back and after some negotiation and a few disgruntled words from the cook,Stephanie assured us we would get a replacement for both pizzas on Monday because she was working. Today is Monday and I call back for my replacement pizzas.for the record I never asked for a replacement for both pizzas but that's what they offered. Today they only replace the cheese whatever. They said 30 minutes, I figured I'd give them 35. I had to wait an extra 5 when I got there and my cheese pizza is Stone Cold. So I have to put it in my oven so my children can eat. Needless to say we will not be going back to this pizza place. Might I suggest Mike's country store or Pat's Pizza!

text: Hannaford Market in Belfast has a great selection of food items, a very nice olive bar, good quality cold cuts and fresh fish.  Their prices are always reasonable given today's good costs. What I appreciate most, is that sale items are truly good foods like cheeses, cold cuts, meats, fish, vegetables and fruits, not just convenience or junk foods.  For example, I found smoked Gouda on sale, a cheese most stores rarely discount or will often overcharge for.  There's a nice selection of produce and dairy products, prepared deli salads, and a good salad bar. It's a great place to grocery shop, and a worthwhile stop if you are camping locally and want to minimize your food prep while expanding your meal options.

name: Sharon Lee
text:
Bell the Cat has been a Belfast cornerstone for at least 20 years.  When I first became aware of them, they were a little sandwich shop at the corner of Main and High Streets, where Out on a Whimsey is now.  They moved to be the in-house cafe for Mr. Paperback, in the Reny's plaza, stayed after the bookstore went indie, and have most recently moved to a former chain restaurant location on Belmont Avenue.  The food has always been a little "off center," not your usual sandwich shop fair, but interesting and inviting.  The staff has always been good-natured and willing to discuss what was on offer with knowledge and flair.

On our last visit, both my husband and I went for comfort food:   I had a grilled cheese sandwich with ruby sweet potato soup; my husband had a tuna melt.  There was live music, and a group of regulars eating lunch, as well as a smattering of early tourists -- and us.  Highly recommended.

name: Perks Advisor
text: Portland International Jetport is one of those lower stress airports with relatively easy access.  The airport feels spacious and there are enough flights you can connect to all the primary hubs.  Parking is reasonable in relation to larger airports and there are some food and beer concessions at the airport.

text: I really enjoyed passing through the Portland International Jetport - PWM in Maine. I do not believe I have ever been in a Jetport before, but it is similar to an airport and a little different from a typical airport. I like the architecture here as there is a lot of natural light that comes in and there is a wide open space with high roofs. I like the wooden ceiling and all of the cool things to see in the airport from local art that features giant bear sculptures to a cool mermaid mural. I liked all of the different options to eat here too. The Jetport was very clean and well maintained and all of the staff here was very helpful in making sure that you find your way and get to where you are going.

text: I really like PWM but there are a few things that are costing it the 5th star it used to have.  For one thing, it used to be small enough to act like the walking distances didn't matter for people with disabilities or who have some trouble waking, but as the Jetport grows, it is time to consider just how long the walk from the rental car center to the ticket counter of American is for someone with luggage who has difficulty walking. There is an uphill ramp and cobblestones to deal with. I've been told there is an indoor, easier way to navigate this, but your out if town visitors don't know this and it can be cold even in summer here when it is rainy and foggy! You need better signage and some consideration for how an older, less mobile crowd is supposed to navigate your Jetport at 5 am!!

name: Stephen Arlaud
text: I have been in alot of airports all over the world and I like this airport to fly out of and into. First the whole airport has been either renovated or expanded as is very new. Probably more than half of the airport is new expansion. There has been ample parking short term and long term in the garage. To pickup someone you can go to the cell phone lot, the garage or at the curb down by baggage area. Rental cars are easy to get to, just walk out the revolving door of the terminal and across under covered crosswalk to the garage elevators straight ahead in glassed structure. Just go down one floor and your in the rental lobby and cars are right out some doors in same building and floor to covered garage area. If your picking someone up and want to go in, go to the short term parking into the garage first floor and then walk toward the curved glass covered walkway to the terminal and straight ahead. There is seating, tv and flight status display right there. The passengers come down the escalator, stairs or elavator right at waiting area. There are 3 luggage belts right to left of the waiting area as you come in the revolving door. The airport is pretty well laid out and has quite a few covered boarding walkways and some outside boarding walkways if needed.

I've had the unfortunate pleasure of asking for help to jump start my car and I met a very friendly guy from North Carolina (I think that was it) who tried to help me and then waited until someone came and got me.

name: jack gondela
text: No potable water. So you can't drink the water. You can wash your hands with the water and then touch your lunch. The bathroom doors are so heavy that they must be propped open or only the strongest visitors can enter or exit. This sort of design is rarely seen outside buildings designed by a government committee with too many members.  There is here a room full of tourist brochures and helpful staff during bankers hours. Just brochures in off times. Every garbage can has signs warning about the dangers of eating out of garbage cans. This is extremely useful if you didn't know eating out of garbage cans was a bad idea. That said there are nice flower garden here in the summer and a covered picnic table for those who would like to eat lunch at 108 decibels of traffic noise. Sometimes when you come here the bathrooms are closed for cleaning. The look on the face of someone looking forward to a bathroom visit for the last fifty miles when they discover they have to hold it for another 89 miles is worth the price of a visit. Free!

resp.text:
Lori, Thank you for taking the time to review Marden's.  As a surplus/salvage store, we know we aren't always in perfect shape and aren't right for every shopper.  Our focus as a surplus/salvage bargain store is to provide our customers with the best possible price on name brand goods.  As such, we don't spend a lot of time or money on making our stores "pretty".  Our goal is to be clean, simple and full of constantly changing bargains.  I hope you understand.
Sandy - Customer service team

resp.text:
Annie, Thank you for leaving us a review.  We really appreciate it when our customers take the time to let us know how they feel. For over 55 years, we have taken pride in our bargain pricing and this has not changed. Our typical discount runs from 30%-60% off retail (and even more in some cases).  If you are ever in our stores and see any item that isn't priced right, please let one of our supervisors or managers know. When comparing identical items, we want to be the lowest price! We do our best to price all items accurately, but sometimes mistakes can be made.
Sandy - Customer service team

name: Christina Levitan
text: We booked a cottage here pretty much at the last minute for an unplanned weekend trip. The price could not be beat for what we received. Even though it was technically an off season visit, the property overall was extremely well taken care of. The grass was very healthy and had been cut that day. They do ask that you clean up after yourself. For example, sweep up before you leave, tie up the trash, no dishes in the sink, no smoking, just keep the place orderly which isn't a lot to ask for. We did have to go to the office to request a broom, as they asked us to sweep. We only had a dust pan available but unfortunately the grass they cut that day stuck to our shoes and came in. We wanted to make sure we stuck by their requests. They gave us a broom right out of their office, so that was nice. We had all the forks, knives, spoons, pans, salt, pepper, plates, and cleaning supplies for the dishes that we needed and then some. They had an ac /heating unit on the wall that provided heat for the entire cottage as long as we kept all the doors open. So that had its own pros and cons if you want privacy and the cottage or rooms do get cold quickly if you don't have access to that unit. All of these things were really easy to deal with and we would love to come back during the summer season so we could enjoy it during warmer weather. My only complaint which was a bit unsettling to me was our bed was clearly not new (clean) sheets and they were from at least the guests before us as the sheets had many hairs in the bedding. I completely understand that the price reflects this and cleaning up after ourselves helps keep the price down but there should always always always be clean sheets in between guests.

resp.text:
Dear Christina,

Thank you for staying with us and taking the time to share your experience. We are glad to hear you enjoyed your stay. Our housekeeping staff always services each room and cottage before being rented to another guest. I do apologize that you feel your room was not properly serviced. I will be sure to address this, and appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

Thank you again, we hope to see you the next time your travels bring you to the area!

Thought at first that there was trouble: my reservation made 6 months ago had been canceled by a summer temp person erroniously.  Luckily they fixed it, else there wpuld have been a meltdown.  All ended well but just lucky they had a free site.

name: Cory Ricker
text: One of the best brew festivals in Maine is held here!

text: This is wonderful place to go out camping with your family-friends.

name: Jimmy Lebel
text:
(Translated by Google) Quiet, clean, exceptional service and close to walking trails.

(Original)
Tranquille, propre, service exceptionnel et pres des sentiers de marche.

name: Abhishek Master
text:
This is an excellent campground location. You just need to reserve them well in advance as the spaces run out quickly.
The restroom facilities are brilliant. You can get wood for fire from vendors right outside the campground. Similarly you can get coin operated bathing facilities as well around. There is a little trail towards the ocean that you can try, the views are mesmerizing. All in all, you won't be disappointed with your stay here.

name: Heather Walters
text: A very nice campground.  Rangers try to keep it pretty quiet and family friendly.  No showers or  cell signal but convenient for using the island explorer buses when the are running

name: Lubel Lubel
text: I recommend it for good and relaxing times with friends

name: Corey
text:
It's a simple camp ground no showers,no hookups and not built for mega RVs. If you want that stuff don't come. We stayed for 4 nights and used our site to launch to the many things to do in the park. Sites can be small but have enough room to set tents tarps and in A loop and some of B a camper.
The staff was help full and friendly and from the campground you can get to the island explorer bus or drive right out onto the main roads. Showers are close as are places to get ice and wood.
We did have so issues with loud obnoxious nehibors playing with fire and blasting music but the rangers handled it when the complaints were raised. Only issue is you can't find a ranger up front after 10 and without cell coverage you can't even call the number for help.
Be prepared to camp on the rougher side and don't expect cell service. Use it as a place to base your national park adventure and you are all set due to its great location. Hopefully you get quiet good company.

name: Oliver Peckham
text: Had a great stay at Blackwoods Campground. The camping area was clean and spacious, bathrooms were nearby, there was a nice fire pit, and the location was pretty convenient to the most scenic views of the park. Check-in and check-out were very easy.

name: Ayana Pimental
text: My husband and I stayed here and we LOVED it. You can walk RIGHT into the park right around Otter Cove. Everyone was polite and very helpful with our questions. The one downfall is there are no showers in the campground, BUT there are some coin operated ones if you pull a right out of their driveway. You can't miss it right on the left. They also sell firewood there and you can do your laundry!! Very nice so close to the camp.

name: Heleen Raes
text: A great camping site that I enjoyed staying at. The camping lots are close to each other so you can see your neighbors, but there’s still a lot of forest in between you so you still have a lot of privacy. The camp site comes with an individual firepit and picnic table, which makes it comfortable. People sell firewood near the camping so you can get a lot of wood there, as it is not allowed to bring wood from out of state. The restrooms are clean as well and there’s a water faucet where you can get water. The only reason why I don’t give it 5 stars is because the campsite doesn’t have showers, while they definitely build them.

name: Jacob Mulligan
text: Make your reservation far in advanced! It's a simple campground with 1 national park trail running through it. You're close to everything Acadia has to offer. There is little space between sites. You can have more than 1 car and 2 tents, even though their website says so, it just costs $25 for the additional car that must be parked 5-15min walk from the campsites.

name: Nicholas Ceffalo
text: Pretty crowded but great if you're just using it as a home base while you explore all that Acadia has to offer. Make reservations!

name: Kelly Johnson
text: Basic wooded campground. Quiet and relatively close to bathrooms. Close to the park. Can hang hammocks up so that is a plus 🙂

name: Joe
text: One of the more quiet campgrounds I have been to given its capacity. There are also some great views and access to trails near the campground.

name: Kevin White
text: Campsites are way to close and everyone was very loud and nothing was done. I would definitely camp somewhere else. When you can hear your neighbors snoring your campsites are to close.

name: Kahli C
text: Best campground ever! Make sure to check their seasonal price & availability differences before going!

name: Nick Tanski
text: Love the camping grate commutes close by for hiking boating whatever you would like

name: Frankie Dioguardi
text: Beautiful camping experience. Bit crowded on the large holiday weekends, but very convenient with nice bathrooms.

name: Dakota Hewlett
text: Beautiful setting for camping, great for tents and close to Bar Harbor and the park loop road.

name: Thanassi Karageorgiou
text:
The scenery and campsite were extraordinary, but I'm taking one star off for two reasons:

1) When booking online, they never mention the mandatory $25 park access / parking fee. They just hit you with it at the registration booth.

2) No showers on campground. You have to get in your car and drive 7 minutes outside the campgrounds to a PAID shower facility. Not a huge inconvenience, but come-on. You're already capitalizing on a "nature experience" which isn't even real nature becuase you're providing conveniences like paced roads, parking spaces, running water and garbage disposal. Why not go all the way and make the showers part of the campground? Just lump the extra cost into the booking.

name: Ed Weber
text: Clean and well-run.

name: Polly Kirchner

name: Al Stuart

There is drinking water in the compound and a very nice area for cars, food and equipment. recommended! Close to lots of tracks

name: Mark Robinson
text: One of the best kayak trips I've had in a long time. I put in at the bistro, or at the dock right behind it. There was no parking right there on the dock so they directed me about two-tenths of a mile down the street where I parked at the school. I walked back to the boat landing and launch The Kayaks. Rowed down to Chauncey Creek and down to the bridge and around the point where the water got a little rough.

name: Kelly Botti
text: Stopped for a look at the boats. There was a double rainbow. Just beautiful.

name: Neal Fillmore
text: Food, as always, was excellent! Obviously, it may have been a challenging day, as the phone wasn't answered for 2 calls, a third call the person answering the phone was challenged to get the order and then a call was returned from the missed calls! I hope they all can catch their breathe!

name: Branden Keller
text: Great food, great drinks and a great view.

name: Astroid YT
text: Nice little stop! Try the restaurant as well, fare for all tastes. Also if youd like to just have an ive cream theres a little shop out back.

name: Tom Philbrook
text: Not really a marina ! Room for a couple boats ..Parking needs to be addressed as not much parking at town dock and will get a ticket if you stay more than one hr..Owners need to do more informing customers to park across the street on there own property..
